– Conversation: follow-up questions take the last questions and answers into account; New conversation starts over. The conversation stays in this browser tab only and is not stored on the server.

– The search uses the full-text index; the best-matching passages go with your question to the provider shown at the top of the panel. The AI only reads what you may read and what is open to the AI (What the AI may access). A page's tags and property values count as part of its text.
– While the answer is written, a shimmer and a typing cursor show progress; the sources appear one after another.

Questions about the last or latest thing ("What did I last do with …?") always consider the newest journal days that match the question. The AI also reads handwriting in drawing blocks and notebooks (typed text and text recognised on iPhone/iPad) and the text of a page's PDFs, Office files and images – with the same rights as the page; journals with a PIN stay closed to the AI.

en.heading: Semantic search (optional)
paragraphs: Questions in Chinese, Japanese, Korean or Thai are split into words even though these languages don't use spaces. "浦东新区的发票在哪里" searches for 浦东新区 and 发票; small particles like 的 are left out.
In addition to full text, Flowplan can store content as vectors ("embeddings"). Ask AI then also finds passages without the same words – "trip" finds "company outing".
– Set an embedding model at the instance provider:
– Ollama: download nomic-embed-text (under Administration → AI → Download model or ollama pull nomic-embed-text) and enter it.
– OpenAI-compatible: e.g. text-embedding-3-small; Gemini: text-embedding-004. Anthropic has no embeddings.
– Turn on semantic search and save. Or via the environment: FLOWPLAN_AI_SEMANTIC_SEARCH=on and FLOWPLAN_AI_EMBEDDING_MODEL=nomic-embed-text.
– A background job embeds changed pages and records chunk by chunk; unchanged chunks are not embedded again. At most FLOWPLAN_AI_EMBED_PER_HOUR chunks per hour (default 5,000).
– Never embedded: journals with a PIN, pages and spaces closed to AI, and the trash. Permissions and personal AI rules apply to every question.
– Semantic search always uses the instance provider. People using their own provider search full text only.

– Storage: 4 bytes per dimension and chunk (up to about 900 characters) – with nomic-embed-text (768 dimensions) about 3 KB per chunk, roughly three to four times the text; with 1,536 dimensions about 6 KB. Only a checksum of each chunk is stored, not its text. The administration shows the number and size.
– Switching off deletes all vectors; changing the model rebuilds them.
– For very large instances (hundreds of thousands of chunks) there is no vector index yet; the search stays correct but gets slower.

en.heading: Related pages
paragraphs: Below a page and in a database record, Related pages shows up to eight pages and records that belong with it. It also works without AI:
– Without semantic search, it counts links from the page, links to the page, pages with the same links, the same tags (multi-select) for records, and similar titles in the full-text index.

– With semantic search, pages with similar content are added ("by meaning"). Only the vectors already stored are compared – no request goes to the provider, no text leaves the server. The open page must be readable for the AI; every hit passes the same rules as Ask AI.
Only what you may read is shown – no private spaces of others, no hidden records, nothing from the trash or locked journals.

Every block has a handle on its left: drag it to move the block, click it to open the block menu for turning it into something else, colouring, duplicating and moving. Select several blocks at once with the mouse or the keyboard.
More on this topic: Documents and the editor · Formatting, callouts and captions · Keyboard shortcuts

en.heading: Handle and dragging
paragraphs: + and a handle (⋮⋮) appear to the left of a block – to keep the page calm, only at the block under the mouse pointer (anywhere on its row, the margin to its left included); while you type, they stay hidden until you move the mouse again. The handle sits where the block's text starts, so an indented paragraph has it next to its text. Blocks inside toggles, callouts and quotes have a handle of their own; the box keeps its handle too. In callouts and quotes the box's handle also stands for its first line; further paragraphs inside have their own. {since=0.9.6} A meeting block has one handle at its title row for the whole block; the blocks in its summary keep theirs. Blocks inside a closed toggle have no handle until it is opened. You can still reach the handles by keyboard (Tab outside the text); a handle with keyboard focus always shows, with a ring. On touch devices only the block with the cursor has a handle, large enough to tap – so tap into the block first. Empty paragraphs have no handle unless the cursor is in them. To see every handle, turn on Settings → Appearance & language → Editor → Always show block handles (on this device). Reading mode and locked pages have no handles.

– + adds an empty block below and opens the block menu with / right away; hold ⌥/Alt to add it above. This works below any block, including tables, images, embeds and columns. Blocks inside columns have no + of their own – Enter and / work there. {since=0.9.6}

– Dragging the handle shows an insertion line – also into callouts, quotes or columns. How far left or right you drag picks the level: to the right over a list item the block becomes its sub-item (the line indents), to the left it lands one level up – that's how you nest lists and move blocks into or out of toggles. The block that will receive the drop – a list item, list, toggle, callout, quote or column – is lightly tinted while you drag. At the left or right edge of a block you get columns. Hold ⌥/Alt when you let go to drop a copy; the original stays.

List items and tasks stay what they are when moved: outside their list they form a list of the same kind of their own, and a numbered item keeps its number. Right next to a matching list they become part of it; in another kind of list they adapt. Dropped into a list, blocks land at the level of the drop line without empty items: paragraphs become items, other blocks such as tables become part of the item before them.
⌘ ⇧ ↑/↓ moves the current block past its neighbour. Every block action can be undone on its own.

Between two blocks without text (such as a table and an image), click into the gap or on the edge. With the keyboard, use the arrow keys until the blinking line appears, then type or press Enter. Enter on a selected image adds a paragraph below it. The + in the toolbar above the text inserts the chosen block below the current one – only in an empty paragraph does it replace it. To convert a block, use Turn into … in the block menu. {since=0.9.6}

en.heading: Block menu
paragraphs: A click on the handle selects the block and opens the block menu (from the bottom on phones). Esc closes the menu and keeps the block selected. {since=0.9.6} With a mouse it opens to the left of the handle, so the block stays visible; only without room on the left does it open to the right. Its heading names the kind of block. At its top is a search field: typing filters every action and block type, Enter runs the first hit. With a mouse, submenus open to the side – further left, or over the menu when there is no room, never over the block; on phones in place. Entries show their keyboard shortcuts.

– Turn into … – text, heading 1–4, bulleted list, numbered list, task list, toggle, toggle heading 1–4, quote, callout, code, block equation, page (the block becomes a sub-page, a link to it stays) or 2 or 3 columns; list items become a toggle with their sub-items as its content, quotes and callouts can be dissolved
– Colour – text or background colour for the whole block (see block colours)
– Add block below and Add block above – an empty block with the block menu with /, also on touch devices {since=0.9.6}
– Copy (⌘ C), Cut (⌘ X) {since=0.9.6}, Duplicate (⌘ D), Move (up, down, below a heading of the page, to the top or to the end), Comment, Ask AI, Copy link to block and Delete
– Callout type, Symbol and Colour (callouts), Width (videos and embeds) and Text direction where they fit
– Select several – the selection mode on touch devices

en.heading: Selecting several blocks
paragraphs: With a mouse, drag a rectangle from the margin or an empty spot: every block it touches is selected and tinted light blue. Esc in a block or a click on its handle selects it (after the click, Esc first closes the block menu and the selection stays). ↑/↓ select the block before or after, ⇧ ↑/⇧ ↓ or ⇧-click on a handle extend the selection, ⌘ A (Ctrl A) selects all blocks. In text, the first ⌘ A selects the block's text, the second all blocks. {since=0.9.6} On the selection, Delete, ⌘ D (duplicate), ⌘ ⇧ ↑/↓ (move), Tab/⇧ Tab (indent), ⌘ C/⌘ X/⌘ V (copy, cut, paste blocks after it) and / (block menu for all) work; dragging any of their handles moves all. Copied or cut blocks are pasted back as blocks, also in another page; other apps get the text. A click into the text or Esc ends the selection.

On touch devices Select several in the block menu starts the selection mode: circles take the place of the handles, a tap selects a block, another one extends the selection up to it; when all items of a list are chosen, the whole list is. The bar at the bottom moves, copies, duplicates, moves below a heading or deletes the selection, ⋯ holds the rest of the block menu, Cut included. {since=0.9.6} Done or Esc ends the mode.

en.heading: Indent
paragraphs: – Tab at the start of a paragraph or heading indents it (up to eight levels), ⇧ Tab outdents it. If a toggle is directly above, Tab moves the block into it instead, and ⇧ Tab moves it back out. Lines indented before stay as they are.

– Without a keyboard {since=0.9.8}: the block menu has Indent and Outdent – they do the same as Tab and ⇧ Tab and are greyed out when nothing would move. With several blocks selected (on touch devices via Select several) they all move at once, and one undo brings them all back. As buttons in the formatting toolbar you can add them under Customize formatting toolbar.
– Backspace at the start of an indented line first removes one level.

– In lists Tab nests the item below the previous one; if it can't be indented, nothing happens – Tab never leaves the text. Enter in an empty list item moves only that item one level up, one level per Enter; at the top level it becomes a normal paragraph. Enter at the end of an item with sub-items starts a new first sub-item. In code blocks Tab inserts two spaces, in tables it moves to the next cell. With a block selection, Tab also moves code blocks and tables into a toggle.

en.heading: Tabs
paragraphs: The Tabs block stacks content in tabs – for example instructions for different systems or variants of a text. Type /tabs to insert it. Each tab has a title and can hold any blocks: paragraphs, lists, tables, images, toggles and even more tabs.
– Add: + at the right of the tab strip – type its name right away.
– Rename: double-click the tab or press F2.
– Reorder: drag the tab or press ⌘ ⇧ ←/⌘ ⇧ → (Windows/Linux: Ctrl+Shift+←/→).
– Delete: Delete on the tab; Undo brings it back. The last tab stays – delete the whole block from its block menu.
– On phones: swipe the tab strip; every action is in the ⋯ menu.
– Keyboard: ←/→, Home and End switch tabs, Enter jumps into the tab's content.
Flowplan remembers which tab you're looking at, for you on this device. Others see their own tab, and switching never creates a new version. You can write in different tabs at the same time.
Turn into → Tabs makes tabs from selected blocks, each heading starting a new tab. Turn into → Headings with content turns them back into plain text.
Printing, PDF, e-books, the HTML export and published pages show all tabs one after another, each with its title as a heading; Word, Confluence and Jira also get a heading per tab.
Markdown: Flowplan writes and reads the format of the Obsidian "Tabs" plugin:
tab: Windows Download the installer.
tab: Linux Install the package with your package manager.
If a tab contains code blocks itself, the outer fence gets longer (` ``tabs ) – or use ~~~tabs. A plugin options line such as top, multi` is ignored on import.

en.heading: Text direction
paragraphs: Paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, callouts and table cells in Arabic, Hebrew or Persian run right to left automatically: the direction follows the block's first letter. Bullets, checkboxes, quote bars, callout icons and block handles are then on the right.

In the block menu (click the handle ⋮⋮) → Text direction you set Automatic, Left to right or Right to left for a block and everything inside it. The direction is kept in the HTML export; Markdown has no place for it.
With the browser extension you save web pages to Flowplan in one click: the whole article, just the selection, a bookmark or single highlights. It runs in Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera and Firefox.

en.heading: Setting up
paragraphs: – In Flowplan, create a personal API token under Settings → API & AI assistants (or Settings → Web clipper → Create token) and choose the permission Browser extension only. Such a token can do nothing else: it opens neither the API nor MCP and cannot read anything but the list of your targets.
– Install the extension (see below) and click its icon.
– Enter the address of your instance, for example https://flowplan.example.com, and the token. The browser now asks once for access to exactly this address – the extension never accesses other sites.
Sign out in the extension's window removes the token from the browser and gives up the access to the instance. You can revoke the token in the settings at any time.

en.heading: Saving
paragraphs: Click the extension's icon or press Alt+Shift+F. Choose the target – the extension remembers it – and optionally tags:

– Whole page: the extension finds the actual article and leaves out navigation, ads, cookie notices, comments and sidebars. Links and images keep pointing to the original page. The link to the source sits at the top of the new page.
– Selection: only the selected part of the page, with formatting and links.
– Bookmark only: title, address, description and favicon go into the space's Lesezeichen (bookmarks) database (see Web clipper). Duplicate links are refused.
Depending on the target you get:
Target Whole page / selection Bookmark
A space a new page in the space a record in its bookmarks database
A page a new sub-page a record in the bookmarks database of its space
A database a new record with the text as its document; the link goes into the first URL property as for a page

Tags go into a property named Tags (or Schlagwörter, Labels) when the database has one; new tags are added as options. In the bookmarks database the extension creates the Tags property the first time. On pages the tags appear as #tag below the source link.
The server cleans the content once more: scripts, forms, embedded foreign pages and event attributes are dropped, just like when pasting into the editor.

en.heading: Highlights
paragraphs: Select text on a web page and choose Highlight in Flowplan in the context menu (or press Alt+Shift+H). The passage is appended as a quote with a link to the source:
– If the target is a page, all highlights end up one below the other on that page.
– If the target is a space, the first highlight of a web page creates a new page for that source; further highlights of the same web page go onto the same page.
– If the target is a database, every highlight becomes a record.
A green check mark on the icon confirms the save, a red exclamation mark reports an error (such as an expired token).
Change the shortcuts in Chrome at chrome://extensions/shortcuts, in Firefox under Add-ons → gear → Manage Extension Shortcuts.

en.heading: Installing
paragraphs: The extension lives in the source code under extensions/browser/ and needs no build step.
– Chrome, Edge, Brave: open chrome://extensions, turn on Developer mode, click Load unpacked and choose the folder extensions/browser.
– Firefox: open about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox and Load Temporary Add-on → extensions/browser/manifest.json. For a permanent installation, have the ZIP signed at addons.mozilla.org.
– Building the package: npm run extension:zip writes extensions/browser/dist/flowplan-.zip – upload this file to the Chrome Web Store, Edge Add-ons or addons.mozilla.org.

en.heading: Privacy and permissions
paragraphs: – The extension reads a page only when you call it (icon, context menu or shortcut) – it does not run in the background on every page.

– Permissions: activeTab (the current page, only after your click), scripting (to read it then), contextMenus, storage (address, token, the target chosen last) and access to exactly your Flowplan address, asked for only when connecting.
– It only sends to your instance. Cookies are not sent along; the token alone signs in.
– End-to-end encrypted spaces are not offered as targets: the server never writes plaintext into them.
– The server allows requests from browser extensions (CORS) only for the two clipper addresses /api/clipper/targets and /api/clipper/save, and only with a token – see API and webhooks.
Instead of JSON, a webhook can post a ready message to a chat. On the webhook's page under Settings → Webhooks, choose the format in the card Target:
Format Target What arrives
JSON n8n, Home Assistant, your own services The signed JSON above
Slack Incoming Webhook or a Slack app Block Kit: header, text with the record as a link, fields for changed properties, a line with who and when
Matrix Room webhook (e.g. hookshot) or the Matrix client API HTML message (formatted_body) with plain text as body
Microsoft Teams Incoming Webhook or the workflow "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received" Adaptive Card with a fact list and an Open in Flowplan button
Discord Channel webhook Embed with title, link, fields and timestamp
Next to the form a preview shows the message for a sample event, and below it the content that is actually sent.

en.heading: Setup
paragraphs: Slack
– Messages only: Create an app in Slack (api.slack.com/apps), turn on Incoming Webhooks, pick a channel and enter the address https://hooks.slack.com/services/… in Flowplan.

– With thread replies: Give the app the chat:write scope under OAuth & Permissions, install it and enter the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…) and the channel ID (in Slack: channel details, at the bottom); invite the bot to the channel (/invite @App). For replies, also enter the signing secret (Basic Information). After saving, the webhook's page (card Delivery) shows a Request URL (…/api/webhooks/slack/): turn on Event Subscriptions in the app, enter that address and subscribe to the bot event message.channels (message.groups for private channels). Replies in the thread of a Flowplan message then appear as a comment on the record – written in the name of the person who set up the webhook, prefixed with "Slack:". Threads are matched for 30 days.
Matrix
– Room webhook: Create a "generic webhook" in the room with a bridge such as hookshot and enter its address. Flowplan sends text and html (plus the fields of a Matrix message).

– Client API: Create an access token for a bot account, invite the account to the room and enter the homeserver address (e.g. https://matrix.example.org), the access token and the room (!id:server or #alias:server) in Flowplan. Flowplan sends with PUT /_matrix/client/v3/rooms/{room}/send/m.room.message/{txn}; retries of the same delivery never create duplicate messages.
Microsoft Teams
– In Teams, add a workflow to the channel from the template "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received" (or a classic Incoming Webhook) and enter the address it shows.
Discord
– In the channel settings under Integrations → Webhooks create a webhook and enter the address https://discord.com/api/webhooks/…. Mentions (@everyone etc.) are never triggered.

Access tokens, bot tokens and signing secrets are stored encrypted and never shown again; when editing, an empty field keeps the stored value, and Remove stored credentials deletes them. Chat addresses follow the same rule as other webhooks: public HTTPS only, and every delivery checks the address again.

en.heading: Templates
paragraphs: Every event has a default text that you can change in the form (Template for event). The buttons insert placeholders:
Placeholder Content
{title} Title of the record or page
{actor} Who caused it
{page} Database or parent page
{changes} Changed properties as a list (in the digest: the due records)
{url} Link in Flowplan
{text} Comment text or the name of the mentioned person
{date} Date and time (in the digest: the day)
{count} Number of changes or due records

A small Markdown is allowed: bold, _italic_, ` code , text, lines starting with - as a list and > as a quote. Flowplan converts it to the platform's markup (Slack mrkdwn, Matrix HTML, Teams Markdown, Discord Markdown). Values from Flowplan are never read as markup – a in a title stays a . When {changes}` is not in the template, Slack, Teams and Discord show the changes as fields of their own and Matrix as a list below. Long values are shortened (titles 200 characters, comments 1,000, at most 10 changes and 25 due records) so the platforms' limits are kept. The language of the messages (default texts, date format) is set per webhook.
Example:
{actor} changed [{title}]({url}) in **{page}**:
{changes}

en.heading: Daily digest
paragraphs: With the event Due today (digest.due, "daily at …") a list of the open records that are due today or overdue arrives once a day at the chosen time (the browser's time zone when the webhook was created) – from all databases of the workspace or only the chosen one. The due date is the date property with "Due", "Fällig", "Deadline" or similar in its name, otherwise the first date property; done is what the database's done rule says. Private records are never listed. When nothing is due, nothing is sent.

In cluster mode, several Flowplan instances serve one installation: one PostgreSQL database, one Redis, one S3 bucket and any number of instances behind a load balancer – for more people active at the same time and updates without downtime.

en.heading: Do you need it?
paragraphs: Most teams do not: a single container carries about 20 simultaneously active people with SQLite and about 30 with PostgreSQL (see Sizing). Cluster mode pays off when more people regularly work at the same time, or when Flowplan should keep running through updates and the loss of a server. In return it brings three services you have to run (or rent) and back up.
If Flowplan only has to survive the loss of a server, active/passive without cluster mode is often enough – see High availability, with an example at Hetzner. {since=0.10.0}

en.heading: Requirements
paragraphs: Switch it on with FLOWPLAN_CLUSTER=1. Then these are required:
What Variable For
PostgreSQL 16+ DATABASE_URL=postgres://… All data. SQLite is a file on one host and does not work. See PostgreSQL.
Redis (tested with 7) REDIS_URL=redis://… or rediss://… (TLS) Live editing, presence and rate limits between the instances. Redis does not need to persist any of it.
S3 storage S3_BUCKET, S3_ENDPOINT, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY All files; the local uploads/ folder is only a cache. See Storage, S3 and backups.
If one is missing, an instance does not start and lists every problem at once in the log. REDIS_URL without cluster mode is ignored with a warning.

Also required – here too an instance refuses to start without them: keys that are identical on every instance. A single container creates some keys itself in its data folder – in a cluster every instance has its own folder, and each would create different ones. So set the same values everywhere:

– FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY or FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY (or their …_FILE variants, e.g. for Docker secrets) – otherwise an instance cannot read stored secrets and signatures of the others (two-factor sign-in, AI keys, unlocked share links). See Stored secrets.
– WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY and WEB_PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY (a VAPID key pair, e.g. from npx web-push generate-vapid-keys) – otherwise push subscriptions only match one instance. See Push notifications.

Coming from a single container without these variables, take the values from its data folder so stored secrets and push subscriptions stay valid: the content of secrets.key as FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY (in addition to a FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY; both are read), and publicKey/privateKey from web-push-keys.json as WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY/WEB_PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY.

en.heading: What the instances share
paragraphs: – Live editing and presence: changes to documents, records and whiteboards, cursors and "who is here" reach every instance through Redis. Two people on different instances work together as on one. The data itself is in PostgreSQL; if a message is lost, the browser catches up on its next sync. No sticky sessions are needed.

– Rate limits: limits such as those for AI requests count across all instances (through Redis). Limits already kept in the database (failed sign-ins, demos, MCP) applied to all of them anyway. So do the at most three parallel AI answers per person. {since=0.10.0}
– Imports and print views: their state is in the database, so any instance answers the progress of a background import and serves a print view. {since=0.10.0}

– Leader-only jobs: exactly one instance leads at any time (elected through a lock in PostgreSQL). Only it runs the timed jobs: reminders, automations, page reviews, the search indexer, text extraction from files, cleanup and retention, digests, scheduled backups and Markdown exports, LDAP, calendar and issue sync, inbound e-mail, Telegram, AI background work and the monitoring alerts. If it fails, another one takes over within seconds. Every round is guarded: taking the lead raises a counter in the database, a round starts only while it is still its own, and each job holds a lock of its own while its round runs – so a round of an instance that lost its connection never runs twice beside the new leader's. {since=0.10.0}
– Queues: every instance sends e-mails, push messages, webhooks and chat-app messages; each message is taken by exactly one instance.

– Files: the bucket is the truth. A request that stores a file answers only once the file is in the bucket; every instance reads through its cache and fetches from the bucket what it lacks. Uploads in several requests (long transcriptions, recordings of meetings and notebooks, an import between its preview and the import) keep their parts in the bucket under /tmp/, so each request may reach another instance. {since=0.10.0}

en.heading: Health, readiness and shutdown
paragraphs: Address Answers Meant for
/api/health/live 200 as long as the process answers – no database check, since a restart does not fix a database outage Liveness probe
/api/health/ready 200 when the schema and the data steps are done {since=0.10.0} and the database, Redis and the bucket answer; 503 otherwise and while shutting down Readiness probe, load balancer
/api/health as before, see Health check Docker health check, apps
Without a token, /api/health/ready only answers ok/error per check; with FLOWPLAN_METRICS_TOKEN as a bearer token, response times and error messages are added.

FLOWPLAN_READY_REQUIRE decides which checks count for readiness – a list of database, redis and objectStorage, by default all three. The database always counts. If Redis fails, the default turns every instance "not ready" at once and the load balancer has nothing left. With FLOWPLAN_READY_REQUIRE=database,objectStorage they stay ready: editing and saving keep working, only live changes between instances arrive on the next sync, and each instance counts rate limits on its own. The Helm chart sets it so. {since=0.10.0}

Shutdown: on SIGTERM the instance immediately answers 503 on /api/health/ready, closes its live connections (browsers reconnect through the load balancer to another instance), finishes open requests, hands over the lead and signs off from the others. Give it 30 seconds for this (stop_grace_period, terminationGracePeriodSeconds). Running jobs and workflow steps still finish, uploads under way reach the bucket, then it hands back leases and the lead – all within FLOWPLAN_SHUTDOWN_SECONDS (20). {since=0.10.0}

en.heading: Schema before the start
paragraphs: Each instance brings the database schema up to its version on start (under a lock; they wait for each other). Cleaner is a separate step before the instances start, which fails loudly:
DATABASE_URL=postgres://… node /app/scripts/db-schema.mjs

The Docker Compose example and the Helm chart work this way. The instances still check the schema at their start under the same lock (nothing to do then) and are ready only once it is current; FLOWPLAN_PG_SCHEMA_AUTO=off leaves it to the separate step alone. {since=0.10.0} The schema is only extended, never shrunk: during a rolling update, old and new instances run side by side.
So that browsers do not mix versions meanwhile, every image carries a deployment id. {since=0.10.0}

en.heading: Docker Compose
paragraphs: A complete example lives in deploy/compose/cluster: PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7 with a password and without persistence, MinIO as S3 including bucket creation, the schema step, two Flowplan instances and Caddy as load balancer. It is meant for trying things out on one host and as a starting point; in production, run the database, Redis and storage as separate, backed-up services.
git clone https://github.com/yannicschuller/flowplan.git
cd flowplan/deploy/compose/cluster
cp .env.example .env    # replace every "change-me" value
docker compose up -d
In it:

– .env holds APP_URL, FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN and the passwords for PostgreSQL (POSTGRES_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_ADMIN_PASSWORD), Redis and MinIO – placeholders only, to be replaced. FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY and WEB_PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY are required too – empty in .env.example; without them docker compose up stops with a hint (see Requirements).
– The schema service runs once before the instances (node /app/scripts/db-schema.mjs); the instances have FLOWPLAN_PG_SCHEMA_AUTO=off.

– flowplan-1 and flowplan-2 each have their own volume as a cache, FLOWPLAN_PG_POOL=20 and a health check on /api/health/ready. More instances: copy the flowplan-2 service and add it to the Caddyfile.

– Caddy distributes round robin over ready instances (health check on /api/health/ready) and passes live connections through unbuffered (flush_interval -1). For HTTPS, replace :8080 in the Caddyfile with your host name.

– PostgreSQL runs with max_connections=200. Flowplan connects as the role flowplan, which owns the database but is no superuser: POSTGRES_PASSWORD is its password, POSTGRES_ADMIN_PASSWORD that of the image's superuser postgres, for administration only. On the database's first start postgres-init.sh creates the role and installs pg_trgm (and pgvector when the image has it) into flowplan_ext. A volume made with an older version of the example keeps its roles – there flowplan is still a superuser until you demote it.

Another load balancer (nginx, Traefik, HAProxy) needs the same: health check on /api/health/ready, no buffering for server-sent events (/api/documents/live, /api/live and the cursor channels), long read timeouts, uploads up to 110 MB and FLOWPLAN_TRUSTED_PROXIES matching the number of proxies.

en.heading: Kubernetes (Helm)
paragraphs: Installation, moving from a SQLite container, updates, backups and troubleshooting are on the page Kubernetes. {since=0.10.0}

The chart in deploy/helm/flowplan has cluster mode built in (cluster.enabled=true). It does not create PostgreSQL, Redis or S3 – use managed services or their own charts. The connection addresses live only in Secrets you create yourself:
kubectl create namespace flowplan
kubectl -n flowplan create secret generic flowplan-cluster \
--from-literal=DATABASE_URL='postgres://flowplan:<password>@postgres:5432/flowplan' \
--from-literal=REDIS_URL='redis://:<password>@redis-master:6379/0'
kubectl -n flowplan create secret generic flowplan-s3 \
--from-literal=S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID='<key-id>' \
--from-literal=S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY='<secret>'
# the keys every pod shares (push keys: npx web-push generate-vapid-keys)
kubectl -n flowplan create secret generic flowplan-keys \
--from-literal=FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(openssl rand -base64 32)" \
--from-literal=WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY='<public VAPID key>' \
--from-literal=WEB_PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY='<private VAPID key>'
helm install flowplan deploy/helm/flowplan -n flowplan \
--set appUrl=https://flowplan.example.org \
--set cluster.enabled=true \
--set cluster.replicas=3 \
--set cluster.database.existingSecret=flowplan-cluster \
--set cluster.redis.existingSecret=flowplan-cluster \
--set cluster.keys.existingSecret=flowplan-keys \
--set s3.bucket=flowplan --set s3.endpoint=https://s3.example.org \
--set s3.existingSecret=flowplan-s3

The example values-ha.yaml holds the same with ingress, SSO, metrics and network policy. The chart takes secrets only as references to Secrets (s3.existingSecret, existingSecret), not as values. {since=0.10.0}
What the chart does in cluster mode:
– Schema job as a pre-install/pre-upgrade hook (node /app/scripts/db-schema.mjs) before pods of a new version start. Without it (cluster.migration.enabled=false) the pods do it on start.
– Rolling updates without downtime (maxUnavailable: 0), a PodDisruptionBudget (cluster.podDisruptionBudget.minAvailable, default 1) and pods spread over nodes where possible.

– Probes: liveness on /api/health/live, readiness on /api/health/ready – without Redis (cluster.readyRequire: database,objectStorage) {since=0.10.0}; before stopping, a pod waits cluster.preStopSeconds (5) so the load balancer takes it out.

– No volume: /app/data is an emptyDir per pod (cluster.cacheSizeLimit, 5 Gi) that keeps itself below 70 % of its limit (FLOWPLAN_CACHE_MAX_MB) {since=0.10.0}; files live in the bucket, backups come from PostgreSQL (pg_dump).

– Database role: the role in DATABASE_URL should own the database but not be a superuser. Many PostgreSQL charts make their user a superuser – create a role of its own then, see Role without superuser rights.
– Connections: cluster.poolSize (10) per pod plus three of its own {since=0.10.0}; replicas × (poolSize + 3) must stay below the server's max_connections.

– Shared keys: every pod gets FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY and WEB_PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY from the Secret in cluster.keys.existingSecret. If the keys are named differently in your Secret, name them with cluster.keys.encryptionKey, cluster.keys.webPushPublicKey and cluster.keys.webPushPrivateKey. Keep a copy of the encryption key apart from the backups.
– The chart refuses to install if the database, Redis, the bucket or cluster.keys.existingSecret is missing.

For ingress-nginx, the chart sets the annotations for live connections and uploads itself (no buffering, timeouts of an hour, ingress.bodySize); the chart's README describes other controllers and explains every value. {since=0.10.0}

en.heading: Administration → Monitoring → System
paragraphs: The System section under Administration → Monitoring shows how the installation runs:
– Mode (single container, or cluster with the number of instances), Database with version and reachability,
– Connections of this instance (open, idle, waiting) and the Timeouts,
– Redis with version and messages sent, received and failed, Object storage with bucket and reachability,
– the Leader and since when it leads,
– the Shared queues (files, mail, push, webhooks, chat apps),
– in a cluster, a table of all Instances with their state (leader, ready, stopping), busy and waiting connections, memory and last heartbeat. An instance silent for 30 seconds drops off the list.
"Waiting" connections mean requests are waiting for a free database connection – raise FLOWPLAN_PG_POOL or add instances.

A second instance without cluster mode: when two instances run against the same PostgreSQL database without FLOWPLAN_CLUSTER=1, the log and Monitoring warn: "A second Flowplan instance is running against the same database without cluster mode …" – timed jobs then run twice. {since=0.10.0}

en.heading: More variables
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning
FLOWPLAN_CLUSTER empty 1 (or true, on) switches cluster mode on. Equivalent: FLOWPLAN_MODE=cluster.
REDIS_URL empty redis://:@host:6379/0, with TLS rediss://…. User, password and database number go into the address.
FLOWPLAN_READY_REQUIRE database,redis,objectStorage Checks that decide /api/health/ready (above).
FLOWPLAN_INSTANCE_ID host name + random Name of the instance in the overview and in the application_name of its database connections. The Helm chart uses the pod name.
FLOWPLAN_REDIS_PREFIX flowplan: Prefix for keys and channels when several installations share one Redis.
FLOWPLAN_LEADER_INTERVAL 5000 How often (ms) instances check the lead; decides how fast a failed leader is replaced.

FLOWPLAN_SHUTDOWN_SECONDS 20 How long stopping on SIGTERM may take (running jobs, uploads, handing over the lead) – a few seconds below the platform's grace period. Applies to the single container too. The Helm chart sets terminationGracePeriodSeconds less the pause less 5. {since=0.10.0}

FLOWPLAN_CACHE_MAX_MB empty Size (MB) above which an instance in a cluster removes the longest unused files from its cache; they stay in the bucket. Empty: no limit. The Helm chart sets 70 % of cluster.cacheSizeLimit. {since=0.10.0}

en.heading: Workflows in a cluster
paragraphs: The steps of workflows wait in a queue in the database. Every instance claims steps that are due with a lease (2 minutes); a fencing token makes sure an instance whose lease has run out can no longer commit. If an instance fails, another takes over its steps once the lease has expired. New steps wake the other instances through Redis; without the bus they check on a timer. Schedules and date triggers run only on the leader and exactly once per slot. FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_WORKERS sets how many steps an instance runs at once.

en.heading: Known limits
paragraphs: – Files: if the bucket does not answer, uploads fail with 503 – a file counts as stored only once it is in the bucket. {since=0.10.0}

– Restores and instance moves with one instance. An uploaded backup sits in the cache of the instance that received it and is only applied once that instance leads. Applying it replaces every table in one transaction; requests from other instances wait meanwhile and fail after FLOWPLAN_PG_LOCK_TIMEOUT. On Kubernetes, an emptyDir is lost on restart. So scale down to one instance first (cluster.replicas=1, or only flowplan-1), restore, then scale up again. The same goes for the move tool.

– Redis is a single point: if it fails, editing and saving keep working, but live changes between instances only arrive on the next sync, each instance counts rate limits on its own, and with the default FLOWPLAN_READY_REQUIRE every instance turns "not ready" (above; the Helm chart leaves Redis out {since=0.10.0}).
– No Redis Sentinel and no Redis Cluster: Flowplan talks to exactly one Redis address. A managed Redis with a stable address works.
– Per instance remain the progress displays of restores and moves and the search indexer's backlog figures.

en.heading: Next
paragraphs: – Sizing: how many instances and what hardware.

– Switching the database: bring an existing instance to PostgreSQL. For a cluster, first turn on S3 in the single container and wait until every file is in the bucket (Administration → Storage & backup, or objectStorage.pending at 0 in /api/health).
Several people write on the same page at the same time without overwriting each other. Comments, mentions and the inbox keep conversations next to the content.

en.heading: Edit at the same time
paragraphs: – Documents and record contents are merged with Yjs (CRDT): every change is kept, even when two people type in the same paragraph.

– Changes reach the others within a fraction of a second: the server pushes every saved change right away to everyone who has the same document open (server-sent events). Only what changed is sent, not the whole document.
– Coloured cursors and selections with names show where others are writing; their movements arrive immediately too.

– The sidebar, open databases and the inbox stay current too, without reloading: when someone creates or renames a page, changes a record in the database you have open, or mentions you, you see it within a few seconds. The server only says that something changed – never titles or pages you may not see; your browser then fetches what changed with your permissions. Several tabs share one connection for this. Without that connection (for example behind a proxy that buffers server-sent events), Flowplan syncs every 10 seconds as before. {since=0.10.2}
– Without a connection you keep working; changes are merged as soon as the network is back.
– Database changes are checked for version conflicts: if someone changed the same record in the meantime, your change is not silently written over it but refused, and you see the new state.
– Guests with an edit link also work live and see the members' cursors; members see the guests as "Guest · ".
– Whiteboards also have live cursors as in Miro.

en.heading: Suggest changes
paragraphs: The pen button Suggest in the toolbar turns on suggestion mode. Typing then does not change the text directly:
– Inserted text appears underlined in green, deleted text stays in place, struck through in red. Typing over a selection creates both.
– Deleting your own suggestion removes it completely.

– Above the text, a bar shows the number of open suggestions. Expanded, it lists each one with person and text; a click jumps to the spot. ✓ accepts a suggestion (the insertion stays, the deleted text disappears), ✗ rejects it. Accept all and Reject all settle everything at once.
– Suggestions are part of the document: they appear for everyone right away and stay saved until someone accepts or rejects them. Everyone who may edit the page can accept and reject.
– Formatting, paragraph breaks and moved blocks are applied directly even in suggestion mode; other people's changes never become your suggestions.

– Changes in code blocks are marked as suggestions too. When accepting or rejecting leaves a paragraph or list item completely empty (a suggested new paragraph rejected, a fully deleted one accepted), it disappears as well.
– Suggestions by the AI: in Ask AI, Suggest as changes puts the answer into the page as suggestions in the same way – with your name and "(AI)".

en.heading: Reactions
paragraphs: – Comments: below every page and record comment, the smiley adds a reaction (👍 ❤️ 🎉 😄 👀 ✅ 🙏 🔥). A click on an existing reaction joins it or takes your own back; the tooltip shows who reacted. Everyone who may see the page can react.

– Paragraphs and headings: selecting text or right-clicking in the text opens the text menu. At the top are the reactions for the paragraph, below them formatting (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, highlight, code, link), Comment and Copy, in tasks also Due date. The reactions sit as small pills on the block, are saved in the document and appear for everyone right away; a click on your own takes it back. This works for everyone who may edit the page. Shift + right-click brings up the browser's menu.
– Text comments have their own reactions in the thread.

en.heading: Follow pages
paragraphs: The bell at the top of a page (on a phone Follow at the top of the ⋯ menu) turns Follow on or off. Whoever follows a page gets a notification as soon as someone else changes it – one per page, until you have looked at it again – and for every new comment on it (for a database: also on its records). With e-mail set up, it lands in the e-mail digest. Whoever creates a page follows it automatically. Under Settings → Notifications, the kind "Changes to pages you follow" can be switched off for inbox, push and e-mail separately.

en.heading: Who has seen the page?
paragraphs: The eye next to the bell shows who opened the page and when. A tick means the person has seen the latest state; "older" means the page has changed since. Only people who may still see the page are shown.

en.heading: Changes since your last visit
paragraphs: If someone else changed a page since you last opened it, a notice with their names appears at the top. For documents, Show changes shows the text changes since your last visit (inserted and deleted, as in the version history). For databases the notice gives the number of edited records.
On the home screen, Recently viewed lists the pages you opened last; the quick search with nothing typed shows records too, grouped by day.

en.heading: Page comments
paragraphs: The speech bubble icon in the header opens the page's comments (on a phone it shows there only when there are open comments, with their count, otherwise Comments is in the ⋯ menu); comments on database records sit below the record. ⌘ Enter sends. Page and record comments are plain text. @ followed by a member's full name or e-mail address – say @Anna Berg – mentions the person: they get a notification, provided they may see the page and the record.

en.heading: Text comments
paragraphs: Below a document and in a database record's content, Text comments (n) opens the comment panel with all threads and the Show filter. Select text or a block and click New at the top of the panel to write a comment; if nothing is selected, Flowplan reminds you to select something first. The speech-bubble icon in the toolbar, in the text menu, or ⌘/Ctrl ⌥/Alt M takes you straight to a new comment. The X or clicking Text comments again closes the panel. {since=0.9.8}
– The commented text is highlighted; a click on it opens the thread.
– Replies, emoji reactions, Resolve and Reopen.
– Posts can be formatted (lists, links, quotes, code); @ opens the person search.
– Your own posts can be edited and deleted. People newly mentioned in an edit get a notification; those mentioned before are not notified again.
– If the text is deleted later, the quote stays in the thread.
– Line breaks in the passage stay line breaks in the quote, and embedded media show as “media block”. When you move a block up or down (or drag it), its comments move with it. {since=0.9.8}
– Drafts stay saved until you send or discard them.

en.heading: In the margin beside the text
paragraphs: On wide screens – with the sidebar open from a window about 1280 pixels wide – open text comments appear as cards in the right margin, each at the height of its passage, on pages and on records opened as a page. A card shows the start of the first post, who wrote it and how many replies there are. When passages are close together, the cards stack below each other in the order of the text.

– A click on the highlight or the card opens the thread right in the card, with replies, reactions, mentions and Resolve thread; the passage is highlighted more strongly and the page does not jump away. Esc or a click in the text collapses the card again.
– A new comment (⌘/Ctrl ⌥/Alt M or Comment in the text menu) opens its field right in the margin beside the passage.
– Resolved threads leave the margin. Text comments (n) below the document stays the overview of all threads, with the Show filter.
– While cards are in the margin, the table of contents folds into its small button at the edge of the text; a click on it opens it as a list.

– When there is too little room beside the text – a narrow window, the page comments are open – and on phones, the threads are in the comment panel below the document. A click on a highlight opens the thread there and scrolls to it.
Under Settings → Appearance & language → Editor, set Text comments to In the margin (the default) or Below the document. The setting applies to your account on all devices.
Text comments exist in documents and in the contents of database records, also in exports and content archives.

en.heading: Mentions
paragraphs: – @Name in text or a comment notifies the person. The person search only shows members who may read the page.

– Only people who may see the page – and, for a record, the record – are notified; never the author. Someone who would hear about the comment anyway gets a single notification, the mention. If the page lies in a journal with a PIN, the notification only says “This journal is locked.” until the PIN is entered.
– Guests do not see other members; their mentions notify nobody.

en.heading: Inbox
paragraphs: The Inbox in the sidebar collects mentions, comments and replies that concern you (who hears about comments), date reminders as well as comments and records from guests. Unread items are marked; a click jumps to the spot – for text comments straight into the thread. You choose which events arrive as push notifications under Settings → Notifications (see Search, inbox and push).

en.page: Configuration: AI, voice notes and push
paragraphs: The environment variables for AI providers, transcribing voice notes with Whisper and push notifications up to running your own push relay.

en.page: Configuration: AI, voice notes and push
en.heading: Voice notes (Whisper)
paragraphs: Voice notes in the editor are always stored as audio. With a Whisper service in your own network, Flowplan also turns them into text; the recording never leaves your server.
Variable Default Meaning
WHISPER_URL empty Address of an OpenAI-compatible Whisper server (POST /v1/audio/transcriptions), e.g. http://whisper:8000. Turns transcription on.
WHISPER_MODEL Systran/faster-whisper-small The model name as the service expects it.
WHISPER_LANGUAGE de Language of the recordings (e.g. en).
WHISPER_API_KEY empty Only if the service requires a key.
WHISPER_MAX_MB 200 Largest recording in MB.
WHISPER_RESPONSE_FORMAT verbose_json Response format of speech recognition; falls back to json once.
WHISPER_DIARIZE empty on: ask for speaker separation (diarize=true), only for services that support it.
WHISPER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS empty How long one transcription may take, in seconds. Without it a minute per MB of audio, at least 3 minutes, at most 2 hours. Raise it for slow CPUs.
WHISPER_PROMPT empty Vocabulary for all workspaces (names, acronyms, separated by commas), sent to Whisper as prompt – before the workspace's glossary, together at most about 550 characters.
WHISPER_VAD empty on: skip silence first (vad_filter=true, faster-whisper/speaches) – fewer made-up lines.
MEETING_LIVE_TRANSCRIPTION on off: transcribe meetings only after they stop instead of while recording.
Example with speaches (formerly faster-whisper-server) in the same Compose project:
whisper:
image: ghcr.io/speaches-ai/speaches:latest-cpu
volumes:
- whisper-models:/home/ubuntu/.cache/huggingface/hub
restart: unless-stopped
Then set WHISPER_URL=http://whisper:8000 for Flowplan. Newer speaches versions do not download models by themselves; download it once, for example from the Flowplan container:
node -e "fetch('http://whisper:8000/v1/models/Systran/faster-whisper-small',{method:'POST'}).then(r=>console.log(r.status))"

small needs about 1 GB of memory and transcribes roughly in real time on a normal CPU; base is faster and less accurate, medium more accurate and considerably slower. Do not make the Whisper service publicly reachable – only Flowplan talks to it.

whisper.cpp as the Whisper service (fast on Apple Silicon or with a GPU): start whisper-server with the OpenAI path, with conversion of the recordings (needs ffmpeg on the service's machine, for WebM) and with voice activity detection:
whisper-server -m models/ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
--inference-path /v1/audio/transcriptions --convert \
--vad -vm models/ggml-silero-v5.1.2.bin -mc 0 -ml 400 -sow

--vad -vm … skips silence (whisper.cpp's models/download-vad-model.sh downloads the Silero model), -mc 0 stops Whisper from latching onto a made-up line and repeating it, -ml 400 -sow limits the segment length and splits on word boundaries – which gives more precise source chips. Then set WHISPER_URL=http://whisper:8080 for Flowplan. With faster-whisper/speaches, WHISPER_VAD=on does the same.

Long recordings: whisper.cpp with large-v3-turbo needed about 380 seconds for 8.4 MB on an M2; on a CPU it takes considerably longer. Flowplan waits a minute per MB; if that is not enough, raise WHISPER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. When a transcription fails, admins see the cause in the meeting block.

en.page: Configuration: AI, voice notes and push
en.heading: AI
paragraphs: All optional; the values apply until an admin saves under Administration → AI. Details: AI.
Variable Default Meaning
FLOWPLAN_AI off on switches AI on.
FLOWPLAN_AI_PROVIDER empty ollama, openai (OpenAI-compatible), anthropic or gemini. If only OLLAMA_URL is set, Ollama is used.
OLLAMA_URL empty Address of Ollama, e.g. http://ollama:11434 with the Compose service.
FLOWPLAN_AI_BASE_URL per provider Address of the provider, e.g. https://api.mistral.ai/v1 for an OpenAI-compatible service.
FLOWPLAN_AI_MODEL empty Model, e.g. llama3.1 or gpt-4o-mini.
FLOWPLAN_AI_EMBEDDING_MODEL empty Model for semantic search, e.g. nomic-embed-text (Ollama). Without it: full-text search only.
FLOWPLAN_AI_API_KEY / FLOWPLAN_AI_API_KEY_FILE empty The provider's key. Never stored in the database and only used for the provider from the variables.
FLOWPLAN_AI_ACCESS everyone selected: only people who were enabled.
FLOWPLAN_AI_GUESTS off on: guests may use AI too.
FLOWPLAN_AI_USER_PROVIDERS off on: people may add their own provider and key.
FLOWPLAN_AI_FEATURES all Allowed features, comma-separated: write, summarize, ask, database, actions, whiteboard.
FLOWPLAN_AI_DEVICE on off: no on-device AI in the apps for iPhone, iPad and Mac. Independent of FLOWPLAN_AI.
FLOWPLAN_AI_SEMANTIC_SEARCH off on: semantic search with the embedding model.
FLOWPLAN_AI_EMBED_PER_HOUR 5000 Maximum chunks embedded per hour for semantic search.
FLOWPLAN_AI_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR 300 Maximum AI requests per person and hour (plus 30 per minute, 3 at once).

en.page: Configuration: AI, voice notes and push
en.heading: Push notifications
paragraphs: Variable Meaning
WEB_PUSH_SUBJECT Contact for the push services, e.g. mailto:admin@example.com.
WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY / WEB_PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY VAPID key pair. If not given, Flowplan creates one in FLOWPLAN_DATA_DIR/web-push-keys.json. Required in cluster mode.
MOBILE_PUSH Notifications to the apps for iPhone, iPad and Android. Nothing to set up; off turns them off altogether. Default: on.
PUSH_RELAY_URL The push relay notifications to the apps go through. An HTTPS origin only (http only for localhost), without a path. Default: https://push.flowplan.org.
PUSH_RELAY off: no relay. Apps then only get notifications if they have an Expo token (older app versions), through Expo's push service. Default: on.

MOBILE_PUSH_CONTENT Whether the notification's text comes along – and with it the buttons Done and Tomorrow on due tasks and Reply on comments (Buttons on notifications); Mark as read is always there. Empty (default): only where it is end-to-end encrypted, i.e. through the relay; through Expo (older apps) only "something new in the inbox" as with Web Push, and Live Activities only with times, no titles. on: also through Expo and with titles in Live Activities – readable by Expo, Apple and Google. off: never, not even through the relay.
The VAPID keys must not change, otherwise all browsers lose their subscription. Outgoing HTTPS to the push services of Apple, Google and Mozilla (Web Push) and to the push relay must be possible.

en.page: Configuration: AI, voice notes and push
en.heading: Push relay and end-to-end encryption
paragraphs: Notifications to the apps go through the Flowplan push relay (push.flowplan.org). Only the relay holds the credentials for Apple (APNs) and Google (Firebase); your instance needs none of its own – self-hosted instances, too, reach the apps from the App Store and Google Play this way.

– End-to-end encrypted: every app installation creates a key pair (X25519) per instance and gives the instance only the public key. The instance encrypts every notification with it (HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM, a fresh one-time key per notification); only the app on the device decrypts it. The relay, Apple and Google only see ciphertext – plus the kind of message, which buttons it has, the number on the app icon and when it was sent. If a notification cannot be decrypted, the app shows "New notification".

– Signed: the instance has a signing key pair of its own (Ed25519), created on first use. The private key is stored only encrypted in the database (like stored secrets, see above); the public key is published at /.well-known/flowplan-push. The relay only accepts signed requests, and only for devices that registered for exactly this instance. For this, APP_URL must be the public HTTPS address, and /.well-known/flowplan-push must be reachable from outside.

– What is stored: per app installation the relay token (only encrypted) and the public key. Both go with signing out, removing the device under Signed-in devices, or when the relay reports that the device can no longer be reached. Neither tokens nor keys nor content are logged.

– Live Activities (iPhone) for the timer and focus are also updated by the instance through the relay when their state changes. iOS renders their content itself – it cannot be encrypted. By default it therefore holds only times and the phase, no titles (MOBILE_PUSH_CONTENT=on sends the title along).
– Older app versions without the relay keep getting notifications through Expo's push service (exp.host), without text by default.

– Rotating the signing key: node --import tsx scripts/push-relay-key.mjs rotate in the repository, or as an administrator POST /api/admin/operations with {"action":"pushRelay.rotate"}. The new key is published at once and signs after a little more than an hour; the old one stays listed for 7 days (--grace-days or graceDays). For a key that may have leaked, --immediate or "immediate": true: the new one signs at once, all old ones are removed. {"action":"pushRelay.keys"} lists the keys (ids and dates only). Or under Administration → Push notifications → Rotate key ….
– Your own relay: only together with your own app build – see Running your own push relay.

– Checking it: Settings → Notifications → Send test notification sends at once through the relay, Expo and Web Push to your own devices and shows the result per device – for example that the relay could not verify the instance (/.well-known/flowplan-push not reachable) or cannot be reached. Administrators also see the relay address, whether /.well-known/flowplan-push is enabled and the APP_URL in use. See Test notification.

– State in the administration: Administration → Push notifications shows the relay in use (official or your own), whether it is on and otherwise why not, whether it is reachable right now (/healthz, with response time), whether the instance can fetch its own /.well-known/flowplan-push at APP_URL, the signing keys with Rotate key …, the deliveries of the last 24 hours per channel and the last error. See Administration → Push notifications.

For an instance's privacy policy, for example: "Push notifications to the Flowplan apps are delivered end-to-end encrypted through Flowplan's push service (push.flowplan.org) and the services of Apple (APNs) or Google (Firebase Cloud Messaging). These services receive a device token, the address of this instance, the time and the kind of the notification, but not its content." – extend it accordingly with MOBILE_PUSH_CONTENT=on or notifications through Expo.

en.page: Configuration: AI, voice notes and push
en.heading: Running your own push relay
paragraphs: The relay is open source (github.com/yannicschuller/flowplan-push) and can be self-hosted. The official Flowplan apps (iPhone and iPad from the App Store, Android from flowplan.org/download) don't need it – they only accept notifications through push.flowplan.org, because Apple and Google deliver to these apps only with Flowplan's keys. Your own relay makes sense if you build your own app version (own bundle ID, own Apple team) or want to reach instances in an internal network.

– Start the relay – as the Docker image ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan-push:latest (or built from the repository), e.g. in Coolify at https://push.example.com, port 8080, a volume on /data. Environment variables:
Variable Value
RELAY_STORAGE_KEY openssl rand -base64 32 – encrypts the stored device tokens
RELAY_PUBLIC_URL the relay's public address without a path, e.g. https://push.example.com (otherwise https://push.flowplan.org applies)
APNS_KEY_ID, APNS_TEAM_ID, APNS_KEY your Apple team's APNs key (.p8): key ID, team ID and the file's contents (base64 also works)
ALLOWED_BUNDLE_IDS your app's bundle ID, e.g. com.example.notes
FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT optional, your Firebase project's service-account JSON for Android
TRUST_PROXY 1 behind Coolify/Traefik

ALLOW_PRIVATE_INSTANCES true if instances in an internal network (private addresses, http://localhost) should send notifications – meant for development and closed networks only, as the relay's README says
https://push.example.com/healthz answers {"status":"ok"}; the start-up log says whether APNs and FCM are set up.

– Build the app – with your bundle ID and Apple team, PUSH_RELAY_URL=https://push.example.com (the app's build variable) and, for Android, your google-services.json. The app only registers with the relay it was built for.

– Configure the instance – PUSH_RELAY_URL=https://push.example.com. APP_URL must be the instance's HTTPS address and /.well-known/flowplan-push reachable for the relay. An instance can use one relay only: pointed at yours, it no longer reaches the store apps through the relay.
– Check – with the test notification.
Operations, key rotation, blocking abusive instances (node dist/src/cli.js block in the container) and backups are described in the relay's README.
The environment variables for sending mail and inbound e-mail, integrations such as GitHub and calendars, chat apps and workflows.

en.heading: E-mail (SMTP)
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning
SMTP_HOST empty Turns on sending e-mail: invitations, address confirmations, password resets and digests of unread notifications.
SMTP_PORT 587 Port. With 465 Flowplan speaks TLS directly, STARTTLS otherwise.
SMTP_SECURE by port true/false forces TLS from the start of the connection.
SMTP_USER / SMTP_PASSWORD empty Sign-in at the mail server.
SMTP_FROM Flowplan Sender, e.g. Flowplan .

SMTP_TLS_CA empty CA certificate of a mail server with a private or self-signed certificate (file path or PEM text, also on one line with \n). It is trusted in addition to the public CAs. {since=0.9.7}
SMTP_TLS_SERVERNAME empty The name the certificate is checked against when SMTP_HOST is an IP address or another name (e.g. mail.internal). {since=0.9.7}

SMTP_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED empty (verify) false turns certificate verification off – only this value (case and surrounding spaces ignored); any other keeps verifying. Flowplan then warns at startup and in Administration. {since=0.9.7}
Check delivery under Administration → E-mail → Send test email.

Internal servers with their own certificates: Flowplan verifies certificates by default. For a mail or directory server with a private or self-signed certificate, give its CA: SMTP_TLS_CA for e-mail, LDAP_TLS_CA for LDAP. In Docker, mount the CA file into the container (for example ./ca.pem:/certs/ca.pem:ro) and set SMTP_TLS_CA=/certs/ca.pem. If you reach the server by its IP address or by a name that is not in its certificate (such as 192.168.1.10 or pve.local), set the name from the certificate in SMTP_TLS_SERVERNAME or LDAP_TLS_SERVERNAME – verification stays on. For every connection Flowplan makes – also webhooks or AI providers inside your network – Node's NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/certs/ca.pem adds the CA to all of them; it is read at startup. If the test e-mail fails with "unable to verify the first certificate", the CA is missing; with "Hostname/IP does not match certificate's altnames", the name is. Only if neither is possible (for example a Proxmox relay with an auto-generated certificate), turn verification off with SMTP_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=false or LDAP_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=false. Then anyone on the network can pose as the server and read the SMTP or LDAP password – so Flowplan warns in the server log at startup, in Administration → E-mail or → Sign-in & SSO, and in the security overview. {since=0.9.7}

en.heading: Inbound e-mail (IMAP)
paragraphs: For inbound e-mail via webhook (Mailgun, Postmark, SendGrid, Cloudflare) nothing needs to be set. A mailbox of your own is polled over IMAP every two minutes:
Variable Default Meaning
INBOUND_MAIL_DOMAIN empty Domain of the inbound addresses, e.g. mail.example.com. The settings then show inbox+@mail.example.com for each address.
INBOUND_IMAP_HOST empty Turns on IMAP polling (together with INBOUND_IMAP_USER).
INBOUND_IMAP_PORT 993 Port (143 when INBOUND_IMAP_TLS=false).
INBOUND_IMAP_USER / INBOUND_IMAP_PASSWORD empty Sign-in at the mailbox. The part before @ is also the part before + in the addresses.
INBOUND_IMAP_FOLDER INBOX Folder that is polled.
INBOUND_IMAP_TLS true false only for a mail server on the same host or network (unencrypted).

INBOUND_MAIL_AUTHSERV_ID empty The id (authserv-id) your own receiving mail server or provider starts its Authentication-Results header with, e.g. mx.example.com. Also applies to inbound e-mail via webhook.

The mail server must support plus addressing (inbox+anything@… is delivered to inbox@…); Dovecot, Postfix, Gmail/Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 (switch it on there) do. Flowplan marks processed e-mails as read and deletes nothing.

Sender check: whether a sender counts as verified (SPF/DKIM/DMARC passed for the From domain) is read from the Authentication-Results header. The sender can put one in the message too – so only the topmost header with the id from INBOUND_MAIL_AUTHSERV_ID counts. Without the variable no sender counts as verified: workflows set to Verified senders only then never start, the default (all but failed ones) keeps running. The id is at the start of the header your server writes into received e-mails (Authentication-Results: mx.example.com; spf=pass …).

en.heading: Integrations
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning

FLOWPLAN_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE empty true allows webhooks to internal addresses and http:// – such as Home Assistant or n8n in the same network. Without this variable only public HTTPS addresses are allowed.
SPACE_GIT_EXPORT empty true turns on the Git export of spaces: space owners push their space into a repository of their own, daily or weekly.
SPACE_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS empty Allowed Git servers for it, comma-separated (e.g. git.example.org). Without it any public https:// server is allowed; internal addresses never.

SPACE_GIT_ALLOW_PRIVATE empty true also allows internal addresses for the servers listed in SPACE_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS – for example a Forgejo on the same host that the container reaches via --add-host git.example.org:host-gateway. Only works together with the list; every other server stays limited to public addresses.

ISSUE_SYNC_ALLOWED_HOSTS empty Own servers for the GitHub, GitLab and Forgejo issue sync, comma-separated (e.g. gitlab.example.org). github.com, gitlab.com and codeberg.org are always allowed; other servers only when listed here.
ISSUE_SYNC_ALLOW_PRIVATE empty true also allows internal addresses for the servers listed in ISSUE_SYNC_ALLOWED_HOSTS – for example a GitLab in the same network. Only works together with the list.

NETBOX_ALLOW_PRIVATE empty true also allows internal addresses and http:// for the NetBox import on whiteboards – for example a NetBox in the same network. Without it, only public HTTPS addresses. The address and token are never stored on the server.

PLUGIN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS empty HTTPS origins owners may register block extensions from, comma-separated (e.g. https://plugins.example.org). Without it only when the administration switches on Block extensions from any HTTPS address. The origins are also added to the frame-src of the Content Security Policy.

GIPHY_API_KEY / TENOR_API_KEY empty Key for the GIF search on whiteboards at GIPHY or Tenor (if both are set, GIPHY wins). Without a key the GIFs tab is hidden. Searches run through the server; chosen GIFs up to 8 MB are stored on the server.
EXPORT_GIT_* empty Deprecated: the Git export of the whole instance, see Push into a Git repository. Keeps working; the Git export of spaces is the better choice.

en.heading: Calendar sync
paragraphs: Two-way sync of database views with Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook / 365. Each person connects their own account; without a client ID that provider stays hidden. Flowplan asks for changes every ten minutes (the providers' push notifications are not used – they would need a publicly reachable HTTPS address verified with the provider).
Variable Default Meaning

GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CLIENT_SECRET empty OAuth client (type “Web application”) from the Google Cloud Console, with the Google Calendar API enabled and the scope …/auth/calendar. Redirect URI: /api/calendar-sync/callback/google.

MS_CALENDAR_CLIENT_ID / MS_CALENDAR_CLIENT_SECRET empty App registration in Microsoft Entra ID (web platform) with the delegated permissions Calendars.ReadWrite and offline_access. Redirect URI: /api/calendar-sync/callback/microsoft.
MS_CALENDAR_TENANT common common (work and personal accounts), organizations or a tenant ID.
People's refresh tokens are stored sealed in the database (like all stored secrets).

en.heading: Chat apps
paragraphs: Notifications to Telegram, Gotify, ntfy and Matrix. Everything can also be set under Administration → Chat apps; values saved there take precedence.
Variable Default Meaning
FLOWPLAN_MESSENGERS all Services people may connect, comma-separated: telegram, gotify, ntfy, matrix; off for none.
FLOWPLAN_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN empty Token of the instance's Telegram bot (from @BotFather). With it people connect Telegram through a link with a one-time code, without an own bot.
FLOWPLAN_TELEGRAM_API_URL https://api.telegram.org Address of the Bot API for the instance's bot – a self-hosted Telegram Bot API server or a relay/proxy. May be in the own network and http://.

FLOWPLAN_MESSENGER_ALLOW_PRIVATE as FLOWPLAN_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE true: people may name servers in the own network (internal addresses, http://) – e.g. Gotify or ntfy at home. Otherwise internal addresses are blocked, also when a name is later pointed at one.

The instance's bot without a public address: Flowplan uses no webhook but reads the bot's messages with getUpdates – only while a connection code waits (at most 15 minutes). Outgoing HTTPS to the Bot API is enough. The bot must therefore not have a webhook at the same time or be polled by another program (Telegram then reports a conflict, the administration shows it) – use a separate bot just for Flowplan.

Outgoing connections: to api.telegram.org (or the own API address), ntfy.sh and the servers people name. They go through the same check as link previews and webhooks: resolve the address, refuse internal addresses, use exactly the checked address, no redirects. Refused attempts appear as the security event “Internal address refused (SSRF)”.

The tokens of people and of the bot are stored encrypted like other stored secrets. If the key is missing after a restore, the administration enters the bot token again; connections with an own token are switched off after three failed attempts, and their owners learn it in the inbox.

en.heading: Workflows
paragraphs: Defaults for workflows; the administration can override them.
Variable Default Meaning
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOWS on Main switch; off: no new workflow pages, all paused
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_RUNS_PER_MINUTE 60 Runs per minute and workflow
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE_RUNS_PER_MINUTE 600 Runs per minute and workspace
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_STEPS_PER_RUN 200 Steps per run
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_CASCADE_DEPTH 5 Depth of workflows triggering each other
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_FOREACH_MAX 100 Items per “For each”
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_AI_TOKENS_PER_DAY 100000 AI tokens per workflow and day (0 = AI nodes off)
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_MAILS_PER_DAY 100 E-mails per workflow and day
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_RUN_DAYS 30 Days runs are kept
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_MAX_WAIT_DAYS 365 Longest wait or approval deadline
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_ACTIVE_PER_WORKSPACE 100 Active workflows per workspace
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_WORKERS 4 Steps at once per instance
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_HTTP on HTTP node allowed
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_HTTP_HOSTS empty Only these hosts (comma-separated)
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_HTTP_ALLOW_PRIVATE false Allow internal addresses (home network, n8n)
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_EXTERNAL_MAIL on E-mails to addresses outside the members

FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_EXTERNAL_MAIL_DYNAMIC off {since=0.10.0} such e-mail also to addresses from placeholders (form answer, inbound e-mail, AI answer); instances whose workflows already use it keep it on the update
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_TEST_RUNS_PER_MINUTE 10 Test and dry runs per person and minute
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_PARALLEL_RUNS 10 Runs of one workflow running at the same time (1–100); further ones wait in the queue
FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_RUNS_KEPT 10000 Keep at most this many runs per workflow (100–1,000,000); older finished ones are deleted daily, open ones never

> Development and tests only: FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_LEASE_MS (default 120000, a step's lease), FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_POLL_MS (5000, how often each instance looks for due steps) and FLOWPLAN_WORKFLOW_SWEEP_MS (60000, how often expired leases go back to the queue) shorten the queue's timings, in milliseconds. Do not set them in production.
The environment variables for S3 and database backups, PostgreSQL and cluster, encryption, stored secrets, moving an instance and legal pages.

en.heading: S3 and database backup
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning
S3_BUCKET empty Turns S3 on. Without this variable everything stays local.
S3_ENDPOINT AWS API address of the storage, e.g. http://minio:9000.
S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID / S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY – Access keys with read and write access to the bucket.
S3_REGION us-east-1 Region. Garage requires its own value (often garage).
S3_PREFIX flowplan Folder in the bucket; files under /uploads/, the database under /db/.

S3_LOCAL_CACHE empty Keep only part of the files on this server, e.g. 2GB or 500MB: above it, the least recently used files confirmed in the bucket are removed locally and fetched again when needed (details). Empty: every file stays local. Ignored without S3_BUCKET; never affects the database. {since=0.10.2}
FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM on off: only mirror files, do not back up the database.
FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM_LOG_LEVEL info How much Litestream logs: debug, info, warn or error. warn leaves out the routine lines of every compaction and keeps warnings and errors. {since=0.10.2}
FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM_AUTOHEAL on off: only report a stuck Litestream replica, do not rebuild it by itself on the next restart. {since=0.10.0}
LITESTREAM_SSE_C_KEY empty Optional: the storage provider encrypts the Litestream replica (SSE-C, 32 bytes base64, only over https and with providers that support SSE-C).
Details: Storage, S3 and backups.

en.heading: Database and cluster
paragraphs: Without these variables, Flowplan uses SQLite in one container. They are also listed, with comments, in the .env.example. Every value with its default and explanation is under PostgreSQL and Cluster mode.
Variable Default Meaning
DATABASE_URL empty postgres://… switches to PostgreSQL. Its role should own the database but not be a superuser (PostgreSQL).
FLOWPLAN_PG_SCHEMA, FLOWPLAN_PG_POOL, FLOWPLAN_PG_*_TIMEOUT public, 10, … Schema, connections per instance and time limits.
FLOWPLAN_PG_PREPARE on off: unnamed queries instead of named prepared statements – for PgBouncer in transaction mode without max_prepared_statements.

DATABASE_SESSION_URL DATABASE_URL A direct connection (or a session-mode pool) for notifications, the lead in a cluster and pg_dump/pg_restore, when DATABASE_URL points at PgBouncer in transaction mode.
FLOWPLAN_BACKUP_FORMAT pg_dump sqlite: scheduled backups on PostgreSQL in the portable SQLite format.
FLOWPLAN_CLUSTER empty 1: several instances; requires DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, S3_BUCKET, FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (or FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY) and WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY/WEB_PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY.
REDIS_URL empty Redis for cluster mode, redis://… or rediss://….
FLOWPLAN_READY_REQUIRE all Which checks decide /api/health/ready.

en.heading: Encryption
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning
FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY empty 32 bytes, base64 (openssl rand -base64 32). Encrypts files in the bucket, scheduled backups, Markdown exports and the instance backup. Without a key nothing changes.
FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE empty Instead of the variable: path to a file holding the key (Docker secret).
FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS empty Earlier keys, comma-separated – only for reading after a key change.
Details: Encryption.

en.heading: Stored secrets
paragraphs: Flowplan stores AI provider keys, the keys of authenticator apps (two-factor sign-in), the access tokens of the Git export of spaces and the tokens of chat apps only encrypted (AES-256-GCM, bound to their place). The key for this comes, in this order, from:
Source Meaning
FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY If set, it also encrypts the stored secrets.
FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY / FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY_FILE A key just for this: 32 bytes, base64 or hex (openssl rand -base64 32), or the path to a file (Docker secret).
secrets.key in the data folder Without the two variables, Flowplan creates this file itself when first needed (readable only by its owner).

> The instance backup deliberately leaves out secrets.key – it doesn't belong next to the data it protects. Back up the file separately or set the key as a variable. If it is missing after a restore, admins and users enter their AI keys and chat-app tokens again, and for two-factor sign-in recovery codes or a reset by an administrator help. The move tool, by contrast, takes secrets.key along, as it moves the whole instance.

en.heading: Instance move
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning

FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE empty On the new instance: true allows taking over an instance at an internal address (LAN, VPN, localhost) and over http:// – a home server, say. Without it only public HTTPS addresses. Remove it after the move.
Details: Moving an instance.

en.heading: Legal and interface
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning

IMPRINT_URL empty Link to the legal notice, e.g. https://example.com/imprint. Shown on the sign-in page, under shared pages and forms and in the account menu (on a phone under More in the sidebar) – only when set.
PRIVACY_URL empty Link to the privacy policy, in the same places and also only when set.

FLOWPLAN_SOURCE_URL Flowplan’s GitHub repository Address of the source of the code running on this instance (http or https). The AGPL-3.0 requires that whoever runs a modified version for others offers them its source (§ 13). When set, Settings → About Flowplan and the sign-in page (footer “Source code”) link to this address instead of github.com/yannicschuller/flowplan; the commit is then no longer linked to GitHub.
