DRAWIO_URL https://embed.diagrams.net Address of the draw.io editor for the /drawio block, e.g. your own jgraph/drawio container. https only (http only for localhost); an invalid value turns draw.io off. Viewing never loads draw.io.

FLOWPLAN_HIDE_SPONSOR false true hides only the Support Flowplan ♥ part (link to GitHub Sponsors) under Settings → About Flowplan. Licence and source code always stay visible. In the iPhone, iPad and Android apps the link never shows regardless; in browsers and the desktop app it does.
All environment variables at a glance. Many values can also be set in the interface of the Administration (see In the interface); values set there take precedence.
More on this topic: Configuration: storage, database and security · Configuration: e-mail, integrations and workflows · Configuration: AI, voice notes and push

en.heading: Required
paragraphs: Variable Example Meaning

APP_URL https://flowplan.example.com The public address exactly as it appears in the browser – scheme, host, port if any, without a trailing slash. The basis for sign-in redirects, cookies, passkeys, links in e-mails and push notifications and the origin check.

en.heading: Sign-in
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning
FLOWPLAN_LOCAL_LOGIN on false turns off e-mail, password and passkeys; then only single sign-on remains.

FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN empty (Helm: generated) Recommended for instances reachable from the internet: the first account and the restore on the setup screen only work via /register?setup=. No effect afterwards. If it is missing and APP_URL is not a local address, Flowplan warns at start in the log and on the setup screen. See Sign-in.
OIDC_ISSUER empty The login provider for single sign-on. Without it there are only e-mail, password and passkeys.
OIDC_CLIENT_ID – Client ID.
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET – Client secret. Never put it into the image or into Git. Empty: a public client, PKCE only.

OIDC_LINKED_SSO_ONLY off true: accounts connected to SSO sign in through SSO only. A password or passkey sign-in is refused with a note; passkeys and the authenticator app stay for confirming important steps. See Connect an existing account to SSO.

OIDC_NEW_ACCOUNTS on false: SSO sign-in creates no new accounts – only existing, connected or SCIM-provisioned accounts sign in. At a first SSO sign-in with a known address, "Create a separate account instead" is then not offered.

SESSION_HOURS 8 Browser session without "Stay signed in": ends this many hours after signing in (1–24). Also under Administration → Sign-in & SSO → Sessions; a value saved there takes precedence (for every SESSION_* except SESSION_MAX_DAYS and SESSION_GROUPS_HOURS).
SESSION_REMEMBER off true offers Stay signed in in the browser when signing in – see Sign-in. The apps stay signed in regardless.
SESSION_IDLE_HOURS 168 With "stay signed in" in the browser: the session ends this many hours after it was last used (1–8760).

SESSION_APP_REMEMBER on The desktop and mobile apps stay signed in while they (or their widgets) are used – for sign-ins the app proves (hand-off through the browser, or password with the app's device key; see Sign-in). false: their sessions end like a browser session without "Stay signed in".
SESSION_APP_DAYS 90 An app's session ends after this many days without use (1–365).

SESSION_MAX_DAYS 30 / 365 Sessions that stay signed in end at the latest this many days after signing in (1–365; default 30 in the browser, 365 in the apps; never shorter than the time without use) – with SSO just as with password and passkey.

SESSION_GROUPS_HOURS empty Only when set: SSO sessions with "stay signed in" end after this many hours already, so group changes at the provider take effect with the new sign-in. Without it they follow through SCIM, the LDAP sync or the next sign-in.
LDAP_URL empty Sign-in with an LDAP directory (ldap:// or ldaps://) – see Sign-in with LDAP.
LDAP_BIND_DN / LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD empty Search account for LDAP; without it, anonymous search.
LDAP_BASE_DN – Where LDAP accounts are searched.
LDAP_USER_FILTER (\ (uid={user})(mail={user})) Search filter; {user} is the escaped sign-in name.
LDAP_GROUP_ATTRIBUTE memberOf Groups for SSO mappings and the admin group, synced hourly.
LDAP_TLS_CA empty CA for ldaps:///StartTLS (path or PEM).
LDAP_STARTTLS false ldap:// with StartTLS.
LDAP_TIMEOUT_MS 8000 Time limit per LDAP operation.
LDAP_CONTACTS_BASE_DN LDAP_BASE_DN Base for contacts from LDAP; the OU tree starts here.
LDAP_CONTACTS_FILTER people without computers Which entries count as contacts.
LDAP_CONTACTS_SYNC_MINUTES 60 Sync of contacts from the directory (15–1440 minutes).
LDAP_CONTACTS_ATTRIBUTES – More LDAP attributes contacts databases may map (separated by commas or spaces), on top of those of the default mapping.
LDAP_CONTACTS on off turns contacts from LDAP off.
The other OIDC variables and everything about passwords and passkeys are described under Sign-in.

en.heading: Operations
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning
FLOWPLAN_DATA_DIR /app/data in the image, ./data otherwise Data directory for SQLite, uploads, push keys and text recognition data.

PUID / PGID 1000 / same as PUID Only in the image, without user: (as with linuxserver.io): at start Flowplan gives the data folder to this user and group and runs as them, never as root; 0 is refused. With user: "UID:GID" Flowplan runs as that user directly instead – see Volume permissions.
FLOWPLAN_WORKSPACE_QUOTA_MB unlimited Default storage quota per workspace in MB (0 = unlimited).

FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_MB empty Largest file for imports from AFFiNE and other tools in MB, for everyone. Without it the largest upload applies (Administration → Limits & retention, or the person's own limit), at least 100 MB. Only the AFFiNE workspace file (.affine) may exceed 100 MB; ZIP exports stay at 100 MB. A proxy in front must let such large requests through.

FLOWPLAN_MAX_DOCUMENT_MB 16 Largest size of a collaboratively edited document (page or record document) in MB. Changes that would make a document grow beyond it are refused ("The document is too large …"); split larger content across several pages. Keeps every edit of a huge document from slowing the server down.

FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_DOCS 10000 Largest number of pages per import from AFFiNE, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, Obsidian and Notion/Markdown: documents, folders, databases, whiteboards and collections; when importing as a new database, the number of records. Above it the preview shows the count and the import is refused (the message names the variable). Documents are converted one at a time; a higher value costs time, hardly memory.

FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_FILES 20000 Largest number of files (images, attachments) per import from an AFFiNE workspace or snapshot; further ones are left out, the preview names their number and the variable. ZIP exports may have as many entries as pages and files together (at least 12,000).

FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_ALLOW_PRIVATE off true lets the import from BookStack reach internal addresses (local network, VPN, such as http://192.168.1.20) and http:// – for a BookStack in your own network. Without the variable, the import only takes public HTTPS addresses. {since=0.10.0}
FLOWPLAN_SNAPSHOT_RETENTION_DAYS 180 How long automatic versions are kept, in days (0 = forever).
FLOWPLAN_OCR on 0 turns off text recognition for scanned PDFs and images.

FLOWPLAN_OCR_LANGS deu,eng Languages of the text recognition, e.g. fra,eng; the first is the main language. deu, eng, fra and chi_sim (Chinese, Simplified, e.g. chi_sim,eng) are bundled. Each extra language costs memory and time per page; Chinese the most (about 100 MB more memory, roughly one and a half times as long per page).

FLOWPLAN_WORKERS cores − 1, at least 1 Worker threads for long computing work: exports (Markdown/ZIP, PDF, Word, EPUB, Jira, Confluence) and the reading of imports run there, so the server keeps answering every other request meanwhile. Default: as many threads as the container may use cores, minus one (at least one). A thread only starts when it is needed, ends after a minute without work and, while it runs, takes about 200–400 MB of memory and, with PostgreSQL, up to two database connections. When more than 16 jobs per thread are waiting, the server answers 503 ("busy"). 0 switches the threads off: everything runs in the main process as before. {since=0.10.2}

FLOWPLAN_METRICS on off switches off the usage statistics of the monitoring: requests, errors and response times per minute, active people per hour, storage history and AI tokens. Only numbers are collected – no IP addresses, paths or names; minutes are kept 48 hours, hours 35 days, days 400 days. With off nothing is collected, and the switch Collect usage statistics under Administration → Monitoring → Statistics is locked. /api/metrics does not depend on it.

FLOWPLAN_LOG_FILE on off: no server log in /app/data/logs/ (Flowplan's and Litestream's output, redacted, about 2,000 lines each). Restarts are then listed without log lines; when and why stays. {since=0.10.0}
FLOWPLAN_METRICS_TOKEN empty At least 16 characters; enables /api/metrics in Prometheus format. Sent as Authorization: Bearer …, it also unlocks the details of /api/health (see Health check).

FLOWPLAN_PUBLIC_API_DOCS false true makes /api/openapi.json and /api/docs readable without signing in; visitors only see the major version (0.x) there. Otherwise only for signed-in people and API tokens.

FLOWPLAN_UPDATE_CHECK on false turns off the check for new versions (for instances without internet). Otherwise the server asks GitHub for the latest release at most every 12 hours and shows admins a notice in the administration.

FLOWPLAN_MARKETPLACE_URL https://marketplace.flowplan.org Address of the Flowplan Marketplace (default https://marketplace.flowplan.org); off switches it off. The instance never connects to it itself – the address only decides which window the browser exchanges templates with. See Marketplace.

FLOWPLAN_UPDATE_URL GitHub API Another address for the latest release (same format as api.github.com/repos/yannicschuller/flowplan/releases/latest), such as an internal mirror. Not to be confused with the desktop app's variable of the same name, which names the app's update source on the computer running it.

FLOWPLAN_TRUSTED_PROXIES 1 Number of proxies in front of Flowplan (Traefik alone: 1, Pangolin in front of Traefik: 2, 0 = trust no header). Decides which entry in X-Forwarded-For is the real address – for limiting sign-in attempts, demo starts and anonymous form answers. Entries made up by the browser are ignored this way. When no address arrives at all (the proxy does not set the header), only the limits per account and per link apply, and the log shows a note once.
FLOWPLAN_SECURITY_LOG on Security events as a JSON line on stdout: on (with address, for fail2ban/CrowdSec), anonymous, off (Security).
FLOWPLAN_SECURITY_RETENTION_DAYS 90 How long security events stay in the database (at least 7).
FLOWPLAN_COUNTRY_HEADER empty The proxy's header with the country of the request (e.g. CF-IPCountry); turns on the rule "two countries in a short time".
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT empty OTLP collector (HTTP); security events go there as OpenTelemetry logs. With OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME.

FLOWPLAN_ANONYMOUS_UPLOAD_MB 1024 How many MB visitors without an account may upload per day on the whole instance – through anonymous forms and editing links (0 = unlimited). Each form or link additionally gets 200 MB per day, independent of the workspace's storage quota.
The Typst preview loads its compiler and fonts (WebAssembly, about 11 MB compressed) on first use from /typst/… of your own server; nothing is fetched from a CDN.

en.heading: Do not set
paragraphs: The image sets NODE_ENV, PORT, HOSTNAME and NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED itself, and FLOWPLAN_DROP_ROOT=1 (Flowplan's tools in the container give up root and run as PUID:PGID). The container's start sets FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM_SSE_C when LITESTREAM_SSE_C_KEY is set; the administration uses it to show whether the Litestream copy is encrypted. FLOWPLAN_DIST_DIR is only meant for parallel development servers, OIDC_ALLOW_LOCAL_HTTP only for tests with a provider on http://localhost, FLOWPLAN_GIT_ALLOW_HTTP only for tests of the Git export with an http:// server (no effect in production). FLOWPLAN_E2E_BUILD and FLOWPLAN_E2E_DEMO are only for the browser tests' own build (the demo sign-in in a production build); a published image doesn't contain that switch, and the variables have no effect there. {since=0.10.0} Version and commit (FLOWPLAN_VERSION, GIT_COMMIT, SOURCE_COMMIT) come from the build; FLOWPLAN_VERSION in .env only picks the image tag in compose.yaml.

en.heading: In the interface
paragraphs: In the Administration, administrators set (see Administering the instance):
– Instance: the instance name and whether the instance offers a public demo (running and total started demos are shown under Administration → Monitoring → Instance in numbers),

– Sign-in & SSO: whether anyone may sign up with e-mail and password, whether everyone may create workspaces of their own, after how many days without sign-in accounts are blocked, required two-factor sign-in,
– Limits & retention: the default storage quota, storage and own workspaces per person, the maximum upload size, how long versions are kept,
– Storage & backup: the daily or hourly database backup and how many copies are kept,
– Maintenance & notices: a notice banner for everyone and the maintenance notice,
– Extensions & domains: Custom domains for publications (off) and Block extensions from any HTTPS address (off) – see Coolify and reverse proxies and Block extensions,
– Monitoring → Statistics: whether usage statistics are collected (locked with FLOWPLAN_METRICS=off).
Empty fields fall back to the environment variables.

A contacts database is an address book for people: every record has a profile page with a contact card, with room for notes below. Contacts can be imported from an LDAP directory and kept in sync, imported and exported as vCard, and subscribed to as an address book (CardDAV) on your phone.

en.heading: Create a contacts database
paragraphs: New page → Database → Contacts. The database comes with:
Property Type
Name Text – the display name “First Last”
First name, Last name Text
Company, Position Text
E-mail Email
Phone, Mobile Phone
Street, Postal code, City, Country Text
Birthday Date
Tags Multi-select
Plus the views All contacts (list sorted by last name), Table, Birthdays (calendar) and Gallery. Records open as a full page.

– Name: a new record is called “New contact”. Type a full name into the title (“Anna Maria Smith”) and Flowplan fills first and last name (the last word is the last name). When you change first or last name, the title follows – until you write a different one yourself, such as “Dr. A. Smith”.
– Birthdays repeat yearly: the “Birthdays” calendar shows them every year, and the contact card shows the age.

– Closed to AI: contacts are personal data, so new contacts databases are closed to the AI; whoever manages the page can open it. Who sees the contacts is decided, as always, by the permissions of the space and page (and, if set, permissions per record).

en.heading: The profile page
paragraphs: At the top is the contact card: photo (or initials), position and company, clickable buttons for e-mail (mailto:), phone and mobile (tel:), the address with a link to the map (OpenStreetMap) and the birthday. ⤓ on the right downloads the contact as a vCard. Below follow the properties for editing and the document for notes – with everything the editor can do.
The photo is the record's icon: Change icon → Image sets one; vCard and LDAP imports bring it along.

The contact card is a layout setting: Adjust layout (sliders in the record) → Contact card on top. That way an existing database gets a contact card too, if its properties have the IDs firstName, lastName, company, email …

en.heading: Mention contacts
paragraphs: Type @ in text to find contacts like any other record. Hovering (or tapping) the mention shows a card with name, position, company, e-mail and phone – e-mail and phone are clickable – and Open profile. The card only shows what you may read.

en.heading: Import and export vCards
paragraphs: The address book icon in the database toolbar opens the Contacts menu:

– Import vCard (.vcf): files from Apple Contacts, Google Contacts, Outlook or Thunderbird, vCard 2.1, 3.0 and 4.0, any number of contacts per file (up to 5 MB). Name, company, position, first e-mail, phone and mobile, the (work) address, birthday, categories as tags, the note as the record's text and embedded photos (JPEG/PNG up to 256 KB) are imported. Flowplan never fetches photos from a link. A card exported from this database updates its record instead of creating a new one.

– Export all as vCard, or – with records selected – Export selection as vCard: one .vcf file (vCard 3.0) with note and photo. Single contacts via ⤓ on the contact card. Exports only contain records and properties you may read, and appear in the security log.

en.heading: Subscribe as an address book (CardDAV)
paragraphs: Contacts → Subscribe as address book (CardDAV) turns the database into an address book in Apple Contacts, Thunderbird or DAVx⁵ (Android) – read-only: you make changes in Flowplan.
– Set up access shows the server, user name and a password that is shown only once, plus the address book's address. Create new password or End access ends the old access.
– Set up on iPhone, iPad or Mac downloads a configuration profile with the CardDAV account (in the app through Safari; on a computer as a QR code). The link works once and for ten minutes.
– By hand in Apple: Settings → Contacts → Accounts → Add account → Other → CardDAV account with server, user name and password. Discovery works through /.well-known/carddav.
– Permissions: every request checks your permissions again. You only see records and properties you may read in Flowplan; if you lose access to the database, the address book returns nothing.

en.heading: Contacts from the LDAP directory
paragraphs: When an LDAP directory is set up (see Contacts from LDAP), editors of a contacts database import people from it.

The directory is only for people of the organisation: instance administrators, accounts that sign in with LDAP, and full members (not guests) of at least one workspace someone else created. Guests of the contacts database's workspace can never browse or import it, and neither can an API token. Anyone without access sees Import from LDAP greyed out with the reason.
– Contacts → Import from LDAP opens the tree of organizational units (OUs) below the base DN; sub-OUs load when expanded.
– Pick an OU: the people in it are listed on the right (search: in the OU and everything below). People already imported are marked.
– Tick people and import them – or Import the whole OU (also future members): everyone in the OU and its sub-OUs; new people are added by the sync.
– Attribute mapping (expandable) sets which LDAP attribute fills which property; the first attribute with a value wins. Default:
Property LDAP attributes
Name displayName, cn
First / last name givenName / sn
Company company, o
Position title
E-mail mail
Phone / Mobile telephoneNumber / mobile
Street street, streetAddress
Postal code / City / Country postalCode / l / co, c
Birthday birthDate, dateOfBirth (if present)
Photo thumbnailPhoto, jpegPhoto (JPEG/PNG up to 256 KB)

Only allowed attributes can be mapped: those of the default mapping and the ones the administration allows on top (LDAP_CONTACTS_ATTRIBUTES or More attributes, see Contacts from LDAP). The dialog lists the allowed attributes; a mapping with any other one is refused. When the administration takes an attribute off the list again, the sync stops reading it too.
Sync – directory → Flowplan only:
– Flowplan syncs every hour (configurable) and on Contacts → Sync now; the menu shows the last result.
– Properties from the directory are read-only in Flowplan and marked LDAP; the contact card says from LDAP. Notes, tags and your own properties stay editable.

– When an entry disappears from the directory, the contact stays and gets the tag No longer in directory; when it comes back, the tag goes. A run that would mark more than half of the contacts (at least five) as gone stops instead – that is more likely a wrong configuration.
– Contacts are found again by entryUUID (OpenLDAP), objectGUID (Active Directory) or nsUniqueId (389 DS), otherwise by DN – renamed or moved entries keep their contact.
– To stop following an OU: Stop following in the import dialog; the contacts stay.
– Imports appear in the administration's security log.
Flowplan only needs an HTTPS proxy in front of it. WebSockets are not needed: collaboration runs over normal HTTP requests and server-sent events.

en.heading: Coolify
paragraphs: – Choose New resource → Docker Image (ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest) or Dockerfile from the Git repository.
– Ports Exposes: 3000.
– Enter the domain, e.g. https://flowplan.example.com. Coolify gets the certificate via Traefik.
– Persistent Storage: a volume with the target /app/data.
– Set the environment variables from the configuration.
– Deploy. After about 20 seconds the health check reports the container as healthy.

en.heading: Checklist
paragraphs: Before an instance goes into regular use, check the resource's settings:
– Health check on, port 3000, path /api/health (Health check).

– Restart policy left at Coolify's default (unless-stopped): the container comes back after a crash and after Restart now in the administration. For Max restart count, check the field's tooltip in Coolify for what 0 means there.
– With SQLite: Container naming set to Consistent name (no rolling updates) plus a Custom container name (Roll out SQLite without overlap).
– Stop grace period 30 seconds or more, so Flowplan and Litestream end cleanly.
– A memory limit with room for Litestream next to the app – or, without a limit, enough free memory on the host (Sizing, when the host runs out).
– Beta and production as separate resources, rolled out by COOLIFY_BETA_WEBHOOK and COOLIFY_WEBHOOK (Roll out automatically).
– The beta instance with its own volume and its own bucket or S3_PREFIX – never the production volume.

en.heading: Health check
paragraphs: The image comes with its own health check. If you set it up in Coolify:
Field Value
Check type HTTP request
Method / scheme / host GET / HTTP / localhost
Port 3000 – empty means 80, where nothing listens
Path /api/health
Expected code 200
Start period 30 seconds (with S3, Litestream restores the database on the first start)
Flowplan sends no X-Powered-By header. The health check only needs the status code; its details are not public without a token (see Health check).

en.heading: Volume permissions
paragraphs: Flowplan runs as UID 1000 (the user node) by default. A new Docker volume gets the permissions automatically. For a mounted host folder that belongs to someone else, set PUID and PGID – as with the linuxserver.io images, no user: needed:
services:
flowplan:
image: ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest
environment:
volumes:
- /path/to/flowplan-data:/app/data

At start, before anything else, Flowplan gives the data folder to PUID:PGID and then runs the app as that user – never as root. chown only runs while the folder or something directly in it still belongs to someone else – so once, not on every start. Without a value, PGID equals PUID; both must be numbers greater than 0 (0 is refused). Without PUID/PGID, Flowplan runs as UID 1000 and hands the folder to it the same way.

Alternatively, Docker's own user: – Flowplan then runs as that user from the start and changes no owners; the folder must already belong to it. Any UID/GID works, also one without an entry in the image's /etc/passwd. Kubernetes (runAsUser, the Helm chart) works this way.
services:
flowplan:
image: ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest
user: "1001:1001"          # or "${UID}:${GID}", with UID and GID in .env
volumes:
- /path/to/flowplan-data:/app/data

With user:, PUID/PGID have no effect; Flowplan says so in one line at start. Or give the folder to UID 1000 instead: sudo chown -R 1000:1000 /path/to/flowplan-data. If nothing fits, the start stops with "Flowplan cannot write to its data folder …".

Commands in the container (docker exec, docker compose exec/run, docker run … node …) run as root without user:. Flowplan's own tools – /app/move.mjs, /app/decrypt.mjs, /app/scripts/db-*.mjs – switch to PUID:PGID (default 1000:1000) by themselves before they write anything. For any other command that writes into the data folder, add the user: docker compose exec -u 1001:1001 flowplan … (-u 1000:1000 without PUID). Whatever a command run as root leaves directly in the data folder, Flowplan hands over at the next start.

en.heading: Roll out automatically
paragraphs: Coolify does not watch the registry itself. The repositories' image workflows therefore trigger a deployment through the Coolify API after pushing a new image (POST /api/v1/deploy?uuid=… with an API token). Coolify's built-in GitHub webhook does not fit: it builds from source and fires on the push, before the image is ready.
– In Coolify, turn on API access under Settings (and allow the CI runner's address if needed).
– Under Keys & Tokens → API tokens, create a token with the deploy permission.
– In the resource under Webhooks, copy the Deploy Webhook address, e.g. https://coolify.example.com/api/v1/deploy?uuid=…&force=false.

– In the GitHub repository under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions, create the secrets COOLIFY_WEBHOOK (the address) and COOLIFY_TOKEN (the token). For a second instance of the flowplan repository that follows :beta, add its address as COOLIFY_BETA_WEBHOOK; COOLIFY_WEBHOOK is then the instance on :latest.
Repository Image in Coolify Rolled out on
flowplan, beta instance (COOLIFY_BETA_WEBHOOK) ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:beta every beta build (Actions → Docker image → Run workflow)
flowplan, production instance (COOLIFY_WEBHOOK) ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest every release
flowplan-website ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan-website:latest every push to main, once CI has passed and the new image serves its pages
flowplan-docs ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan-docs:latest every push to main, once CI has passed and the new image serves its pages

Pull requests and Dependabot never deploy; without the secrets (in forks, for example) the step is skipped. If Coolify does not pull the new image on deploy, set pull_policy: always in the compose file.
> Keep the number of instances at 1 in Coolify. Several containers would write to the same SQLite file.

en.heading: A beta instance that tests replication
paragraphs: A beta instance without S3 never runs Litestream – its replication, the self-healing and the bucket reset are then first exercised on production. To test them with every :beta, give the beta instance replication of its own:

– At your S3 provider, create a separate bucket for the beta instance (e.g. flowplan-beta) and an access key that may only use that bucket. A separate bucket is safest: a reset of the beta replica can never touch production. If you can only use one bucket, give the beta instance at least its own S3_PREFIX (e.g. flowplan-beta) – never the prefix of production.

– In Coolify, in the beta resource's environment variables, set S3_BUCKET, S3_ENDPOINT, S3_REGION, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and S3_PREFIX for that bucket. Its data volume stays its own, too.
– Deploy. The log shows Litestream restoring (an empty bucket: nothing to restore) and then replicating; Administration → Monitoring shows the replica's state.
Files uploaded on the beta instance then go to the beta bucket as well. Delete the bucket when you no longer need the beta instance.

en.heading: Roll out SQLite without overlap
paragraphs: With SQLite (no DATABASE_URL), only one Flowplan container may run on a data volume at any time – not even for the seconds of an update. If a deployment starts the new container while the old one still runs (a rolling update that waits for the new one's health check), two Litestream processes work on the same database. That damages the replication state in .flowplan.sqlite-litestream: the log first shows sync error … rename …ltx.tmp …: no such file or directory, then every 30 seconds compaction failed … file checksum mismatch. How to repair it is under Repair the Litestream state.
So avoid:
– a rollout that starts the new container before the old one has stopped – roll out with stop first, then start;
– more than one instance, replica or copy of the resource on the same volume (a second resource, for :beta for example, needs its own volume and its own S3_PREFIX);
– docker compose up under a second project name on the same volume, or an extra docker run … -v flowplan-data:/app/data, while the instance runs.

In Coolify: in the resource's settings, section Container, set Container naming to Consistent name (no rolling updates) and give it a Custom container name (e.g. flowplan-production), then deploy once. Coolify then stops the old container before it starts the new one; an update interrupts Flowplan for a few seconds. Keep the health check on and the Stop grace period at 30 seconds or more, so Flowplan and Litestream end cleanly.
If you need updates without interruption, use PostgreSQL – an update may overlap briefly there – or cluster mode.
The safety net: every container takes an exclusive lock on /app/data/.flowplan.lock (flock) when it starts and holds it while it runs. If a second container finds the lock taken, it
– starts the app anyway, so that a rolling update's health check passes and the old container gets stopped;

– starts no second Litestream and no restore from the bucket; a pending instance restore (and a database that does not exist yet, which the other container may be restoring right now) waits completely before the app starts;
– logs ANOTHER CONTAINER IS USING THE DATA FOLDER …;

– starts replication by itself as soon as the other container has stopped and the lock is free. If that Litestream crashes, the app keeps running and Flowplan restarts it after FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM_RESTART_SECONDS seconds (default 5) – twice as late with each further crash, after 300 seconds at most.

While it waits, Administration → Monitoring shows the warning “A second Flowplan container (host) has been using the same data folder since time …” on both containers (on the waiting one: “This container … has been waiting …”). It ends once only one container runs. The net prevents the damaged state, but it does not replace a rollout without overlap: for the time of the overlap, two apps write to the same file. The lock needs a file system with flock – a local Docker volume or a local folder, not SMB.

en.heading: Pangolin, Traefik and other proxies
paragraphs: – APP_URL must exactly match the address under which Flowplan appears in the browser.

– If TLS ends at the front proxy (such as Pangolin) and it passes on to Traefik, turn off TLS to the target there and set a custom host header with the Flowplan domain – otherwise Traefik finds no route and answers with 404.

– Large uploads: content archives can be up to 2 GB, AFFiNE workspace files as large as the import limit (largest upload, at least 100 MB, or FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_MB). Traefik does not limit the request size by itself – only a buffering middleware of your own with maxRequestBodyBytes does; it then has to be at least that large. nginx needs client_max_body_size (the example below allows 2 GB; the default is just 1 MB), Caddy only limits with request_body { max_size … }. Cloudflare (proxied) lets at most 100 MB per request through on the Free and Pro plans – import larger AFFiNE files through a route without the Cloudflare proxy. Flowplan takes large imports as a stream and writes them to disk; the request must state its size (Content-Length), which browsers always do.
– Timeouts: exporting and importing large archives can take minutes; raise proxy timeouts if needed.

– Server-sent events (live editing in documents, live cursors on whiteboards, updates of the sidebar and the inbox through /api/live) must not be buffered; nginx: proxy_buffering off (see the example below). Flowplan also sends X-Accel-Buffering: no for this.

– Client address: the proxy must set X-Forwarded-For (Traefik and Caddy do so by default, nginx needs the line from the example). Only then does Flowplan limit sign-in attempts, demo starts and anonymous form answers per address. Without the header only the limits per account and per link apply, and the log shows a note on the first request. FLOWPLAN_TRUSTED_PROXIES names the number of proxies (Configuration).

en.heading: nginx
paragraphs: server {
server_name flowplan.example.com;
client_max_body_size 2g;
location / {
proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
proxy_set_header Host $host;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_read_timeout 600s;

en.heading: Caddy
paragraphs: flowplan.example.com {
reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
Never expose the internal port 3000 publicly as well.

en.heading: Custom domains for publications
paragraphs: With Custom domains for publications under Administration → Extensions & domains, owners show published pages under their domain (Sharing and publishing). Flowplan recognises the domain by the Host header and serves only the publication. The certificate stays the reverse proxy's job; it must pass requests for any host on to Flowplan and keep the Host unchanged.
Flowplan answers GET /api/domains/allowed?domain= with 200 for verified domains of active publications and with 404 otherwise – exactly the question Caddy asks before a new certificate.

en.heading: Caddy with on-demand TLS
paragraphs: on_demand_tls {
ask http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/domains/allowed
flowplan.example.com {
reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
# Every other host: a certificate only when Flowplan knows the domain.
https:// {
tls {
on_demand
reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
Caddy fetches the certificate on the first request for the domain. Domains Flowplan has not verified get none – so nobody can trigger certificates for other people's names.

en.heading: Traefik
paragraphs: Traefik does not ask before issuing a certificate. Add a router per domain (file provider or labels) – after the domain is verified in Flowplan:
http:
routers:
flowplan-docs-example:
rule: Host(`docs.example.org`)
service: flowplan
tls:
certResolver: letsencrypt
services:
flowplan:
loadBalancer:
servers:
- url: http://flowplan:3000
Verification does not depend on the router: Flowplan only checks the TXT record _flowplan-verify..

en.heading: Coolify
paragraphs: In Coolify add the extra domain to the Domains field of the Flowplan resource (comma-separated, e.g. https://flowplan.example.com,https://docs.example.org) and redeploy. Coolify creates the router and certificate for Traefik. APP_URL stays the address of the app.

en.heading: Security
paragraphs: – Under a custom domain Flowplan only answers the publication's read access, its files and the interface's static files. Sign-in, app and API answer with 404 – also when someone forges the Host header.
– Cookies and Authorization headers are dropped there, and Flowplan never sets a cookie.
– The pages carry frame-ancestors 'none' and X-Frame-Options: DENY.
– An entry for the instance's own address is not possible.

– A domain is verified only by the DNS TXT record _flowplan-verify. – a domain already pointing at the instance is not enough. Unverified entries expire after 7 days, so nobody can block someone else's domain for good.
A page made of tiles: metrics, charts and views of your databases, tasks due, your journal streak and notes – at a glance, and for everyone with exactly the data they may see.

en.heading: Creating a dashboard
paragraphs: – New page → Dashboard, or > New dashboard in the quick search. Like any page, the dashboard sits in a space of the page tree and can have subpages.
– A new dashboard is empty: Add the first tile switches to edit mode and opens the settings of the first tile.
– Choose the Type, an optional Title and the Size, then the source and what the tile shows (below). Add places the tile; further tiles come with Add tile.

A dashboard holds up to 48 tiles. Without a title of its own a tile is named after its source – “Projects · Board” for a view, the database's or journal's name for charts and the streak, otherwise the tile's type.

en.heading: Tiles
paragraphs: Tile Shows
Database view A view of a database, as the linked database in a document shows it. With Records editable here records can be changed right on the dashboard, otherwise they are read-only.
Metric The number of records of a view (with its filters) or the sum, average, minimum or maximum of a number property. With a target a progress bar appears.
Chart Columns, bars, line or donut over a property – drawn like the chart view; a click on a record opens it.
Journal streak How many days in a row you have written in a journal, plus today's entry or Write today.
My due tasks Your tasks from My tasks that are due today or overdue.
Recently changed The most recently changed pages and the number of unread notifications in the inbox.
Text Free text in Markdown – for headings, notes or links.

en.heading: Sources and settings
paragraphs: The settings of a tile offer only what you may read yourself: the databases and journals of the dashboard's workspace, without those behind a journal PIN you have not entered. If there is no database you can read, the dialog says so.
Tile What you choose
Database view The Database and one of its Views (forms are left out; empty means the first view), and whether Records editable here. The view keeps its own filters, sorting and layout.

Metric The database, the view whose filters count (or All records), the Value – number of records, sum, average, minimum or maximum – with the Number property it is calculated from, and an optional Target.

Chart The database and the view whose records it draws (or all records), the Chart type (columns, bars, line, donut), Group by (a property, or automatic) and the value per group – number of records or the sum, average, minimum or maximum of a number property. Donuts get a legend.
Journal streak The Journal. A day counts once something is written or tracked in it.
Recently changed The Number of pages (1 to 20, six by default). The dashboard itself and pages you may not read are left out.
Text The Text (Markdown).
My due tasks needs no source: it shows up to twelve of your own tasks due today or overdue, with a link to All tasks.

en.heading: Arranging and sizing
paragraphs: Edit at the top right switches to edit mode:
– Add tile creates a new tile.
– Drag tiles to change their order – or use Move earlier/Move later in the tile menu (…).
– Choose the size in the tile menu: Small (a quarter), Medium (half), Large (two thirds) or Full width. On phones all tiles stack.
– Configure … changes source, title and values; Remove deletes the tile.

Tiles of different heights leave no gaps: the first row follows the order from left to right, then each tile moves up into the column with the least above it. Wide tiles sit under the lowest point of the columns they cover. Edit mode shows the same arrangement.
Done leaves edit mode. Every change is saved right away.

en.heading: Permissions
paragraphs: – People with edit rights on the page add and change tiles; readers only look at the dashboard.

– Every tile is calculated with the rights of the person looking: private records only count for those who may see them. A tile over a database or journal someone may not read (or that is locked with a PIN) shows that person only Not available – no title, no values.
– Sources must be in the same workspace.

en.heading: Dashboard or home page?
paragraphs: The home page is built from widgets too, and some look alike – tasks, journal, a database view. The difference is whose page it is:
Dashboard Home page
What it is A page in a space, with a title, a place in the page tree, a link and the trash Your personal start, under Home in the sidebar
Who sees it Everyone who may read the page – each with the values they may see Only you; owners can set a default for members
Who arranges it Everyone with edit rights on the page You, per workspace or for all your workspaces

Contents Database views, metrics with target, charts, journal streak, due tasks, recently changed, text Greeting, tasks, agenda, journal, database view, pinned page, habits, focus & time, scratchpad, my activity, due flashcards and more
Export, duplicate, API Yes (see below) No – the layout is a setting

Use a dashboard for figures a team looks at together – a project's progress, a sales pipeline, open tickets by status – and the home page for your own day. A dashboard you open often can be added to the home page as a Pinned page or to the favourites.

en.heading: Copying, export and trash
paragraphs: – Duplicate copies the dashboard with all tiles; when a database is copied along, the tile in the copy points to the copy.
– The Markdown export contains a text overview of the tiles (title, type, source, texts), and so do PDF, Word and EPUB. The values themselves depend on who is looking and are therefore not exported.
– Deleted dashboards go to the trash like any page and come back with all their tiles.
– Through the API, the dashboard.save action stores the tiles of a dashboard page.

en.page: Switching the database: SQLite and PostgreSQL
paragraphs: With the bundled tool you move an instance from SQLite to PostgreSQL – or back. The downtime is the copy itself, usually a few minutes; afterwards every table is compared row by row.

en.page: Switching the database: SQLite and PostgreSQL
en.heading: How it works
paragraphs: The tool db-migrate.mjs lives in the Docker image under /app/scripts/ (in the source code under scripts/). It copies every table from the source into an empty target and then compares each table by its row count and a checksum over all values. The source stays unchanged – so the way back is always open, as long as nobody has worked in the target yet.
Not copied but rebuilt on the first start: the search index and the pgvector table. The AI embeddings themselves are copied, so semantic search needs no new calls to the AI provider afterwards.

The tool does not move files; they stay where they are: in the uploads/ folder of the data folder or in the S3 bucket. So keep the same data folder (the same volume) and the same S3_* values. secrets.key and web-push-keys.json also stay in the data folder and are still needed.
Roughly, copying takes a second per few tens of thousands of rows; documents and embeddings make up most of it. Add the first start with the search index build (see Search on PostgreSQL).

en.page: Switching the database: SQLite and PostgreSQL
en.heading: From SQLite to PostgreSQL
paragraphs: The commands assume the Docker Compose installation (service flowplan, volume on /app/data) and a PostgreSQL the container reaches as postgres. Replace `` and the address with your values.
– Same version. Update Flowplan to the version that will run afterwards and start it once. The tool refuses a database from another version.
– Prepare the target: an empty database on PostgreSQL 16 or newer and a role that owns it – see Requirements, also for pg_trgm and pgvector.
– Back up: Administration → Storage & backup → Whole instance → Download. Keep the file until the new instance runs.
– Stop Flowplan – the tool only reads a consistent state when nothing writes:
``bash docker compose stop flowplan ``
– Copy and verify:
``bash docker compose run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint node flowplan \ /app/scripts/db-migrate.mjs \ --from sqlite:/app/data/flowplan.sqlite \ --to postgres://flowplan:@postgres:5432/flowplan ``

The output shows progress per table and at the end a table with the row counts and the checksums of source and target. The last line reads verified: every table has the same rows (exit code 0). With DIFFERENCES found (exit code 1), the tables concerned are marked DIFFERENT; nobody uses the target yet – fix the cause, empty the target database and run it again.
– Switch over: in .env, set DATABASE_URL=postgres://flowplan:@postgres:5432/flowplan (and FLOWPLAN_PG_SCHEMA if not public). The data folder and the S3_* values stay as they are.
– Start and check:
``bash docker compose up -d ``
Sign in, open a page, search for something (the index fills within seconds to minutes) and check that Administration → Monitoring → System says PostgreSQL.
– Clean up, but not right away: the old flowplan.sqlite stays in the data folder and is ignored as long as DATABASE_URL is set. Delete it only once the new instance's first scheduled backup has run.
With S3: Litestream no longer runs with PostgreSQL; scheduled backups become pg_dump archives (Backups with pg_dump). You can delete the old Litestream copy under /db/ in the bucket later.
Without Docker Compose, the same works with docker run – pass the container's volume and network:
docker run --rm --network <network> -v flowplan-data:/app/data --entrypoint node \
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest /app/scripts/db-migrate.mjs \
--from sqlite:/app/data/flowplan.sqlite \
--to postgres://flowplan:<password>@postgres:5432/flowplan

en.page: Switching the database: SQLite and PostgreSQL
en.heading: From PostgreSQL to SQLite
paragraphs: The same way in reverse. The target file must not exist yet – if the data folder still holds a flowplan.sqlite from before PostgreSQL, move it aside first.
– Same version on both sides, download the instance backup (as above).
– Stop Flowplan: docker compose stop flowplan.
– Move an old SQLite file aside:

``bash docker compose run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint sh flowplan -c \ 'mkdir -p /app/data/sqlite-old && for f in /app/data/flowplan.sqlite*; do [ -e "$f" ] && mv "$f" /app/data/sqlite-old/; done; true' ``
– Copy and verify:
``bash docker compose run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint node flowplan \ /app/scripts/db-migrate.mjs \ --from postgres://flowplan:@postgres:5432/flowplan \ --to sqlite:/app/data/flowplan.sqlite ``
– Remove DATABASE_URL (and FLOWPLAN_PG_SCHEMA) from .env, then docker compose up -d and check as above.

– With S3: Litestream backs up the new file continuously again from the start. If the bucket still holds a copy from before PostgreSQL under /db/, delete or move it before starting – otherwise a later restore from the bucket could end up at that old state.
The PostgreSQL database stays unchanged; keep it until the SQLite instance's first scheduled backup has run.

en.page: Switching the database: SQLite and PostgreSQL
en.heading: Tool options
paragraphs: Option Meaning
--from, --to Source and target: sqlite: on one side, postgres://… on the other.
--schema Schema in PostgreSQL (default public; created if missing). Matches FLOWPLAN_PG_SCHEMA.
--verify-only Copy nothing, only compare row counts and checksums of both sides.
--batch Rows per read (default 1000).
--quiet No progress lines.

The tool refuses: a source from another Flowplan version, a target table that already has rows, a target file that already exists, and values that do not fit the PostgreSQL column (SQLite accepts anything in any column) – naming the row concerned.

en.page: Switching the database: SQLite and PostgreSQL
en.heading: Verifying
paragraphs: As long as nobody has worked in the new instance, you can repeat the comparison at any time:
docker compose run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint node flowplan \
/app/scripts/db-migrate.mjs --verify-only \
--from sqlite:/app/data/flowplan.sqlite \
--to postgres://flowplan:<password>@postgres:5432/flowplan
Each table shows its row count and the checksums of source and target side by side. The checksum does not depend on row order and compares the values as both databases store them.

en.page: Switching the database: SQLite and PostgreSQL
en.heading: Going back if something goes wrong
paragraphs: – Before anyone works in the new instance: stop Flowplan, undo the setting (remove or set DATABASE_URL again) and start. The source is unchanged.
– If people have already worked: move in the opposite direction (section above), so nothing is lost.
– As a last resort: restore the downloaded instance backup under Administration → Storage & backup → Restore from backup or on the setup screen – it fits both databases.
An aborted copy does not resume: empty the target database (or delete the half-written file) and start over.

en.page: Switching the database: SQLite and PostgreSQL
en.heading: Rebuilding the search index
paragraphs: After a switch, Flowplan rebuilds the search index by itself on the first start. By hand:
docker compose exec flowplan node /app/scripts/db-search-rebuild.mjs
With DATABASE_URL in the environment it acts on PostgreSQL, otherwise on the SQLite file in the data folder (--sqlite for another one).

en.page: Switching the database: SQLite and PostgreSQL
en.heading: Other ways
paragraphs: – The instance backup (ZIP) and the move tool carry the database in the portable SQLite format and restore on SQLite as well as PostgreSQL. To move to another server and switch the database at once, that is often the easier way.
– For cluster mode, the files must be in the S3 bucket first – see there.
A database's property types at a glance, colours for select options, formatted text in fields and multi-selects with the workspace's tags.

en.heading: Properties
paragraphs: Type Content
Text Formatted text: bold, italic, strikethrough, code, links, line breaks (see below)
Number Numbers with a format: currency, percent, decimal places, thousands separators
Date With or without time and end date, time zone, personal reminders, recurrence
Select, multi-select Options with a colour each (see below), e.g. for status or tags
Checkbox, checklist Tick off; checklists with several items and progress
URL, e-mail, phone Clickable
Person Members of the workspace; assigning someone notifies them
Files Attachments and images right on the record
Relation, rollup A link to records of another database and calculations over them
Formula A value calculated from other properties
Created time/by, edited time/by Maintained automatically
Relations, rollups and formulas are described under Properties, formulas and rollups.

en.heading: Collapsing properties in a record
paragraphs: Below a record's title, the Properties arrow folds the properties into one line: the two or three most relevant values as small chips (status first, then selects, dates and people) and “+4 properties”. A tap on the line opens it again. The record's content moves up – especially useful on a phone.
– The choice applies to all records of the database and is stored in your account, separately for phone and computer: collapsing on the phone leaves everything visible on the computer.

– Without a choice of your own, properties are expanded on a computer; on a phone they are collapsed as soon as the record shows more than four properties. A record you have just created always opens expanded so you can fill it in.
– Collapsing changes no values and no permissions and only applies to you. Printing and exports always show all properties – unless you turn them off in the print options.
– Ordinary pages have the same in the bar with tags and properties.

en.heading: Option colours
paragraphs: Every option of a select or multi-select can have its own colour – grey, blue, green, red, yellow, orange, purple, pink or teal, the same colours as tags. The colour shows wherever the value appears: table, board columns, list, gallery, feed, groups, filters, in the record, in forms (multi-selects) and on published pages.

– Changing it: in the property's settings (click the column header), every option is listed as a chip below the options – click one to pick its colour. Faster, on the value itself: right-click a chip in the table or the header of a board column and choose a colour. It is saved at once; Undo in the notice brings the old colour back.

– New options get the next colour in turn by themselves – whether you type them in the settings, add a board column or they come in through an import, the API or AI. A renamed option keeps its colour.
– Assign colours automatically colours all options of the property in turn at once (replacing the colours set so far). Undo next to it or closing without saving discards it, Save keeps it.
– Existing databases look as before until you set colours: options without a colour are grey, only a few fixed words such as “Done” or “High” are coloured.

– Import: Notion's HTML export brings the options' colours along (Notion's brown becomes orange, “default” grey), as does AFFiNE; CSV, Markdown, Jira and Trello get colours in turn. When records are moved or copied to another database, new options take their colour along. The CSV export has no colours.
– API and MCP: database.update accepts and returns optionColors, e.g. {"Open": "blue"}. Without optionColors the stored colours stay; {} removes them.
– A multi-select with the workspace's tags (below) shows the tags' colours.

en.heading: Formatted text
paragraphs: Text properties – all except the title – can contain bold, italic, ~~strikethrough~~, code, links and line breaks. These are marks within the text only, no blocks: headings, lists, quotes or tables are not available there (that is what the record's own text is for). There is no underline.
– Editing: click the cell in the table, or the field in the record. When text is selected, a small bar with bold, italic, strikethrough, code and link appears above it.

– Shortcuts: ⌘ B bold, ⌘ I italic, ⌘ ⇧ X strikethrough, ⌘ E code, ⌘ K links the selected text (without a selection ⌘ K opens the quick search as everywhere). Links only go to http, https and mailto; example.com becomes https://example.com, an e-mail address a mailto: link. An empty field removes the link.

– Line break: ⇧ Enter. In a table cell Enter ends editing and saves, Esc discards it. In the record, in the feed and when editing through a share link, Enter also makes a line break; the value is saved when you leave the field.

– Display: formatted in table, board, gallery, list, feed, the record, published pages and embedded views. In table cells and on cards a line break shows as a space (the row stays one line), in the record and the feed as a break. Links open in a new tab; on cards that are links themselves they stay text.

– As plain text the value counts for search, filters (contains …), sorting, grouping, formulas (prop("Note") returns the text without formatting), copying to the clipboard, the CSV export, the apps' widgets and placeholders in templates and automations.
– Pasting from Word, Google Docs or web pages keeps bold, italic, strikethrough, code and links; headings become bold, paragraphs and list items line breaks, images and tables are left out.

– Import and export: CSV (including Notion exports), Jira and Trello, vCards, LDAP and form answers are plain text – asterisks and underscores stay as written. Tables from AFFiNE and tables from documents (Turn into database) keep their formatting. The Markdown export writes the formatting as Markdown, the CSV export plain text. Older content archives come in as plain text.
– Existing values from before this feature look as they did: asterisks keep their asterisks.
– Changing the type: when another property becomes text, its values stay as written; when text becomes another type, the text without formatting counts.

– API and MCP: the value is a string with inline Markdown: bold, _italic_ (or italic), ~~strikethrough~~, ` code , label and \n for a line break. A backslash keeps \ * _ ~ [ ] ` as characters – so send plain text escaped. Links with other schemes (such as javascript:) show only their label; # or - ` at the start stay text. The title is plain text.

en.heading: Multi-select with the workspace tags
paragraphs: Instead of its own list, a multi-select can have the workspace's tags as its options – the same tags pages carry. In the property's settings (click the column header), under Options, choose between Own list and Workspace tags.

– The property offers the tags that apply in the database's space – those of the whole workspace and those of the space (see scope) –, with their colours and in their order; a new tag from a record belongs to the database's space; cells, board columns and cards show the tag colours. In a record you pick with + Tag as on pages: typing suggests matching tags, Enter takes one.

– A value that is not a tag yet creates the tag – as on pages, members with edit rights may do that. Readers, guests and read tokens only pick existing tags. On a board, + Group creates a new tag for such a property.
– It stays a multi-select: filters, sorting, grouping, board columns, formulas, automations, import and export (Markdown, CSV, Git), API and MCP work as usual. The tag names are stored.

– Renaming, merging and deleting a tag (Settings → Tags & properties) changes every record with that tag as well: a renamed tag shows under its new name, merging turns the one tag into the other (without duplicates), a deleted tag disappears from the records. Filters and board columns of views follow; Flowplan first keeps a version of every database affected in its version history.
– Records with tags appear in the tag view next to the pages and are found with #tag / -#tag in the search.

– Switching an existing multi-select to the tags: its options are matched to tags (ignoring case), missing tags are created; the records keep their values, now with the tag's exact name. Back to “Own list”, the tags become its own options – the ones in use first, at most 100; the values stay. The options keep the tags' colours.
– Guests only see the tags used in the records shared with them as options and create none. Through share links a record only offers its own tags.
– In encrypted spaces the option does not exist (like tags on pages).
A database is a collection of records with properties. The same records can be shown as a table, board, calendar, timeline, gallery, list, feed, chart or form.
More on this topic: Database properties

en.heading: Create a database
paragraphs: New page → Database shows the Kind right below as one row to choose from, with the properties of the chosen one underneath:
Kind Properties First view
Tasks Task, Status, Priority, Due, Assignee, Tags Table "All tasks", plus board, calendar, timeline …
Documents Title, Tags, Created, Edited List "All documents" (last edited first), gallery, table; records open as a full page, empty properties are hidden

Contacts Name, First name, Last name, Company, Position, E-mail, Phone, Mobile, Street, Postal code, City, Country, Birthday, Tags List “All contacts” (by last name), Table, calendar “Birthdays”, Gallery; records open as a profile page with a contact card – see Contacts
Empty only a title Table

Below are Your templates: saved database templates, such as your own "Notes (PARA)" database with relations and views. The device remembers the last choice. Alternatively use a template, such as "Tasks" or "Projects", or import a CSV file (see Import, export and versions).

en.heading: Records
paragraphs: – New at the bottom of the table or at the top right creates a record and opens it with the title selected – just start typing, Enter saves.

– Editing: in the table Enter saves numbers too; a double-click on a multi-select only opens it without ticking an option. Esc closes an open record – what you typed into the title or properties stays saved.

– A click on the title opens the record as a page: the title at the top to edit directly, the properties below it, and below them a full document with the same editor as every other page – including comments, version history and editing together.

– Open records as (sliders at the top of the record → layout, for all records of the database; a view can choose differently under Configure view): Side peek to the right of the view, Centred as a dialog over the view (the default) or Full page – the record then fills the content area next to the sidebar like any page, with no database behind it.

– Side peek beside the view {since=0.10.2}: in a timeline it docks beside the view, which narrows and stays clickable – another bar switches the record, ↑/↓ step through the view, Esc closes. Drag the left edge for its width (kept per device). Tables, boards and lists choose Beside or Over under Configure view → Side peek. Below 1000 pixels the record opens as a page.

– Order of properties {since=0.9.8}: whoever may change the database's structure reorders the properties in an open record – drag the handle (⋮⋮), or tap or click it for To the top, Move up, Move down and To the end (with the keyboard also ⌥ ↑/↓ on the handle). The order applies to all records of the database and everyone who sees them – also as a full page, in shared records, in print and in a record's export. Tables, boards and other views keep their own column order; new properties go to the end.

– Open as page (arrows at the top of the record) shows a record once as a full page, in a new tab with ⌘/Ctrl-click or the middle mouse button. Get back through the path in the top bar, the back button or the arrows at the top of the record (back to the side peek or the dialog).

– Also at the top right of a record: the star for favourites (in the sidebar a favourite opens the record as a full page), Copy link for the record's address, Share for links and the publication of only this record (Share a single record), the lock for the record's permissions and the sliders for the layout of all records. Icon and Cover appear when the pointer is over the title.

– Reading mode (book icon at the top of the record or ⌘ ⌥ E) opens a record's text for reading only, as for pages; the device remembers it per record. Opened as a full page, Full width uses the whole screen – the properties keep a readable width, the text gets the space.

– An open record has its own address (/#page=&row=, as a full page with &full=1). It can be shared, bookmarked or linked in texts with @; the browser's back and forward move between database, dialog and full page. Below the properties, Linked from shows which records refer to it through a relation and which pages and records link to it in their text.
– Record templates give new records properties and content. One template can be the default for new records.
– Select several records (checkboxes on the left) and edit, duplicate or delete them together – up to 500 at once. Flowplan saves a state beforehand that can be restored from the version history.

– Deleted records sit in the database's trash and can be brought back – with their versions, the comments visitors left through a share link and the reactions on comments. This also works when a record linked two-way has been deleted meanwhile; only that link is dropped. Right after deleting it is quicker: Undo in the notice at the bottom (or ⌘ Z while it shows). A bulk edit of several records, a record dragged into another column, a removed date and a deleted property can be taken back the same way.

en.heading: Sub-pages of a record
paragraphs: A record can hold pages of its own – call notes, a specification and flowcharts below a requirement, for example:
– Add sub-page below the record's document (in the dialog and as a full page) creates a page below the record and opens it. Its Sub-pages are listed above.

– Existing pages go there with Page actions → Move (the database as parent page, then choose Below record) or by drag and drop onto the record's sub-pages or onto the record in the sidebar. Several selected pages can be moved onto a record that already has sub-pages.
– In the sidebar, an expanded database shows the records that have sub-pages, with their sub-pages; the other records stay in the database. The path in the top bar shows database → record → sub-page.

– Sub-pages follow the record's permissions: whoever does not see a private record does not see its sub-pages either; a read-only record makes them read-only for editors. Adding or moving pages there needs edit rights on the record.

– Deleting the record moves its sub-pages to the trash with it; restoring brings them back, deleting for good removes them. Move to … another database takes them along; Convert to page makes them sub-pages of the new page. Duplicate and Copy to … copy the record alone; a copy of the whole database includes the sub-pages.
– Stand-in pages from an earlier Notion migration (a same-named page holding the sub-pages) are dissolved by moving their sub-pages below the record and deleting the empty page.

en.heading: Move a page into a database
paragraphs: Page actions → Move into database … turns a document page into a record of a database you may write to – for example to bring grown documentation into a notes database:
– Title, icon and cover become the record's title, icon and cover, the content its document; files and images stay the same files (they then belong to the database).
– The page's tags go into the database's (first) multi-select with the workspace's tags, if there is one and you may change it.
– Comments, text comments, tasks and versions come along; favourites become record favourites.
– Links to the page in all pages and records of the workspace then point to the record.
– Sub-pages stay pages and become sub-pages of the record; with a database in another space they move up one level. Permissions for people set on the page keep applying to them.

– Sharing of only this page (permissions for people, share links, publication) ends – the dialog lists it first; the record follows the database's permissions. The database's default record template applies.
– The page itself goes to the trash.

en.heading: Turn a record into a page
paragraphs: The other way round, Turn into page … makes a record a document page again – in the … menu at the top of the open record or with a right-click on the record. You need edit access to the record and write access at the target location:
– Title, icon and cover become the page's title, icon and cover, the record's document its content; files and images stay the same files (they then belong to the page).
– The properties stay as a short "Property: value" list at the top of the page (readable in a Markdown export too); in the dialog you can drop them instead.
– The tags from multi-selects with the workspace's tags become the page's tags.
– Comments, text comments, tasks and versions come along; record favourites become page favourites.
– Links to the record in all pages and records of the workspace then point to the page – @ links and backlinks keep working.

– The page goes where the database is, or to another location of your choice, and follows its permissions. The record's own permissions and relations from other records to it end – the dialog lists them first.
– The record itself goes to the database's trash and can be brought back.

en.heading: Copy and move records
paragraphs: A right-click on a record – in a table, board, list, gallery, calendar or timeline – opens its menu: Open, Duplicate, Copy to …, Move to …, Turn into page … and Delete. When several records are selected, the menu applies to all of them; the selection bar also has Move / copy to ….

Copying records: with records selected in the table view, Copy in the selection bar (or ⌘/Ctrl C while no text is selected) puts them on the clipboard – with the view's visible columns as the header row, in the table's order. Pasted into Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets, every value lands in its own cell; in a document it becomes a table. Values come out as the table shows them: numbers in the column's format, select and person columns by name, relations by the record's title, checkboxes as Yes/No.
In the dialog you choose the target database in the same workspace:

– Copy creates new records – with properties, content, icon and cover. Files and images of the source database are copied too, so the copy does not depend on the source. Only files that belong to the source database, that you may see and that are not in the trash are copied; a reference to any other file stays a reference and keeps that file's permissions.
– Move takes the record itself: content, comments, version history, tracked time and Git links stay with it. In the new database it gets the next number (ticket ID).

– Properties are matched by name, the title always to the title. Compatible types are converted (text ↔ e-mail, select ↔ multi-select, number → text …); missing select options are added to the target. Create missing properties in the target adds properties the target does not have yet.
– Calculated values (formulas, rollups, progress, created/edited) are worked out again in the target.

Dragging is quicker: drag records by their handle (with the mouse also by the card) onto a database in the sidebar to move them there – the target database is highlighted; hold Alt when you let go to copy them instead. Flowplan saves a state of the source beforehand.

en.heading: Large databases
paragraphs: Tables, lists and galleries first show 100 records; the next 100 follow as you scroll, and groups and board columns have Show more. Search, filters, sorting and column calculations still always apply to all records. This way even databases with thousands of records open in a fraction of a second.

en.heading: Filter, sort, group
paragraphs: Every view has its own settings:
– Filters with AND/OR groups; for date fields also relative periods ("this week", "last 30 days") that update themselves every day.

– Dates and time zone: on Created at, Edited at and date fields with a time, is, is not, before, after, on or before, on or after and is between count the day the moment falls on in the filter's time zone – a record from 11:30 pm belongs to that day, not the next. The default is your browser's time zone; it shows in the filter and can be changed there, as for relative periods. Dates without a time stay calendar days. Older filters keep using the UTC day until you edit them. The same goes for conditions in automations.
– Sorting by several properties. People, Created by, Edited by and sprints sort by name, relations by the title of the linked record – the way the table shows them.
– Grouping by almost any property (except files and checklists), with up to five levels in tables and lists; boards show the second level as rows (swimlanes).
– Search within the database, also in the text of the record documents.
– Column calculations below table columns: sum, average, median, minimum, maximum, percentages, earliest and latest dates and more.

en.heading: Recurring records
paragraphs: Date fields can repeat daily, weekly, monthly or yearly. Calendar and timeline show the occurrences; it remains a single record. If needed, a single occurrence can be detached as a record of its own.

en.heading: Repeating tasks
paragraphs: For tasks that are ticked off one by one each time (“monthly closing”, “server updates”), set a rhythm in the record under Repeating task: daily, weekly (optionally on certain weekdays, e.g. Mo, We, Fr), monthly or yearly, each every N days, weeks, months or years. The setting reads as one sentence, e.g. “Weekly · every 1 weeks · Mo · counted from Due”. Counted from only appears when there are several date properties and sets which date the next record counts on from; below it, a hint says when it follows. {since=0.9.8}

As soon as the record is done (status or checkbox, see When is a record done?), Flowplan creates the next record: a copy with the status it had before, the chosen date on the next occurrence and every other date field moved by as many days. The rhythm moves to the new record; reopening and completing the old one again creates nothing more.
– Month ends are clamped but the day is kept: 31 January → 28 February → 31 March.
– 29 February becomes the 28th in common years and the 29th again in leap years.
New records at fixed times – whether or not the last one is done – come from scheduled automations.

en.heading: Date reminders
paragraphs: In a record, everyone can set a personal reminder for every filled date field – for times at the appointment or 5 minutes to 1 week before, for all-day dates on the day or 1, 2 or 7 days before at 09:00. Reminders appear in the inbox and as a push notification and do not change the record.

en.heading: Permissions per record
paragraphs: The permissions icon at the top of a record restricts a record beyond the permissions of the database:
– Same as database: the default.
– Read-only record: only its managers (page owners and the person who created the record) and people it is explicitly shared with may change it.
– Private record: only its managers and people it is shared with see it – together with its comments, tasks and files (in the file list, search, media library, copies, templates and backups).
Shares with people or groups never go beyond their role on the database page.

en.heading: Automations and workflows
paragraphs: Recurring steps of a database – set a date, notify, apply a template – are done by automations under … → Automations. For longer flows with branches, waits, approvals, AI, e-mails or other services there are workflows; every rule can be extended into one with Open in canvas.

en.page: Desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux
paragraphs: A slim desktop app wraps your Flowplan instance. On first start it asks for the address and suggests https://app.flowplan.org – for your own instance enter its address instead (e.g. https://flowplan.example.com). More instances are added as profiles.
– All data stays on the server.

– The app remembers the window size and position and opens external links in the default browser. Right-click menu with spelling suggestions, quick capture from anywhere, an icon in the menu bar or notification area, pages in windows of their own and more: see More from the desktop app.

– Offline use works in the desktop app too: turn on Settings → Offline & devices in the app – it keeps its own offline copies, separate from the browser or the installed web app. Without a connection it then opens the stored copy; its own offline page (Try again, Profiles) only appears when there is no copy on the device.
– Notifications: the app shows new inbox notifications as system notifications and the unread count on the app icon – also with the window minimised or hidden. See Notifications in the desktop app.
– It only accepts real Flowplan instances – an address running something else or redirecting to another site is refused.

– Handoff (Mac): the page open in the window appears on your iPad and iPhone (same Apple Account, Handoff on) and opens there in the Flowplan app – or in the browser without the app. A page open in the iPad or iPhone app appears in the Mac's Dock and opens in the desktop app, in the profile of its instance. See iPad: windows, keyboard and Handoff.

– Sign in with a passkey and Sign in with SSO open the sign-in in the default browser, where passkeys (iCloud Keychain, Windows Hello, password managers) are available. After Sign in to the app the app takes over the sign-in; e-mail and password work directly in the app (With e-mail and password opens the form). This needs Flowplan 0.3.3 or newer. If your password manager doesn't fill in anything in the app, Sign in in the browser below the form signs you in through the browser as well (Flowplan 0.8.8 or newer).

– Windows: with a current desktop app and Flowplan newer than 0.8.13, Sign in with a passkey signs you in right in the app window with Windows Hello (face, fingerprint, PIN or security key). If that doesn't work or you cancel, Sign in in the browser below it goes through the browser as before. SSO still goes through the browser, and so do passkeys on macOS and Linux.

– Adding a passkey {since=0.10.0} (Settings → Account) on macOS and Linux: the app's window cannot create passkeys, so the settings say to open the page in your browser with Navigation → Open in Browser and add the passkey there. Signing in with it then works in the app through the browser.

– In the iCloud Keychain {since=0.10.2} (Mac, desktop app newer than 1.3.11): Add a passkey → In the Keychain (iCloud) opens a one-time link (valid five minutes) in the default browser, which stores the passkey in the iCloud Keychain – usable in Safari and on the iPhone too. Then close the browser window; the app shows the new passkey by itself. With Touch ID in the app window, Only in this app (Touch ID) is offered as well.

– Signing in with a passkey on a Mac {since=0.10.2}: Sign in with a passkey always opens your browser – that's where the passkeys of your iCloud Keychain and your password manager are, the same ones as in Safari, Chrome and on the iPhone. If the app has Touch ID in its window, With this app's Touch ID below it is for passkeys you created in this app only (the app window can't see the Keychain, even though macOS lets "Flowplan" ask for your passkey). If the page then says This passkey is not known here., Passkey from the Keychain? Sign in in the browser right in the message goes through the browser.

The apps for macOS, Windows and Linux are at flowplan.org/download – the page detects your system. Updates install themselves (macOS, Windows installer, Linux AppImage). The Mac app is signed and notarized; with 1.0.5 or older, download the current version once – after that it updates itself. Windows shows SmartScreen. More under Operations and troubleshooting.

> The environment variable FLOWPLAN_UPDATE_URL exists twice: on the computer running the desktop app it names another source for app updates (see Updates); on the server, the variable of the same name points the instance's release check at a mirror (see Configuration). They mean different things and belong in different places.

en.page: Desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux
en.heading: Several instances (profiles)
paragraphs: If you work with more than one Flowplan instance, say Work – flowplan.company.com and Private – notes.example, the desktop app keeps each one as a profile:
– Add: menu Profiles → Add Profile…, enter the address and, if you like, a name (without one the app shows the address). The address is checked as on first start.

– Switch: in the Profiles menu (macOS: in the Flowplan menu, Windows and Linux: in the File menu), with Next Profile (⌘ ⇧ P or Ctrl Shift P), from the Dock icon on the Mac and from the taskbar jump list on Windows.

– Rename and remove: Profiles → Manage Profiles… (also reachable from the offline page). Removing asks first, signs the profile out and deletes what it stored on this computer. Your data stays on the server.

Every profile has its own sign-in, its own offline copy and its own cookies – also two profiles on the same instance, for example for two accounts. Only the active profile's instance opens in the window; links to another instance go to the browser. With more than one profile, the window title names the active one.
If you had set up an address before, it becomes the first profile after the update – still signed in and with its offline copy.

en.page: Desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux
en.heading: Notifications in the desktop app
paragraphs: Browsers receive notifications through Web Push, which the desktop app does not have. It therefore asks your instance itself, about once a minute while it runs:

– What appears: each new unread notification once, with the inbox line as title and the record below it (with several profiles also the profile name).
