Your notification kinds under Settings → Notifications apply: only kinds with push switched on pop up. More than three at once become one notification that opens the inbox.
– Click: brings the window to the front, switches to the right profile if needed and opens the page.
– Count on the icon: the unread notifications – on the Dock (macOS), in the launcher (Linux, where the desktop shows counts) and as a red dot on the taskbar button (Windows).

– Settings: in the Notifications menu (macOS: in the Flowplan menu, Windows and Linux: in the File menu): Show Notifications, Do Not Disturb for an hour or until tomorrow morning, and All Profiles (otherwise only the active profile). In the app, Settings → Notifications shows the same switch instead of Web Push.
Nothing pops up for the window in front – its inbox is in view anyway. What was there at the first start is not shown again, not even after a restart.

On a Mac the app keeps running in the Dock after closing the window and keeps notifying. On Windows and Linux closing the window quits the app; notifications arrive while it runs (minimised is enough) – or, with the notification area icon, also without a window.
This needs a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer and desktop app 1.0.7 or newer. The app only asks the profile's own instance, with its sign-in; nothing is stored on the server for it.

en.page: Desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux
en.heading: Self-signed certificates
paragraphs: The desktop app connects to your server the way Chrome does: it trusts every certificate your system trusts. If your server uses its own certificate authority (CA), install it once in your system's certificate store and everything works without asking:
– macOS: double-click the CA file (.crt/.pem), add it to the "System" keychain in Keychain Access, open it there and set "Trust" to "Always Trust".
– Windows: double-click the CA file → "Install Certificate" → "Current User" → "Place all certificates in the following store" → "Trusted Root Certification Authorities".
– Linux: certutil -d sql:$HOME/.pki/nssdb -A -t "C,," -n "My CA" -i ca.crt (package libnss3-tools or nss-tools), then restart Flowplan.

If your system does not trust the certificate – a self-signed one, for example –, the app shows it when you add the server: server, issued to, issued by, validity and SHA-256 fingerprint. Compare the fingerprint with the one on your server (openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256) and choose Trust This Certificate. Flowplan then trusts exactly this certificate for exactly this server in this profile. Expired or revoked certificates are never accepted.

If the server later presents a different certificate, the app loads nothing and warns you with the old and the new fingerprint. Only trust the new one if you know the certificate was renewed. Manage Profiles… shows which certificate a profile trusts, and Stop Trusting Certificate removes it (Flowplan restarts for this). From version 1.3.9.

en.page: Desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux
en.heading: More from the desktop app
paragraphs: From desktop app 1.1.0 there is more around the window. Its switches are under Settings… (macOS: in the Flowplan menu, Windows and Linux: in the File menu).

– Right-click and spelling: a right click in fields, on links and images shows a system menu – suggestions for a misspelled word, Add to Dictionary, cut, copy, paste, Paste as Plain Text, open a link in the browser or in a new window, copy or save an image, Look Up on a Mac. In the editor Flowplan's own text menu stays; the app's suggestions appear at its top (needs a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer). Choose the spell checker's languages – German, English, French – under Spelling in the right-click menu, in the Edit menu or in the settings. Spell checking covers German, English and French only; Chromium, which the desktop app is built on, has no dictionary for Chinese.

– Quick capture from anywhere: Ctrl Shift Space (Mac: ⇧ ⌘ Space) opens a small window above every app – into the inbox, a database, today's journal entry or a page, with shorthand like tomorrow 3pm #client @anna !high, links from the clipboard, files, screen regions and voice notes, Undo and Recently captured, quick actions with shortcuts of their own and an optional AI suggestion. Offline, the capture waits encrypted in a queue and is sent later without arriving twice. Everything about it: Quick capture (desktop).

– Icon in the menu bar (Mac) or notification area (Windows, Linux): Quick Capture, the tasks due today or overdue from My tasks, the unread notifications, open Flowplan, the profiles and quit. On by default on a Mac, switched on in the settings on Windows and Linux; the app then keeps running in the notification area after its window is closed.

– Open pages from links: links like flowplan://open?instance=…&page=… open the page in the app, in the profile of its instance. In a browser on a computer, a page's actions (… at the top right) offer Open in desktop app. For an instance without a profile the app asks first whether to add it.

– Pages in windows of their own: Open Page in New Window (⌘ ⇧ N or Ctrl Shift N), a Shift- or middle-click on a link, or Open in new window in a page's menu. The app remembers these windows with their size and place and opens them again on the next start.

– Back and forward: the Navigation menu → Back / Forward (⌘ [ / ⌘ ], Windows and Linux: Alt ← / Alt →), the mouse's side buttons and, on a Mac, a three-finger swipe take the same steps as the arrows at the top left; the menu items are greyed out when there is nothing in that direction. For the swipe, choose Swipe with two or three fingers under System Settings → Trackpad → More Gestures → Swipe between pages.

– Drop files: drop PDFs, images, Markdown and text files on the Dock icon, open them with Open With → Flowplan, or drop them on the window where Flowplan does not take them itself. The app asks where to: Into the Inbox (one record per file) or As New Pages (Markdown becomes a real page). Images and PDFs up to 50 MB, text up to 5 MB, at most 10 files at once.
– Open at login: in the settings, optionally Start without a window.
– Print and PDF: Print… shows a preview and prints through the system's dialog, Save as PDF… saves the page as a PDF – both without sidebar and tools, as when printing from the browser.

– Updates without interruptions: a new update downloads in the background; a small notice at the bottom of the window shows progress, size and speed, and the progress also shows on the app icon. Once it is ready the notice (and the menu) offer Restart; otherwise it installs when you quit. No dialog interrupts your typing. What's new? in the notice unfolds the release notes of every version between the installed one and the new one, breaking changes highlighted (desktop app 1.3.8 and later). The notes come with the update from the GitHub releases the app checks anyway – no extra request. Whether and what the button shows is set in the app's Settings under Updates → What's new after updates: Show all, Only breaking changes or Never. What's new in Flowplan itself is shown by the instance after its update (What's new after updates).
A shortcut opens a small window above every app: a thought, a task, a link, a file, a screen region or a voice note – into the inbox, a database, today's journal entry or a page. Offline too.
Quick capture is part of the desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux. It saves straight to your instance with the active profile's sign-in; nothing goes to third parties.

en.heading: At a glance
paragraphs: Key What happens
Ctrl Shift Space (Mac: ⇧ ⌘ Space) opens the window above every app – also while Flowplan is minimised, hidden or (Mac, tray icon) closed
Enter saves
Shift Enter new line
Tab choose the target: typing filters, ↑ ↓ moves, Enter takes it
Alt ↑ / ↓ previous / next target without opening the list
⌘/Ctrl Shift V paste the clipboard – a link gets its title
hold ⌘/Ctrl Shift R record a voice note, release to stop
↓ in the empty field Recently captured
Esc closes an open list, otherwise the window – the text stays as a draft
The buttons in the window do the same: Paste, Attach…, Region, Hold to talk, Suggest and As a task for today. The first line becomes the title, the rest the text.

en.heading: Where it goes: targets
paragraphs: The top right shows where the capture goes. You can choose:
Target What is created
Inbox (default) a record in your capture database – the default chosen under Capture (see Capture into a database)
a database a new record; its default template applies, shorthand fills its properties
a journal appended to today's entry – if the day does not exist yet, Flowplan creates it
a page appended at the end of the page, as a new paragraph (or as a task)
The list only shows where you may write. Recently used targets come first; the app remembers them per profile and starts with the last target next time.

> End-to-end encrypted spaces are not in the list. The server cannot write into them, and the capture window – unlike the Flowplan window – has no keys. The list says how many pages are missing for that reason. For encrypted spaces, capture directly in the Flowplan window. Journals behind a PIN are left out too.

As a task for today turns the first line into an open task – due today or on the day from the text, assigned to you or to the person from the text. It shows up at once under My tasks and in the app's tray icon.

en.heading: Shorthand in the text
paragraphs: Flowplan reads what you type as you type and shows it as chips below the text – for example for “Write offer tomorrow 3pm #client @anna !high”:
Due: Tue, Oct 27, 3:00 PM · Tags: Client · Assignee: Anna Schmidt · Priority: High

What a chip takes over disappears from the title. The × on a chip keeps the text exactly as typed. Shorthand only fills properties the target has – otherwise the text stays, and the chip says “stays text”.
Shorthand Examples (German · English · French) Becomes
Days heute, morgen, übermorgen · today, tomorrow, day after tomorrow · aujourd'hui, demain, après-demain due date
Weekdays Freitag, nächsten Montag · friday, next monday · vendredi, lundi prochain the next such day
Spans in 3 Tagen, nächste Woche · in two weeks, next week · dans une semaine, la semaine prochaine a day (next week: its Monday)
Dates 24.12., 24.12.2026, 2026-12-24, 24. Dezember · 12/24, Dec 24th · 24/12, le 5 novembre that day (without a year: the next one)
Times 15 Uhr, um 15:30 · 3pm, at 3:30 pm · 15h, à 9h30 time of the date (alone: today)
Tag #client an option of a multi-select (“Tags” first), if it exists
Person @anna a person property (“Assignee” first) – first name, full name without spaces or e-mail name, when exactly one person matches
Priority !hoch, !niedrig · !high, !urgent, !low · !haute, !basse · !1–!4, !!!, !! an option of a “Priority” select (or one with priority options)
– The due date goes into the first date property (first one named “Due”, “Fällig”, “Échéance” …). A time counts in your computer's time zone, also when the record is only sent later from the queue.
– #27 is a number, not a tag; name@example.org stays an e-mail address; an exclamation mark at the end of a sentence stays one.
– Offline the window shows no chips; the shorthand is read when the capture is sent – with the day and time zone of capturing.
– The server reads the shorthand (one place for all apps). Older servers without this feature take only text into the inbox – the window says so.

en.heading: Clipboard and links
paragraphs: ⌘/Ctrl Shift V or Paste inserts the clipboard text. If it is a link (https://…), it appears as a link chip with title and provider – your instance fetches the preview (like link cards in the editor, protected against internal addresses), never the app itself. It is saved into the database's link property (otherwise into the text) and as a link card; with an empty text, the page's title becomes the title. Offline, the link is saved without a title.

en.heading: Files, screen regions and voice notes
paragraphs: – Files: drop images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, HEIC), PDFs, Markdown and text files on the window, or choose them with Attach…. They are checked as when dropping files on the main window: extension and content, images and PDFs up to 50 MB, text up to 5 MB (the instance may allow less), at most 10 attachments. The list below the text shows them, × removes one. Images and PDFs go into the database's files property and into the text; Markdown and text become text.

– Screen region: Region – the window steps aside and you drag a region; it is attached as a PNG. On the Mac this uses the system's screenshot tool (Space picks a window, Esc cancels); on Windows and Linux Flowplan shows the screen under the pointer, you drag the region, Enter takes the whole screen, Esc cancels. Temporary files sit only briefly in the app's data folder and are deleted right away.

– Voice note: press and hold Hold to talk (or ⌘/Ctrl Shift R), release to stop. If your instance has transcription (Whisper, see Configuration), the recording becomes text there and appears in the field – to check before saving. Without transcription, offline or if it fails, the recording is attached; the instance tries again when it is saved.

en.heading: Permissions per system
paragraphs: System Screen region Microphone

macOS System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording → switch on Flowplan, then restart Flowplan. Without it the window says so and opens the page with Open System Settings. macOS asks the first time (“Flowplan uses the microphone for voice notes.”). Declined: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone.
Windows no permission needed Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone must allow desktop apps
Linux X11: none. Wayland: the desktop asks (portal) and often offers a screen or a window – Flowplan takes what it hands over. depends on the desktop (PipeWire/PulseAudio)
Flowplan never uses the camera, and the capture window may only use the microphone – and only while you hold the button.

en.heading: Offline: the queue
paragraphs: If the instance cannot be reached, the capture goes into a queue – with text, target, shorthand, link and attachments. The window says “No connection to … – queued, sent automatically”, the top shows “1 queued”, and the tray icon and the settings show the number too.

– Sent by itself: as soon as the connection is back, the computer wakes up or is unlocked, otherwise with growing pauses (5 s, 15 s, 30 s … at most every 15 minutes). Send now (window, tray icon, settings) tries right away.

– Nothing twice: every capture has its own key (Idempotency-Key) from the first moment, and every attempt sends exactly the same request. If an answer gets lost after the instance has already saved it, the next attempt receives the stored answer instead of a second record.

– Nothing lost: if the instance refuses something for good (target deleted, file too large), it stays in the queue and the window shows it with Copy (back into the field) and Discard. While signed out, the capture waits until you are signed in again.

– Stored encrypted: the queue and “Recently captured” are kept per profile in the app's data folder (capture/), encrypted with the system's key store (macOS Keychain, Windows DPAPI, Secret Service/KWallet on Linux). Without a key store on Linux they are stored unencrypted, readable only by your user account – the settings say which applies. Removing a profile deletes them.

en.heading: Undo and “Recently captured”
paragraphs: After saving, the window shows “✓ Saved to …” with Open (the record or page in the Flowplan window) and Undo – for ten seconds. Then the window goes away unless you started something new.

– Undo moves a captured record to the database's trash (restorable from there) and removes appended content from a page or the journal again – as long as it is still unchanged at the end. If someone has written on since, it stays, and the window says so. A capture still in the queue is simply not sent.

– Recently captured: ↓ in the empty field shows the profile's last 20 captures with target and time; Enter or Open opens one. The same list (the last 8) is in the menu bar or tray icon under Recently Captured; waiting ones are marked with ⏳.

en.heading: Quick actions
paragraphs: Under Settings → Quick actions you add more shortcuts that open the window ready for one thing:
Quick action Opens the window …
Task with As a task for today and the chosen target
Journal entry with the chosen journal – appended to today's entry
Bookmark with the link from the clipboard and its title
Meeting note with a chosen database and one of its templates (default, or e.g. “Meeting”), the text starting with “Meeting: ”
Note with a fixed target, optionally as a task

Each has a name, a target, a shortcut (Change, Off), Try it and Remove. None is active without a shortcut – after the update only the main shortcut is on. If another app already holds a shortcut, the action says so; a shortcut always belongs to one action only and never also to the main shortcut. At most eight quick actions.

en.heading: AI suggestion (optional)
paragraphs: Suggest asks an AI where the text belongs: database, a short title and properties the text clearly names. The result appears as chips with ✓ (accept) and × (ignore) – nothing is applied by itself. Every suggestion is checked on the server: only databases you may write to, only existing options, only real people and days.

– Where the AI runs: through your instance's AI (the AI actions feature, see AI) – or on a Mac with macOS 26 and Apple Intelligence switched on, on the Mac itself (On-device AI): the instance only builds the question, the Mac answers it, and the text reaches no AI on the server. Which is preferred follows your setting for on-device AI.
– What the AI sees: the text in the window and the names of the databases, their properties and options – no content. Databases closed to the AI are left out.
– Off: the button is missing when the administration or you switched off AI (or AI actions).

Improve text comes with the desktop app's next version: as when capturing in the browser, the AI corrects spelling and grammar and you decide in a preview. The shorthand (#tag, @person, !priority, dates) and links stay; if the AI changed or dropped any of it, the window warns you before you take the text. Only with a connection and when the writing assistant is allowed for you.

en.heading: Setup and the one-time hint
paragraphs: After the first sign-in the app shows one more step: How Flowplan should run on this computer – Turn on quick capture (with the shortcut, Change, Try it now; a taken shortcut is reported), Icon in the menu bar / notification area, Start when you sign in to the computer and Start minimized / in the background (only together with starting at sign-in). The switches start with your system's defaults (icon: on for Mac, off for Windows and Linux), everything can be skipped and changed later under Settings – they are the same settings.

People who had the app before and never captured see “New: quick capture with …” once in the lower left of the window, with Try it and Settings. After closing it, a click or the first capture, the hint never comes back.

en.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: – Captures are only stored on your instance, with the profile's sign-in and its origin check. Link previews, transcription and AI run through the instance (or on the Mac); the app itself fetches no other addresses.

– The computer only keeps the queue and “Recently captured” (encrypted, see above), the recently used targets (identifiers only) and, briefly, screen regions. The window has a session of its own without cookies or storage.
– End-to-end encrypted spaces are never a target.

en.heading: Requirements
paragraphs: The desktop app after 1.2.0 and a Flowplan server newer than 0.7.0. With an older server the window takes text (and As a task for today) into the inbox and says that targets, shorthand, links and attachments need a server update. Voice notes as text need transcription on the server; the AI suggestion needs AI actions switched on, or Apple Intelligence on the Mac.
Ask Claude, ChatGPT or your coding assistant about Flowplan directly: the documentation is available as a public MCP server, as buttons on every page and as Markdown for language models.
This page is about this documentation. To give your assistant access to your own pages and databases in Flowplan, see MCP: AI assistants.

en.heading: The docs' MCP server
paragraphs: The docs are an MCP server (Model Context Protocol) at this address:
https://docs.flowplan.org/mcp
It is public, needs no account and no key, and can only read. Your assistant uses it to search the docs itself and read the right pages, instead of answering from memory. It has three tools:
Tool What it does
search_docs Searches every page – with the same search as the search box here – and returns pages and sections with address and snippet
get_page Returns a page as Markdown, by its name (installation) or its address
list_pages Lists every page with title, description and section
Every page exists in English and German. English is the default; if you write in German, the assistant usually picks the German pages by itself.

en.heading: Claude
paragraphs: In Claude (in the browser and in the desktop app), add the server as a custom connector:
– Open Settings → Connectors and choose Add custom connector.
– Enter a name, for example Flowplan docs, and the address https://docs.flowplan.org/mcp.
– Save. No sign-in is needed.
Whether and how many custom connectors you can add depends on your plan and, for teams, on your organization's settings.

en.heading: Claude Code
paragraphs: claude mcp add --transport http flowplan-docs https://docs.flowplan.org/mcp
With --scope user the docs are available in all your projects. /mcp shows the connection and its tools.

en.heading: Cursor
paragraphs: In .cursor/mcp.json in your project (or ~/.cursor/mcp.json for all projects):
"mcpServers": {
"flowplan-docs": {
"url": "https://docs.flowplan.org/mcp"

en.heading: VS Code
paragraphs: In .vscode/mcp.json in your project:
"servers": {
"flowplan-docs": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://docs.flowplan.org/mcp"

en.heading: ChatGPT and others
paragraphs: In ChatGPT, custom MCP connectors are available in developer mode, depending on your plan and workspace settings. Create a new connector there with the address https://docs.flowplan.org/mcp and choose No authentication. Where exactly this lives changes from time to time; if in doubt, check ChatGPT's help.
Other clients only need the address: the server speaks Streamable HTTP and answers with JSON, without a session and without sign-in.

en.heading: Buttons on every page
paragraphs: Below the title of every page there are four buttons:

– Ask Claude and Ask ChatGPT open the assistant with a ready-made question: it should read the page as Markdown and then answer your questions about it. The question is part of the link's address – you see it before you send it.
– Copy as Markdown puts the whole page on the clipboard as Markdown, to paste into any chat.
– View as Markdown shows the page as Markdown text.
The buttons are ordinary links. The docs load no script from Anthropic or OpenAI for them and do not count who uses them.
Without an assistant of your own, ask Flo: the Ask Flo button at the bottom right of every page answers questions from these docs, with sources.

en.heading: llms.txt and Markdown
paragraphs: For language models and your own tools, the docs are also available as text:
Address Content
/llms.txt Index of every page with description and Markdown address (llmstxt.org)
/llms-full.txt Every page in one file
/en/installation.md One page as Markdown: the page's address with .md at the end
With /de in front, llms.txt, llms-full.txt and the .md addresses are in German.

en.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: – The MCP server needs no account, no key and no cookies.
– Search queries are answered, not stored or logged.
– A per-minute limit prevents abuse. For it, the server counts requests under a hash of the IP address that changes every day and is only kept in memory; the IP address itself is not stored.
– What you ask your assistant goes to its provider, under that provider's privacy terms.
> The server returns only what is written here. If your assistant tells you something you cannot find on these pages, ask for the source – the tools return the address of every result.
The editor works with blocks: every paragraph, list, table or embed is a block you can insert, format, indent and move. Everything is saved continuously, even without a connection.

More on this topic: Working with blocks · Markdown in the editor · Formatting, callouts and captions · Tasks in documents · Images, files and voice notes · Math, diagrams, code and calculations · Links, mentions and the graph · Footnotes, citations and bibliography · Reading, presenting and overview · Printing and PDF

en.heading: The block menu with /
paragraphs: At the start of a line or after a space, / opens the block menu right at the cursor. Keep typing to filter: /h2, /todo, /code, /tab. Arrow keys choose, Enter or Tab inserts, Esc closes.
> To type a plain slash, type a space after / or close the menu with Esc. In code blocks / is always an ordinary character.
Block Shortcut in the menu What for
Text /text A normal paragraph
Heading 1–4 /h1, /h2, /h3, /h4 Structure; they appear in the table of contents
Task list /todo Tasks to tick off
Bulleted list, numbered list /ul, /ol Lists, nested as deep as you like
Quote /quote A highlighted quotation
Note, Tip, Important, Warning, Caution /note, /tip, /important, /warning, /caution A coloured box with icon and title – the five kinds of GitHub alerts
Toggle /toggle Content that folds in and out
Code /code Syntax highlighting for more than 240 languages (as in VS Code), preview for HTML, SVG, Markdown, Mermaid, LaTeX and Typst
Table /table A simple table in the text
Image or file /image, /file Upload or pick from the media library
Mermaid diagram /mermaid Flowcharts, sequence and class diagrams as text
draw.io diagram /drawio Draw diagrams with the draw.io editor
Formula, inline formula /math, /inlinemath LaTeX, rendered with KaTeX
Mention a page, record or person /mention or @ A reference to a page, database record or person
Whiteboard /board Embed a whiteboard in the document
Draw /draw, /sketch, /handwriting Handwriting and sketches with a pen or finger (Handwriting in documents)
Linked database /db A view of an existing database
Two columns /columns Content side by side
Embed /embed Players for YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Spotify, Figma, CodePen; a link card otherwise
Spoiler /spoiler Hidden text, revealed by a click
Voice note /voice Record (up to two hours) and insert as audio, optionally also as a transcript
Synced block /sync Content that stays the same on several pages
Insert synced block /sync Show an existing synced block
Divider /hr A horizontal line
Page break /page break, /pagebreak Continue on a new page in print, PDF and Word (Page break)
AI /ai, /ki Let the AI write (when switched on)
Footnote /footnote, /fußnote Numbered note at the end of the page (Footnotes)
Citation /cite, /zitat Cite a source – DOI, BibTeX or Zotero (Citations)
Bibliography /bibliography, /references All cited works as a list

Tables: tables are compact – low rows, a left-aligned header, as wide as their content (dragged column widths stay). Point at a column border to see a blue line; drag it to make the column wider or narrower. {since=0.9.6} Point at a cell and two handles ⋮⋮ appear: on the left edge of its row and on the top edge of its column. A click selects the row or column (outlined in blue) and opens its menu: a search field, Colour (text or background), Insert row above/below or Insert column left/right, Duplicate (⌘ D), Clear contents, Delete row/column, Header row or Header column, Caption and Convert to database. Drag a handle to move the row or column – a line shows where it lands; the header row stays the first row. With a row selected, ⌘ ⇧ ↑/↓ moves it (⌘ ⇧ ←/→ a column). The + bars below the table and at its right edge add a row or a column at the end. Drag across several cells and the selection gets a button at its top right with Colour, Clear contents, Merge cells and Split cell. Rows across merged cells, and columns in tables with merged cells, cannot be moved. On phones and tablets the handles and + bars belong to the cell you tap; the menu opens as a sheet from the bottom. Cell colours survive the Markdown export (as a comment before the table that other tools ignore) and come back as colours on import. Tab moves to the next cell and adds a row in the last one.

Convert a table to a database: when a table outgrows itself, choose Convert to database in the menu of a row or column handle. Flowplan creates a database from it below the document and puts an embedded view of it where the table was. The first row gives the column names, the first column becomes the records' titles. The other columns get their type from the filled cells: number (German or English separators), date (2026-11-04 or 04.11.2026), checkbox (✓, x, yes/no, ja/nein, true/false), URL, otherwise text. The database is named after the table's caption, else the nearest heading above it, else "Table". ⌘/Ctrl Z brings the table back. Limits as for CSV import: up to 80 columns and 5,000 rows. Encrypted spaces don't offer it; in a database record the new database goes to the top of the space.

Hiding the keyboard (phone): while you write, the formatting bar sits above the on-screen keyboard. Its last button on the right, Hide keyboard, closes the keyboard so you see more of the document; the text and the cursor position stay. A tap into the text brings it back. In the content of a database record the bar sits above the keyboard in the same way while you write. For every other text field – titles of pages, databases and records, tags, properties, the name in the New page dialog, search fields, comments – the same button appears as a round button on the right, just above the keyboard. This works in the browser and in the apps.

en.heading: Emojis with :
paragraphs: Type : and at least two letters, and a row of matching emojis appears at the cursor: :smi, :thu, :rock or :rocket. The search covers English names (and German ones in the German interface), shortcodes like :+1: and keywords – exact names and shortcodes come first, then names that start that way, then keywords. Emojis you inserted recently move up front. The first one is selected and its name shows below. ← and → choose, Enter or Tab replaces :rock with 🚀, and so does a click or tap on an emoji. Typing on narrows the row; a closing colon after a known shortcode (:smile:, :tada:) inserts the emoji right away.

With Esc, a space right after the colon or no match, the text stays as it is. The row only opens at the start of a line, after a space or after an opening bracket – not in code blocks, inline code, links or times like 12:30. If you last picked a skin tone in the emoji picker (for a page icon, say), the row suggests emojis in that tone. The same works in text comments and in comments on pages and records. On a phone, swipe the row sideways.

en.heading: Toggles
paragraphs: A toggle has a title and content below it that folds in and out. Insert one with /toggle, or type > and a space at the start of an empty line. The cursor lands in the empty title (grey "Toggle"); text already after the > becomes the title.

– Collapse and expand: click (or tap) the arrow in front of the title. By keyboard: ⌘ ⌥ Enter (Windows/Linux: Ctrl Alt Enter) in the content collapses it and puts the cursor in the title, where the same keys expand it again.

– Edit the title: a click in the title puts the cursor there. In an expanded toggle, Enter or ↓ moves into the content, and ↑ at the start of the content moves back to the title. In a collapsed toggle, ↓ expands it and moves into the content.

– A list of toggles: Enter at the end of the title of a collapsed toggle adds a new collapsed toggle right below it, with the cursor in its title – handy for an FAQ. Enter in an empty title ends the list: the toggle becomes a normal paragraph, its content stays below.

– From existing text: in the block menu, Turn into … → Toggle turns a paragraph into a toggle with the text as its title. A list item becomes a toggle with the item's text as its title, and its indented sub-items go into the content. A single Undo reverses it.
– Toggle headings: Turn into … → Toggle heading 1–4 shows the title as a heading. In Markdown it is then a heading inside ` (Title`), as GitHub renders it.

– Back to text: Turn into also makes a toggle text, a heading, a list, a quote, a callout or code again: the title becomes the block, its content follows below. ⌫ at the start of the title turns it into plain text in the same way.

– Move in with Tab: Tab at the start of a block right below a toggle moves the block into the toggle, as the last block of its content. This works with paragraphs, headings, quotes, callouts, other toggles and the first items of a list; a collapsed toggle expands. So what is indented belongs to the toggle and hides with it when you collapse it. ⇧ Tab moves a block back out, right below the toggle; the blocks after it stay inside. One Undo reverts each step.

– Nesting: Tab in a toggle's title moves the whole toggle into the toggle above it (or under the last item of a list above it), ⇧ Tab moves it back out. The cursor stays in the title, and from there Tab never moves the focus out of the document. To undo, press Esc first – in the title, ⌘/Ctrl Z only undoes typing in the title.
– What belongs to it: when the mouse is over a toggle's arrow or its ⋮⋮ handle, the whole toggle (title and content) is lightly shaded. The content is indented by exactly one Tab step.

– Nothing gets lost: when the cursor gets into a collapsed toggle (arrow keys, undo) or Find on page goes to a match in it, it expands. Collapse it while the cursor is inside, and the cursor moves in front of the toggle.

– Just for you: as with collapsed sections, collapsing does not change the document – others editing at the same time keep their own state. Your browser or the app remembers what you collapsed on this device for your account, so it is still collapsed the next time you open the page. On another device the toggles are expanded. A toggle is always stored, exported (Markdown `, HTML) and published expanded; readers collapse it there themselves. What you collapsed is remembered on imported and API-created pages too. A toggle without a title is exported to Markdown with an empty ` and comes back the same way on import.
– In reading mode a click on the whole title line collapses and expands it.

en.heading: Synced blocks
paragraphs: A synced block (/sync → Synced block) is content that is the same in several places – such as contact details, a checklist or a status notice. Insert synced block shows it on another page. You can edit it everywhere; the change appears on all pages, live on pages that are open.
– An orange frame marks the block; at the top it shows the number of pages and the page it was created on.
– The trash icon in the frame removes the block only in this place; it stays in the others.
– Permissions come from the page the block was created on: whoever may not read that page sees a notice instead of the content.
– The search finds the text on the original page. The block does not appear on published pages.

en.heading: More blocks
paragraphs: – Table of contents: lists the headings of the page and jumps there on click.
– Two columns: blocks side by side; stacked on a phone.
– Linked database: a view of an existing database with its own filters and sorting; changes to records go to the source. See Views.
– Whiteboard: a whiteboard right in the document; the button at the top right opens it large.
– Draw (/draw): a block for handwriting across the full width, blank, lined or grid, with a height you drag; several people draw at once without overwriting each other. See Handwriting in documents.
So your family can reach your content in an emergency: trusted contacts with read access after a waiting period, and a message Flowplan sends when you haven't used it for a long time.

en.heading: Emergency access
paragraphs: Under Settings → Account & security → Emergency access you name up to five trusted contacts – people with an account on this instance – each with a waiting period (1, 2, 7, 14 or 30 days) and an access length (until you end it, or 7, 30 or 90 days). The person has to accept the role.

– Request: In an emergency they request access under "I am a trusted contact for …". You are told right away – in Flowplan, by push, chat app and an e-mail whose link denies the request without signing in – and reminded before the waiting period ends. After a denial they can ask again after 24 hours at the earliest.

– Grant: Unless you deny, after the waiting period the person can read your private spaces and export them as Markdown or ZIP. They cannot change, delete or share anything or touch your settings, and they don't take over your account; only admins reset credentials.
– Not included: team spaces, content you only see through a workspace (the person needs their own membership for that), other people's private spaces shared with you, and journals with a PIN.

– Encrypted spaces are included once the person has set up encryption: your browser seals the keys for them the next time you unlock, and the server never sees them in plaintext. When the access ends, those spaces get a new key at your next visit.
– You can end an access or remove a trusted contact at any time; every step is in the activity log and the security events, and an export also notifies you.
– Admins switch the feature off under Administration → Sign-in & SSO → Emergency access (or with FLOWPLAN_EMERGENCY_ACCESS=off); granted access is suspended then.

en.heading: Inactivity message
paragraphs: If you don't use Flowplan for a while, Flowplan sends a note of yours to people you choose – so your family knows how to reach your data, for example. Set it up under Settings → Account & security → Inactivity message, separately for each workspace you're a member of (not as a guest; up to three).
– Period: 30, 60, 90 (default), 180 or 365 days without use.
– What counts as use: any use of your account (signing in, working in the open app), or only use of this workspace. A tab that is only open in the background, and API tokens, don't count.

– Note and recipients: text or Markdown, up to 5000 characters, to up to ten e-mail addresses. Recipients need no account. They only get your note, from " via Flowplan ()", with a footer explaining the e-mail – no workspace content, no links, no tracking. Don't put passwords in it.

– Reminders: 7, 3 and 1 day before you get a notification, a push message and an e-mail with an I'm here button. It works without signing in, only once and for ten days. Any sign-in or use resets the period too. Nothing is sent without a last reminder a day before.
– Sending: the note goes to each recipient exactly once; afterwards you're told when and to whom. As soon as you use Flowplan again, the message is switched on again.

– With emergency access: with Grant emergency access to my trusted contacts at once, your trusted contacts get read access without their waiting period when the message is sent – only those who accepted the role at least as long ago as their own waiting period.

– Protection: we e-mail you at once about every change of recipients or note. Setting it up works only when signed in in the browser, not with API tokens. Preview the e-mail shows the e-mail without sending it.

For administrators: the feature needs e-mail delivery (SMTP). It can be switched off under Administration → Sign-in & SSO → Allow inactivity messages (default: on); FLOWPLAN_DEAD_MAN_SWITCH=off switches it off for good. Every sending and every change of recipients shows in the security events. Disabled accounts still send their message; an account deleted for inactivity sends it right before the deletion.

An encrypted space is meant for journals, passwords and other confidential notes. Content, files and – if you choose – titles are encrypted and decrypted in your browser. The server – and with it the operators, backups and the storage provider – only sees ciphertext.

en.heading: What is protected – and what is not
paragraphs: Encrypted
Text of the documents yes
Files and images in the documents yes, including file name and type
Page titles only with Encrypt titles when creating the space
Page structure, icons, times, sizes no
Name of the space and who is a member no

The encryption protects against reading along on the server and in backups. It does not protect against a server that deliberately serves modified program code: a web app runs the code the server sends. If you do not trust the operator of an instance at all, do not edit confidential data on that instance.

en.heading: Set up your keys
paragraphs: With your first encrypted space – or under Settings → Account & security → End-to-end encryption – you set up your keys:
– Choose a passphrase (at least 10 characters, ideally a whole sentence). It is not your sign-in password and never leaves your browser.
– Keep the recovery key safe: 52 characters in groups of four, to Download or Print. Setup only completes once you confirm you have stored it safely.
> whoever loses the passphrase and the recovery key loses access to their encrypted data. Neither the administrators nor the operator can restore it – the server never saw the keys.

Under Settings → Account & security → End-to-end encryption you can change the passphrase and create a new recovery key (the old one stops working). Only if both are lost: Reset keys … at the very bottom, in the Danger zone. Afterwards a member has to give you access to each encrypted space again.

en.heading: Unlock and automatic locking
paragraphs: Encrypted pages first show Unlock. With the passphrase (or the recovery key plus a new passphrase) you decrypt your keys – only in this browser tab and only in memory. Reloading, Lock now or a period without activity (15 minutes by default, adjustable to 5, 15, 30 or 60) locks again. No readable copy stays on the device; that is why encrypted pages cannot be edited offline.

en.heading: Create a space
paragraphs: Add space → name → tick Encrypted space, optionally Encrypt titles → Create space. An encrypted space is always private. In the sidebar it carries a green lock.
Encrypted spaces hold documents only. Databases, whiteboards, dashboards and journals are not possible here (yet) – write a journal as documents, e.g. one page per month.

en.heading: Members
paragraphs: The lock next to the space name (or Members on a page) opens Members and keys:

– Add: owners of the space or of the workspace give a member the key (Give key). This works only while unlocked, and only for people who have already set up their own keys. New members also read all older content.

– Remove or Leave space: the space gets a new key right away; the removed person cannot read new content. What they could decrypt before, they may have kept – old content is not re-encrypted. Whoever is removed from the workspace loses the keys as well.

en.heading: What does not work in encrypted spaces
paragraphs: Everything that would need the server to read the content is switched off here and refused by the server:
– Search, AI, previews, "Related pages" and unlinked mentions
– Comments and text comments, mentions with notifications
– Share links, sharing single pages and publishing
– Version history, templates, duplicating, moving to other spaces (in or out)
– Tags and page properties
– Export as PDF, DOCX, EPUB, server-side Markdown, Git export
– Webhooks only receive the page ID, MCP clients only metadata

en.heading: Export and backup
paragraphs: The editor offers two ways:
– Markdown (decrypted): the browser turns the page into Markdown and saves the file – the plaintext does not pass through the server.
– Encrypted archive: all pages of the space as ciphertext, plus your encrypted space keys and your key secured with passphrase and recovery key. Without passphrase or recovery key it is unreadable.
Regular instance backups also contain encrypted spaces only as ciphertext.

en.heading: Technical details
paragraphs: X25519 key pairs, AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations for the passphrase, all through the browser's WebCrypto interface (current versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari). The full design with the threat model is in docs/e2ee-design.md.
Every environment variable of Flowplan in one table, from A to Z – with its default, its meaning in one sentence and the section that describes it in full.

The variables are read when the container starts, for example from the .env file next to compose.yaml or from the environment variables in Coolify (Installation). Many values can also be set in the Administration; what is saved there takes precedence (In the interface).

The list is put together from the pages of this documentation; a test checks against Flowplan's code that no variable is missing. The field above the table filters it, also by parts such as S3_ or OIDC.
Export pages, databases and whole spaces as Markdown, HTML, Word, PDF or e-book – and as text for Jira and Confluence.
Page actions → Export:
Format Content
Markdown (.md) One file with the page content; databases with an overview, properties and the documents of all records.

Markdown with files (.zip) index.md, sub-pages under pages/, the days of a journal in its folder under 2026/10/2026-10-27.md (see below), record documents under records/, databases also as CSV under tables/, attachments under assets/ – all linked relatively. Every record under records/ starts with its properties as YAML frontmatter (see below). With Include comments and earlier versions, .comments.md and .versions/ come along.
As Word (DOCX) A Word document of the page – see Word, PDF with sub-pages and e-book.
As PDF (with sub-pages) The page with its sub-pages as one document with a cover and a table of contents, which the print dialog saves as PDF.
As e-book (EPUB) The page with its sub-pages as an e-book for e-readers and e-book apps.
Jira (wiki markup) The page as Jira wiki markup to paste into descriptions and comments – see Jira and Confluence.
Confluence (storage format) The page in Confluence's storage format (XHTML) – see Jira and Confluence.
HTML / JSON The older format for documents and databases.

To the clipboard instead of a file. For the text formats – Markdown (.md), Jira, Confluence and HTML / JSON – choose between File and Clipboard under Destination. With Clipboard the button says Copy: the text goes straight to the clipboard, a message confirms it, and you paste it into an e-mail, a chat, a Jira ticket or an editor. HTML also comes along as formatted text, so mail programs and word processors take over headings, lists and tables; a code editor gets the HTML source. Pictures and attachments do not come along – they stay links to Flowplan with their full address and open only for people with access. Flowplan remembers your choice on this device. File formats (Markdown with files, Word, PDF, e-book) are files only. This works in the browser, in the desktop app and in the apps for iPhone, iPad and Android.

Print / PDF opens the browser's print view; save as PDF there. First a small window asks for the print options. Home screen apps on iPhone and iPad cannot print themselves: they open the page in Safari under a secret address for 15 minutes. This print view shows content only – no form fields, buttons or scripts – and at the top who created it.
The export respects read permissions and contains all records regardless of view filters. Formulas and Mermaid are kept as source.
Captions in Markdown: an image's caption becomes its title, a table's a line Table: … below it (as in Pandoc), a code block's Listing: …:
Item Amount
Server €40
Table: Costs at a glance
``ts const x = 1; ``
Listing: An example

The Markdown import (also ZIP, Git and Edit as Markdown) reads these back as captions, as well as Pandoc's short form : … below a table. The title of an image from other sources (`) becomes its caption. A plain paragraph that happens to start with Table: or Listing: right below a table or code block without a caption is exported as Table\: and so stays a paragraph. When the page numbers its captions, the frontmatter says so (flowplan: captions: numbered`); the numbers themselves are not written into the text, so an import doesn't make them part of the caption.

Whiteboards come along in the ZIP as SVG images under assets/: a whiteboard page shows its image, and a whiteboard embedded in a document becomes the image with a link to the board in Flowplan. The image is cropped like Export as SVG in the board; pictures on the board sit next to it under assets/. Covered items stay covered, comment pins are not included; an empty board gives a short note instead of an image. Since SVG is text, Git shows changes to a board as a readable diff. The board cannot be edited outside Flowplan.

Journal days sort by path in the ZIP, in their journal's folder: 2026/10/2026-10-27.md next to the index.md of an exported journal, for a journal below another page under pages/-/2026/10/…. The heading is the day's title in the export's language ("Tuesday, 27 October 2026"; a renamed day keeps its title), the frontmatter names id and date (flowplan: id, date). This applies to the page and space export, the scheduled export and Git. The ZIP import turns them back into a journal with its days, without folder pages "2026" or "10"; a second file of the same date does not become a second day.

Block links in the Markdown export. Links to blocks become relative links with an anchor in the ZIP, the way Obsidian writes them: Project › Goals. The linked block carries its id as a marker: a paragraph, heading or list item at the end of its line (Our goals for 2027 ^k3x9a2b1), any other block (table, code, quote, list …) on a line of its own right below it (^k3x9a2b1). Only blocks that a link in the workspace points to are marked – the rest of the Markdown stays clean. Obsidian reads both as block references; other Markdown tools show the short marker as text. On import (ZIP, Obsidian vault, Git export with taking over changes, Edit as Markdown) the marker becomes the block's id again and the links point to it again. Outside a ZIP (a single Markdown file, MCP) the link stays the Flowplan address with &block=….

Limits per export: 500 pages, 200,000 records, 250 MB of content (at most 200 MB of it text); the ZIP may be up to 100 MB. The same limits apply to the scheduled Markdown export, which backs up whole databases with their comments and versions.

en.heading: Word, PDF with sub-pages and e-book
paragraphs: Three more formats for handbooks, reports and everything that is read or edited outside Flowplan. All three start from the same cleaned page content as the Markdown export and respect read permissions in the same way: they contain only what you may read – other people's private records, PIN-locked journals and pictures from pages you may not open stay out (a note stands in for such a picture, and a link to an inaccessible page becomes plain text).

As Word (DOCX) – Page actions → Export → As Word (DOCX), for a database also via Export in the toolbar, for a single record via the … menu in the record's header. The file is written by Flowplan itself, without a Word library, and opens in Word, LibreOffice and Pages:
– Headings (as Word heading styles, so the navigation pane works), paragraphs with alignment, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, highlights, text colour, superscript and subscript, links.
– Bulleted and numbered lists, also nested, tasks with ☐/☑ and their due date.
– Tables with merged cells and a shaded header row.
– Pictures (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) embedded and scaled to the text width; the page's cover image at the top.
– Captions of images, tables and code in Word's "Caption" style below the block; when the page numbers its captions, the numbers are Word fields (SEQ), so a table of figures in Word picks them up.

– Callouts (note, tip, important, warning, caution) as shaded paragraphs, quotes with a side line, code blocks, formulas and Mermaid diagrams in a monospace style, toggles with their title, columns one after another.
– Footnotes as real Word footnotes, citations and the bibliography as text.
– A database becomes a table of all records followed by every record's document; a single record starts with its properties as a table.
– Not included: whiteboards, embedded videos, audio, PDFs, link cards and linked databases (they stay links to Flowplan), function plots and metrics (a note), comments and versions.

As PDF (with sub-pages) – Page actions → Export → As PDF (with sub-pages): the page with all accessible sub-pages (can be turned off) becomes a print view with a cover, a table of contents and every page as a numbered chapter on a new page; links between the pages jump within the document. As with Print / PDF, the browser's print dialog opens – save as PDF there. Home screen apps on iPhone and iPad open the view in Safari as usual. Whiteboards come along as pictures, databases as a table with the records' documents. Before the print dialog you can choose the title page, table of contents, cover images, page numbers, paper size, fonts and links (print options). Chrome and Edge put page numbers in the footer; page numbers in the table of contents appear only in renderers that know target-counter (Prince, Paged.js). For scripts: GET /api/export/pdf?page=&children=1 returns the HTML of the print view.

As e-book (EPUB) – Page actions → Export → As e-book (EPUB): the page with its sub-pages as EPUB 3 – every page a chapter, the table of contents nested like the page tree, pictures and whiteboards as resources, links between the pages within the book, footnotes at the end of each chapter. Suitable for Apple Books, Kindle (after conversion), Calibre, Thorium and other readers. For scripts: GET /api/export/epub?page=&children=1.
Limits: 200 pages per PDF or EPUB export, 5,000 records, 100 MB of attachments (files over 25 MB are left out). Database tables with more than 200 columns cannot be exported to Word.

en.heading: Jira and Confluence
paragraphs: Two text formats for teams that work with Atlassian tools. Both export only the open page (or a single record), without sub-pages – like Markdown (.md). They respect read permissions like the other exports: pictures from pages you may not open become a note, links to inaccessible pages become text. Links and pictures keep their full address in Flowplan; Jira and Confluence show pictures from Flowplan only while the browser is signed in there.
Jira (wiki markup) – to paste into descriptions and comments of Jira Server/Data Center (and Jira Cloud fields that accept wiki markup):
– Headings as h1. to h6., bold, _italic_, -strikethrough-, +underline+, {{code}}, superscript and subscript, text colour, links as [text address].
– Bulleted and numbered lists with ` and #, nested too (#); tasks as * [ ] and * [x]` (cancelled ones struck through).
– Tables with head and cell ; merged cells become empty cells.
– Code blocks as {code:language}, without a language as {noformat}; formulas as {noformat}, Mermaid as {code}.
– Quotes as {quote}, callouts as {info} (note, important), {tip}, {note} (warning) and {warning} (caution), toggles and meetings as {panel}, dividers as ----.
– Pictures as !address!, mentions as the name, footnotes as superscript numbers with a list at the end.
– Characters that would start formatting in Jira (* _ { } [ ] ! ^ ~ +, dashes at the edge of a word, ??, (y) …) are escaped and show exactly as you typed them.

Confluence (storage format) – the XHTML Confluence stores its pages in: for the source editor, the REST API (representation: storage) or tools that publish to Confluence. Code blocks become the code macro with their language, callouts the info, tip, note and warning macros, toggles "expand", meetings panels, tasks Confluence task lists (with due date), pictures `` with their address in Flowplan. Tables, lists, links, quotes and footnotes stay plain XHTML.

As files the exports are called .jira.txt and .confluence.xhtml. For scripts: GET /api/export/jira?page= or GET /api/export/confluence?page=, with &row= for a single record of a database; personal API tokens with read access are enough.

en.heading: Export a whole space
paragraphs: The download icon next to a space's name in the sidebar (or Settings → Import & export → Export → One space) opens the space export. Besides the Markdown ZIP it offers Space as PDF (a print view of all pages of the space with a cover and a table of contents, see above) and Space as e-book (EPUB) – each with everything you may read, up to 200 pages (GET /api/export/pdf?space= or /api/export/epub?space=). The Markdown ZIP downloads the whole space as one archive – to archive, read offline or put into your own Git repository:
– Every top-level page is in a folder of its own, -/, with everything below it – the same layout as the scheduled Markdown export. Inside, the format of Markdown with files (.zip) applies.
– index.md at the top lists the space's pages; links between pages of the space are relative, links into other spaces keep pointing to Flowplan.

– Anyone who can read the space may export it, no administrator needed. It contains only what that person may read: other people's private records and PIN-locked journals stay out, and other people's private spaces cannot be exported.
– Include comments and earlier versions works as for the page export; the same limits apply, for the whole space.
– For scripts with a read token: {"spaceId":"…","format":"zip","history":true} to /api/markdown-export (see API tokens). The space's id is shown in the export dialog.
– Regularly into a Git repository, without a script of your own: the Git export of a space, set up by the owner of the space.
From signing in for the first time to your first own page: what you do with Flowplan in the first ten minutes.

en.heading: Sign in or sign up
paragraphs: You sign in with your e-mail and password, with a passkey (fingerprint, face or device PIN) or – if your organisation has set it up – with Sign in with SSO through your organisation's login (OpenID Connect, such as Keycloak, Authentik, Zitadel or Entra ID). The sign-in page offers the way you last used on this device as one large button; With e-mail and password opens the form. You create an account with Create account, provided the instance allows sign-ups or you have been invited. Afterwards you set up passkeys under Settings → Account & security. Everything else is described under Sign-in.
On a brand-new instance you create the first account – it administers the instance. If you are moving or reinstalling, choose Restore from a backup there instead (Restore while setting up).

When you sign in for the first time, Flowplan creates a private workspace with example pages. With single sign-on, your name, e-mail address and – if available – your profile picture come from the login provider.

> If the instance offers a demo, you can try Flowplan without an account. The demo gets its own example workspace and is deleted completely when you end it, sign out or after 45 minutes without activity.

Language: Flowplan follows your browser's language. Under Settings → Appearance & language → Language you pick German 🇩🇪, English 🇬🇧, English (US) 🇺🇸, French 🇫🇷 or Chinese 🇨🇳 from the list – it then applies on all devices, also to e-mails and push notifications. Further languages can be added: Languages and translations.

en.heading: The introduction
paragraphs: After creating an account, Flowplan walks you through the essentials once: language and appearance, for admins the setup of the instance, if you like the move from the tool you used so far, first pages, notifications and offline on this device. Every step can be skipped, and afterwards the Getting started list in the sidebar helps you on. The steps in detail are in Introduction and settings. {since=0.9.7}

> Moving from Notion, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Evernote, Confluence or Google Docs? You can do it in the introduction (step Where are you coming from?) and at any time under Settings → Import & export. What comes along and how best to go about it is in Moving to Flowplan.

The settings open with an overview: one tile per section, grouped into Personal, Connections, Workspace and Help & info. The search at the top (“Search settings …”) helps – “passkeys” finds Account & security, for example –, and every section has its own link, e.g. /#settings/notifications.
Which settings you see depends on your settings level: Beginner, Normal or Expert. {since=0.9.7}

en.heading: The interface
paragraphs: – Sidebar on the left: workspace switcher, search, home, inbox, your spaces with the page tree, and below them templates, media, trash and settings.
– Home: recently edited pages, quick starts for a new idea or project, and all pages of your workspace – customizable with widgets (see Customize your home page).
– Header of a page: path, share, comments, favourite and the Page actions menu (…).

– Path: workspace → parent pages → page, and for an open record → database → record. Every part is a link (also into a new tab). The path follows the structure, not the way you came. When it gets long, … folds the middle – a click lists the hidden levels; on a phone only … and the current page remain. Pages you may not read do not appear: guests see the path from the page shared with them.

On a computer, drag the sidebar's right edge to make it wider or narrower (200 to 480 pixels); a double click on the edge restores the original width. Flowplan remembers the width per device. On a phone the sidebar folds away: the icon at the top left opens it, and so does a swipe to the right from the left edge (or Navigation in the bar at the bottom). The bar at the bottom also has Home, Search, Inbox and, in the middle, the round + for a new page (without a label; screen readers call it "New page"). {since=0.9.7} It lies over the current page, which stays visible, dimmed, beside it – nothing is left. Swipe it to the left, tap beside it or press Esc to close it. Over the page it has a width of its own, wider than docked by default (up to 360 pixels on a phone, 400 on a tablet); drag its right edge to change it, a double tap restores the default. Flowplan remembers this width per device, separately from the docked width. On an iPad and other tablets the same swipe opens the collapsed sidebar over the page. In Safari the very edge stays Safari's back gesture – there the swipe starts just inside the edge; the arrows at the top left go back. {since=0.9.7} For iPhone and iPad there is also an app on the App Store, for Android an app to download (Apps for iPhone, iPad and Android).

en.heading: Back and forward
paragraphs: At the top left, next to the sidebar icon, the arrows ← and → take you to the page opened before and forward again. Every place with an address of its own is a step: pages, databases, journal days, whiteboards, a record opened from a database (as a dialog and as a full page, one step each), home, inbox, My tasks, tags, collections, media, trash and the sections of the settings. Dialogs, menus and the search do not count, and closing a record you opened in its database takes you back there without an extra step. When there is nothing in one direction, its arrow is greyed out. Every page and view opens at its top; back and forward take you to where you left it. {since=0.9.6}
– List: a right click or a long press on an arrow shows the last (up to ten) pages in that direction with their icon and title – a click jumps straight there.

– Keyboard shortcuts: ⌘ [ and ⌘ ] or ⌥ ← and ⌥ → (Windows and Linux: Alt ← / Alt → or Ctrl [ / Ctrl ]). While typing, ⌥/Alt with an arrow moves the cursor as usual; the shortcuts can be changed like all others (Keyboard shortcuts).
– Browser: the arrows take the same steps as the browser's back and forward buttons and the mouse's side buttons – you can mix them.
– Desktop app: also the Navigation menu → Back / Forward, the mouse's side buttons and, on a Mac, swiping on the trackpad (More from the desktop app).
– Phone: there are no arrows there – the back gesture (iPhone) or the back button (Android) goes back.

Short animations show what just moved: cards and rows glide into their new place, bars that move along in the timeline visibly follow, and the target of a jump – from the table of contents, search or a notification – lights up briefly. Moving to another page only cross-fades the content area briefly, and the title is in its place at once {since=0.9.6}; a card from a board or gallery grows into its record (on a phone the record comes up as a sheet). A tap or a key ends such a transition at once, and clicking quickly from one page to the next goes without one. While uploaded images load, they show a blurred preview in their final size and then fade in – nothing below them moves. How much moves is up to you under Settings → Appearance & language → Animations (Light and dark). {since=0.9.6} When Reduce motion is on in your device's settings, everything moves to its target without motion, and jump targets are only highlighted briefly and still.

en.heading: Customize your home page
paragraphs: The home page is yours: Customize at the top right (or “Customize home page” in quick search) lets you arrange it from widgets the way you work. On phones everything sits in one column, on tablets in two, on large screens in three or four – the iPhone, iPad and Android apps and the desktop app show the same home page. Widgets of different heights leave no gaps: the first row follows your order from left to right, then each widget moves into the column with the least above it – so next to a tall My activity, short widgets such as Agenda stack on top of each other. Wide widgets sit under the lowest point of the columns they cover. With the keyboard and a screen reader you still go through the widgets in your order.
While customizing:

– Widget opens the gallery: greeting, recently edited or viewed, favourites, the workspace's pages, my tasks, inbox, journal today, agenda, database view, pinned page, quick capture, focus & time, habits, counter, scratchpad, activity, my activity, this week, links and – for administrators – the instance status.
– Move: drag the handle, use the up/down arrows, or the keyboard – focus the handle, then the arrow keys, Home and End.
– Size: small (one column), medium (two), large (three) or full width. A widget never gets wider than the space there is.

– Settings (gear): a heading of your own and what the widget shows – for My tasks “Due today and overdue”, “Due today”, “Overdue” or “All open”, from your tasks or the open records of a database view; for the Agenda the period (today, 3 or 7 days) and which calendar and timeline views count (also those connected to Google, Microsoft 365 or CalDAV).
– Appearance: a header with a colour, a gradient or a page's cover image, an emoji as icon, comfortable or compact spacing, a subtle background (dots, grid, tinted) and a normal or wide page.
– Done saves, Cancel discards. In the … menu you save the home page for all your workspaces (otherwise it applies to this one only) or reset it.

My activity shows how many pages you created and edited – per week, month or year (switchable in the widget), with a chart and the comparison with the same stretch of the previous period. An edited page counts at most once per day, and autosaves don't add to it. Only you see these numbers; Flowplan records nothing new for them and no times – it counts from what is stored anyway (creator, versions, activity log).

{since=0.10.0} Due cards shows what is due today in your flashcards: the number of cards, new and due ones per deck, your streak and Study, which opens all decks. In its settings you choose all decks or certain ones; the numbers are your own.

You tick off tasks right in the widget, habits too; the journal widget adds a few lines to today's entry, and the scratchpad holds whatever fits nowhere else – it saves as you type and is the same on all devices.
Widgets only show what you may see anyway: pages of other workspaces do not appear, journals behind a PIN only show their name, and the home page sees no content of end-to-end encrypted spaces.
A page of figures and charts that several people look at together is a dashboard.
> Workspace owners can use … → Set as default for members to choose the home page new members (and everyone without their own) see. Personal notes are not passed on.

en.heading: Your first page
paragraphs: – Click + next to a space in the sidebar or choose New page on the home screen.

– Enter a name at the top and choose the kind below it: Document, Database, Whiteboard, Journal, Dashboard, Notebook, Workflow or From a template (the arrow keys work too). A line below describes the chosen kind, a database or notebook shows its options right there, and Space sets where the page is created.
– Create page (on phones the buttons stay above the on-screen keyboard) and start writing. Everything is saved automatically, even without a connection.
In a document, / opens the block menu: type /h2, /todo or /table and press Enter to insert. How the editor works in detail is explained under Documents and the editor.

en.heading: Find instead of search
paragraphs: ⌘ K (Windows/Linux: Ctrl K) opens the quick search across titles, text, database records, comments and even the content of uploaded PDFs and Office files. More under Search, inbox and push.

en.heading: Where to go next
paragraphs: – Pages and spaces: page tree, favourites, moving and trash.
– Databases: tables, boards, calendars and more from the same records.
– Collaboration and comments: write together, comment, mention.

en.heading: Help and community
paragraphs: Questions, ideas or just saying hello: in the Flowplan Discord users and admins help each other. Bugs and feature requests are best filed as GitHub issues, so nothing gets lost.
Using flowplan.org and something isn't working right now? The status page shows whether there is a disruption or maintenance. {since=0.9.8}

en.heading: About Flowplan
paragraphs: Settings → Help & info → About Flowplan (/#settings/about, also in the account menu ⋯ at the bottom of the sidebar – on a phone under More – and with ⌘/Ctrl K → “About Flowplan”) shows:

– Version: the running version, the commit and the build date; for our Docker images also whether it is a beta (:beta) or a release. Admins also see here when a newer version is known. Best mention the version when reporting a bug.
– What's new: opens the release notes of the latest versions (see What's new after updates).
– Licence & source code: Flowplan is free software under the GNU AGPL-3.0 – with links to the licence text and to the source of the code running on this instance.
– Links: website, documentation, Discord and “Report a bug” (GitHub issues).
– Support Flowplan ♥: a link to GitHub Sponsors. It never appears in the iPhone, iPad and Android apps (app store rules); admins can hide it with FLOWPLAN_HIDE_SPONSOR=true (Configuration).

The search finds the page with “About”, “Version”, “Licence”, “Source”, “Support” or “Sponsor” (and the German words). The sign-in page also names the licence (AGPL-3.0) and the source code at the bottom.
The AI proposes flashcards from your study material – from a page, a selected passage, a PDF or pasted text. You review every card before anything is added.
> This needs the AI switched on and the feature Create flashcards allowed – by the administration and in your own AI settings.

en.heading: How it works
paragraphs: These ways open the dialog Create flashcards with AI:
– Create with AI in a deck's study view – the cards go into this deck.
– Create flashcards in the text menu when you select text in a document.
– Create flashcards with AI in the quick search (⌘ K, then >) – for the open page.
– Create flashcards in the PDF viewer – with the PDF as the source and the page you are reading. {since=0.10.2}
In the dialog you choose:

– Source: This page (or the record), Selected text, PDF or file (PDFs, Word and other documents of the page – their text, which Flowplan reads for the search, scanned ones through text recognition too) or Paste text. For a PDF you take All pages or only Pages from … to … (at most 300) – a chapter, say; your browser reads the text of those pages from the PDF. Scanned pages without a text layer only work with All pages. {since=0.10.2}
– Deck: an existing flashcard deck or New deck … with a name and a space – it becomes a database of the kind Flashcards.
– At most how many cards (up to 200), which card types (front/back, cloze, type the answer, multiple choice) and, if you like, a focus such as “only terms and definitions”.
Before anything is sent you see about how many tokens the request needs. Propose cards sends the source to the AI; long sources go in parts.

en.heading: Review and add
paragraphs: The suggestions are listed with checkboxes:
– Edit changes front and back, the hint and, for multiple choice, the wrong answers.
– similar to an existing card – the deck has this card already (case, accents and punctuation do not count); Yes/no question – such cards are poor to learn. Both start unticked.
– Source names the passage the card comes from – to check it.
– Regenerate asks the AI again without repeating the cards suggested so far.
– Tags for all gives every card the same tags, such as “Chapter 3”.

Only Add … cards creates the ticked cards as records of the deck – with your permissions, like an import. Clozes are written as {{c1::…}} on the front, the card type into the property Card type, wrong answers into the answer options when the deck has such a property.

If the deck's front or back comes from the record's document, Flowplan writes the card into the document: the front above the divider (---), the back below it – formatting and formulas stay, clozes become the Cloze mark. The record's title gets the front as text when it is not a side of the card. {since=0.10.2}

en.heading: What the AI keeps to
paragraphs: – Only from the source: the AI is told not to invent anything or add knowledge from elsewhere; if the source holds little, fewer cards come.
– One fact per card, short answers, no yes/no questions, no cards from examples or footnotes; gaps only around key terms.
– The source's language – the cards are in the language of the material.
– No duplicates: the deck's fronts go along so the AI does not repeat them; afterwards the server compares once more itself.
Still: read the cards before adding them – an AI can be wrong.

en.heading: Privacy and limits
paragraphs: – The AI only reads what you may read and what it may read: no pages closed to AI, no encrypted spaces, no private records of others. Secrets such as passwords and keys are redacted first.
– The deck's fronts only go along when the AI may read the deck. Nothing from your study sessions – ratings, times, learning state – ever goes to the AI.
– Your instance's provider applies, a local one such as Ollama too; the dialog's footer names it.
– At most 200 cards per run and 400,000 characters of source – for longer ones choose a section. Each part counts towards the instance's limit like every AI request.
– Cards are only added with write access to the deck; the audit log records ai.cards.

en.page: Flashcards: reminder, app, offline and API
paragraphs: To keep you going: a daily reminder, flashcards in the apps for iPhone, iPad and Android and studying without a connection – plus the commands for your own programs.

en.page: Flashcards: reminder, app, offline and API
en.heading: Study reminder
paragraphs: Under Study, Study reminder switches on a daily reminder: Remind me daily at and a time (default 18:00), in your device's time zone. It comes only on days with cards due – new cards within your limits count – that you have not studied yet, at most once a day. The text names the number and the deck with the most cards, such as “12 cards are waiting for you – “Spanish A1” and 2 more decks.”; a tap opens Study.
– The reminder is the notification kind Study reminders: by default as push to your phone and desktop, not in the inbox and not by e-mail. Change that under Settings → Notifications (notifications).
– No nagging: after 30 days without studying, “Study reminders paused” comes once and then nothing – until you rate a card again. Saving the time again also counts as a sign of life.
– If the time has already passed today when you switch it on, the reminder starts tomorrow.
– The time applies to all workspaces; the reminder counts the decks of all your workspaces together.
– If the instance cannot send notifications, the app for iPhone, iPad and Android reminds you itself at the time you set, as long as cards are due (in the app).

en.page: Flashcards: reminder, app, offline and API
en.heading: Studying offline
paragraphs: With offline use switched on – in the browser and in the apps – the device keeps every deck you studied in the last 14 days whole: all cards with their content, your learning state, today's ratings and your limits (up to 5,000 cards per deck, the next ones first). After every session with a connection the device brings its copy up to date.

– Without a connection the overview and the focus mode open as usual. The device puts the cards together itself and schedules with FSRS – by the same rules as the server, sub-decks through filters, daily limits and learning steps included.

– Your ratings stay on the device and are sent once the connection is back; until then the overview, Study and the focus mode say, for example, 2 ratings are waiting for the connection. Undo takes a waiting rating back right on the device.

– Ratings never arrive twice, not even after days. If you studied the same card on another device meanwhile, Flowplan orders the ratings by their time and works out the learning state from them – without asking. Two ratings on the same day both count.
– A rating with a time in the future counts at most five minutes ahead. If a card was deleted meanwhile or you may no longer see it, the rating stays in your statistics only.
– Decks the device has not kept say offline “This deck is not available offline on this device.”
– Only with a connection: creating cards with AI, the Anki import and the export as CSV or Anki package, your own settings and Study more today.
See also What works offline.

en.page: Flashcards: reminder, app, offline and API
en.heading: In the app
paragraphs: The focus mode runs in the apps for iPhone, iPad and Android as in the browser. On top of that:
– the widget Cards due for the home screen (on iPhone and iPad also for the lock screen): how many cards are up today, the deck with the most and your streak. A tap opens Study.
– Study among the quick actions on the app icon (iPhone, iPad) and the app shortcuts (Android), once you have flashcards.
– the action Study due cards in the Shortcuts app (iPhone, iPad); with a shortcut of your own you start it with Siri too.
– the study reminder as a notification – or, when the instance cannot send notifications, as a reminder of the app itself.

en.page: Flashcards: reminder, app, offline and API
en.heading: API and MCP
