paragraphs: With the API you can study from your own programs too: study.queue (or GET /api/pages/{id}/study) returns the next cards with the counts, study.review rates, study.undo undoes, study.prefs sets your own limits, study.settings sets up the cards. {since=0.10.0} study.due (or GET /api/study/due) counts the due cards of all decks of a workspace, study.stats (or GET /api/study/stats) returns the statistics, GET /api/pages/{id}/study/export the CSV (with format=apkg the Anki package); study.queue with ahead brings learning cards that would only be due later today. {since=0.10.0} GET /api/pages/{id}/study?offline=1 returns the whole deck for studying without a connection, study.reviews takes up to 500 ratings sent later at once (idempotent by their id, ordered by their time), study.reminder sets the daily study reminder (remindAt as HH:MM or null). {since=0.10.0} study.history returns your ratings for optimising the parameters, study.params stores or resets them. {since=0.10.2} study.optimize optimises them on the server and recommends a retention; both work for a part of a deck too (group). Read-only tokens can read cards and counts but not rate. The MCP server has the tool study_decks: your decks of a workspace with what is due today; {since=0.10.2} plus optimize_flashcard_parameters (calculates, read tokens too) and set_flashcard_parameters (stores, needs a write token). All shapes are in the OpenAPI description.

Besides front and back, Flowplan knows cloze, type the answer and multiple choice – here is how you write them and how Flowplan asks them. Which type applies to a record and how you create a deck is under Flashcards; pictures you learn with image occlusion.

en.heading: Cloze
paragraphs: In a text property you write a cloze as in Anki: {{c1::Paris}} lies on the {{c2::Seine::river}}. The number is the cloze's number; after a second :: comes a hint shown in the gap. Every number becomes a card of its own; the same number twice asks both places on one card. The card for c1 shows “[…] lies on the Seine” – the other clozes as plain text –, after revealing the answer is highlighted.

In a record's document you select the text and choose As cloze (new number) or As cloze (same number as before) under … in the text menu – or type / Cloze. With the keyboard: ⌘⌥G / Ctrl+Alt+G for a new number, with Shift for the number of the cloze before it; on a cloze the same shortcut removes it. In the editor clozes are tinted and carry their number (c1, c2 …); when reading the page they are covered like a spoiler, a click shows them. In the Markdown export they are written as {{c1::…}}, and the Markdown import turns them back into clozes.
– A front/back record with clozes on a side becomes cloze cards by itself – so imported cards need no type of their own.
– With the clozes in the document (the back), the card shows the title above it; with the clozes on the front, the back comes as a note after revealing.
– Learning states belong to the number: renumber clozes and the learning state goes with the new number.
– Nested clozes ({{c1::… {{c2::…}} …}}) are read flat: the inner one counts as text of the outer one.
– {since=0.10.0} Cloze (flashcard) in the formatting toolbar does the same; it starts hidden (customize the toolbar).
– {since=0.10.0} Search reads {{c2::Seine::river}} as “Seine”.

en.heading: Type the answer
paragraphs: A field sits under the front; Enter checks. Flowplan compares with the back (for a document its first paragraph) and shows the differences character by character – what you typed too much struck through, what is missing underlined. Separate several right answers in the back with , such as colour color.

– Correct suggests Good, Almost (one character different, for answers of six characters or more) Hard, otherwise Again. The suggestion is highlighted, Enter or Space take it – but you may choose any rating.

– What the comparison passes over is set per deck: upper and lower case, accents (é = e, off by default because they matter in languages) and punctuation. Spaces at the ends and double spaces never count.
– Esc in a field with text first leaves the field; a second Esc ends the session.
– {since=0.10.2} If the back holds only the expected answer, Flowplan does not show it a second time after checking; extra and note stay.

en.heading: Multiple choice
paragraphs: The card shows the right answer (the back) among wrong ones. The wrong ones come from the property under Answer options (one option per line, on one line separated by ;, or the values of a multi-select) – if some are missing, Flowplan adds backs of other cards of the same deck, preferably with the same tags and a similar length. Only cards you may study yourself come into question: no private records of others, no hidden properties, in a sub-deck only its cards.
– The order of the answers is shuffled anew for every review and stays while the card is shown.
– Pick with a tap or the keys A to E (before revealing also 1 to 5). Right suggests Good, wrong Again; you may rate otherwise.
– {since=0.10.2} After your pick the right answer carries ✓ “correct” and a wrong pick ✗ “your choice, wrong” – not just a colour. If the back is only the right answer, it is not repeated below.
– Multiple choice is easier than free recall – good to start with; for remembering, front/back and type the answer work better.

Cards for a flashcard deck need not come one by one: the wizard Import cards reads text from CSV, TSV, Quizlet and other study apps, Import from Anki takes over whole Anki decks with images, sounds and, if you like, your learning state. Export gives a deck's cards back as CSV – with your learning state if you like – or as an Anki package. Cards from a page or a PDF are proposed by the AI.

en.heading: Import cards: CSV and Quizlet
paragraphs: Import cards in the study view (with write access) creates records from text:
– Paste text or choose a file (CSV, TSV, TXT, up to 5 MB).

– Flowplan detects the separators – between term and definition tab, comma or semicolon, between cards a new line or a semicolon – and whether the first line names the columns. Both can be changed, to separators of your own too.

– Map every column to a property or skip it. Front and back, hint, extra, tags, card type and answer options are suggested by the column names (“Front”, “Back”, “Term”, “Definition”, the names of your properties …), without a header the first column as the front and the second as the back.
– The preview shows the first cards and every line that will not become a card – with its number and the reason (front or back missing, value too long). Duplicate lines come only once.
– Import … cards creates the records, at most 5000 at once.

Quizlet: open the set, choose Export and copy the text – tab between term and definition, new line or semicolon between cards. Images do not come along this way. The same form fits the text export of Anki, Brainscape and others. Clozes in Anki's syntax ({{c1::…}}) are kept and become cloze cards. Separate tags in a column with commas or semicolons, otherwise with spaces (as in Anki).
The import writes into properties; it does not fill a side that comes from the record's document. Values that are no option of a select become new options.

en.heading: Export as CSV
paragraphs: Export → Cards as CSV downloads one line per card you may study (suspended ones too): front, back, hint, extra, tags, card type and card (empty for the card, r for the reverse one, c1, c2 … for clozes). Documents are written as Markdown, clozes as {{c1::…}}. Cards with my learning state as CSV adds your own state: state, due, stability, difficulty, reviews, lapses, suspended – never anyone else's. Import cards reads the file back; the lines of a card's siblings become one record.

en.heading: Import from Anki
paragraphs: Import from Anki at the top of the Study page – or under Settings → Import & Export → Import with the source Anki (flashcards) – turns Anki decks into flashcard databases:

– In Anki, export an Anki Deck Package (.apkg) via File → Export …, or the whole collection (.colpkg). Flowplan reads the old and the new format (Anki 2.1.50 and later), with or without “Support older Anki versions”.

– Choose the file and the target space. The preview shows the decks with their sub-decks, the number of notes, cards and media files, and notes on what changes. {since=0.10.2} If the package has sub-decks, choose under Sub-decks what they become: Into the property “Deck” (the default) or As databases of their own.

– Check per note type what its fields become – Front, Back, Hint, Extra or skip – plus the card type and Also ask in reverse (not for cloze and image occlusion). The suggestion is what Anki itself shows on front and back; a sample card is shown below. {since=0.10.2} It shows gaps as […] and, revealed, marked; the masks of an image occlusion as Mask 1 and so on – not as {{c1::…}}.
– If you like, Take over my learning state.
– Import … notes. Then Open the deck opens the first deck. {since=0.10.2} If the package has no notes, the wizard says so instead of offering a button.
Anki Flowplan
top-level deck a flashcard database with the views Study and All cards
sub-deck (Spanish::Lesson 1) a value of the select Deck (Lesson 1) – to filter a study view; or a database of its own (see below)
Basic, Basic (and reversed card) front/back, with the reverse card
Basic (type in the answer) type the answer
Cloze cloze, {{c1::…}} is kept
Image Occlusion {since=0.10.0} image occlusion with the masks; on request front/back with the image, without masks
own note type by its templates: fields of the question on the front, fields only of the answer on the back, {{hint:…}} as the hint
tags the multi-select Tags
images, sounds ([sound:…]) files of the deck, sounds as an audio block

– Property or document: a side with simple formatting (bold, italic, links) becomes a property. If it has images, sounds, formulas (\(…\)), lists, tables or super- and subscript anywhere in the deck, it goes into the record's document – the front above a rule, the back below.
– Cleaned: scripts, styles, fonts and colours from Anki are dropped, images from the web stay a link.
– Reverse cards apply to the whole deck in Flowplan. If a deck mixes notes with and without a reverse card, the majority decides – the preview says so.

– Learning state: Flowplan replays Anki's review log with FSRS and so knows every card's stability, difficulty and due date – for you only; nobody else gets a learning state. If Anki has stored FSRS values already, those apply. Suspended cards stay suspended, new cards stay new. {since=0.10.2} A suspended card you never studied stays suspended too – as a new card that does not come up in a session; the statistics count it as suspended. The checkbox then shows for packages without reviews as well.

– Limits: packages up to 100 MB and 50,000 notes. Each media file may be as large as an upload and counts towards the storage; unused ones are left out. Missing files and what was only approximated are listed in the import report.

en.heading: Sub-decks as databases of their own
paragraphs: With As databases of their own, every deck with notes becomes a flashcard database of its own, nested as in Anki: Languages::Spanish::Lesson 1 sits below Spanish, which sits below Languages. A deck without notes of its own – often the top-level one – becomes a plain page holding the databases below it. Each database has its own limits, statistics and parameters; there is no property Deck then. This works for up to 200 decks per import – with more, the property Deck is used.

With the property Deck (the default), a deck stays one database and you study its sub-decks through filters. The property is set up as the cards' Sub-decks, so each sub-deck can get parameters of its own.

en.heading: Export as an Anki package
paragraphs: Export → As an Anki package (.apkg) downloads the view's cards as a package every Anki version (desktop, AnkiDroid, AnkiMobile) imports: one note per record with the note types Basic, Basic with reverse card, Type the answer and Cloze, multiple choice as Basic with the options on the front, image occlusion as Image Occlusion (one note per picture, Anki 23.10 and later). Hint and extra become fields of their own, tags stay tags, the select Deck becomes sub-decks, images and sounds of the deck come along as media. The learning state stays in Flowplan – in Anki the cards are new.

With image occlusion you learn pictures: masks cover parts of a diagram, a map or an anatomy atlas, and each card asks for one of them. The masks lie over the picture – the picture itself stays unchanged. The basics of decks are under Flashcards.

en.heading: Drawing masks
paragraphs: – In the deck, set the Card type to Image occlusion under Set up cards – for all records or as an option of the select Card type (Flowplan recognises “Image occlusion” and “Bildverdeckung” by themselves).
– Open a record and add a picture to its document.
– Select the picture, then in the image tools … → Edit image occlusion (flashcards).
– Draw masks and Save.
Tool How it works
Rectangle, ellipse drag over the picture
Polygon tap its corners one after another; a tap on the first corner, a double click, Enter or Finish polygon closes it
Select and move drag a mask; drag the selected one at its corners to resize it
Add a mask puts a rectangle in the middle – without a mouse
Group, Ungroup several masks become one card (“ask together”)
Preview of the card shows the selected card as it comes in focus mode

Next to the picture is the list of masks with their card number. There you give each mask a label – it is the answer on the back – and on a phone you pick several masks to group them. Asking applies to the whole picture:
– Hide all, ask one (default): every mask is closed, the one asked is highlighted.
– Hide one, show the rest: only the mask asked is closed.

With the keyboard: the arrow keys move the selection (with Shift further, with Alt they change its size), Delete removes, G groups or ungroups, ⌘/Ctrl Z undoes, Esc cancels a polygon or the selection.

en.heading: Cards and learning state
paragraphs: Each mask is a card of its own, each group one together. A record may have several pictures with masks. The cards count like the gaps of a cloze – in the counters, in New cards per day and Reviews per day, and in the statistics.

Masks keep their identity: move a mask, resize it or change its label, and its learning state stays. A new mask is a new card, a deleted one rests with its learning state. Combine masks into a group and you learn the group anew; the group keeps its state as long as it exists.

The record's front and back are still there: the front – say the title “Which region is marked?” – shows above the picture, the back comes after revealing, below the label. If a side takes the document, the picture with masks is not part of its text.

en.heading: Studying
paragraphs: In focus mode the card shows the picture with the masks closed, the one asked highlighted in colour. Show answer opens it – it keeps an outline – and shows the label. You rate it like any card. This works offline too: the pictures of the cards come to the device with the stored deck.

On a phone or tablet you zoom the picture with two fingers – only the picture, not the page. While it is zoomed in, one finger moves the picture instead of rating the card; a double tap shows the whole picture again. Without zoom, swiping rates the card as always. Each new card starts unzoomed. {since=0.10.2}

For screen readers: the picture is announced with its alternative text, plus “Area 3 of 7 covered”, after revealing the label. Give the picture an alternative text in the image occlusion editor; if it has none, the editor points it out.

en.heading: Anki
paragraphs: Notes of the type Image Occlusion (Anki 23.10 and later) come with their masks in the Anki import: rectangles, ellipses and polygons, masks of the same number as a group, Anki's “Hide all” as Hide all, ask one. The learning state applies per mask. Text on the picture comes along as Text on the picture, in its place and size: it shows on both sides of the card above the masks and is never asked; screen readers read it too. In the image occlusion editor you change its wording or remove it. {since=0.10.2} Only shapes of an unknown kind are not taken over; the report gives their number. The export as an Anki package writes the cards back as Image Occlusion notes, one per picture – the text on the picture as Anki's text fields. {since=0.10.2}

FSRS schedules with 21 parameters that suit most people. Once you have studied enough, Flowplan fits them to your own memory – and suggests a retention. This is optional; the default parameters work well.

en.heading: Optimise parameters
paragraphs: In a deck, open My settings; under Memory model (FSRS) it says which parameters the deck uses for you. Optimise parameters … opens the dialog.

– Choose which ratings to learn from: This deck or All my decks – {since=0.10.2} or Part of the deck (see below). Only your own ratings count – imported ones and those made offline too, undone ones not.
– Optimise starts the calculation. It runs in your browser and the page stays usable; with many thousand ratings it takes a few seconds. Only the 21 numbers go to the server.

– The result is one sentence: {since=0.10.2} The new parameters fit you better – with them Flowplan predicts more accurately when you forget a card – or No improvement. Calculation details opens the table: how well the model predicts your ratings, with the default parameters, the current ones (if you optimised before) and the new ones. Lower is better:
– Log loss: how surprised the model is by your ratings on average.
– RMSE (bins): how far the predicted chance of remembering is from your actual share of correct answers, in percentage points.
– Use parameters stores the new parameters; Keep defaults or Keep current closes without a change. This is only offered when the new parameters are better; otherwise Close closes the dialog.
Optimising needs at least 1,000 ratings in the chosen scope. Below that the dialog says how many there are and offers nothing – with few ratings the parameters would be mostly chance.
What applies afterwards:
– Parameters for this deck come first, then those for all decks, then the defaults. {since=0.10.2} Before all of them come those of a part of the deck. Other people keep their own.

– When you apply, Flowplan works out the stability and difficulty of your cards again from their history, as Anki does. Due dates stay; from the next rating FSRS schedules with the new parameters – offline in the apps as well.
– Reset to defaults in the dialog brings the default parameters back.
– The deck's statistics name the memory model: the defaults or your parameters, with the date and the number of ratings.

en.heading: Parts of a deck
paragraphs: If a deck mixes very different things – vocabulary and grammar, easy and hard lessons, cloze cards next to front/back –, each part can get parameters of its own. Part of the deck offers:
– Sub-deck: the values of the select chosen under Set up cards → Sub-decks (with the Anki import, the property Deck).
– Card type: each card type, when the deck has more than one.

Only the ratings of that part's cards count – here too at least 1,000. Applied parameters hold for those cards: a sub-deck before a card type, both before the whole deck. Use the deck's parameters takes them away again. My settings says how many parts have parameters of their own. The buttons of a session show the intervals with the card's parameters, offline as well.
Later, My settings gently suggests optimising again: after 1,000 new ratings, or after a month with at least 200 new ones. There is no notification for it.

en.heading: Recommend retention
paragraphs: After optimising, the dialog names a recommended retention between 70 % and 95 %. To find it, Flowplan plays through a year of studying with your new parameters and looks for the retention at which you spend the least time per card remembered. The times come from your own answer times; forgotten cards count 2.5 times, because forgetting is more annoying than reviewing.

{since=0.10.2} The year is played with the deck's cards as they stand now – their stability, their due dates, the new cards – and with your daily limits: what goes beyond the review limit stays due, and new cards come only as many as allowed. Below the recommendation it says what it means: “At 84 % that is about 42 cards and 9 minutes a day on average.”

en.heading: Workload per retention
paragraphs: The line Cards per day shows for each retention from 70 % to 95 % how many cards you would study a day on average; the retention now and the recommended one are marked. Move the mouse or a finger over it to read the values; As a table adds the minutes per day.

Under Time per day (minutes, optional) enter how much time you have each day; Recalculate plays the year again with that budget. If the time is not enough for everything, Flowplan recommends the retention that keeps the most in memory in your time.
{since=0.10.2} Set retention to 84 % (with the recommended number) sets it as your retention in My settings. A higher retention stays allowed: it costs more reviews, and you forget less often.
The recommendation resembles Anki's “optimal retention” and its simulator, but it is not the same calculation.

en.heading: How the optimisation works
paragraphs: Flowplan looks for the parameters with which FSRS-6 would have predicted your past ratings best – the same goal as Anki's optimiser, in code of its own without an extra program. Reviews count when they come at least one study day after the one before; reviews on the same day only change the card's state. The parameters stay within the bounds FSRS sets, and a short history moves them only a little from the defaults. The same ratings always give the same parameters. The numbers are similar to Anki's, but not the same.

{since=0.10.2} Like Anki's optimiser (fsrs-rs), Flowplan first estimates the initial stability per first rating (Again, Hard, Good, Easy) from the first review a day or more later, leaving out outliers: very rare intervals and intervals over 100 days (over a year for Easy). Cards with such intervals do not count for the other parameters either. Only then are all parameters fitted together.

en.heading: API
paragraphs: study.history returns your ratings of a deck (scope: "deck") or of all decks ("all") as the optimiser reads them; study.params stores 21 parameters or resets them with weights: null. {since=0.10.2} Both take group for a part of the deck (subdeck: or type:; study.history lists the parts under groups).

{since=0.10.2} study.optimize optimises on the server – with the same optimiser as the browser – and returns the parameters, their fit, the recommended retention and the workload per retention (minutesPerDay for a time budget); with apply: true it stores the parameters when they are better. To spare the server: at most 50,000 ratings (those of the cards studied longest), one optimisation per server at a time, five per person in ten minutes, 30 seconds at most. In the MCP server the tools are optimize_flashcard_parameters (only calculates) and set_flashcard_parameters (stores). See Flashcards: API and MCP.

Any database can become a deck of flashcards: a record is a card, and the view Study quizzes you. Flowplan uses FSRS to plan when you see a card again – shortly before you would forget it. Everyone has their own learning state; read access is enough to study.

en.heading: Creating a deck
paragraphs: There are several ways to a deck:
– New page → Database → Flashcards: the database comes with the properties Front (the title), Back, Tags and {since=0.10.0} Card type, and the views Study and All cards. The cards are set up already.
– Template “Flashcard database” (category Knowledge): as above, with the properties Example and Wrong answers and {since=0.10.0} one sample card per card type. More decks: templates.
– {since=0.10.0} Import cards in the study view brings cards from CSV, Quizlet and other text (Import and export flashcards), Import from Anki on the Study page whole Anki decks (Import from Anki).
– {since=0.10.0} Create with AI proposes cards from a page, a selection or a PDF (Flashcards with AI).
– An existing database: Add view → Study gives it a study view. If nothing is set up yet, Set up cards opens right away.

en.heading: Setting up cards
paragraphs: Set up cards decides what goes on a card. It applies to the whole database, not to one view – so two study views of the same database study the same cards with the same learning state.
Setting Meaning
Front a property (usually the title) or the record's document above a line
Back a property, the record's whole document or the document below a line
Hint a property you can show before revealing
Extra a property shown under the answer after revealing
Card type {since=0.10.0} the same for all records or from a select property (card types)
Answer options {since=0.10.0} for multiple choice: a property with the wrong answers; without one, Flowplan takes the backs of other cards
Tags {since=0.10.0} a select or multi-select property; generated answer options prefer cards with the same tags
Sub-decks {since=0.10.2} a select property whose values are sub-decks; each can get parameters of its own
Typed answers: ignore {since=0.10.0} what the comparison passes over: upper and lower case (on), accents (off), punctuation (on)
Also study in reverse a second card per record: back → front
New cards per day default 20
Reviews per day default 200
Retention default 90 %
Text, number, select, multi-select, URL, email and phone properties work as sides. Front and back need different content. A record only becomes a card when both sides have something in them.
Anyone who may edit the database may set up its cards. If you change the mapping later, everybody's learning state is kept – the cards keep their keys.

en.heading: Content from the document
paragraphs: For images, formulas, code or longer answers, use the record's document. The simplest form: title as the front, document as the back. If the front needs more than a sentence too, split the document with a horizontal line – type ---, as for presenting. Everything above the first line is the question, everything below it the answer. Without a line, the whole document is the answer.

en.heading: Card types
paragraphs: Card type How Flowplan asks Cards per record
Front/back show the front, reveal the answer, rate yourself 1, with reverse 2
Cloze show the text with a gap one per cloze number
Type the answer type the answer into a field, Flowplan compares 1, with reverse 2
Multiple choice three to five answers to pick from 1
Image occlusion a picture with covered areas (image occlusion) one per mask or group

Under Card type in Set up cards, one type applies to all records, or it comes from a select property: options named “Cloze”, “Type the answer”, “Multiple choice” or “Image occlusion” (German names too) are recognised by themselves, others you map to a type in the dialog; empty means front/back. Switching between front/back and type the answer keeps the learning state.
How you write gaps and how Flowplan compares typed answers or offers choices is under Card types.

en.heading: Sub-decks through filters
paragraphs: A study view studies the cards that match its filters. With the filter Tags contains “Chapter 3” it becomes a sub-deck. Sub-decks share the deck's daily limits. In the view's settings you also choose whether new cards come between, before or after the reviews, and whether in the order they were added or at random.

en.heading: The overview
paragraphs: The study view shows what is left today: new, learning and due, each already within your daily limits. Below are the number of cards, your limits and the retention.
{since=0.10.2} A study view has no sorting and no search – FSRS plans the order. The filter stays; on a phone it is an icon on one line with the other buttons, with Start studying right below.
– Start studying opens the focus mode.
– Study more today gives you +10 new cards or +50 reviews for today – on the next study day the normal limit applies again.
– My settings: your own limits and your own retention for this deck. An empty field takes the deck's default. Nothing changes for others.
– {since=0.10.0} Statistics opens the deck's statistics, Import cards the import, Create with AI the AI suggestions, Export downloads the cards as CSV or an Anki package.

en.heading: Studying in focus mode
paragraphs: The focus mode fills the screen with one card. {since=0.10.2} At the top are the counts as three coloured numbers – New · Learning · Due –, the kind of the card you see underlined. On a phone a tap on the numbers shows their names. Below them the progress shows as a bar with “1 / 20”, at the top right Undo.
– Read the front and recall the answer.
– Reveal it: Space, Enter, a tap on the card or Show answer.
– Rate yourself honestly. Each button shows when the card comes back, such as “10 min” or “10 days”.
Rating Key Swipe Meaning
Again 1 left not known – comes back in a few minutes
Hard 2 down known with effort
Good 3, Space right known
Easy 4 up known at once – the gap grows more
– Z (or ⌘/Ctrl Z) undoes the last rating; the card comes back unrated. This works for the last ratings of the session, at most 24 hours back.
– H shows the hint, Esc ends the session.

– Swiping on phones and tablets works after revealing. A gesture that starts at the edge of the screen (24 pixels) belongs to the system or the app – such as “back” – and does not move the card. The buttons are always there.

– {since=0.10.2} While you swipe, the card takes the rating's colour and shows the rating large in its middle. On touch devices a line above the buttons recalls the directions: “← Again · ↑ Easy · ↓ Hard · Good →”.

– {since=0.10.2} At the end a summary shows how many cards you studied (each card counted once, with how many of them were new), the study time, the share known (Good or Easy) and your streak. Below, your ratings spread over Again, Hard, Good and Easy, and how many cards are due tomorrow.

– {since=0.10.0} When only cards in the learning phase are left that come back later, the session shows Next card in 25 min and loads it by itself when it is time. Show sooner (or Space) brings it at once.

The focus mode works fully with the keyboard and a screen reader: the answer is read out after revealing, every button says its rating and the next date. {since=0.10.2} On revealing, the answer briefly folds down below the question; the question stays in its place. If you choose less motion in the settings or reduce it in your system, there are no animations.

en.heading: How Flowplan schedules
paragraphs: Flowplan uses FSRS-6, the method Anki offers as well. For every card it estimates how stable it is in your memory and puts the next review where you still know it with the chosen retention (90 %). A higher retention means reviewing more often and forgetting less. Optimising fits FSRS to you.
– New: never studied. New cards only count against the daily limit when you rate them for the first time.
– Learning steps: a new card comes back after 1 and 10 minutes, a forgotten one after 10 minutes. Learning steps do not count against the limits.
– Review: after that, the card comes back after days, weeks or months. So that the cards of one day do not all come back on the same day, Flowplan spreads the gaps a little.
– Siblings: once you study one card of a record, its reverse card waits for the next study day.
– The study day starts at 04:00 in your time zone – studying after midnight still counts for the day before. Flowplan takes the time zone from your device.

en.heading: All decks: Study
paragraphs: Study at the bottom of the sidebar (or “Study: due cards” in quick search, a shortcut of your own in the keyboard shortcuts) shows all decks of the workspace with what is left today: new, learning, due – within your daily limits. {since=0.10.2} At the top, Today: … cards counts all three together; due means the reviews only. Study next to a deck starts it, Study all decks goes through the decks one after the other, each with its limits; at the end of a deck Continue with … moves on to the next. Below are the statistics of all decks, at the top your streak.
The numbers are for the whole deck. A study view with filters studies only part of it, and siblings of a card studied today wait until tomorrow – so a session may show a few cards less.

On the home page the widget Due cards shows the same: how many cards are due today, the decks with new and due cards, your streak and Study. In the widget's settings you choose all decks or certain ones.
{since=0.10.0} Quick search offers every deck with cards for today as a command, such as Study: Spanish A1.

en.heading: Reminder, app and offline
paragraphs: Study reminder, widget Cards due, studying without a connection, and API and MCP: Flashcards: reminder, app, offline and API.

en.heading: Statistics
paragraphs: The statistics show your own numbers only – for one deck (Statistics in the study view) or for all (under Study):
Figure Meaning
Today ratings, new cards, minutes and share correct
Streak study days in a row up to today; if you have not studied yet today, the streak counts on up to yesterday
Ratings per day a year as squares, the darker the more; as a table per month
Due in the next 30 days cards per study day; overdue ones count today

True retention the share of reviews you did not rate “Again”, over 7, 30 and 365 days – next to your target. {since=0.10.2} With fewer than 20 reviews in 30 days the tile shows Too few reviews yet instead of a number
Cards by state new, learning, young (remembered under 21 days, that is stability under 21 days), mature (21 days or more), suspended
Days are study days (starting at 04:00). Every chart has a table for screen readers.

en.heading: In the journal
paragraphs: Below every journal day, Completed this day has one line per deck you studied that day, such as Studied 32 cards in Spanish A1 – with the time of the last rating and a link to the deck. The journal counts by the calendar day in your time zone like all its entries, not by the study day: study at 01:30 and the line is on the new day, while the statistics still count the cards for the day before. The line is always yours – under All too, nobody sees what others studied. A day on which you only studied is not empty and stays.

en.heading: Import and export
paragraphs: CSV, TSV, Quizlet and Anki in, CSV and Anki packages out: Import and export flashcards.

en.heading: Sharing and publishing
paragraphs: Shared or published, a deck can be browsed and practised without an account: Flashcards through a link.

{since=0.10.2} In the marketplace you share a deck as a template – with its cards, pictures and masks, without learning states and without details about people. The template's page shows a few sample cards; whoever takes the deck over starts with new cards.

en.heading: Who sees what
paragraphs: – Studying is open to everyone who may read the database – members, guests of a shared page and readers. The learning state is yours alone: nobody else sees it, not the workspace's owners and not the administration.
– Setting up and editing cards needs write access. A rating is no edit: it does not show in the page's activity.
– Other people's private records and hidden properties never become cards. If a side of the cards is hidden from you, there are no cards for you.
– A record in the trash leaves the deck; restore it and its learning state is back. If you leave the workspace, your learning state there is deleted. Deleting the account removes everything.
– Encrypted spaces have no flashcards.
Flo is the assistant of these docs: ask a question about Flowplan in your own words and get a short answer from these pages, with links to the sections it comes from.

en.heading: What Flo is
paragraphs: Flo – the small otter with the notepad – lives in the Ask Flo button at the bottom right of every page. Click it, type your question and press Enter. Flo answers in a few sentences and lists the pages under Sources, so you can read on there. Links to these docs open in the same tab, and the conversation is still there when you open Flo again on the next page.

You can also start from the search: type what you are looking for (⌘K, Ctrl+K or /) and choose Ask Flo: … at the end of the results. Flo opens with your search term in the question box – you can still change it, and it goes to Flo only when you send it.

Flo understands follow-up questions – "and on Android?" – because the last few questions and answers of the conversation go along with the next question. Start over clears the conversation. On a phone, Flo opens as a sheet from the bottom of the screen.
Flo answers in German or English, depending on the language you read the docs in and write your question in.

en.heading: How Flo answers
paragraphs: Flo answers only from these docs. For each question, the Flo service searches the public pages of docs.flowplan.org, picks the sections that fit best and hands them to the language model Claude by Anthropic together with your question. Claude is told to answer only from those sections and to name the pages it used. Flo has no web access, cannot use tools and cannot see your Flowplan instance, your pages or your account.
If the docs do not cover something, Flo says so and points you to the docs, the community on Discord or GitHub. Questions that are not about Flowplan get a short refusal.

Answers are plain text with a little formatting – lists, bold, code – and only links to the docs, flowplan.org, Flowplan's GitHub repositories and the Discord invite. Everything else in an answer is shown as text, never as a working link or as code that runs.

> Answers can be wrong. A language model can misread a section, mix up two features or leave out a condition. For anything important – an update, a backup, a setting on your server – read the linked section before you act on it.

en.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: The short version, shown under the question box too: your question goes to Anthropic (Claude) and is answered only from the public docs.
What goes to Anthropic:
– your question,

– the last few questions and answers of this conversation (at most the last six messages – each question and each answer counts as one – and at most about 4,000 characters together), so follow-ups work,
– the excerpts from these docs that Flo picked for the answer.

What does not go to Anthropic: your name, your IP address, cookies, the session key described below or anything else about you. Flo cannot tell who you are, and it does not need to. Do not put personal or confidential information into a question – it would be sent along as part of the text.
What stays in your browser:

– No cookie. Flo sets none and sends none. Requests go out without cookies and without the page's address; only the name of the page you are reading goes along, as a hint for finding the right sections.
– The conversation stays in this tab. It is kept in the tab's session storage, so it survives moving between pages, and it is gone when you close the tab – or as soon as you choose Start over.

– A session key. Before the first question, your browser solves a small computing task, which takes about a second ("Getting Flo ready …"). In return, the service hands out a session key valid for two hours. It is bound to nothing personal and also only kept in the tab. It keeps automated scripts from asking in bulk and lets the service count the limits below.
– Nothing is counted on this site. Questions are not part of the docs' visitor statistics.
On the Flo service:
– Limits are counted per session key, and – as a fallback – under a keyed hash of the IP address. The IP address itself is never stored.

– Logging is off by default. If the operator turns it on to improve Flo, only anonymised question–answer pairs are kept – without session key, address or any identifier – and they are deleted automatically after a set number of days.
Anthropic processes the text it receives under the terms for its API.

en.heading: Limits
paragraphs: So that Flo stays available to everyone and its costs stay predictable, there are limits:
Limit What happens
Length of a question About 500 characters by default; the counter under the box shows how many are left
Questions per session A few per minute, hour and day. When you reach one, Flo tells you from what time you can ask again
All questions together A daily and monthly limit for everyone. When it is reached, Flo takes a break and the button disappears until then
Monthly budget When the month's budget is used up, Flo pauses until the next month
When Flo takes a break, the panel closes, a short note tells you why and the button disappears. The docs, the search and every other feature of this site work as always.

en.heading: Flo on Discord
paragraphs: In the Flowplan Discord, Flo answers with the slash command /ask in the channels meant for it: type /ask followed by your question. The answer opens a public thread in the channel – everyone in the channel can read your question and the answer – and you can ask follow-up questions right in the thread.

The same rules apply there: answers only from these docs, with sources, and limits per person and overall. Flo does not send your Discord name or ID to Anthropic; the service only receives a pseudonymous key that the Discord bot derives from your account to count the limits. When Flo is off or has reached a limit, /ask tells you so in a message only you can see.

en.heading: Other ways to ask
paragraphs: – Flowplan docs in your AI: use these docs in Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or another assistant of your own, as an MCP server or with the Ask Claude and Ask ChatGPT buttons under every page title.
– The community on Discord – people who use and run Flowplan help each other there.
– A bug or something missing from the docs: open an issue on GitHub.
Format text, use callouts in five kinds and with your own icon, caption and number images and tables.

en.heading: Format text
paragraphs: The toolbar above the text has all formatting and blocks: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, highlight, colour and background colour, superscript and subscript, Hide (spoiler), link, heading, task, alignment, lists, inline formulas and more blocks. Text style and alignment are small menus: the button shows what applies at the cursor ("Aa" for text, "H1" … "H4", or the alignment's icon). {since=0.9.7} The text style button is as wide as the others, with a small caret in its corner; its full name is the tooltip ("Text style: Text"). In the menu you choose Text or Heading 1–4 (⌘ ⌥ 0 to ⌘ ⌥ 4), or Align left, Centred (⌘ ⇧ E), Align right (⌘ ⇧ R) or Justified (⌘ ⇧ J); while Suggest is on, the green button shows the word "Suggest". {since=0.9.6} Selecting text – or right-clicking it – opens the text menu with the quick actions right at the text: reactions for the paragraph, bold, italic, link, code, Comment, Footnote and Copy, the results of a selected calculation, and in tasks also Due date. The text menu appears above the selection – right under the toolbar it appears below it, so it never covers the toolbar. Underline, strikethrough and highlight are in the toolbar and on their shortcuts (Ctrl/⌘ U, Ctrl/⌘ ⇧ S, Ctrl/⌘ ⇧ H); where no toolbar is shown (e.g. in focus mode), the text menu offers them as well.

– Menu on text selection: under Settings → Appearance & language → Editor → Menu on text selection you choose when selecting shows the text menu – Always, Only on a computer (the default) or Never. "Only on a computer" depends on what you select with: with a mouse, trackpad or the keyboard (⇧ + arrow keys) the menu appears, with a finger on a phone or tablet it does not – there the system's selection menu (cut, copy, paste) and the toolbar above the keyboard, with formatting and Comment, take over. On an iPad with a trackpad it appears when you select with the trackpad, not with your finger. A right click opens the text menu with every setting, also with "Never". The setting applies to your account on all devices.

– Formatting toolbar: under Settings → Appearance & language → Editor → Formatting toolbar you can hide the fixed bar above the text of pages and records (Show is the default, Hide). Hidden, the text menu over selected text offers all formatting, as in focus mode: Turn into at its start with the current block type ("Text ⌄" – text, heading 1–3, bulleted list, numbered list, task list, toggle, quote, callout, code, block equation), then bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, highlight, colour (text and background), link, inline formula and clear formatting (links and comments stay). … holds superscript and subscript, hide (spoiler), alignment, move block up/down, suggest, show authors and the table of contents. Comment, AI, footnote and copy stay as before; undo and redo are ⌘ Z and ⌘ ⇧ Z. On a phone the bar above the keyboard stays – there it is the keyboard's formatting row. The setting applies to your account on all devices.

– Customize formatting toolbar {since=0.9.7}: under Settings → Appearance & language → Editor → Customize formatting toolbar (the Expert level), Customize … opens the list of every button of the bar above pages and records. A checkbox shows or hides a button; you change the order by dragging its handle or with Move up / Move down (with the keyboard and screen readers too). Insert divider after adds a divider, Remove divider takes it away again. Group with the next button puts buttons together into one: in the bar it shows the icon of the active one (else the first) with a small caret and opens a menu with all of them; Take out of the group and Ungroup undo it. Two ready-made groups exist already: Lists (bulleted list, numbered list, task list) and Superscript, subscript & strikethrough. Bulleted and numbered list are new buttons and hidden at first, so the bar looks as before. Add divider next to the ready-made groups asks after which button the divider goes. Above the list you see the bar as it will look; groups like Aa open there to look inside. Under Blocks you find every block of the / menu (table, callout, code, formula, diagram, database …), hidden at first: shown in the bar, a click inserts the block below the current one, like +; text, headings and quote turn the current paragraph, mention, fraction, footnote and citation go at the cursor. Blocks that don't work on a page (such as AI when it isn't enabled) are left out of the bar there. The line above Customize … shows whether your bar is Customized or follows the Instance default or the Default. Reset goes back to the default – the instance's, if the administration set one (Instance). Every change is saved right away and applies to your account on all devices, also to the bar above the keyboard on a phone (which still scrolls sideways). If you hide underline, strikethrough or highlight, the text menu offers them over selected text. The bar on shared pages and the text menu itself do not change.

– On a phone: Comment is in the toolbar above the keyboard (and below the document Text comments with New {since=0.9.8}), Footnote in the + menu or with /footnote. Reactions are in the text menu – with Always when selecting, and on Android also by a long press where the browser reports it as a right click.
– Formatting only applies to the current line. After Enter the new line starts as normal text – only lists and tasks continue with a new item, and a heading is followed by a paragraph.

– Turn into: in the text menu (also on right-click in a line; with the formatting toolbar hidden or in focus mode as the list "Text ⌄" at its start) a line changes its type without losing its text – text, heading 1–3, bulleted list, numbered list, task, quote or code block. The current type is highlighted.

– Nested lists change their markers per level: numbered 1. → a. → i., bullets • → ◦ → ▪, starting over from the fourth level. The level counts across list types – a numbered list below a bullet or a task starts with a. Published pages, print, PDF and Word look the same; the Markdown export keeps writing 1..

– Code and highlight: inline code shows in an accent colour on a grey background and can be combined with bold, italic, strikethrough and links (also when importing `code` from Markdown). A highlight without a colour is yellow, see-through in dark mode.

en.heading: Spoiler
paragraphs: Hidden text stays hidden while you write. A click on the area reveals it, another one hides it again. ⌘ ⌥ H hides the selection. Sticky notes and text on whiteboards can be hidden too.

en.heading: Block colours
paragraphs: In the block menu, Colour gives a whole block (paragraph, heading, list item, quote, toggle) a text colour or a background colour – the same nine colours as for text; Default removes it. Several selected blocks are coloured at once. The colours adapt to the light and dark theme.
The Markdown export writes the colour as a comment before the block (for list items at the end of the line); other apps don't show it, and the import reads it back:
<!-- flowplan:color red-background -->
Important paragraph

en.heading: Callouts
paragraphs: Callouts come in five kinds, as on GitHub, Forgejo and Obsidian: Note (blue), Tip (green), Important (purple), Warning (yellow) and Caution (red). Each kind has its icon and a title in the reader's language. With the cursor in a callout, /tip, /warning etc. change its kind; so does the block menu (click the handle ⋮⋮) → Callout type.

en.heading: Your own symbol and colour
paragraphs: So that a callout serves other purposes too – an idea 💡, a date 📅, a key point ★ –, the block menu gives it a symbol and a colour of its own:

– Symbol → Choose emoji or character … opens the emoji picker (the same as for page icons, with search, categories and skin tone). Under Or a character of your own you can also type a character such as ★, → or ✓ – exactly one emoji or symbol character is allowed, no letters, digits, punctuation or spaces. Remove symbol brings back the icon of the kind.
– Colour offers the nine text colours (grey, brown, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, red); Default goes back to the kind's colour. The colours read well in the light and the dark theme.

The kind stays: it gives the title (“Tip”, “Warning” …) and is used for the Markdown export. Symbol and colour are kept when copying, duplicating, in templates, versions, published pages, when printing and in the PDF, EPUB and Word export. Encrypted spaces have no callouts.

en.heading: Callouts in Markdown
paragraphs: Markdown export writes callouts as GitHub alerts (> [!WARNING]). A symbol of its own leads the text, a colour of its own follows as a comment at the end that GitHub does not show:
> 💡 The / menu is quicker.
> <!-- flowplan:callout color=green -->

Import (Markdown, ZIP, Notion) turns > [!NOTE] to > [!CAUTION] back into callouts of that kind; Obsidian's further kinds map to the nearest one (e.g. danger → Caution, hint → Tip), and a custom title (> [!WARNING] Read first) becomes a bold first line. A single emoji or symbol followed by a space at the start of the text becomes the callout's symbol; the colour comment restores the colour. Callouts from Notion's Markdown export (💡 …) become callouts with their emoji.

en.heading: Captions
paragraphs: Images, tables and code blocks can have a short caption – one line that says what the block shows. It appears small and muted below the block.

– Add: for an image, Caption in its toolbar at the top right; for a table, Caption in the menu of a row or column handle; for a code block, Add caption in its bottom corner (when you point at it or the cursor is in it). Or use the block menu (handle ⋮⋮) → Add caption.

– Typing: a caption is plain text on one line (up to 500 characters). Enter or ↓ continue below the block, Esc or ↑ go back into it. Others see the caption right away when editing together; ⌘ Z in the document undoes changes.
– Remove: delete the text and leave the field (or press ⌫ in the empty field), or block menu → Remove caption.
– Images: the caption does not replace the alt text for screen readers. When an image has a caption, the block menu offers Use caption as alt text.

– Captions are kept when copying and pasting, moving, duplicating, in templates, versions, on published pages, when printing and in every export, and search finds them. From HTML (for example pasted web pages or Notion's HTML export), ` with and tables with ` become captions.

en.heading: Numbering captions
paragraphs: Page actions (…) → Number captions puts a number in front of the captions of a page: "Figure 1", "Table 1", "Listing 1" (for code). Each kind is counted separately in document order, and only blocks that have a caption count. The label follows the language Flowplan is shown in (English: Figure/Table/Listing, German: Abbildung/Tabelle/Listing, French: Figure/Tableau/Listing). The switch applies to the whole page and everyone who reads it – also on published pages, when printing and in the exports. Copies of the page keep it. Record documents in databases don't have it.
A form view collects answers directly as records in the database – from members or, if enabled, from anyone with the link.

en.heading: Design a form
paragraphs: – Create a view of the type Form in the database.
– Design form opens the editor:
– title, description and the label of the submit button,
– questions: order, hide, required, help text per question,
– question type: short or long text, radio buttons instead of a list, a linear scale 1–10 for numbers,
– Enter fixed suggestions and Suggest earlier answers for short text questions (see Fixed suggestion lists and Earlier answers as suggestions),
– Only show if … per question (see Conditions and pages),
– Text block before, Text block at the end and New page from here for explanations and several pages,
– title after submitting and confirmation text,
– what happens after sending (see Settings).
– Save form.
Flowplan checks required fields and input types in the browser and on the server. Files properties allow uploads in the form.

Formatted descriptions {since=0.9.8}: the form's description and the questions' help texts are small editors. Selected text gets bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, a link (http, https or mailto) or a text colour from a small bar; ⌘ B, ⌘ I, ⌘ U, ⌘ ⇧ X, ⌘ E and ⌘ K work too. Enter starts a new line. It shows like that in the form in Flowplan and on the published form; existing descriptions stay as they are.

en.heading: Conditions and pages
paragraphs: Every question, text block and page break can Only show if … an earlier answer matches – for example “Kind is Bug”, “Topics includes Billing”, “Subject contains the text invoice”, “Importance is greater than 7” or “E-mail is answered”. A hidden page break hides its whole page.
– Hidden questions are not required, and their answers are not saved – not even when they are sent anyway. The server checks the same rules as the browser.
– A question that depends on a hidden question stays hidden as well.
– With several pages a progress bar shows how far along you are (can be switched off); Back and Next change the page, and required questions are checked per page.

en.heading: Settings
paragraphs: Under After sending, Confirmation by e-mail and Notify the team – in the form editor as well as in a survey's settings:
– Then redirect to: an address with https:// that the thank-you page leads to after a few seconds (0–60, default 3).

– Placeholders: {Name of the question} inserts the answer to that question – in the title and text after submitting, in the redirect (there only after the domain name, e.g. https://example.com/thanks?name={Name}) and in the e-mail. Unknown names stay as they are; people, relations and files are not inserted.

– Confirmation by e-mail to the people answering: subject and text are up to you. The e-mail contains the text and the answered questions as a list – without hidden and internal properties – and, with the customer portal, the link to the request (then only this one e-mail is sent). It goes to the first answered e-mail question; in forms that are not anonymous, otherwise to the signed-in account's address. Anonymous forms only write when the person types their address. E-mail must be set up (Configuration); at most 5 e-mails per hour go to an address, 10 per sender and 300 per form.
– Notify the team: the chosen members get a notification of the kind “Guest comments and guest records” for each new answer – if they may see the record.

en.heading: Fixed suggestion lists
paragraphs: For a short text question that should offer set answers – places, departments, items –, enter them in Design form at the question with Enter fixed suggestions, one per line. While typing, the matching entries appear under the field from the first letter on: those starting with the typed letters first, then those containing them, each in your order. In an empty field, ↓ shows the list from the top. The answer stays free – anyone who needs something else just types it.
– The list works in every form, public and anonymous ones too: it only holds what you entered yourself, no answers of other people.
– Spaces at the start and end and empty lines are dropped, duplicate entries (also in other upper and lower case) count once.
– At most 200 suggestions per question, each at most 200 characters long. Below the field it says how many there are; with too many or too long ones the form cannot be saved.
– The published form only gets the lists of the questions it asks – not those of hidden questions.
If earlier answers are switched on for the same question too, the fixed suggestions come first, earlier answers after them, without duplicates.

en.heading: Earlier answers as suggestions
paragraphs: For questions that get the same answers again and again – a shopping or order list, a room, a project – Flowplan can suggest earlier answers while typing. Switch on Suggest earlier answers for a short text question in Design form and choose where they come from:
– Own answers: only values from records the person answering created.
– All answers: values from all records the person answering may see.

From two letters on, up to eight distinct values appear under the field – those starting with the typed letters first, then those containing them, the frequent and recent ones first. ↑ and ↓ choose, Enter or a tap takes one, Esc closes the list.
Privacy comes first:

– Suggestions from the server exist only in forms that are Members only and not Anonymous – otherwise anyone with the link could read other people's answers. In other forms the switch cannot be turned on; the reason stands right next to it, together with Switch to “Members only”. The button makes the form one for members and turns anonymous answers off (like the two switches under Share form); then the switch can be turned on. If the form should stay public, use a fixed suggestion list.

– They only come from records the person answering may read, with all permissions: the database's sharing, private records and properties with a read rule. A member who may send the form but not read the database gets no suggestions.
– Only the asked question's values are sent, nothing else of the records; very long values are not suggested.
In anonymous and public forms the browser can still offer what was typed on this device before (its own form history, if switched on in the browser). Flowplan stores nothing for that.

en.heading: Continue later
paragraphs: In forms and surveys that are not anonymous, Save and continue later keeps your answers so far as a draft for you (without files). When you open the link again, you continue on the same page; after sending, the draft is gone. Drafts unchanged for half a year are deleted.

en.heading: Share a form
paragraphs: Under Share form, switch the form on and copy the link.
– Members only: answering requires signing in; the answer carries the person's name.

– Anonymous: anyone with the link can answer, without an account and without a name. Files from anonymous answers count against a daily budget: 200 MB per form and FLOWPLAN_ANONYMOUS_UPLOAD_MB for the whole instance (Configuration); each form also accepts at most 1000 answers per hour.
Person and relation questions only exist in forms for members, because they would reveal members and records.
> Copied or imported forms start switched off and for members only. In the demo, forms can be designed but not made public, and confirmation e-mails cannot be switched on.

en.heading: Answers
paragraphs: Every answer is a normal record: it appears in all views and can be filtered, assigned and commented on.

en.heading: Surveys
paragraphs: Turn into a survey makes a form a survey – or create a new page from the Survey template. The builder has five tabs: Questions, Preview, Settings, Share and Results.

On the left is the flow with numbered questions, text blocks and page breaks; on the right you edit the selected item. Add question shows the question types grouped into choice, rating, and text and details. Everything is saved automatically shortly after you stop typing – the dot at the top right shows the state. If something is still missing (a question without text, an empty answer, a redirect without https://), saving waits and says why.

en.heading: Question types
paragraphs: Surveys have 19 question types:
– Text: short answer, long text, e-mail, phone, website, number, date, time
– Choice: single choice, multiple choice, dropdown, yes / no – optionally with “Other” and a text field, a random order and a minimum or maximum number
– Rating: stars (3 to 10), Net Promoter Score (0–10), a scale with labels at both ends, a slider
– Matrix (Likert): several statements with the same answers
– Ranking: put items in order
– File upload
– Also text blocks for explanations and page breaks for several pages.
Pasting several lines into an answer field adds several answers at once.

en.heading: Conditions
paragraphs: Every question, text block and page break can Only show if … an earlier answer matches – with the same comparisons as in forms. Example: “What should we improve?” only appears for a recommendation score up to 6. Hidden questions are not required, and their answers are not saved.

en.heading: Survey settings
paragraphs: – a welcome page, a progress bar for several pages, a thank-you text with placeholders
– redirect, confirmation e-mail and team notification as for forms
– Closes on and At most this many answers – after that the survey takes no more answers
– One answer per person – signed-in people by their account, anonymous ones by their connection
– an accent colour

en.heading: Sharing and results
paragraphs: Share opens the survey. It can be public, so anyone with the link can take part, and anonymous, so without signing in and without names.
Every answer is a record of the database. Each question is a property, a matrix one property per row. So you can filter and sort answers, export them as CSV and process them with automations.
Results shows:
– the answers per day,
– per question the count and share of every answer,
– averages, minimum and maximum,
– the NPS score with promoters, passives and detractors,
– matrix tables, the average places of rankings (options nobody has ranked yet show “–” and come last) and the latest text answers.
> Renaming a question keeps its answers. Changing the type so that the stored kind changes (e.g. from text to number) creates a new property – earlier answers stay in the old one.

en.heading: Customer portal
paragraphs: The customer portal turns a form into a service desk: whoever sends it can follow their request afterwards.
– Under Share form, switch on the customer portal.

– Choose which properties are visible in the portal – for example Status or a due date. A select property named “Status” is preselected when you switch it on. People, relations and files always stay internal.

After sending, the person sees a private link to their request. If they answered an e-mail question and e-mail is set up, the link also arrives by e-mail – in their language; with the confirmation e-mail switched on, it is part of that one e-mail. The page shows the status, their answers and a conversation with the team.

The team replies in the record under Customer request. Replies go to the person by e-mail; when they write back, the people on the record, everyone who already replied and whoever created the database get a notification. Copy customer link passes the link on when there is no e-mail address.
> The link is the key: anyone who has it sees the request and can reply. Switching off the customer portal or the form stops all links from working; switching it back on restores them.

en.heading: Processing form answers
paragraphs: The workflow trigger Form answer starts a workflow for every answer – for example with the template Form → AI category → assignment: the AI puts the answer into a category, the person responsible is set and notified.
Connect databases to GitHub, GitLab and Forgejo: branches, commits and pull requests on the record, issues synced both ways.

en.heading: Git connection
paragraphs: … → Git connection connects the database to GitHub, GitLab or Gitea/Forgejo:
– Set up Git connection creates a webhook address and a secret.
– In the repository, add a webhook with both:
– content type JSON,
– events for pushes and pull or merge requests. The exact steps are in the dialog.

– Commits and pull requests that mention a ticket number of this database like WEB-123 appear in the record under Development. Numbers of other databases are left alone – they have their own connection.
– “closes WEB-123” (also fixes, resolves) marks the record done. This happens once the commit is on the default branch or the pull request is merged – through the database's workflow and automations.
Every request is checked against the secret. Only people who may edit the database see the address and the secret. New address and secret invalidates the old ones.
Pull requests show their state as a badge: Open, Merged or Closed.

en.heading: Back-link on the pull request
paragraphs: Like Notion, Flowplan can link back to the record in the pull or merge request itself. In the dialog, under Back-link on the pull request → Add access token, enter the provider, the server (empty for github.com or gitlab.com, required for Gitea/Forgejo) and an access token:
– GitHub: fine-grained token with access to the repository and Pull requests: Read and write (or Issues: Read and write).
– GitLab: project or personal access token with the scope api (role at least Reporter).
– Gitea / Forgejo: token with write:issue (plus read:repository for private repositories).

When a pull/merge request names ticket numbers of this database, Flowplan writes one comment, e.g. Linked in Flowplan: WEB-123 Login form – one line per record, with a link to the record. Later events (edited title, merged, closed) update the same comment instead of writing new ones; if all numbers are gone, it says “No longer linked in Flowplan.”
– The comment shows the ticket number and title. For private records and databases behind a journal PIN, only the ticket number; nothing is written for databases in the trash or in encrypted spaces.

– The token is stored encrypted, never shown again and only sent to the server it was entered for. A webhook from another provider or server does not get it. Own servers are allowed by the administrators with ISSUE_SYNC_ALLOWED_HOSTS, as for the issue sync; internal addresses are blocked.

– The comment is written in the background – the webhook answers at once, even when the Git server is slow. Errors (e.g. 403 for a missing permission) show in the dialog under Last back-link failed. Flowplan writes at most 30 comments per minute and connection.
– Without a token nothing changes: Flowplan writes nothing to the repository. Remove token switches the back-link off.

en.heading: Sync GitHub, GitLab and Forgejo issues
paragraphs: A database can keep itself in step with the issues of a GitHub, GitLab or Forgejo/Gitea repository – both ways or only one. Unlike the Git connection, which only links commits and pull requests, records and issues are created and updated on both sides here.
Setting up the connection (workspace owners and administrators):
– Settings → Calendars & issues → Connect GitHub, GitLab or Forgejo.

– Choose the provider; for an own server enter its address (empty for github.com or gitlab.com), the repository (owner/name) or project (group/project) and an access token that may read and write issues – on GitHub a fine-grained token with Issues: Read and write, on GitLab a token with the api scope. For Forgejo / Gitea the server address is required (e.g. https://codeberg.org); create the token there under Settings → Applications → Generate token with write:issue and read:repository (read:organization optional, so organisation labels are found too).
– Test connection makes one call with the token; Save stores the token encrypted. It is never shown again.
– Optional People: one login = e-mail of a member per line. Assignees are matched through it.

– For immediate updates, add the shown webhook address with the secret in the repository – on GitHub with content type JSON and the events Issues and Issue comments, on GitLab as Secret token with Issues events and Comments, on Forgejo/Gitea under Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook → Forgejo (or Gitea) with POST, content type application/json, the secret and the custom events Issues and Issue comments. Without a webhook, Flowplan syncs every 10 minutes.

The sync acts as the person who set up the connection: they need edit rights on the database, and records they may not read are skipped. If they are no longer an owner of the workspace, the connection pauses until someone saves the token again.
Mapping a database: … → Sync issues in the database. There you choose the connection, repository and direction (both ways, only issues → database, only database → issues) and map properties:
Issue Property
Title Title
Description (Markdown) a text property or the record's document
Open/closed and labels a select – per option "open" or "closed", optionally with a label (e.g. Doing → open + in progress)
Labels a multi-select (only labels that exist as options)
Assignee a person (through the connection's people list)
Milestone due date a date (an existing milestone with that date is set)
Number and address number/text or URL – read-only

Two switches handle comments: issue comments appear as record comments (with name and link), and record comments go out as issue comments. Also take over existing issues fetches all existing issues on the first run; otherwise only what changes after saving. New records become issues once the mapping is saved – older records stay as they are.

Conflicts: if both the record and the issue changed since the last sync, the later change wins. The decision is written to the audit log. Each record is linked to at most one issue; the record then shows a chip like GitHub #123 with a link.

Status: the dialog shows the last pull and push, conflicts, skipped records and errors; Sync now starts a run right away. When the provider reports a rate limit, Flowplan waits for the time it gives. A repository can only be connected to one database. Disconnect ends the sync; records and issues stay.
Pull requests are not synced. Administrators allow own servers (GitHub Enterprise, self-hosted GitLab, your own Forgejo or Gitea) with ISSUE_SYNC_ALLOWED_HOSTS.
Keep Flowplan running when a server fails or is updated: active/passive with a standby server, or active/active in cluster mode – with a complete example at Hetzner.

en.heading: Two ways
paragraphs: Active/passive Active/active (cluster mode)
What runs two servers, Flowplan runs on only one at a time two or more instances at once behind a load balancer
A server fails you start Flowplan on the other one (minutes) the other instances keep working (seconds)
Updates a short interruption while it restarts no interruption, one instance after the other
Database SQLite with Litestream, or PostgreSQL PostgreSQL
Other services S3 (or a volume you can move) PostgreSQL, Redis and S3
More people no, one instance carries everyone yes, about 25–30 active people per instance (Sizing)

For most teams active/passive is the better start: little new to run, and an outage costs minutes instead of hours. The cluster pays off when updates should not interrupt at all, or when one instance is no longer enough.

en.heading: What both need
paragraphs: – Files on more than one server: an S3 bucket (Storage, S3 and backups). Required in a cluster, the simplest way for active/passive; otherwise a volume you can attach to the other server (for SQLite never a network share such as NFS).

– The same keys as variables on every server: FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (or FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY) as well as WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY and WEB_PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY. Without them each instance creates its own in its data folder, and two-factor sign-in, stored secrets and push subscriptions only match one server. How to create them or take them over from an existing data folder: Cluster mode.
– One address: a load balancer or a floating IP in front, the same APP_URL everywhere and FLOWPLAN_TRUSTED_PROXIES matching the number of proxies.
– The same version: the same image tag (FLOWPLAN_VERSION) on every server.

en.heading: Active/passive
paragraphs: Two servers with the same compose.yaml and the same .env. Flowplan runs on the active one; on the passive one the container is stopped. In front sits a load balancer that checks /api/health/ready and sends traffic only to the running server – then nothing about the address changes when you switch. With a floating IP instead of a load balancer, you move the IP to the other server when you switch.

> Without cluster mode only one instance may run at a time. Two instances run timed jobs twice (reminders, digests, backups, workflows), and live changes do not reach the other one. With SQLite and Litestream, two running instances spoil the copy in the bucket.

en.heading: With PostgreSQL
paragraphs: Both servers point DATABASE_URL at the same database and S3_* at the same bucket. If a second instance starts by mistake, Flowplan notices through a lock in the database: it still starts, logs a loud warning every ten minutes, and Administration → Monitoring shows on every instance, until only one runs: {since=0.10.0}

"A second Flowplan instance is running against the same database without cluster mode (instance, since time). Timed jobs such as reminders, digests, backups and workflows then run twice, and live changes do not reach the other instance. Switch cluster mode on for every instance (FLOWPLAN_CLUSTER=1 with Redis and S3) or stop one of the instances. During a rolling restart this is normal for a moment."
Switching over when the active server fails:
– Make sure the old server is really down: stop the container or power the server off in your provider's console. A server that is merely unreachable may otherwise keep running.
– On the passive server, docker compose up -d.
– Wait until /api/health/ready answers 200; the load balancer then sends traffic there by itself (with a floating IP: move the IP now).
– Check under Administration → Monitoring that no warning about a second instance shows.
Switching back works the same way. A stopped server may start again only once the other one is stopped.

en.heading: With SQLite and Litestream
paragraphs: The database is a file on the active server; Litestream copies every change into the bucket continuously (under /db/, every second), and the files are there too. The passive server has the same S3_* variables and keys and an empty data folder. The warning about a second instance does not apply here – each instance would have a file of its own.
– Stop the old server – two Litestream processes must never write into the same folder of the bucket at once.
– No old database may be on the passive server: Litestream restores only when flowplan.sqlite is missing. Empty a data folder from an earlier stint first (or take a new volume).
– docker compose up -d: Litestream fetches the database from the bucket, Flowplan the files on first access.
– Switch the address as above; afterwards empty the old server's data folder before it becomes the passive server.

At most the changes of the last second before the failure, which Litestream had not copied yet, are lost. The steps match way C of moving an instance. Without S3 a block volume works too, which you detach from the failed server and attach to the passive one (at Hetzner: Volumes, within one location only) – never a network share.
Switching automatically (e.g. with keepalived) only with a safe way to power off the old server: after a network glitch both run otherwise.

en.heading: Active/active: cluster mode
paragraphs: In cluster mode all instances run at once. They share live editing, presence, rate limits and the parallel AI answers through Redis, all data is in PostgreSQL, all files in the bucket; any instance answers imports and print views. No sticky sessions are needed. When an instance fails, the load balancer takes it out after the next health check, and another one takes over the timed jobs within seconds.

Two single points remain: PostgreSQL (see Failover and replicas and below) and Redis. When Redis fails, everyone keeps working; only live changes between instances arrive late. Set FLOWPLAN_READY_REQUIRE=database,objectStorage for that – otherwise every instance reports "not ready" and the load balancer has no target left.

en.heading: Updates without downtime
paragraphs: One instance after the other: stop it, start the new image, wait until it is ready, then the next one. On SIGTERM an instance answers 503 on /api/health/ready at once, finishes open requests and hands on live connections and the lead (stop_grace_period: 30s). The new version only extends the schema, so old instances keep working with it.

So that browsers do not mix versions, every image carries a deployment id (v-, fixed at build time). The app requests its files with ?dpl=, so caches on the way serve nothing stale, and when a page of the old version reaches a new instance, the browser reloads the whole page at the next navigation. Should an instance still lack a file of the other version, Flowplan's own build check heals the page. Building the image yourself, set the id with FLOWPLAN_DEPLOYMENT_ID (--build-arg FLOWPLAN_DEPLOYMENT_ID=…) – the same for every instance of one image – or switch it off with off. {since=0.10.0}

en.heading: Example: Hetzner Cloud
paragraphs: A cluster with two Flowplan servers behind the Hetzner Load Balancer, Redis and PostgreSQL in a private network, and files in Hetzner Object Storage. The files for it are in the repository under deploy/compose/hetzner. Names, plans and menus change – the Hetzner Console is what counts.
Internet ── HTTPS ──▶ Load Balancer (public IP, certificate)
│  private network 10.0.0.0/16
app-1 :3000             app-2 :3000      Flowplan (FLOWPLAN_CLUSTER=1)
redis :6379   postgres :5432        private network only
Object Storage (S3, over HTTPS)

en.heading: Servers and network
paragraphs: All servers in the same location (e.g. Falkenstein, fsn1), with Ubuntu 24.04 and your SSH key.
Server Size Note
app-1, app-2 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM each (the smallest type of that size, Arm or x86) each carries about 25–30 active people; more app servers for more people
