– A chapter likewise opens as an overview of its pages, with Start reading and New page.
– A page opens in the editor, as usual.

If a book or chapter has text of its own – written before, or taken over as the description when importing from BookStack – it shows read-only above the table of contents. Edit description opens it in the editor; without text the action is Add a description. Nothing is lost.

Links to a book or chapter (#page=…), search hits and the path above a page lead to the overview; a link with &edit=1 opens the book's text in the editor. Start reading, the arrows and Next go from page to page and skip the overviews; "Page 3 of 12" counts only the pages. Books and chapters that are not documents – a database, for example – still open as themselves. Spaces not shown as a library stay unchanged.
The window for new pages keeps its place while you type: it stays anchored at the top instead of moving with the centre when a hint such as "Similar entries already exist" appears or goes.

en.heading: All shelves at a glance
paragraphs: As soon as you see at least one space shown as a library, Library appears in the navigation below Home – on a phone under Navigation. It shows all shelves side by side in two groups:
– My shelves: your private spaces shown as a library.
– Shared shelves: the team's spaces and private spaces shared with you.

On wide screens the two groups stand side by side, on a phone one below the other. Each shelf shows its books as tiles with cover or icon, title and the number of pages and chapters, in a row you scroll sideways; after twelve books, All n books leads to the shelf. A click on the shelf's name opens its overview, All shelves leads back.
At the top, Continue reading lists the books you read last, with the page you were on and its place in the book ("Page 4 of 37"). A click opens exactly that page.
The sidebar stays as it was: libraries are collapsed with Open library below them. The command palette knows Open library too.

en.heading: Search all shelves
paragraphs: The library's search field searches all shelves at once and sorts the hits by level:
Group What is found A click opens
Shelves Names of the spaces the shelf's overview
Books Titles of the pages at the top of the space the book's table of contents
Chapters Titles of their sub-pages the chapter with the book navigation
Pages and content Titles further down, then text, records, comments and files of any page of a book – with a snippet, the search word marked the page (a record opens in its database)

Below each hit you see its way: shelf › book › chapter. For titles, whole and leading matches come first, then the order of the page tree; a title whose text matches as well appears once, with its snippet. Each group shows at most 50 hits.
– Collapse: a click on a group's name collapses and expands it.
– Keyboard: ↓ moves from the search field to the first group, ↑ and ↓ go through groups and hits, Home and End to the first and last, Esc back to the search field, a second Esc clears it.

– Query language: for the content, the same as in the search – #tag, in:"Space", OR, -word and so on; titles are compared with the words you type. Journal days and spaces that are not a library stay out.
You find only what you would find anyway: the library uses the search index and the same permission checks as the normal search.

en.heading: Permissions for shelves and books
paragraphs: The library has no permissions of its own. A shelf is a space, a book is a page – the workspace's permissions apply:
– Who sees a shelf is set by the space: Whole team or Only people with access, plus View or Edit per group under Settings → Groups & permissions → Access to spaces.

– Who sees a book is inherited from the shelf. Share on the book's page gives additional people or groups access; chapters and pages below inherit it. Someone who is given only one book of a private shelf sees the shelf with exactly that book.

– Who can see this shelf? is there for owners of the space and of the workspace – on the library's start and on the shelf's overview. It says who sees the shelf and leads to Visibility of the space … and – for workspace owners – to Access for groups ….

– Who can see this book? is in a book's table of contents – for owners of the shelf and for you if you created the book – and opens Share of the book's page: it lists who has access through the space, and you add people or groups.
For different audiences, create one shelf per audience (such as a private "Sales handbook" for the group Sales) and share single books only for exceptions.

en.heading: With SSO, SCIM or LDAP groups
paragraphs: Groups from the identity provider fill the workspace's groups – so who sees which shelf maintains itself:
– Settings → Groups & permissions → Groups: create a group such as "Sales".
– SSO groups: map the provider's group (e.g. sales) to that group – see Map SSO groups. SCIM groups and LDAP groups count the same way (SCIM and LDAP).
– Access to spaces: set the shelf to Only people with access and give the group View – or Edit for those who write the books.

Whoever joins the group at the provider sees the shelf at their next sign-in (with SCIM right away, with LDAP after the hourly sync); whoever leaves no longer sees it. Single books are shared with a group the same way through Share.

en.heading: API and MCP
paragraphs: – GET /api/library?workspace=… returns the shelves (personal, shared) with their books, continueReading and per shelf canManage – whether you may change its permissions.
– GET /api/library/search?workspace=…&q=… returns the hits by level (shelves, books, chapters, pages) with their way (path), snippet and total per group.
– GET /api/spaces/{spaceId}/library returns one shelf with every book's table of contents.
– Through MCP: get_library with workspaceId for all shelves or spaceId for one, search_library for the search by level.
Link pages, records and people with @, point at single blocks and see in the graph how everything connects.

en.heading: Page links and mentions
paragraphs: @ searches pages, database records and people – keep typing to narrow the list. The arrow keys move through the hits, Enter inserts the highlighted one. @ opens the list at the start of a line, after a space or after an opening bracket or quote; inside a word – such as an e-mail address like ada@example.org – @ is simply typed. Esc (or Enter without a hit) closes the list and types the @ and what you searched for into the text. Journal days come after the other pages. @today, @yesterday (also @heute, @gestern) or a date such as @2026-10-27 offer a link to that day of the journal under Journal. Records appear with their database, such as "Heating – maintenance · Notes"; only records you may read are offered. Mentioning a person notifies them in the inbox.

Links to pages and records stay valid even if they are renamed or moved. A link that shows the old title gets the new one on a rename – in all documents and records you may edit; a link with its own text keeps it. The target lists all links to it under Linked from – including records whose text contains the link. Records and pages you may not read do not appear there.

A link to a page or record shows the target's icon in front of its text: its emoji, symbol or own picture – without one, the sign of its kind (document, database, whiteboard, record). When someone changes the icon, every link follows, just as the title does on a rename. This also applies in reading mode, comments, published pages, the hover preview, the @ list, Linked from, Related pages and search. A link to a block keeps its paragraph mark unless the page has its own icon. For pages and records you may not read, the link shows only the general link sign. Printing includes the icons; Markdown exports contain only the link text.

Links to the web are underlined and carry a small outward arrow after their text. If you'd rather not see the arrow, switch off Settings → Appearance & language → Icon on external links – links then stay coloured and underlined, only the arrow is gone, in documents, records, comments and reading mode. The setting applies to your account on all devices. When you publish a page, the publication takes your setting; in the Share dialog's Web tab, Show ↗ arrow after links changes it per publication (Publish on the web). {since=0.9.7} The arrow is never printed; a printout shows the link's address after it instead.

en.heading: Automatic links
paragraphs: When an owner has set up automatic links, matching text becomes a link as soon as you type a space, a punctuation mark or Enter after it, and also when you paste it – in pages, in documents of database records and in comments. It is an ordinary link: it stays when you collaborate, work offline or use the apps, and you edit or remove it like any other. ⌘ Z (Ctrl Z) right after takes back only the link; the text stays. Text that is already there does not change; nothing is linked in code, existing links, formulas, titles or database table cells.

en.heading: Links to blocks
paragraphs: Every block can be linked: a paragraph, a heading, a list item, a table, an image, a diagram … The link is the page's address with the block, such as https://flowplan.example.org/#page=…&block=k3x9a2b1 (records add &row=…), and works anywhere in the same workspace.
Copying a link
– in the block menu (the ⠿ handle left of the block, tap it on a phone): Copy link to block,
– for headings via the link symbol that appears after the heading on hover,
– in the table of contents via the link symbol next to each heading (always visible on phones),
– with ⌘ ⇧ L (Windows/Linux: Ctrl Shift L) for the block the cursor is in.
The address is copied; pasted into other apps (mail, chat, Word) it shows as a link with the text "Page › start of the block".
Pasting a link

Paste a copied block link into a document or record of the same workspace (⌘ V): it becomes a link styled like a page link, with the text "Page › start of the block". If text is selected, that text becomes the link. @ also finds headings and blocks of other pages: @Project › Goals (or @Project#Goals) shows the headings of the page "Project" that contain "Goals"; a single search word also finds paragraphs with that text. Headings of the current page are listed as "This page › …".
When the linked page (or record) is renamed, the page title in the link text changes along; the part after "›" stays as it is. On hover, the preview shows the block's current text.
Opening a link

A click opens the page (for a record, the record in its dialog), scrolls to the block and briefly highlights it. A block in a collapsed section is expanded. If the block no longer exists, the page opens with the notice "This block no longer exists – the page is open."
Good to know

– A block keeps its link when it is edited, moved (also cut and pasted) or turned into another kind. Copies – Duplicate or copy and paste within the same document – get a link of their own. When Enter splits a block, the link stays with the first part.
– Preview and link text only show what you may read: for a page you cannot read, only "Linked block" appears, without text.
– In encrypted spaces block links work within the space as well; the server does not know the text there, so there is no text preview.
– People who may only read a page can copy links to its blocks, too.
– Align left no longer has a keyboard shortcut (⌘ ⇧ L now copies the block link); left is the default alignment and stays in the toolbar.

en.heading: Graph of links
paragraphs: The network icon at the bottom of the sidebar (or > graph in the quick search) shows all pages as dots and their links as lines. Database records appear as dots of their own once they link or are linked; a click opens the record. Large dots have many connections; colours tell documents, databases, records, whiteboards and journals apart.
– Drag to pan, scroll or use two fingers to zoom, click to open a page.
– Hovering highlights a page and its neighbours; Highlight marks pages by title.
– Connect sub-pages also shows the page hierarchy (dashed), Pages without links shows or hides single pages.

– Journal days controls the days of journals: hide, one dot per month (default; the dot gathers the links of all days of the month, a click opens the journal) or show each day. The line at the top counts pages and journal days separately.
– Links to pages and records (also from a record's text), embedded whiteboards, linked databases and synced blocks count as connections. The graph only shows what you may see.

en.heading: Unlinked mentions
paragraphs: Below Linked from at the end of a page, Unlinked mentions lists documents and records in which the title of this page appears without being linked (titles of four characters or more), or one of its aliases as a whole word (two characters or more); the alias found is shown in grey next to the hit. Link turns the first mention there into a link to this page, by the title first, else by an alias – the text stays as written. An open record shows the same for its title and aliases below its properties.
The editor understands Markdown: shortcuts as you type, whole pages edited as Markdown text, and answers from ChatGPT that arrive formatted when you paste them.

en.heading: Markdown shortcuts
paragraphs: While you type, the editor converts:
Type Result
#, ##, ### + space Heading 1–3
- or * + space Bulleted list
1. + space Numbered list
[] + space Task
> + space Toggle (or quote, see below)
" + space Quote (also with „ “ ”)
` Code block
--- Divider
bold, italic, ` code , ~~strike~~` Formatting in the text

> as a quote: if you are used to > for quotes from Markdown, switch Settings → Appearance & language → Editor → “>” creates to Quote. The setting applies to your account on all devices. It only affects typing: in imported Markdown files and in answers pasted from ChatGPT & co., > text becomes a quote as before, and the Markdown export still writes quotes as > text.

Code blocks carry their language in the fence: `python , `typescript , `terraform . The export writes the ids of VS Code/Shiki; the import also understands aliases and older names (js, ts, py, sh, yml, cpp, csharp, plaintext …) and stores them with the full id ( `js becomes JavaScript, exported again as `javascript ). Unknown languages are kept and show as "(imported)" in the block, without highlighting.

Line numbers, highlighted lines, the view and collapsing follow the language in the fence, in the usual notation: `ts {3-5} showLineNumbers startLine=10 , plus view=preview/view=split/view=code, collapsed and collapsedLines=15. The import also understands showLineNumbers{10} (rehype-pretty-code), showLineNumbers=10 and hl_lines="3 4"/linenums="10" (MkDocs). The numbers in {…} count from the block's first line, whatever its start number. `mermaid fences become code blocks that show the diagram.

en.heading: Edit as Markdown
paragraphs: Page menu … → Edit as Markdown shows the whole page as Markdown text with line numbers – handy for big rearrangements, find and replace, or if you prefer writing Markdown.
– Apply (⌘ Enter) saves a version first and replaces the content in one step; Undo takes the change back.

– Blocks without a Markdown form – embeds, whiteboards, linked databases, synced blocks, columns, tables with merged cells or widths, sized images, function graphs, metrics and bibliographies – appear as a marker ``. You can move or delete them but not change them; they come back unchanged. If one is deleted, Flowplan asks before applying.
– Formatting without a Markdown form (colours, superscript, spoilers, mentions, citations) is kept as HTML in the text.
– Alignment, indent, text direction and reactions are lost when applying; the view says beforehand what is affected.
– If someone changes the page while you write in Markdown, a notice appears; Apply anyway then overwrites their changes.
– People who may only read – also on locked pages and in reading mode – see View as Markdown without Apply.

en.heading: Pasting answers from ChatGPT
paragraphs: Text copied from ChatGPT or another assistant is formatted when pasted: LaTeX formulas (\[ … \], \( … \), $$ … $$) become formula blocks and inline formulas, Markdown (headings, bold, lists, tables) is applied, lines with tabs become a table, ☐ a task list, and each line becomes its own paragraph. Formulas already rendered on a copied web page stay formulas. This also applies when copying straight from the ChatGPT web page. If formulas are already in the document as text (such as \[ A(3;2;1) \]), select them – or everything with ⌘/Ctrl A – and choose Turn into formulas in the text menu. Ordinary text is pasted as before.

A readable copy outside Flowplan – for emergencies when the instance is down, or as an archive in a Git repository. Administration → Markdown & Git export chooses pages and databases; with every scheduled backup (and with Back up now) each becomes a Markdown ZIP with its sub-pages, comments and earlier versions:

– with S3 in the bucket under /exports/, otherwise in the data folder under exports/; as many are kept as backups (Backups kept). With FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY the ZIPs are encrypted (.zip.enc), the push to Git is not;
– the export reads with the permissions of the person who saved the selection – private records and journals with a PIN stay out;

– file names and paths in the ZIP contain ids, so they stay the same between runs (clean Git diff). Records start with YAML frontmatter, comments are in .comments.md, earlier versions under .versions/.

en.heading: Push into a Git repository
paragraphs: > The instance Git export (EXPORT_GIT_*) is deprecated. It keeps working but is replaced by the Git export of a space, which space owners set up themselves; the administration shows a notice about it. The scheduled Markdown export to S3 or the data folder stays as it is.
With these variables Flowplan pushes every export into a repository itself (Forgejo, Gitea, GitHub, GitLab) – every page in a folder of its own, one commit per run with changes:
Variable Meaning
EXPORT_GIT_URL https:// address of the repository, without credentials.
EXPORT_GIT_TOKEN Token with write access to that repository. Only in the environment, never in the database or a backup.
EXPORT_GIT_USERNAME User name for the token (default flowplan; GitLab: oauth2).
EXPORT_GIT_BRANCH Branch, default main. An empty repository gets it on the first run.
EXPORT_GIT_AUTHOR, EXPORT_GIT_EMAIL Author of the commits.
EXPORT_GIT_IMPORT true: changes made in the repository since the last run are taken over before exporting.
With EXPORT_GIT_IMPORT=true, changed files are handled like this:
– Records (records//…md) are updated by flowplan.id in the frontmatter; new files become new records.
– Document pages (index.md, pages/…-.md) get the file's text; the previous state stays as a version.

– Journal days (/2026/10/2026-10-27.md) are found by their journal (the folder) and the date; flowplan.id in the frontmatter only counts when it names a day of the same journal. Repositories from older versions, where days were still pages/-.md, keep working: changes to those files are still taken over before the export, then the export writes the days to the new paths and removes the old files. No day is created twice; a renamed journal keeps its days because the folder is matched by its id.
– Database tables, comments and versions are copies and are not read back.

Markdown does not know every Flowplan block (such as columns). Whiteboards are in the repository as SVG images; an embedded board carries an invisible marker (``) that makes it an embed again when changes are taken over from Git – please leave the image and link below it in place. If you edit pages with other such blocks in Git, the previous state is in the version history. The administration shows the state of the last push (commit, changes taken over, errors).

en.heading: Git export of a space
paragraphs: Instead of one repository for the whole instance, the owner of a space sets up a repository for that space themselves: Manage space → Git export (via … next to the space or Settings → Spaces). The administration only switches the feature on:
Variable Default Meaning
SPACE_GIT_EXPORT empty true turns on the Git export of spaces. Without it, space owners don't see it and exports already set up don't run.
SPACE_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS empty Git servers, comma-separated, e.g. git.example.org,codeberg.org. When set, only these are allowed; without it, any public https:// server.

SPACE_GIT_ALLOW_PRIVATE empty true also allows internal addresses for the servers listed in SPACE_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS – for example a Forgejo on the same host that the container reaches via --add-host git.example.org:host-gateway. Only works together with the list; every other server stays limited to public addresses.
In the space, the owner enters:
– the repository address (https://, without credentials), branch (default main), user name and an access token with write access (GitLab: user name oauth2);
– the frequency: daily or weekly, plus Run now;
– optionally comments and earlier versions (.comments.md, .versions/).
What happens:

– The repository gets the Markdown export of the space – every top-level page in a folder of its own (-/), plus index.md and README.txt. Other files in the repository (such as LICENSE or CI files) stay untouched.
– One commit per run, and only when something changed; pages no longer in the space are deleted in the same commit.
– Attachments above 10 MB go along, as in the Markdown export.
– The export reads with the owner's permissions: private records of others and journals with a PIN stay out.
– Export only: Flowplan does not take over changes made in the repository.
– The settings show the last run (commit, files changed, error) and when the next one is due. A failed run is retried after an hour.
Security:

– Flowplan stores the token only encrypted (like the other stored secrets, bound to the space). After saving, the interface only shows whether one is stored; it is not in exports, and in the instance backup only encrypted. A new repository address needs the token again.

– Every address is resolved and checked: internal addresses (localhost, private networks) cannot be reached, redirects are not followed. The only exception: servers the administration lists in SPACE_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS when SPACE_GIT_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true is set as well – for example a Git server on the same host. Even then it stays HTTPS, with the pinned address and no redirects.

– The export ends, and token and working copy (git-export/spaces// in the data folder) are deleted, when the owner turns it off, leaves the workspace, becomes a guest or deletes their account – or when the space gets a new owner or moves to the trash.
Administration → Markdown & Git export shows how many spaces use the Git export and their last errors – without addresses or content.

In the Flowplan Marketplace (marketplace.flowplan.org) people share what they built in Flowplan: document and database templates, workflows, whiteboard templates, appearances and rules for automatic links. Browse it and take templates over into your instance with one click – or publish your own. The templates that come with Flowplan are there too (public domain, CC0).
Browsing and taking over need no marketplace account. To publish, you sign in there with GitHub or an e-mail link. Every submission is reviewed before it becomes public.

en.heading: What you can share
paragraphs: Kind Where in Flowplan Who may publish What taking it over creates
Document and database templates Template gallery → Your templates whoever created the template, owners a template in the gallery (for the workspace, a space or only you)
Workflows Head of the workflow page (Marketplace icon) whoever may edit the workflow a new workflow page – paused, as a draft
Whiteboard templates Whiteboard → Templates → Own templates whoever created the template, owners an own whiteboard template of the workspace
Appearance Settings → Appearance owners replaces the workspace's appearance (with its typefaces)
Automatic links Settings → Automatic links owners the rules are added to the existing ones
Guests never publish anything.

en.heading: Publishing
paragraphs: – Choose Publish to the marketplace … on the template, the workflow or in the settings.

– In the dialog, check the title in German (optional) and English {since=0.9.6}, the summary (German and English), category, tags and language, and add up to four preview pictures (PNG, JPEG or WebP, 1 MB each at most). For documents and databases a screenshot pays off – Flowplan doesn't create one itself.

– Open in the marketplace: Flowplan builds the file, opens the marketplace's submit page in a new window and hands it over there. You sign in, choose the licence (default CC BY 4.0, also CC0 and MIT), confirm that you hold the rights to the content and submit.
– Or Download as a file: upload the .flowplan-template file on the submit page yourself.

The marketplace shows visitors the title in their language – switch between DE and EN at the top right. That is why every template needs an English title; Flowplan fills the field of your interface language with the page title, and you add the other one. With the next Flowplan version the English title becomes required; until then the marketplace still accepts packages from older versions without one and shows the German title. {since=0.9.6}

What is never included: a workflow's credentials, runs and webhook addresses, the address of your instance, names of people, pictures uploaded to a whiteboard (only pictures with an https address go along) and record cards. A workflow's references to pages and databases are matched by name on import or stay empty. For appearances with own typefaces: only publish typefaces whose licence allows passing them on.

All templates also leave what concerns people here: mentions of people become the plain text “@Person”, so tasks in documents lose who they are assigned to (the due date stays), comments and their highlights are not included, and neither are the ids and e-mail addresses of members – not even in the text. Database templates also leave out who created or changed a record, values of person properties and page properties of the type person. People a workflow names (recipients, approvers) go along without their names and are chosen again on import or stay empty. Links to pages are kept. The dialog says how many details that is. {since=0.10.2}

en.heading: Flashcard decks
paragraphs: In the marketplace a flashcard deck is a database template – saved with Save as template and then published like any other. It takes along: properties, views (the study views too), the card mapping with the card types and the records with their pictures, clozes and image occlusion masks. Never the learning state: reviews and FSRS values belong to the people who studied. The dialog says so under Learning progress and reviews are never included.

For the template's page Flowplan adds a few sample cards – one per card type, at most five, as plain text, for image occlusion with the picture and its masks. The marketplace shows them under Sample cards with front and back side by side, along with the number of cards and records and the card types. A picture appears there only if it is uploaded to the template as PNG, JPEG or WebP; the built-in decks show their masks without the picture.
When you take a deck over, the preview names it with its cards. A template is created; a deck made from it starts with new cards – for you and everybody else in the workspace.

Older Flowplan versions from 0.10.0 take such decks over too, just without the card preview; even older ones refuse the template with “Template content is invalid.” because they don't know the study view.

en.heading: Taking over
paragraphs: – On a template's page in the marketplace, choose Open in Flowplan. Without a saved instance it says Open in app.flowplan.org – for the hosted Flowplan one click is enough. For your own instance, choose Use your own instance … and enter its address once (e.g. https://flowplan.example.org); from then on the button says Open in flowplan.example.org, and Change instance brings the field back. The address stays in your browser only.
– Flowplan opens in a new window and receives the template. If you're not signed in, sign in first – the template waits in your browser meanwhile (up to 24 hours).

– A preview shows the title, kind, author, licence and what will be created. For workflows you see every node, the external services it talks to, whether it uses AI steps or sends e-mail – and what you need to set in the editor after the import.
– Choose the workspace and space (for workflows also the parent page) and Take over.

When you come to the marketplace from Flowplan – via More templates in the marketplace in the template gallery, Open the marketplace under Settings → Import & export, or when publishing – the marketplace remembers your instance by itself and briefly shows Instance saved: · change once. You don't have to type the address at all.
Workflows always arrive paused, as a draft. Check them, fill in what's missing and activate them yourself.
Take over a downloaded .flowplan-template file under Settings → Import & export → Template from the marketplace, or in the template gallery with Import template.
Flowplan checks every file again itself: size (25 MB at most), the file's structure, paths, compression and the content of each kind – just like an import from another instance.

en.heading: Checking an import
paragraphs: Before a submission goes public, the marketplace team checks it in flowplan-admin in two ways: a security scan looks for risky content in the package – such as executable files, scripts in documents or attachments, credentials, personal data or workflow steps that call internal addresses –, and an import test runs the import in a test workspace of its own on a Flowplan instance. A package with a blocking finding is only published when the team gives an explicit reason.
You can run the import test yourself too: POST /api/marketplace/check tells whether a package would import on your instance.
– Flowplan reads the package exactly like the import: size (25 MB at most), ZIP safety, template.json, the kind's format.

– Then a dry run in the workspace: the kind's import runs inside a database transaction that is always rolled back – the template and a page made from it with its properties, views, records and attachments, the whiteboard template, the appearance with its typefaces, the link rules. That also catches errors that only show when things are created (duplicate ids in a database, storage). Workflows are read, matched against the workspace and validated, but not created.
Nothing stays behind: no page, no file, no log entry, no webhooks or notifications.
curl -X POST https://flowplan.example.com/api/marketplace/check \
-H "Authorization: Bearer fp_…" \
-F file=@template.flowplan-template -F workspaceId=<workspace ID>

– workspaceId (optional): the workspace of the dry run – you must be a member (not a guest); templates need edit rights, the appearance and link rules owner rights. Without it Flowplan uses a workspace you own, otherwise one you can edit.
– dryRun=0: only read, no dry run.

– The answer is 200, also when the package would not import, with ok: true false, kind, creates (what would be created: templates, pages, fields, views, records, files, nodes, items, fonts, rules, theme), errors and warnings (each code, de, en, maybe at) and dryRun (ran, rolledBack, ms).
– Limits: 25 MB per package, 30 checks in 10 minutes per person. When the marketplace is switched off, the endpoint answers 404.
– API tokens need the permission Marketplace check (see API and webhooks).

For flowplan-admin: create a test workspace in an account of its own, a Read only token with Marketplace check there, and set the address, the token and the workspace ID as MARKETPLACE_IMPORT_CHECK_URL, MARKETPLACE_IMPORT_CHECK_TOKEN and MARKETPLACE_IMPORT_CHECK_WORKSPACE in flowplan-admin.

en.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: – Your instance never connects to the marketplace. The hand-over runs in your browser between the two windows; Flowplan only sends to the configured marketplace address and only accepts something from there.

– The marketplace's server doesn't learn your instance's address. Flowplan adds it to its marketplace links only after the #, a part browsers never send to a server; the marketplace keeps it in your browser and removes it from the address bar right away. It only counts anonymously how often a template was downloaded or opened in Flowplan – without IP addresses and without cookies for visitors.
– When you publish, only the file you saw in the dialog goes to the marketplace.

en.heading: Switching it off
paragraphs: > Administrators switch the marketplace off for the whole instance under Administration → Extensions & domains → Marketplace. Flowplan then shows no marketplace buttons and accepts no templates.
The environment works too: FLOWPLAN_MARKETPLACE_URL=off switches the marketplace off, another address (e.g. a marketplace of your own) replaces https://marketplace.flowplan.org.
LaTeX formulas, Mermaid diagrams and code blocks with highlighting, calculating right in the text and figures from databases.

en.heading: Formulas, diagrams and code
paragraphs: – Formulas in LaTeX: as a block with /math, inside the text with /inlinemath. The preview appears while you type. Building blocks such as fraction, root, superscript, subscript, vector, cross product, ±, π and sum sit above the input.

– Mermaid diagrams: a click or Enter opens the source and preview. Up to 20,000 characters and 500 edges. In dark mode Mermaid diagrams are drawn dark, and redrawn when you switch; downloads (SVG/PNG) and printouts stay light.

– draw.io diagrams (/drawio): open the draw.io editor in a large window; Save applies the diagram as one step you can undo. A double-click, Enter or the pencil on the block opens it again. Flowplan stores the drawing and a picture of it: when viewing – on shared pages, in presentations and offline too – it doesn't load draw.io at all and only shows the picture (cleaned, without scripts and without content from elsewhere). Drawing and picture may each be up to 800 kB.

– Maximize: the arrows button at the top right of the window (next to the close button) enlarges draw.io to the whole browser window; the same button (Restore size) brings the window back. It works from the keyboard too. The diagram stays open and unsaved changes are not lost; Esc and Close ask before discarding changes as before. The device remembers the choice: the next diagram opens the way you left the last one. On a phone draw.io fills the screen anyway (keeping clear of the notch and the home indicator), so there is no button there.

– A page for one diagram: the Diagram page template (under Templates, category Knowledge & documentation) creates a full-width page with one empty draw.io diagram and opens draw.io right away. On a full-width page the saved picture uses the whole width, and an empty diagram is a large area rather than a thin strip. There is no separate page type for this as there is for whiteboards – the diagram page is a document, so you can add text, more diagrams or other blocks.

– Where draw.io runs: by default Flowplan uses embed.diagrams.net. While you draw, the diagram's content goes to that service; the window says so. With DRAWIO_URL the instance points to its own draw.io (for example the jgraph/drawio container), and everything stays with you (see Configuration).
– Look: under Settings → Appearance → Editor: draw.io theme Automatic (follows Flowplan), Light or Dark, and draw.io interface Default, Minimal or Sketch. The choice applies to this device.

– Export: in the ZIP export every diagram becomes a .drawio.svg file that draw.io can open again; in a single Markdown file and in the Git export it is a `drawio block with the drawing, which the import turns back into a diagram (the picture is made the next time it is saved). PDF and EPUB show the picture.

– Code blocks: the language is shown in the block's header with its full name ("JavaScript", "C++", "Angular TypeScript", "Plain text"). A click opens a list with a search – it finds names, aliases and file extensions (ts, py, yml, tf, .rs …). The languages you chose last come first (remembered in this browser). There are more than 240 languages with the same grammars as in VS Code – among them Svelte, Vue, Astro, JSX/TSX, Terraform, TOML, Typst, Zig, Prisma, GDScript, Nushell, systemd units, SSH config, Git commit messages, log files, CSV/TSV and .env files. Line wrap and Copy are at hand. Tab indents by two spaces.

– Language detection: when you paste code into a block without a language (plain text), Flowplan suggests a language if it is clearly recognisable – "Looks like Python – set?". One click sets it, the × dismisses the suggestion. Flowplan never changes the language by itself.

– Preview: code blocks in HTML, SVG (language XML with ``), Markdown, Mermaid, LaTeX and Typst show the switch Code / Preview / Split in their header. Split puts code and preview side by side, on a phone one below the other. The view is stored in the block; people who only read a page (read access, published pages, presentations) see the preview unless the block says otherwise, and can switch for themselves without changing anything. Errors (such as a typo in the diagram or in Typst, with the line number) show in place of the preview.
– HTML runs in a sealed frame: no scripts, no forms, no access to Flowplan or the network. Pictures from the web stay blank; embedded pictures (data:) and styles work. The height follows the content.
– SVG, Mermaid and Typst show as a picture – without scripts or links.
– Markdown is converted as on import, LaTeX shows formulas with KaTeX (separated by blank lines, with or without $$ … $$; not whole LaTeX documents with \documentclass).
– Typst loads the first time it is used (a few MB, from your own server, not from the web); Typst packages (@preview/…) and files are not available.
– New Mermaid code blocks ( `mermaid or the language Mermaid chosen) show the diagram right away, empty ones code and diagram side by side. The separate Mermaid block (/mermaid) stays.

– Line numbers: the … menu in a code block's header turns Line numbers on or off for that block, sets the First line number (say 10 for an excerpt) and highlights lines – e.g. 3-5, 8, counted as shown. The numbers cannot be selected and are not copied; with line wrap they stand at the first row of a wrapped line. Blocks without a setting of their own follow Settings → Appearance & language → Editor → Show line numbers by default (on this device).

– Collapse: code blocks with more than 25 lines appear collapsed – 10 lines high, scrolling inside, faded at the bottom. Show all N lines expands them, Collapse folds them again (both reachable by keyboard). People who may edit store the state in the block; readers only expand for themselves. The … menu sets Collapsed and the Collapsed height (5, 10, 15, 20 or 30 lines). Printing and every export always show the whole code.

– A language's highlighting loads with the first code block of that language; until then the code shows briefly without colours. Very long code blocks (more than 50,000 characters) stay without highlighting.
– Fractions: /Fraction (or /Bruch) inserts a formula inside the sentence.

en.heading: Calculating in text
paragraphs: Flowplan only calculates when you want it to – exactly, with fractions, in German or English notation (2,5 or 2.5, ×, ², √, €):
– Hint after "=": type a calculation followed by =, such as 12 × 2,400 € = or 3/4 + 1/6 =, and the result appears greyed out behind it. Tab accepts it, Esc or typing on dismisses it.
– Selected text: select a calculation, a term or an equation; the text menu (also on right-click) shows what is possible under Calculate and inserts the result after it with one click:
– Result and Reduce as an exact fraction, plus As a decimal – 12/18 = 2/3
– Expand, including the binomial formulas – (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

– Factor – x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3), 4x² − 12x + 9 = (2x − 3)², 6x² + 9x = 3x(2x + 3), also with several variables: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²), x² + 2xy + y² − 1 = (x + y − 1)(x + y + 1), by grouping ax + ay + bx + by = (x + y)(a + b); Factor with roots splits further into real factors: x² − 2 = (x − √2)(x + √2)
– Simplify algebraic fractions – (x² − 1)/(x − 1) = x + 1, 1/x + 1/(x + 1) = (2x + 1)/(x(x + 1))

– Solve for x – linear and quadratic equations exactly (x² + 2x − 4 = 0 ⇒ x = −1 ± √5), higher degrees exactly where possible (x³ = 2 ⇒ x = ∛2, x⁴ − 5x² + 6 = 0 ⇒ x = ±√2, ±√3), otherwise as rounded decimals (x³ + x − 1 = 0 ⇒ x ≈ 0.682328); with several variables, for each one that appears linearly. Equations with x in a denominator are solved with the common denominator; values that would make a denominator 0 are excluded and named (x/(x − 1) = 1/(x − 1) ⇒ no solution (x = 1 excluded)).

– Copy result: the button at the end of each result row copies the result as shown (such as y² − 16y + 64) to the clipboard as plain text – for pasting into other apps. Clicking the row itself still inserts it after the selection.

– Function graph: select a term in x, such as x² − 2 or f(x) = 2x + 1, and choose Draw graph in the text menu – a graph with axes, grid and marked zeros appears below. /Function graph inserts one too. The functions are edited below the graph: it changes while you type, + Function adds up to six functions in their own colours (sin(x), cos, tan, exp, ln, abs, √ and π work). Dragging moves the view, +/− or ⌘/Ctrl + scrolling zoom, ⟲ resets the view. On published pages the graph can be moved and zoomed but not changed.

– Vectors: write vectors as (1 2 3), (1; 2; 3) or (1, 2, 3). Flowplan calculates sums and multiples (2 · (1; −2) − (3; 1) = (−1; −5)), the dot product with · including the angle ((1, 0) · (0, 1) = 0 ⇒ ∠ = 90°), the cross product with × ((1 0 0) × (0 1 0) = (0 0 1)) and the magnitude with … ( (1, 1) = √2). A vector selected on its own shows its magnitude and unit vector ((3, 4) ⇒ v⁰ = (3/5, 4/5)). Draw vectors in the text menu shows vectors in the plane as arrows in a coordinate system – for (1, 2) + (3, 1) both vectors and their sum. More vectors such as (3, 2) can be entered in the graph next to functions. Vectors in space such as (1, 2, 3) – cross products too – are drawn in a 3D coordinate system with x, y and z axes, a floor grid and dashed guides to the floor; dragging turns the view, and the view is saved with the page. The formula editor has the building blocks Vector (column vector), Vector arrow and Cross product; column vectors in formulas are calculated the same way.
– In formulas: the formula editor shows the same options under Calculate and appends the result in LaTeX, such as \frac{3}{4} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{11}{12}.

en.heading: Dashboards and metrics
paragraphs: /Metric inserts a card with a number from a database, /Dashboard three side by side. With the gear you choose:
– the database (every database in the workspace you can read),
– optionally a view – then only the records its filters show count, such as “Open tickets”,
– the calculation: number of records, sum, average, minimum or maximum of a number, formula or rollup property,
– a label.

The server calculates the number for the person looking at the page and refreshes it every minute; private records only count for people allowed to see them. On published pages, visitors without access see a dash. Add charts by inserting a linked database below the metrics and choosing a chart view there – that makes a dashboard from several databases.
Connect Claude, ChatGPT and other AI assistants to your Flowplan using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). They search, read and write with exactly your permissions, nothing more.
Looking for these docs in your assistant instead? See Flowplan docs in your AI.
Besides the optional built-in AI, MCP connects the assistant you choose. It works with your pages, databases and tasks. It sees only what you can see in Flowplan.

en.heading: Set up
paragraphs: – Under Settings → API & AI assistants, create a personal API token for the assistant. Choose Read only if the assistant should only search and read. Choose Read and write if it should also create pages and records.
– Copy the address shown under AI assistants (MCP). It is your Flowplan address followed by /api/mcp, for example https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp.
– Enter both in your client (examples below). The settings page has a ready-made configuration for each client and fills in a token you have just created.
Use a separate token for each assistant. That way you can see when each one was last used, and you can revoke one without affecting the others.

en.heading: Claude Code
paragraphs: claude mcp add --transport http flowplan https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp \
--header "Authorization: Bearer fp_…"
With --scope user the connection is available in all your projects. In Claude Code, /mcp shows the connection and its tools.

en.heading: Claude Desktop
paragraphs: Claude Desktop connects to remote MCP servers that use a token through the small mcp-remote bridge, which needs Node.js. Open Settings → Developer → Edit config, add the following to claude_desktop_config.json, and restart Claude:
"mcpServers": {
"flowplan": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp", "--header", "Authorization:${FLOWPLAN_AUTH}"],
"env": { "FLOWPLAN_AUTH": "Bearer fp_…" }
The token goes in env, not in args: that way it does not appear in the process list.

en.heading: ChatGPT
paragraphs: In ChatGPT, custom MCP connectors are available in developer mode, depending on your plan and workspace settings. Under Settings → Apps & Connectors, create a new connector with the address https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp. If ChatGPT offers token or API key authentication, enter fp_… there.

If your ChatGPT version only offers OAuth or "No authentication", ChatGPT cannot connect to Flowplan yet. Flowplan currently signs in only with personal tokens (see What is supported). Never put the token into the address as a workaround: addresses end up in logs.

en.heading: Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf and others
paragraphs: Clients that speak Streamable HTTP and accept their own headers use this configuration (the exact file depends on the client, e.g. .cursor/mcp.json or .vscode/mcp.json):
"mcpServers": {
"flowplan": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp",
"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer fp_…" }

en.heading: Tools
paragraphs: Tool What it does Token
list_workspaces Your workspaces with your role and the spaces you can see Read
list_pages Pages in a workspace, optionally in one space or below one page Read

get_library A space as a library: books, chapters and pages you can read, with their counts {since=0.10.0}; with workspaceId instead of spaceId all shelves of the workspace, your own and the shared ones, and "continue reading" {since=0.10.2} Read
search_library Searches all shelves of the library and groups the hits by level: shelves, books, chapters, pages and content with a snippet {since=0.10.2} Read
search Full-text search across pages, records, comments and file contents; also understands #tag, OR, NOT, created_by:, created:, type:, in:, title: Read
list_collections A workspace's collections (your own and shared ones) with their query Read
run_collection The pages and records that match a collection now, with your permissions Read
read_page A page as Markdown; databases with their records, whiteboards with their racks, devices, ports and cables Read
query_database Records with properties by name, property definitions, views; text filter, a saved view, paging Read
get_record One record with all properties and its record document Read
my_tasks Your tasks from documents and records, with due dates Read

optimize_flashcard_parameters Fits the FSRS parameters of a flashcard deck (or a part of it) to your ratings and recommends a retention with the workload per retention; stores nothing {since=0.10.2} Read
create_page New document, database or whiteboard; documents can start with Markdown content Write
append_to_page Appends Markdown to the end of a document Write
update_page Changes a document's title and emoji, replaces its text or one section, or appends to it {since=0.9.8} Write
move_page Moves a page below another page or record, to the top of a space or next to a page {since=0.9.8} Write
trash_page Moves a page and the pages below it to the trash {since=0.9.8} Write
set_task Checks or unchecks a task, sets its state, due date and assignee {since=0.9.8} Write
create_record New record; properties by name, optionally with its record document (document, Markdown) Write
update_record Changes individual properties and/or the record document of a record Write
trash_record Moves a record to the trash {since=0.9.8} Write
save_collection Creates a collection or changes its name, query, emoji and sharing Write
delete_collection Moves a collection to the trash Write
set_flashcard_parameters Stores your FSRS parameters for a deck, a part of it or all decks, or resets them {since=0.10.2} Write

Properties are named by their name (or ID). Dates are written as YYYY-MM-DD, options by their name, people by e-mail address or name, and relations as a list of record IDs. Text properties (except the title) are formatted text: get_database marks them with markdown: true, and they are read and written as inline Markdown (bold, _italic_, ~~strikethrough~~, ` code , label, \n; see Formatted text). update_record accepts the version from get_record`: if someone changed the record in the meantime, the change is refused instead of being overwritten.

Write the record document with document as Markdown – when creating with create_record, later with update_record. update_record replaces the document; with documentMode: "append" the text is added at the end. The previous state is kept as a version, and open editors see the change right away.

en.heading: Change pages
paragraphs: update_page replaces a document's text with Markdown (mode: "replace", the default), adds it at the end ("append"), or replaces one section: section names a heading, and the heading with everything below it up to the next heading of the same or a higher level is replaced. If the Markdown starts with a heading, it takes the old heading's place; otherwise the heading stays. If the heading doesn't exist or appears more than once, the assistant gets the list of headings (pick a duplicate with occurrence). Before every replacement Flowplan keeps the text as a version, and open editors see the change right away.

read_page also returns the document's revision. Pass it to update_page: if the page changed in the meantime – also through someone typing in the editor – the change is refused, and the assistant reads the page again instead of overwriting newer text. update_page only changes documents; locked pages and pages in encrypted spaces are refused.

move_page follows the same rules as moving in the sidebar: editor rights at both ends, and never below the page itself or one of its sub-pages. trash_page and trash_record only move to the trash – you restore from there under Trash → Restore, and the answer says how long the trash keeps it. Permanent deletion is not available over MCP.

set_task changes one task without replacing the text: check or uncheck it, set its state, its due date or its assignee (by e-mail address or name; the person is notified). read_page, get_record and my_tasks name each task by index and key; with both, set_task refuses if the task changed in the meantime. The task's text alone works too, as long as it is unique.
In addition, each page is available as a resource flowplan://page/ (your favourites are listed). There are two prompts: Summarize a page and Plan my day.

en.heading: Workflows
paragraphs: For workflows there are list_workflows, get_workflow, get_workflow_catalog, list_workflow_runs, get_workflow_run (reading) and, with a write token, save_workflow_draft (graph JSON into the draft, also as a new workflow page – with the check), test_workflow (always a dry run {since=0.10.0}) and run_workflow (only workflows with a manual trigger). Activating and deciding approvals are not available over MCP – those are a person's decisions about rights. So an assistant builds drafts, and you check and activate them in Flowplan.

Over MCP, test_workflow only runs as a dry run without outside connections: no e-mail, no chat message and no HTTP request – not even one the node allows in dry runs. You start a real test run yourself in Flowplan. So an assistant misled by text it read cannot send data out by testing a draft it wrote itself. {since=0.10.0}

en.heading: Permissions
paragraphs: – Every call acts as the person who owns the token, with exactly their rights. The same checks apply as in the browser: workspace membership and guest access, private spaces, page and group permissions, private records, and journals locked with a PIN.
– Read tokens only offer read tools. A write call with a read token is refused.

– Write tools run the same actions as the interface. That means automatic versions, mentions and task notifications, followers, the activity log and webhooks all work as usual. Locked pages stay locked.
– Tokens never have administrator rights and cannot create or revoke tokens.
– The public demo has no MCP access: demo accounts cannot create tokens, and browser sessions are not accepted by /api/mcp.

en.heading: Security notes
paragraphs: – Treat the token like a password. Anyone who has it can read (and with a write token change) everything you can. Revoke a token under Settings → API & AI assistants if you no longer need it or it might have leaked; the connection stops immediately.

– AI assistants can be misled by content they read (prompt injection), for example by text on a page shared with you. Give an assistant a read token if it does not need to write. With a write token, use the client's confirmation prompts for tool calls.

– Other people's content is marked as data {since=0.10.0}: what members, guests, forms, e-mails or clipped web pages wrote comes back with the note that it is data, not instructions – JSON answers (from search, query_database, get_record, my_tasks, get_meeting_note, get_workflow_run, for example) carry a contentNote field, Markdown (read_page, resources) sits between a random boundary the content cannot close. The server's instructions to the client say the same: what the tools return does not decide which tools it calls or whom it contacts.

– No remote images {since=0.10.0}: Markdown written through MCP (create_page, update_page, append_to_page, record documents) keeps only images stored as files on this instance. An image with an outside address is left out and only its alt text stays – otherwise an image address could carry data out when the page is opened. Links stay as they are.
– Answers can contain anything you can read in Flowplan. That content goes to the provider of your assistant, so check its privacy terms first.
– /api/mcp accepts only tokens, not the sign-in cookie, so another website cannot use your browser session. Requests from a foreign Origin are refused.
– Limits: 120 requests per minute per person, 2 MB per request, and answers are cut after 200,000 characters. Write tools have the same size limits as the interface.

en.heading: What is supported
paragraphs: – Transport: Streamable HTTP (POST /api/mcp, JSON answers, no session). Protocol versions 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05.
– Sign-in: personal API tokens as Authorization: Bearer fp_…. OAuth sign-in (for clients that only support OAuth) is not available yet.
– Pages can be updated, moved and moved to the trash, records moved to the trash. {since=0.9.8}
– Not included: deleting content permanently, administration, files and uploads, whiteboard contents.

en.heading: Examples
paragraphs: – "Search Flowplan for the offer for Müller and summarize the open points."
– "Read the page Team meeting and add a section Decisions with today's results."
– "Show my overdue tasks and make a plan for today."
– "Create a record in the Bugs database: title Login on iPad hangs, status Open, assigned to anna@example.com."
Images, files, PDFs and embeds in documents – upload, annotate, delete again – and voice notes that Flowplan can transcribe.

en.heading: Images, files and embeds
paragraphs: – Pasting from the clipboard (⌘ V) or dragging in uploads images and files. Images can be resized at their edges.

– Image toolbar: point at an image (on a phone: tap it) and a small bar appears at its top right: Comment, Caption, Replace image (place, width, caption and alignment stay), Download, Full screen and … with alignment (left, centre, right), Mark up image, Copy image, Copy link to block and Delete.

– Photos are scaled down before uploading: at most 2560 px on the longer side, stored as WebP. The camera rotation is kept, metadata such as the location is removed. GIFs, SVGs and files that would hardly get smaller stay unchanged. Attachments in file properties and forms are stored as they are.

– PDFs appear as a card with a preview of the first page. A click opens the PDF viewer with all pages, zoom and Download. Two fingers zoom smoothly around the spot between them and move the pages – as in notebooks, also while just reading; on a trackpad use the pinch gesture or Ctrl + scroll. The buttons and ⌘ +/− change the zoom in steps of 25 %. Esc closes the viewer. The same applies to PDFs in the media library, in files properties of databases and on published pages. In editable text, ⌘-click a link to a PDF to open the viewer. In the viewer you can write on the PDF – see Annotate PDFs.

– Mark up images: double-click an image (or the pen in the toolbar while the image is selected, or … → Mark up image in the image toolbar) to open it for editing – with pen, highlighter, arrow, rectangle, circle and text, seven colours and three line widths, undo with ⌘ Z. Save creates a new image with the markings; the original and the markings stay with the image, so you can change or remove them later.
– Media in the sidebar collects all uploads of the workspace for reuse.

en.heading: Deleting media
paragraphs: In Media, select files with their checkbox and put them in the trash with Move to trash (or the trash icon on the file). There is no confirmation because it can be undone. Anyone who may edit the file's page may delete it; viewers and guests can't.

– Not used: files that no page, record, whiteboard or comment of the workspace contains any more carry this badge. The Not used filter shows only them, and Delete all unused moves them to the trash together after a confirmation. Older versions in the version history don't count as a use and may still show such files.
– Removing an image from a document doesn't delete the file – it then just counts as not used.
– Old cover images of a page that are no longer used can also be removed right in Change cover, see Page actions. {since=0.10.2}

– While a file is in the trash it can't be opened anywhere, including through shares and publications. Pages that still show it have a File missing placeholder in its place. Restoring brings it back unchanged.

– It is deleted for good – including in the uploads folder and in object storage such as S3 – only when the trash is emptied, with Delete permanently, or when the retention period ends, see Trash. Until then it counts towards storage.
– Embed (/embed) takes an address: YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Spotify, Figma and CodePen appear as players with an adjustable width, other sites as a link card with title and preview image.
– Links to pages and mentions of people show a preview on hover.
– The administrators set the maximum file size (10 MB by default).

en.heading: Annotate PDFs
paragraphs: If you may edit the page a PDF belongs to, the PDF viewer shows Annotate (not in encrypted spaces and on locked pages). A toolbar appears below it: Pen (with the Apple Pencil or another tablet pen, the line width follows the pressure), Highlighter (translucent, stays under the text and the ink), Eraser (Whole strokes or Partial – then only what is under the eraser goes), Lasso, Text and Laser pointer (points at something without staying). Plus colours, three widths, undo and redo (⌘ Z, ⇧ ⌘ Z).
– Favourite pens: the three pens next to the tools remember colour and width; change them while one is chosen and the favourite changes with it. They apply on this device.

– Shapes: hold the pen still for a moment at the end of a stroke – a drawn line becomes straight, a rectangle, circle, triangle or diamond becomes the clean shape. Switch this off in the Pen settings (gear).
– Lasso: draw around strokes and text to move them, resize them with the handle at the bottom right, recolour, copy (⌘ C, paste with ⌘ V – also on another page), duplicate or delete them.
– Text is placed with a tap on the page; a tap on existing text changes it. On the iPad, Scribble writes into it with the pen.

– Draw with the pen only: once you have written with the pen on a device, only the pen writes – fingers scroll and zoom, a resting hand leaves no marks. PDFs, whiteboards and images share the setting; switch it off in the Pen settings, then a finger writes too, and two fingers scroll and zoom.

– Apple Pencil: the eraser end of a pen erases. In the iPad app, double-tap or squeeze switches to the eraser and back – as set in the iPad settings, or in the Pen settings always to the eraser, the last tool or nothing.

The annotations belong to the page of the PDF, not to the screen: they stay in place at any zoom and apply to everyone who opens the PDF – readers see them but cannot change them. The PDF itself stays unchanged. Done (or ⌘ S) saves; every save is a version you can load again from the clock icon. If someone else saved the annotations in the meantime, your version wins and a notice says who; theirs is kept as a version. Search finds text you write on a PDF – in the app for iPhone and iPad also the handwriting itself, and Convert to text turns selected handwriting into typed text (see Recognising handwriting).
To turn a PDF into a notebook you write in page by page and add sheets to, open it as a notebook: every PDF page becomes a sheet.

Download still downloads the original. Download with annotations (next to it once there are annotations) creates a new PDF with the same pages and the annotations on top as vector graphics – they stay sharp when zooming in. Protected (encrypted) PDFs can only be downloaded without annotations; text appears in Helvetica, characters outside the Western European character set as “?”.

en.heading: PDF in the side panel
paragraphs: A PDF can stay open beside the page while you write: right-click (long-press on a touch screen) a PDF card in a document, a PDF in Media or a link to a PDF, then Open in side panel. Media and files among the search results also have their own icon for it. The PDF docks to the right of the page; the document or notebook on the left narrows and stays fully usable. Page and zoom stay where they are while you keep writing on the left; drag the panel's left edge to change its width, the device remembers it. On a phone the PDF comes up as a sheet from the bottom that you swipe down to close. Esc or × closes it, another PDF replaces it.

If you may edit the PDF's page, you write on it right away: these are the same annotations as in the PDF viewer – they belong to the PDF, everyone with access sees them, and they are saved as you write (every save is a version). Readers see them without changing them; encrypted spaces and locked pages have no annotating. Annotate switches the pen off and on.

Taking a region: with Region you draw around part of a page (or drag across it for a rectangle). Insert puts it as a picture into the document or notebook you worked in last; you can also drag the region there. The picture is drawn sharply from the PDF page and uploaded like any image. Below it, “Name.pdf, p. 3” opens the PDF in the side panel at exactly that page.

en.heading: 3D and CAD files
paragraphs: Flowplan shows STL, OBJ, glTF/GLB, 3MF, STEP/STP and IGES/IGS files in the 3D viewer instead of only offering them as downloads. Upload such a file to a document and a card with a cube icon and Open in 3D viewer appears; a click opens the viewer. The same goes for 3D files in Media (filter 3D/CAD), in files properties of databases, in links to such files and on published pages. In editable text, a link opens the viewer with ⌘-click.

– Turn, pan, zoom: dragging with the mouse turns the model, the right mouse button (or Ctrl/⌘ while dragging) pans it, the wheel zooms at the pointer. On touch devices one finger turns, two fingers zoom and pan. With the keyboard focus on the 3D view, the arrow keys pan; +/− zoom, 0 goes to the home view, Esc closes the viewer.

– Views: Front, Top, Side and Iso show the whole model from the front, from above, from the right and at an angle from above (isometric). STL, 3MF, STEP and IGES have Z pointing up (as in CAD programs), glTF and OBJ Y. The house icon (Home view) returns to the isometric view, Fit to view shows the whole model from the current direction.
– Dimensions: the bottom bar shows the edges of the bounding box (width × depth × height) and the number of triangles.

– Measure: after Measure, click (or tap) two points on the surface; a line connects them, a label gives the distance, and the list at the bottom collects all measurements. Dragging still turns the model. The trash icon clears all measurements, the × next to one removes only that one.
– Wireframe shows the model's triangles instead of its surfaces.
– Units: the CAD reader converts STEP and IGES to millimetres, glTF/GLB is in metres, 3MF names its own unit. STL and OBJ store no unit – Flowplan assumes millimetres and says so.

– Size: the viewer opens meshes (STL, OBJ, glTF/GLB, 3MF) up to 200 MB and STEP/IGES up to 100 MB; larger files can still be downloaded. What you may upload depends on the maximum file size set by the administration. glTF files must be self-contained (best as GLB); models compressed with Draco or KTX2 are not shown.

– Offline: for STEP and IGES, Flowplan loads the CAD reader (OpenCascade, about 7 MB) from its own server the first time – never from a third party. It is not part of the offline copy, so without a connection STEP and IGES files open only once the reader has been loaded. STL, OBJ, glTF and 3MF also work offline once the file is on the device.
The file is read in the browser, large ones in a separate thread so the page stays responsive; the original stays unchanged, and Download gets it.
2D drawings: DXF and DWG

Flowplan opens technical drawings in DXF and DWG format (AutoCAD and many other CAD programs) in the drawing viewer. The card in the document has a blueprint icon and Open in drawing viewer; otherwise everything works as for 3D files – also in Media (filter 3D/CAD), in files properties and on published pages.

– Pan and zoom: dragging (with the mouse or a finger) pans the drawing, the wheel or two fingers zoom. With the keyboard focus on the drawing, the arrow keys pan; +/− zoom, 0 fits the whole drawing, Esc closes.

– Layers: Layers opens the list of all layers with their colour and number of objects; a checkbox shows or hides a layer, All on and All off switch them all. Layers that are off or frozen in the drawing start hidden. Fit to view shows everything that is visible.

– Shown are lines, polylines (also with arcs), circles, arcs, ellipses, splines (approximated), texts and multiline texts (without fonts), blocks with their position, rotation, scale and arrays, dimensions (as the CAD program drew them), hatches (solid fills filled, patterns as a light area) and filled areas (SOLID). Colours come from the drawing (colour index, true colours, BYLAYER, BYBLOCK), and so do linetypes such as dashed. Objects drawn in white appear black on white paper. 3D solids, images and tables are not shown – the bottom bar says how many objects that affects; layouts (paper space) are left out, the viewer shows the model space.
– Paper: the moon icon switches to dark paper, the sun back to white.

– Measure: after Measure, click (or tap) two points. Each point snaps to the nearest end, vertex or centre close by, so measurements are exact; the list at the bottom gives the distance and the distances along X and Y.
– Unit and size: the drawing names its own unit (millimetres, inches, metres …); without one, the viewer measures in drawing units and says so. The bottom bar shows the size of the visible drawing.
– File size: DXF up to 100 MB, DWG up to 50 MB. Very large drawings are shown only in part, and the viewer says so. Binary DXF files are not read – save them as DXF in text format.

– DWG: for DWG, Flowplan loads a DWG reader (LibreDWG, about 11 MB) from its own server the first time; it is not part of the offline copy, so DWG files need a connection the first time. DXF also works offline. DWG files from AutoCAD R14 up to the current format (unchanged since AutoCAD 2018) are read, older ones from R11/R12 mostly too. If a file cannot be read, the viewer says so – then export the drawing as DXF from your CAD program and upload that file; the viewer reads DXF from any version.
