en.heading: HTML files
paragraphs: Open an uploaded HTML file (.html, .htm) with Open preview – in documents, Media, files properties and published pages. The preview is isolated: scripts and external content are switched off, and the page cannot reach your data; embedded pictures and its own styles are shown. Up to 5 MB (FLOWPLAN_HTML_PREVIEW_MB); otherwise download it – opened in a browser, this protection no longer applies.

en.heading: Voice notes and meetings
paragraphs: /voice opens the recorder: tap the microphone, speak, Stop recording – up to two hours, enough for a meeting. You can listen to the recording or discard it; Insert puts it into the page as audio (within the instance's upload limit). If speech recognition is set up, the spoken words follow below as text; otherwise the dialog only offers the audio.
– Long recordings go to the server in parts; it puts them together and sends them to speech recognition. WHISPER_MAX_MB limits the size (default 200).

– Transcript with timestamps: if speech recognition returns segments with times (OpenAI-compatible verbose_json, e.g. faster-whisper-server, speaches or whisper.cpp), a collapsible Transcript · duration block appears with one paragraph per passage and its timestamp (00:04, 1:02:05).

– Speakers: only when the service itself separates speakers (diarization, switched on with WHISPER_DIARIZE=on for servers that know diarize) and returns a speaker per segment, each passage starts with Speaker 1, Speaker 2 … Flowplan never guesses speakers from pauses. If the service only knows plain JSON, the text is inserted as paragraphs as before.
– Then summarise with AI summarises the transcript (Summaries).
– In the apps for iPhone, iPad and Android the app records; iPhone and iPad turn the words into text on the device, without speech recognition on the server (Voice notes in pages).

– Generate tasks and summary (when AI actions are on for you): the AI proposes a summary with decisions and a task list with assignees and dates – as a preview with checkboxes; only Run adds them to the page.
Type /meet in a document or a record's document. The block records a meeting, writes the transcript and then summarises it automatically.
Header

– Event ▾: a small menu at the calendar icon lists the day's events from your calendars – calendar databases (with a calendar view, including ones synced from Google or Microsoft 365) and calendar subscriptions – grouped by calendar, with the time first. Dated records of other databases (such as a sync log or tasks) appear only under Other entries of this day. An event fills in title, date and attendees.

– Title (default "New meeting"), the date as a date mention, attendees (+): the plus opens a search – type a name or e-mail address, pick with ↑ ↓ and Enter. Members become mentions; when nobody matches, the last row Add guest "…" adds the person by name.
– Full page enlarges the block. Settings (gear) opens a menu – a bottom sheet on phones:
– Continue recording (red dot), Re-generate summary, Transcribe again (while the audio is kept),

– the meeting's Language (for transcription and summary; Automatic = the interface language), Instructions (presets or Custom … with your own text), Consent (confirm before recording, notice text, play the notice – applies to the whole workspace), Upload recording …, One combined track (when the meeting's sound is recorded too),
– Copy link to meeting,
– Delete audio now … and Delete transcript … (red, asks first; the transcript comes back with ⌘ Z / Ctrl Z).
Menus and pickers float above the content; the block does not move. Escape closes them and returns the focus to their button.
Three tabs

– Summary: always in the same order – first the action items as "Owner: task": real tasks you can tick off, with a due date only when a date was said. The owner is whoever is explicitly named as responsible in the meeting or the notes – or whoever takes the task on themselves ("I'll take care of it", "I'll send the estimate"): that speaker becomes the owner. Otherwise the task has no owner; Flowplan never guesses. {since=0.9.6} When the owner is a member who can read the page, they are mentioned and the task appears in their My tasks. They are notified only once someone confirms it: below the summary the block then says "The AI summary gave tasks to …" with Notify assignees and Don’t notify – the AI chooses the owners from what was said and written, and that should not send notifications unasked. Anyone who may edit the page can confirm (not through an API token); each person is notified once, for their tasks still open then. When you write or change a task with @person yourself, they are notified right away as usual. {since=0.10.0} Then the decisions (with the reason below when one was given), the open questions (with their context) and finally the summary by topic.
– Notes (formerly "Agenda"): your own notes – before, during and after the meeting, editable at any time. The summary takes them into account.

– Transcript: every passage with time and speaker. It is locked, so reading, selecting and copying change nothing. Edit transcript (lock) unlocks it: corrected passages get a ✎, and Flowplan remembers that you corrected them. Unlocked, Find and replace works across the whole transcript (e.g. "Mayr" → "Maier"), with Add to the glossary so speech recognition spells the name right next time (owners only). Lines that speech recognition makes up in silence or noise ("Thanks for watching", "Untertitel im Auftrag des ZDF", "Sous-titres réalisés par …", a lone "Thank you.", the same line many times in a row) are marked no speech, hidden and left out of the summary – nothing is deleted: Show N hidden lines shows them.

Sources: every item of the summary ends with up to three sources – small timestamps like 08:17 that show where the passage starts in the transcript (1:02:05 from an hour on). Hover over one to see the passage; a click opens the transcript there and plays the recording from that point if it is kept. Exports, published pages and printouts show the same times. {since=0.9.6}
Recording

– Start recording, Pause, Resume, Stop (asks once "End the meeting?" – then it is transcribed and summarised). While recording, a small level meter per source (microphone, system sound) shows that sound arrives; when one source stays silent for more than 30 seconds while the other has sound (a muted or wrong microphone, a tab shared without audio), the block says so. Continue recording (in the menu) picks the meeting up later – the transcript continues. When a recording ended unexpectedly (window closed, connection lost), the block offers Continue.

Which sound is recorded depends on where you record: Desktop app: In the desktop app (Windows 10+, macOS 13+) the microphone and the system sound are recorded as two separate tracks: the microphone is you (your name), the system sound is everyone else ("Others"). With WHISPER_DIARIZE=on and a service that separates speakers, the others are told apart ("Others 1", "Others 2"). macOS asks once for "Screen & System Audio Recording"; without it Flowplan records the microphone only and says where to allow it. Browser: In the browser, Start recording records the microphone (everyone in the room on one track); in Chrome and Edge the block points this out first. In Chrome and Edge, Record all participants also records a tab's or the screen's sound: in the sharing dialog pick the video call's tab (or the screen) and tick the box to share the sound (for a tab, “Share tab audio”); Flowplan drops the picture at once. Firefox and Safari pass no sound there – use the desktop app (also for the sound of other programs). Mobile apps: The apps for iPhone, iPad and Android record the microphone only.
– Headphones work best. With loudspeakers the microphone hears the others too; Flowplan removes such duplicate passages from the microphone track (same time, nearly the same words).

– One combined track (menu): microphone and meeting sound are mixed into one track instead of two. Speakers are then only told apart by the Whisper service (WHISPER_DIARIZE=on); separate tracks stay the default.

– The recording goes to the server in 30-second pieces; when the connection drops, the pieces stay in the browser and are sent later. Up to 3 hours per meeting. The server transcribes the pieces while you record – after you stop, only the last piece and the summary are left, so the result is there much sooner. When that does not work (another format, the service briefly unavailable), the whole recording is transcribed at the end; the audio is never lost.
– Upload recording … (menu): M4A, MP3, WAV, AAC or WebM – one file with everyone, or two files (the microphone first, then the meeting's sound).

After the recording: the block goes quiet – no big button any more, just a line like "41:21 recorded · transcribed · summarised". When processing fails, the error shows there with Process again, which only processes what is missing – a track that was already transcribed is not sent again. Instance admins also see the exact cause below it (e.g. "no answer within 504 s", "ECONNREFUSED" or the Whisper service's answer). Transcribe again (menu, only while the audio is kept) sends the recording to speech recognition once more, e.g. after adding to the glossary or changing the Whisper service, and then writes the summary anew; the previous one stays in the page's version history. When passages were corrected, Flowplan asks whether to keep them (the default) or replace them.

Summary: written after you stop, in the meeting's language, by your instance's AI provider. It needs at least one minute of recording and reads the transcript and the notes – including notes you add after the meeting: Re-generate summary always uses the current state. Instructions: Automatic, Status meeting, 1:1, Workshop, Customer call, or your own. Re-generate summary uses other instructions without transcribing again. Ask this meeting answers only from this block's transcript and notes, with source chips.

In a database: when the block is in a record's document (e.g. a "Meetings" database), Flowplan fills existing properties after processing: date, attendees (person), duration (number, minutes) and status (an option such as "Done").
From the journal: the meeting note of a journal day's event ends with a meeting block holding the event's title, date and attendees.
Settings → Workspace → Meetings (owners):
– Instructions: the default for new blocks.

– Vocabulary → Glossary: names, acronyms and terms speech recognition should spell right – one per line or separated by commas. Flowplan passes them, together with the instance's WHISPER_PROMPT, to Whisper as a hint; Whisper reads only about 224 tokens of it (some 550 characters), the rest is cut after the last whole term.
– Keep audio: Delete after the transcript (default), Delete after some days or Keep. Kept audio counts against the storage.
– Consent required with your own notice text: before recording the notice appears with "Everyone being transcribed has agreed"; Play consent notice reads it aloud. Who confirmed is stored.

Who may do what: whoever can read the page sees the block – guests only on pages shared with them. Recording and processing need edit rights. Locked pages, journals behind a PIN (while locked) and end-to-end encrypted spaces: no recording (the server would hear the audio). Transcription needs WHISPER_URL, the summary your instance's AI; neither leaves your server or your configured provider.

en.heading: API and MCP
paragraphs: API tokens have a new permission "AI and transcription" (Settings → API & AI assistants, when creating a token; off by default). Only tokens with it reach the AI features (/api/ai/run, ask, write, summarize), transcription (/api/transcribe) and meetings. Administrators can switch the permission off for the whole instance (Administration → AI → "API tokens with 'AI and transcription'"). Requests count against the same AI limits as the interface.
curl -X POST https://flowplan.example/api/meetings \
-H "Authorization: Bearer fp_…" \
-F pageId=<page id> \          # or databaseId=<database id>
-F title="Kick-off" -F date=2026-11-11 \
-F attendees='["Ben","anna@example.org"]' \
-F instructions=status \
-F me=@microphone.webm -F others=@system.webm   # or -F audio=@everyone.m4a

Answer 202 { id, pageId, rowId, status: "transcribing", statusUrl }. GET /api/meetings/{id}?content=1 returns the status, the summary (Markdown), agenda (the block's Notes) and the transcript. Instead of audio you can send transcript as text (one passage per line, optionally Name: text). When the workspace requires consent, send consent=true. More: POST /api/meetings/{id}/summarize (summarise again), POST /api/meetings/{id}/retranscribe (transcribe the kept audio again; {"dryRun": true} only counts the corrected passages, {"force": true} replaces them too), POST /api/meetings/{id}/ask. In the transcript (content=1) passages carry hallucination (no speech) and edited (corrected); errorDetail is shown to instance admins only.
MCP: create_meeting_note (audio as base64 in audio or me + others, or transcript; target pageId or databaseId) and get_meeting_note – only with a write token that has "AI and transcription".
Environment: FLOWPLAN_AI_TOKENS=off switches the token permission off by default (until an administrator saves the AI settings).
Documents, databases and whiteboards come over from AFFiNE with their images and attachments – through the workspace export.

– In the AFFiNE desktop app, choose the export Full Backup (“Export a complete workspace backup”) in the workspace settings. This gives a file Name_….affine – the whole workspace database with documents, folders, collections, journal and files. The web app has no such file; there you export documents as a Snapshot (ZIP) – this needs Enable Snapshot Import Export switched on under the experimental features of the workspace settings. A snapshot contains documents, databases, whiteboards and files, but no folders, collections, journal dates, properties or icons. Only snapshots from AFFiNE versions up to the end of 2024 (with an info.json file) contain tags; newer versions no longer write tags into snapshots. To bring tags, properties and icons along, use the workspace file (.affine) – the preview points this out.

– In Flowplan: Settings → Import & Export → Import, choose the target space and pick the .affine file or the snapshot ZIP under AFFiNE, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs or Obsidian (source AFFiNE or automatic).

– The preview shows what comes along: pages, folders, files, tags, properties, page icons, whiteboards, databases, collections, days for the journal and how many documents become the content of database records – and what cannot be imported. Import creates everything in one step.
What it becomes:

– Where it goes: a workspace file (.affine) with several items at the top – folders, documents outside folders, collections – arrives below one page named after the AFFiNE workspace; the preview names it (“Everything below a page …”). A snapshot and a workspace with a single item at the top go straight into the target space – no empty page above them. A whiteboard counts with its document; journal documents go into the journal.

– Folders become pages with their documents below them. A document in several folders lives in the first one; the others link to it. Documents outside folders sit at the top level – below the workspace page, if there is one.

– Place documents with exactly one link below it (a switch in the preview, on by default; the preview shows how many): a document outside folders that exactly one other document links to in its text goes below that document instead of the top level. Chains nest (C below B below A). Documents in folders, journal days, the content of database records and documents linked only from a database, whiteboard or journal day stay where they are. When two documents link to each other, the first goes below the other. Links are unchanged; the switch doesn't apply when importing as a database.

– Text: headings, paragraphs, bulleted and numbered lists, to-dos with their check mark, toggle lists, quotes, code blocks with their language, callouts (kind by colour: red → caution, orange/yellow → warning, green → tip, purple → important, otherwise note; their emoji becomes the callout's symbol), dividers, tables, LaTeX (block and inline), bold, italic, underline, strike-through, code, links, text and highlight colours.

– Links between documents – in the text (@ references), as linked-doc or synced-doc cards and as AFFiNE app links – point to the imported pages. Synced documents become links. References to a block (references and doc cards with a block, app links with ?blockIds=) lead to that block; references to shapes on the canvas (elementIds) lead to the page.
– Tags become the page's tags, with their colours from AFFiNE (as a new database: the Tags property).

– Properties of a document (text, number, checkbox, date) become page properties of the same name; missing ones are created by the import if you may manage the workspace. Deleted properties and AFFiNE's own fields (created by, mode, template …) are left out.
– Icons: an emoji as the icon of a document, folder or collection becomes the page's icon. Icons from AFFiNE's own icon library have no counterpart; the preview gives their number.

– Images and attachments are uploaded and shown in their place – as when uploading in the editor: images as images, PDFs with a preview (they open in the viewer), audio and video with a player, other files as links. Bookmarks and embeds (YouTube, Figma, GitHub …) become links.

– Databases become a database page below their document and appear in the document at the same place as an embedded database. Columns: title, text, number, select, multi-select, date, checkbox, link (URL), progress (number in percent) and created. Rows keep their content as the record's document. Table views stay tables, kanban views become boards by the same column. Columns keep the order of the AFFiNE view (not the order they were created in); hidden columns stay hidden and column widths are kept (80 to 800 pixels). Image columns are not imported.

– Documents made from database rows: if you turned a row of a database into a document of its own in AFFiNE (the row's title is then a reference to the document), that document becomes the record's content – text, images, attachments, embedded databases and links, as for any page. It gets no page of its own; links to the document (in text, as cards, from collections and on whiteboards) lead to the record, and a folder that held the document lists a link to it. The record keeps the row's title and columns; if the title is nothing but the reference, it takes the document's title. This also applies when the row's only content is the card of a linked or synced document, and to snapshots that contain the document.

– If such a document consists of nothing but a database (in AFFiNE a database always lives in a document), the record shows that database as an embedded view, and the database itself sits below the record's database page – records have no subpages. Documents linked only from such records also go below the database instead of the top of the space, and databases that sit only on a document's whiteboard in AFFiNE become database pages below their document.

– Templates: documents marked as templates in AFFiNE become workspace templates (category Other, with emoji and tags) instead of pages; a document that is only a database becomes a database template. Links to a template become text. Only the workspace file (.affine) says whether a document is a template – from a snapshot, templates become ordinary pages. If you may not edit the workspace, the templates are saved as "Only me". The import preview shows how many there are.

– From the workspace file (.affine) the document's emoji icon (as the record's icon) comes along, its tags go into a multi-select column “Tags” (or “Schlagwörter”) of the database, and its properties into columns of the same name and a matching type where the row has no value – values in the row's own columns always stay as they are. If the database has no such column, the tags or properties are left out; the preview gives their number.

– If several rows refer to the same document, the first one (in the order of the import) gets the content; the others keep their own content and start with a link to that record. A journal document stays a day in the journal, and a row that refers to the document holding its own database only gets a link.

– The document's own databases are created where the document was (in its folder or at the top) and stay embedded in the record; a whiteboard of the document is placed there too, and its card points to the record.
– When importing as a new database, databases are left out; such documents then become records of the new database like all others.

– Whiteboards (edgeless): a document's text always becomes a document. If its edgeless canvas holds more than the note with the text – shapes, connectors, texts, images, frames, further notes, drawings, mind maps – or AFFiNE opens the document in edgeless mode, a whiteboard “Name – Whiteboard” is created next to it. Document and whiteboard are linked: the document starts with a link to the whiteboard, and a card on the whiteboard points to the document (where the note was). Shapes (rectangle, rounded, ellipse, diamond, triangle) with text and colours, connectors (straight, elbow, curved, with arrows and labels, attached to their shapes), texts, brush strokes, images, frames, further notes (as sticky notes), groups and mind maps (nodes as shapes, branches as connectors) come along. Whatever has no counterpart is left out; the preview gives the number.

– Collections each become a page “Collection: Name” with links to their documents as of the import: those added by hand and those the rules match (tags, created/updated, title, favourites, journal). The rules are written on the page as text. If not every rule can be evaluated (rules on custom properties, for example), only the documents added by hand are listed, with a note. A collection in a folder lives in that folder.

– Journal: AFFiNE's journal documents go into the workspace's journal, each into the matching day – the journal in the target space, else one in the workspace you may write in; if there is none, the import creates one. A missing day is created; an existing day gets the text appended at the end (under the AFFiNE document's title).
– Documents in AFFiNE's trash are not imported. HTML embeds and data views are left out; the preview names them.
– Whiteboards, databases and journal days only come along when importing as pages; as a new database every document becomes a record.

– Large workspaces: the .affine file may be larger than 100 MB (see the limits above). The server writes it straight to disk while it is uploaded, reads the documents one at a time while converting them, and images and attachments one at a time while writing them – memory only ever holds one document and one file. Workspaces with thousands of documents go in one import (up to FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_DOCS, 10,000 pages by default); folders nested deeper than 50 levels are merged into the level above. A reverse proxy in front must let such large requests through (see Coolify and reverse proxies).
– Safety: the file is only read; the size, number and nesting of documents are limited, text never comes in as HTML, and links keep only http, https and mailto.
What you know from Notion, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Evernote, Confluence, Google Docs or BookStack – and what it is called in Flowplan.

The introduction shows the same overview in the step What it's called here, after you picked a tool under Where are you coming from?. The same means the same idea under this name; similar: close, with the difference in the note; no counterpart: Flowplan has nothing comparable – the note says what to use instead. How to bring your content over is in Moving to Flowplan.

en.heading: What stays the same everywhere
paragraphs: – “/” on an empty line opens all blocks – as you are used to.
– “@” mentions pages, records, people and dates; “[[” links a page.
– Markdown shortcuts such as #, - and [] work while typing; “>” makes a toggle (or a quote, as you choose).

en.heading: Notion
paragraphs: How to move: Notion.
In Notion Flowplan Match Note
Workspace Workspace the same
Teamspace Space the same Spaces are for a team or private.
Page Page the same Pages nest as deep as you like.
Database Database the same Table, board, calendar, gallery, list, timeline, form, chart and feed as views.
Linked view of database Linked database the same

Relation / Rollup Relation / Rollup the same Relations between databases of the same import are connected. Rollups come from the export only as values (text); through the Notion API they become rollups where Flowplan knows the calculation.
Formula Formula the same The export brings only the results (as text); you set up the formula again. Through the Notion API, formulas that Flowplan can read come along.
Synced block Synced block the same
Toggle / toggle heading Toggle the same
Callout Callout the same
Database templates Templates the same Save a record as a template, with placeholders like {{Today}}.
Database automations Automations the same
Buttons Workflow button similar A button in the document starts a workflow.
Sub-items Subtasks the same
Inbox / Updates Inbox the same
Page history Versions the same
Publish / Sites Publish on the web similar Publish pages one by one, with or without sub-pages; no separate websites with navigation.
Notion Calendar / Mail – no counterpart No separate apps for this – databases have a calendar view and can be subscribed to as a calendar.

Frame (Edgeless) Frames the same Also for presentations.
Collections Collections similar Collections are saved searches in the sidebar; the import creates AFFiNE collections as pages with links.
Folders (Organize) Sub-pages similar Folders become pages with their documents below them.
Journals Journal the same
Database block Database the same
Doc properties Properties the same
Tags Tags the same
Linked doc Page link (@ or [[) the same
Templates Templates the same
Favorites Favourites the same

en.heading: Obsidian

In Obsidian Flowplan Match Note
Vault Space similar A vault becomes a page tree in a space; several vaults fit into one workspace.
Note Page the same
Folder Sub-pages similar A folder becomes a page with its notes as sub-pages.
[[Wikilinks]] Page link ([[ or @) the same Links follow renames.
Backlinks Linked from the same
Graph view Graph the same
Daily notes Journal the same
Canvas Whiteboard similar Canvas files are not imported; a whiteboard is a page of its own.
Callouts (> [!note]) Callout the same
Properties (frontmatter) Properties the same
#tags Tags the same

Community plugins Extensions similar Obsidian plugins do not run in Flowplan; extensions are in the marketplace.
Local files – no counterpart Flowplan stores on the server, not as Markdown files; export as Markdown at any time, offline on request.

Note Page the same

Reminders Reminder similar Reminders belong to dates and due dates.

Search in images and PDFs Search the same Full-text search also finds text in PDFs and images.
