Recycle bin Trash the same
Markdown folders such as an Obsidian vault become pages or databases, handwritten notebooks from GoodNotes become Flowplan notebooks.

en.heading: From Obsidian and other Markdown folders
paragraphs: – A vault as pages: make a ZIP of the vault folder (with its .obsidian folder) and import it under Settings → Import & export → Import – via AFFiNE, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, GoodNotes, Microsoft Word or Obsidian with a preview, or via the Notion/Markdown import, which recognises a vault as well.
– Folders become pages with their notes below. A folder note (Projects/Projects.md or Projects.md next to the folder) becomes the folder's page itself.

– Wikilinks [[Page]], [[Page text]], [[Folder/Page]] and [[Page#Heading]] become links to the imported pages – resolved like Obsidian does, by path or file name. Links to notes that do not exist stay text.
– [[Page#Heading]], [[Page#^id]], [[#Heading]] and Markdown links with #^id become links to that heading or block; the ^id markers at line ends leave the text and become the block's id.
– Embedded files ![[image.png]] become images, ![[file.pdf]] file links; embedded notes ![[Note]] become links.
– Callouts such as > [!note] or > [!warning] Title become callouts of the matching kind.

– Tasks keep their status: - [ ] open, - [/] in progress, - [x]/- [X] done, - [-] cancelled, - [>] deferred. Other symbols from Obsidian themes or the Tasks plugin ([?], [!], [*], ["], [<] …) are kept: the task counts as open, shows the symbol small in its box and is written back with the same symbol in the Markdown export and in Git. Digits such as [1] stay plain text.

– Tags from the frontmatter (tags:) and in the text (#tag, not in code) are collected: on pages as the page's tags, in a new database in the Tags property – together with Folder for where a note came from. Further frontmatter keys become properties on pages.
– Notes with frontmatter into an existing database: in a database choose Import CSV or Markdown and pick the .md files or a ZIP. The YAML properties become columns – see Frontmatter.

– Aliases: aliases: [PAC, Pompe à chaleur] (or alias:) in the frontmatter becomes the page's aliases or the record's Aliases property. @ mentions, search and unlinked mentions then also find "Chauffage" by "PAC", and the Markdown export writes them back as aliases:.

en.heading: From GoodNotes
paragraphs: Bring notebooks over from GoodNotes (5 and 6, on iPad, iPhone and Mac) as PDF. Every PDF becomes a notebook titled by its file name, every page a sheet with that page as its background – in the same size and orientation. You keep writing on it in Flowplan.

en.heading: Export from GoodNotes
paragraphs: One notebook:
– Open the notebook in GoodNotes.
– Tap Share or Export at the top (depending on the version, the icon with the arrow or in the ⋯ menu) and choose Export this notebook – not just the current page.
– Choose PDF as the format. If GoodNotes offers Include page templates, leave it on; otherwise ruling, grids and inserted PDF pages are missing from the background.
– Save the PDF to Files, AirDrop it to your Mac, or open Flowplan in the browser and import it right away.

Several notebooks: in GoodNotes' document overview, mark several notebooks with Select and export them together as PDF. Whether GoodNotes hands you single PDFs or a ZIP depends on the version – Flowplan takes both.

All notebooks at once: in GoodNotes' settings, turn on Auto-Backup, choose a cloud service (iCloud Drive, Google Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive) and set the format to PDF. GoodNotes then puts every notebook as a PDF into the backup folder, with your folders. Download that folder as a ZIP (Google Drive and Dropbox offer this in the browser; on a Mac, use Compress on the folder in Finder). The menus are named slightly differently depending on the GoodNotes version.

en.heading: Import into Flowplan
paragraphs: – Open Settings → Import & export → Import and choose the target space.
– Choose GoodNotes as the source (a PDF is also detected automatically).
– Click Choose and check file and pick the PDF – or several PDFs at once, or a ZIP of PDFs.
– The preview shows how many notebooks and sheets will be created and what is skipped. Import creates the notebooks and opens the first one.
Good to know:
– Several PDFs give several notebooks. Folders in the ZIP (such as the backup's folders) become parent pages; notebooks are listed in natural order ("Book 2" before "Book 10").

– Handwriting and highlights from GoodNotes are part of the PDF and stay sharp, but in Flowplan they belong to the background: you can write over them, but you cannot move or erase the old strokes one by one.

– Search: the PDF's text – typed text and, when GoodNotes exports it, the recognised handwriting – is indexed as for every PDF (the first 200 pages of each PDF). New handwriting in Flowplan is recognised on iPhone and iPad.

– Limits: up to 500 pages per PDF (the preview names further pages and leaves them out), 1000 sheets per notebook, a PDF or ZIP of up to 100 MB. Damaged or password-protected PDFs and other files in the ZIP are skipped and named in the preview.
– Notebooks are only created when importing as pages, not as a new database.

Flowplan cannot read the GoodNotes format (.goodnotes) and backups in that format: it is GoodNotes' own, undocumented format and changes between versions. Flowplan recognises such files and tells you what to do – export the notebook as PDF, or switch Auto-Backup to PDF. When a ZIP holds .goodnotes files next to PDFs, the PDFs are imported and the others are listed in the preview.
PDFs from other note apps such as Notability, Noteshelf or OneNote become notebooks the same way.

en.page: From Confluence, BookStack, Evernote, Google Docs and Word
paragraphs: Step by step from Confluence, BookStack, Evernote, Google Docs, Microsoft Word and OneNote to Flowplan – with the page tree, images and attachments.

en.page: From Confluence, BookStack, Evernote, Google Docs and Word
en.heading: From Confluence
paragraphs: – In Confluence: Space settings → Export (Confluence Cloud: Space settings → Export space). Choose HTML or XML, each with all pages.
– Import the ZIP in Flowplan as above (source Confluence or automatic).
What it turns into:
– The space's page tree becomes the page tree in Flowplan (from index.html or the parent pages in entities.xml; where a page is missing there, the breadcrumbs help).
– Info, tip, note and warning macros become callouts (info → note, tip → tip, note → warning, warning → caution), code macros code blocks, expand toggles, task lists tasks with their status.

– Images and attachments are uploaded; attachments the text does not show are listed as links at the end of the page. Links to other pages of the space point to the imported pages. Anchor links (Page.html#Page-Heading, #… on the same page, ac:anchor in the XML export) lead to the heading or anchor.
– In the XML export only the current version of each page counts; older versions and blog posts are skipped. Creation and modification dates are kept.
– Macros without a counterpart (such as table of contents or Jira queries) are dropped; the preview names them.

en.page: From Confluence, BookStack, Evernote, Google Docs and Word
en.heading: From BookStack
paragraphs: Flowplan brings pages over from BookStack once, through BookStack's REST API – without an export file, with shelves, books, chapters, images, attachments and tags. There is no ongoing sync: what you change in BookStack afterwards does not come over.
– In BookStack, your account's role needs the permission Access system API (Settings → Roles, among the system permissions). Exactly what your account may see is imported.

– In your profile (top right → My Account → Access & Security, in older versions Edit Profile), create a token under API Tokens with Create Token and copy the Token ID and Token Secret – BookStack shows the secret only once.

– In Flowplan: Settings → Import & export → Import, choose the target space at the top, BookStack (API) as the source, enter the BookStack address (such as https://wiki.example.org, also with a path like https://example.org/wiki), the Token ID and Token secret and choose Load shelves and books.
– What to import lists the shelves with their books and the Books without a shelf, all ticked. Untick what should stay behind – ticking or unticking a shelf takes its books along –, then Check.
– The preview counts shelves, books, chapters, pages, images, attachments and tags and names notes, such as books on several shelves. Import creates everything; then the first imported page opens.

> The token may do everything your account may do in BookStack. Enter it only into the Token ID and Token secret fields in Flowplan – nowhere else. Flowplan sends it only to the address you gave, uses it for this import only and neither stores nor logs it. If you no longer need it afterwards, delete it in BookStack.

en.page: From Confluence, BookStack, Evernote, Google Docs and Word
en.heading: What it becomes
paragraphs: – Each shelf becomes a top-level page with its books below it, in the shelf's order. A book on several shelves comes only once, below the first (shelves by name); the preview names these books. Books on no shelf become top-level pages.
– Chapters become sub-pages of their book, pages sub-pages of their chapter or book – in BookStack's order. The description of a shelf, book or chapter becomes the text of its page.

– Content: headings, lists, task lists, tables, code blocks with their language, quotes, collapsible blocks and callouts (info, success, warning, danger become note, tip, warning and caution) become their blocks. Pages from the Markdown editor come through their Markdown as long as it holds no HTML, otherwise through their HTML like the others.

– Images from BookStack (gallery and draw.io drawings, in original size) and file attachments are downloaded and stored as files of the page, each at most as large as the largest upload. Attachments linked in the text link to the file, the others are listed below the text; link attachments stay links, images from other addresses stay where they are. What cannot be downloaded is named as a note in the result and in the import report – the import carries on regardless.

– Links to pages (/books/…/page/…, /link/123), chapters, books and shelves of the import lead to the new pages, links to a paragraph (#bkmrk-…) to the same block. Links to anything not imported stay links to BookStack.
– Tags become tags of the page: name stays name, a tag with a value becomes name: value.
– Drafts, earlier revisions, comments, permissions and the recycle bin are not imported; templates come as ordinary pages.

en.page: From Confluence, BookStack, Evernote, Google Docs and Word
en.heading: Time and limits
paragraphs: Preview and import run in the background, one at a time per person; the preview does not download images and attachments yet. BookStack limits API requests per minute (180 by default) – when it answers "too many requests", Flowplan waits as long as asked (at most a minute per request). A few hundred pages therefore take a few minutes. The limits of every import apply (FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_DOCS, FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_FILES); shelves, books and chapters count as pages.

en.page: From Confluence, BookStack, Evernote, Google Docs and Word
en.heading: BookStack in your own network
paragraphs: For the import, Flowplan only calls public HTTPS addresses. If BookStack runs in your local network or a VPN (such as http://192.168.1.20), the administration has to set FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true (Configuration) – then internal addresses and http:// are allowed as well. Without the variable, Flowplan refuses such addresses with a note pointing to it.

en.page: From Confluence, BookStack, Evernote, Google Docs and Word
en.heading: From Evernote
paragraphs: – In Evernote, save a notebook via … → Export notebook as ENEX. Put several notebooks into one ZIP.
– Import the .enex file or the ZIP in Flowplan.
What it turns into:
– Every note becomes a page; with several notebooks, every notebook becomes a page with its notes below.
– The note text (ENML) becomes normal text with formatting, lists and tables; checkboxes become tasks.
– Images and attachments (embedded in the ENEX file) are uploaded and shown where they were in the text; PDFs and other files as links. Attachments without a place in the text go to the end.
– Tags, created/updated and the source address are kept – best import as a new database, then they are properties to filter and sort by.
– Encrypted text cannot be imported; the preview warns.

en.page: From Confluence, BookStack, Evernote, Google Docs and Word
en.heading: From Google Docs
paragraphs: – At takeout.google.com choose Drive and set the format for documents to HTML (recommended) or Microsoft Word. Single documents also work via File → Download → Web page (.html, zipped) or Microsoft Word (.docx).
– Import the Takeout ZIP, the web page ZIP or the .docx file in Flowplan (source Google Docs; single .docx files also work with Microsoft Word).
What it turns into:
– Every document becomes a page, Drive folders become parent pages.

– Headings, bold, italic, underline, strike-through, nested lists, tables and links come along; Google's redirect links point straight to their target again. Links to headings and bookmarks in the same document (#h.…, #kix.…) stay links to that place.
– Images are uploaded – including the ones embedded in the HTML.
– Word files: paragraphs, headings, lists (numbered and bulleted, also nested), tables (with merged columns), links and images. Comments, footnotes and headers/footers are dropped.

en.page: From Confluence, BookStack, Evernote, Google Docs and Word
en.heading: From Microsoft Word
paragraphs: Import Word documents (.docx) under Settings → Import & export → Import with the source Microsoft Word (a .docx file is also detected automatically):
– One document: choose the .docx file. It becomes a page titled by its file name.

– Several documents: put the .docx files into a ZIP and choose the ZIP. Every document becomes a page, folders in the ZIP become parent pages. When everything sits in a single folder, that folder is left out.

Paragraphs, headings, bold, italic, underline, strike-through, lists (numbered and bulleted, also nested), tables (with merged columns), links and images come along. Comments, footnotes, headers and footers are dropped. Word's lock files (~$….docx) are skipped.

Older Word files (.doc, Word 97–2003) cannot be read by Flowplan. Open the file in Word, LibreOffice or Pages and save it as .docx, then import it. When a ZIP holds .doc or OneNote files next to .docx files, the .docx files are imported and the others are listed in the preview with the reason.

en.page: From Confluence, BookStack, Evernote, Google Docs and Word
en.heading: OneNote
paragraphs: Flowplan does not read OneNote files (.one, .onetoc2, .onepkg) directly – it recognises them and tells you what to do. The way goes through OneNote's own export:
– In OneNote for Windows, open the page or section and choose File → Export, with Word Document (.docx) as the format.
– Import the .docx file (or several as a ZIP) in Flowplan with Microsoft Word.
If your version of OneNote offers no export as a Word document but only PDF, import the PDF as a notebook (as from GoodNotes) or upload it as a file to a page.
Flowplan is an open-source alternative to Notion, Confluence and AppFlowy under the AGPL-3.0. This is how you bring over pages, databases, images and files from the tool you use now.
More on this topic: Terms when moving · From AFFiNE · From Confluence, BookStack, Evernote, Google Docs and Word · From Obsidian and GoodNotes

en.heading: How to move
paragraphs: Three ways lead over:

– In the introduction: right after creating your account, the introduction asks Where are you coming from? – Notion, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Evernote, Confluence, Google Docs / Word, BookStack {since=0.10.0} or Start fresh. It shows step by step where the tool keeps its export, imports the file right into your first space and then explains under What it's called here what the things you know are called in Flowplan (Terms when moving).
– At any time under Settings → Import & export → Import, with target space, preview and every source – see below.

– Notion and BookStack without an export: straight through the Notion API with an integration token (Through the Notion API) or through the BookStack API with an API token (From BookStack). {since=0.10.0}
From What you need Guide
Notion ZIP export (HTML is best) or an integration token From Notion
AFFiNE the workspace's .affine file or a snapshot ZIP From AFFiNE
Obsidian the vault's folder as a ZIP From Obsidian
Evernote an .enex file or a ZIP with several From Evernote
Confluence the space export's ZIP From Confluence
Google Docs, Word Takeout ZIP, .docx or HTML file From Google Docs, From Word
BookStack the instance's address and an API token {since=0.10.0} From BookStack
AppFlowy Markdown and CSV as a ZIP From AppFlowy
GoodNotes the notebooks' export From GoodNotes
What an import could not carry over, or only approximately, is listed afterwards in the import report at the top of the target space.

en.heading: Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs and Obsidian
paragraphs: Under Settings → Import & export → Import choose the target space at the top and, at AFFiNE, Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs, GoodNotes, Microsoft Word or Obsidian, the source (or let it be detected) and whether you want a page tree or a new database. Then choose the file:

– Flowplan uploads the file (with a progress bar) and shows a preview: how many pages, folders, files (with their size) and tags will be imported, and what will not work – such as encrypted text, unsupported macros or images missing from the export.
– Import creates everything in one step. If something fails, nothing is left half imported.
For all sources:
– End-to-end encrypted spaces cannot be targets (the server sees no plaintext there).
– You need write access to the target space; the workspace's storage quota and your personal limit are checked first (the preview already warns).

– Limits per import: by default 10,000 pages (documents, folders, databases, whiteboards and collections each count as a page; as a database: 10,000 records) and 20,000 files, 5,000 records per table, per file in the ZIP as much as the largest upload, at least 10 MB (PDFs and ZIPs inside the ZIP, such as Notion's “Export-…-Part-1.zip”, up to 100 MB – all within the import's overall limits). The operator sets pages and files with FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_DOCS and FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_FILES (Configuration). When a file brings more pages, the preview shows how many, names the limit and the variable, and Import stays disabled; files above the limit are left out (the preview says how many). ZIP exports and single files may be up to 100 MB. The AFFiNE workspace file (.affine) may be as large as the largest upload (Administration → Limits & retention, can differ per person), but at least 100 MB; FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_MB sets the limit for the whole instance (Configuration). When a file is too large, the message names the limit and where to change it.

– Preview and import run in the background. After the upload the page shows the progress and then the preview or the result. A reverse proxy timeout (such as a 504) no longer cancels the import; keep the page open until it is done. Each person can run one import at a time. While Flowplan creates the pages, the server doesn't answer for a moment – with very large workspaces for longer.

– If there isn't enough memory for a very large workspace, Flowplan refuses the import with a message naming what it needs, instead of crashing. Give Flowplan more memory with NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size= (e.g. 4096) in the container, or export the workspace in several parts.
– The file is uploaded only once: the preview keeps it on the server and Import uses it. Cancelling deletes it; otherwise it is deleted after six hours at the latest.
– The content is cleaned like when pasting: scripts, forms and embedded foreign pages are dropped. File names are cleaned; files a browser could run (HTML, SVG) are only stored for download.
– Links between imported pages point to the new pages. Images and attachments are uploaded – every file once, even if several pages show it.

– As a new database, every note becomes a record with the properties Tags, Created, Updated, Folder (the folder path) and – where present – Source. As pages, tags become the page's tags; missing ones are created in the workspace.

en.heading: From Notion
paragraphs: – In Notion: Settings → Export (for the whole workspace) or Export in a page's … menu. Choose the format HTML (recommended) or Markdown & CSV and turn on Include subpages. Only the HTML export keeps toggles, toggle headings and colours.
– In Flowplan: Settings → Import & export → Import, choose the target space at the top and the ZIP at Notion, AppFlowy or Markdown export (ZIP).
– Done – the import runs in one step. If it fails, nothing is left half imported.
What it turns into:
– Every HTML or Markdown file becomes a page, every folder named like a page holds its sub-pages. The IDs Notion appends to file and folder names are dropped.

– From the HTML export: toggles become toggles, toggle headings become headings that fold (or, where their content does not reach the next heading, toggles with the heading as their title). Text and background colours, tasks, nested lists, tables, formulas and image captions are kept.
– Every CSV file becomes a database. When both versions are there, Flowplan takes Name_all.csv (all records) instead of the current view.

– Properties get their type. From the HTML export, Flowplan reads it from the tables' icons and the rows of the record pages: select and status, multi-select with Notion's colours, date with time and ranges, number with its format, checkbox, URL, e-mail, phone, person (when every name is a member of the workspace); created and last edited time become the record's timestamps. Without HTML, Flowplan recognises numbers, checkboxes, dates (also in Notion's format "September 24, 2026"), selects, multi-selects, links, e-mails and relations from the values; the rest stays text. {since=0.9.7}

– Relations point to the imported records – through the record pages' paths, Notion addresses or titles, also between databases of the same export. The export holds formulas and rollups only as values: they come as text and are listed in the import report. {since=0.9.7}
– Record pages are matched to their records as their document. Pages below a record in Notion (the folder named like the record) become its sub-pages – no loose pages and no stand-in pages any more.
– Images and files the pages refer to are uploaded.
– Callouts become callouts and keep their emoji as their symbol.

– Links to headings (Page.md#heading) lead to the heading; notion.so links to pages of the export lead to the imported page (Notion's Markdown has no block ids, so links to single paragraphs lead to the page).
– Large exports that Notion splits into several ZIP files inside the ZIP are recognised.
Limits per import: 100 MB, by default 10,000 pages (FLOWPLAN_IMPORT_MAX_DOCS) and 5,000 records per table. Export larger workspaces in parts, for instance page by page.

en.heading: Through the Notion API
paragraphs: Instead of an export file, Flowplan can also fetch pages and databases straight from Notion – with the token of an internal integration you create in Notion.
– In Notion, open notion.so/profile/integrations and create an internal integration for your workspace with New integration.
– Give it the capability Read content; with Read user information, Flowplan can match person properties to your workspace's members. Copy the secret under Configuration – it starts with ntn_.
– In Notion, share the pages and databases with the integration: on the page, … at the top right → Connections → choose the integration. Sub-pages are included.
– In Flowplan: Settings → Import & export → Import, choose the target space at the top, Notion (API) as the source, paste the token into the Integration token field and choose Load shared pages.

– What to import lists the top-level shared pages and databases, all ticked. Untick what should stay behind, then Import …. If the integration sees nothing, Flowplan tells you to share the pages via Connections first.

> The token reads everything shared with the integration. Paste it only into the Integration token field in Flowplan – nowhere else, not into chats, issues or e-mails either. Flowplan uses it for this import only and neither stores nor logs it. If you no longer need the integration afterwards, delete it in Notion.

The import runs in the background like a file import and fetches everything below the chosen pages: paragraphs, headings (toggle headings too), lists, to-dos, toggles, quotes, callouts, code, equations, dividers, tables, images and files, sub-pages and databases inside pages, synced blocks with the original's content, columns one after the other, page links and mentions as links to the imported pages, text styles and colours, emoji icons and covers. Bookmarks and embeds become links. Files Notion hosts itself are downloaded during the import (up to the limit for the largest file); files from elsewhere stay links. Databases keep their properties' types, options and colours; relations to databases imported along, rollups with calculations Flowplan knows, and formulas Flowplan can read become their counterparts, the rest text – listed in the import report. Notion allows at most three requests a second, so large workspaces take a while.

en.heading: From AppFlowy
paragraphs: – In AppFlowy, export pages as Markdown and databases as CSV.
– Put the files into one folder – sub-folders become sub-pages – and make a ZIP of it.
– Import it in Flowplan under Settings → Import & export → Import.
Markdown becomes pages, CSV becomes databases; linked images and files come along.

en.heading: Import report
paragraphs: What an import could not carry over, or only approximately, Flowplan collects on a page Import report: … with 📋 at the top of the target space, such as "Import report: Notion". It is grouped by kind, with the count: Blocks not carried over, Synced blocks (content copied), Embeds and bookmarks kept as links, Formulas and Rollups without counterpart (values as text), Properties with an approximated type, Relations that could not be resolved and Files too large, missing or not downloaded – each item with a link to the page or record concerned. Under Settings → Import & export the result names the count with a link to it ("12 notes in the import report"). With nothing to report, no page is created.

The report is written by the Notion import (export and API), the Markdown ZIP import and the imports from AFFiNE, Obsidian, Evernote and BookStack {since=0.10.0} – in the introduction too. It is an ordinary page: work through it and delete it when you are done.

en.heading: After the move
paragraphs: – Check links: links between imported pages point to the new pages; links to pages outside the export still point to the old tool.

– Links to blocks and headings are kept. If a link in the source points to a particular place of another (or the same) page, it points to the same block in Flowplan after the import: a click opens the page and jumps there (see Links to blocks). If the place cannot be found (for example because the export does not contain it), the link leads to the page.
– Set up views: an import creates one table per database. Add board, calendar, gallery or timeline afterwards – see Views.
– Sharing: permissions are not carried over. Invite members or share single pages – see Sharing and publishing.
– Your data stays portable: Flowplan exports again at any time as Markdown with frontmatter, CSV and ZIP, scheduled and pushed to Git if you like – see Import, export and versions.

en.heading: Why move?
paragraphs: – Completely open source: all of the source code is on GitHub under the AGPL-3.0 – with no closed enterprise edition and no features behind a licence.
– Your data, your server: hosted on flowplan.org in Germany or as one Docker container on your own server – see Installation.
– No tracking.

en.page: Apps for iPhone, iPad and Android
paragraphs: The apps for iPhone, iPad and Android: install and update them, connect them to your own instance, several instances as profiles.
iPhone and iPad:

The iPhone and iPad app is on the App Store: Flowplan on the App Store – open the link on the iPhone or iPad and download the app, or search the App Store for “Flowplan”. New versions arrive through the App Store as with any other app. Android:
The Android app comes straight from us, without the Play Store: flowplan.org/download/android.apk or on flowplan.org/download. See Installing and updating the Android app.

en.page: Apps for iPhone, iPad and Android
en.heading: Installing and updating the Android app
paragraphs: – On the Android device, open flowplan.org/download and tap Download the app.
– Open the downloaded file (the browser's notification or Downloads).
– The first time, Android asks whether the browser may install apps: Settings → Allow from this source, then go back and tap Install.
– If Google Play Protect warns about an unknown app: More details → Install anyway. The app is signed with our key, just not distributed through Google Play.

Updates: once a day the app checks for a new version and asks. Update downloads it in the app (cancellable), checks it and opens Android's installer – sign-in, profiles and settings stay; the file is deleted afterwards. The first time, Android asks whether Flowplan may install apps: Allow from this source, then go back. Later asks again after a week. If something fails, the app says why and offers Download in browser. New Flowplan features arrive through the server anyway.
Obtainium: add the GitHub releases of flowplan-app; each carries the signed Flowplan--android.apk.
You can also do without the Android app: Flowplan can be installed on Android as a web app as described above.
Requirements: iPhone and iPad with iOS/iPadOS 16.4 or later (the share sheet and the configurable widgets from iOS 17), Android 8.0 or later.
Like the desktop app, the mobile apps show your Flowplan instance; all data stays on the server and new features arrive without an app update. On top comes what only an app can do:

– Notifications: mentions, comments, tasks and reminders arrive as notifications, the number of unread ones shows on the app icon. The app asks for permission once after the first sign-in; a tap opens the page concerned. Which kinds arrive is set as in the browser under Settings → Notifications; there, Send test notification checks whether notifications reach all your devices and otherwise says why (more). Buttons tick off a task, postpone it to tomorrow, answer a comment or mark it read – without opening the app.

– Widgets for the home screen (on the iPhone also for the lock screen), each with settings of its own – tasks to check off, appointments, counters, time tracking and more; plus widgets for administrators.
– Live Activities: the timer, focus, the meeting, imports/exports and voice memos on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island, or as an ongoing notification.
– Capture, Siri, Control Center: notes, tasks, voice memos and photos from widgets, Siri, Control Center, the app icon and Android tiles; ask Siri what is due, open a page or search.
– Focus filters (iPhone, iPad): one profile or workspace per Focus, optionally without notifications from the others.
– Share from other apps: text, links, photos and PDFs from any app straight into the inbox, a database or onto a page.
– Scanner and Spotlight (iPhone, iPad): documents scanned into searchable PDFs, your pages and tasks in the phone's search.
– Voice notes in pages are recorded by the app; on the iPhone and iPad they become text on the device itself.
– On-device AI (iPhone, iPad, optional): writing assistant and summaries with Apple Intelligence without the text leaving the device; Apple's Writing Tools in the editor.
– Calendars in Apple Calendar with one configuration profile instead of typing CalDAV credentials.

– Staying signed in and app lock: the app stays signed in while you use it or its widgets (default: 90 days without use, see Stay signed in). If you like, Flowplan only unlocks with Face ID, Touch ID, a fingerprint or the device code – on iPhone, iPad and Android, again after more than a minute in the background.

– Swipe from the left edge (iPhone, iPad, Android): opens the sidebar over the current page instead of going back – the arrows at the top left go back. In Settings → Appearance & language → Swipe from the left edge you can choose Back per device: a swipe at the very edge then goes one step back as before, and a swipe a little further in opens the sidebar. On iPhone and iPad this needs an app version after 1.0.12. In the Android app {since=0.9.7}, with Open sidebar the app keeps a strip of the left edge (in the middle of its height) from the system's back gesture so the swipe reaches the page; with Back the edge stays the system's back gesture. This needs an Android app after 1.0.13; older Android apps are not offered the choice.

– Back: the back gesture or button (Android) – and on iPhone and iPad the swipe from the left edge if you chose Back – first closes what is open (menu, dialog, sidebar) and then goes up a level: from a settings section to the overview, from a record to its database, from a page to the previous page.
– Exports and downloads go to the system's share menu (e.g. "Save to Files").
– Without a connection: the app opens the profile's offline copy, on iPhone and iPad too – see Offline in the app for iPhone and iPad.

– iPad and tablets: every orientation, Split View, Slide Over and Stage Manager, several windows, a hardware keyboard with the shortcuts listed when you hold ⌘, the trackpad, and Handoff to the Mac – see iPad: windows, keyboard and Handoff. With the Apple Pencil you write in notebooks and drawing blocks, draw on whiteboards and write on PDFs (see Annotate PDFs) with pressure while fingers move the board and a resting hand leaves no marks; double-tap and squeeze switch the tool, Scribble writes into any text field (see Whiteboards). The app recognises your handwriting on the device: search finds it, and Convert to text turns selected strokes into text (see Recognising handwriting).

– iPhone Duo: open or close it while you work – the page stays as it is (no reload, the same place, the text you are typing) and lays itself out anew: the phone layout with the bottom bar on the closed display and on the open one held upright, the sidebar on the open display held sideways. Content stays clear of the status bar and camera at the side of the closed display. On the open display you can use several windows as on the iPad (see below); the closed display has one. Full screen on iPhone Duo needs an app built for iOS 27.1 or later.
Also:

– On first start they ask for the address and suggest https://app.flowplan.org. They only accept real Flowplan instances that do not redirect to another site. More instances are saved as profiles. Sign out and remove the profile in the app settings (via Settings → Notifications → Open app settings) signs the app out of the active profile's instance and removes it there.

– Managed devices (MDM/EMM): through managed app configuration (iOS Managed App Configuration or Android app restrictions), the key server presets the address of your own instance; the app suggests it on first start.

– Sign in with a passkey and Sign in with SSO open the system's sign-in sheet (iOS) or a browser tab (Android); after Sign in to the app the app takes over the sign-in. E-mail and password work directly in the app: With e-mail and password opens the form.

– Adding a passkey {since=0.10.2}: Settings → Account → Passkeys → Add a passkey opens the system's sign-in sheet (iOS) or a browser tab (Android) with a one-time link (valid five minutes). It stores the passkey (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager or your password manager) and returns to the app. Needs an app version after 1.0.17; older apps offer Add in the browser – inside the app, iOS and Android offer passkeys only for built-in addresses. Then sign in with Sign in with a passkey.

– Password manager not filling in? Tap With e-mail and password first, then Sign in in the browser below the form (or at the two-factor code). The sign-in opens in the same sheet as for passkeys and SSO; there your password manager recognises your instance's address and fills in the password and code. Inside the app itself, iOS only matches saved passwords to addresses built into the app – which isn't possible for self-hosted instances. This needs Flowplan 0.8.8 or newer; the app doesn't need an update.
– Signing in through the browser as well as notifications and widgets (the app interface) need Flowplan 0.4.0 or newer.
– Links to other sites open in the browser; without a connection the app shows a page of its own and reconnects by itself.
– Flowplan appears in other apps' Share menu – as Flowplan on iPhone and iPad, as Save to Flowplan on Android, see Share from other apps.
Instances on your own network without HTTPS and certificates of your own are under Apps: own network and certificates.

en.page: Apps for iPhone, iPad and Android
en.heading: Profiles in the mobile apps
paragraphs: The apps for iPhone, iPad and Android also keep several instances as profiles:
– Switch: tap a profile under Profiles in the app settings, or long-press the app icon → Switch profile (on the iPhone while signed out). The same list is a tap away from the offline page.

– Switch quickly: at the top of the sidebar, the workspace menu has Switch instance… {since=0.10.0}, or long-press your name at the bottom of the sidebar. The app then shows its profiles as a sheet from the bottom (a window in the middle on the iPad): name and address, the active one with a checkmark. Tap another profile to switch to it; below are Add profile… and Manage profiles (the app settings). The instance learns nothing about your other profiles. The app icon's Switch profile action and, on the iPad with a keyboard, ⇧⌘P open the same list. This needs an app version after 1.0.16; older apps open the profile screen from Switch instance….

– Before signing in: at the bottom of the sign-in and registration page (also for "Forgot password", the two-factor code and the new-password page) there is Other server? Switch profile. Cancel (on Android also the back button) takes you back to the page.

– Wrong address: a profile that has never been signed in can be corrected with Change address or deleted with Remove profile on the profile screen. If no Flowplan answers at the address, the app shows its own page with Try again and Switch profile.
– Add: App settings → Add profile, enter the address and, if you like, a name. If the address already has a profile, the app simply switches to it – there is one profile per instance.
– Rename: tap Rename next to a profile in the app settings.
– Remove: Sign out and remove the profile applies to the active profile; the next profile then becomes active.

Notifications, widgets, Live Activities, the number on the app icon and the running timer always belong to the active profile. On a switch the app unregisters the device from the previous instance's notifications; the sign-in there stays, so you are still signed in when you switch back. What the app keeps for a profile (the device token for widgets, the last summary) is stored separately in the keychain or Keystore and never goes to another instance. An address set up before becomes the first profile after the update.

en.page: Apps for iPhone, iPad and Android
en.heading: What the app keeps on the instance
paragraphs: After signing in, the app registers with the instance: the entry belongs to that sign-in; signing in again on the device moves it to the new session. It disappears with signing out, removing it under Signed-in devices or deleting the account. With its device token, widgets, Live Activities and Shortcuts read in the background only what you may see in Flowplan – in small answers of at most ten items per widget – and run their buttons (check off a task or habit, start/stop the timer, mark as read, save what you captured) – as do the buttons on notifications, which name only the notification: what they act on comes from the instance. The share sheet and the scanner save with it as well, and Spotlight reads your page titles and open tasks with it. For notifications the app leaves a token of the push relay (the instance stores it only encrypted) and a public key; the private key stays in the Keychain or Keystore. Notifications thus arrive end-to-end encrypted: the relay, Apple and Google do not see their content, only the app decrypts it. Older app versions get them through Expo's push service – there, as with Web Push, they only say that something new is in the inbox. Operators can turn notifications off or send their text through Expo as well, see Configuration. A focus filter that hides notifications leaves a rule for this device there: which workspace may still notify it, for at most a day.

en.page: Capturing, sharing and scanning in the apps
paragraphs: Capture notes, tasks and voice notes quickly, share from other apps, scan documents – and what the apps on iPhone and iPad can do on top.

en.page: Capturing, sharing and scanning in the apps
en.heading: Capture, Siri, Control Center
paragraphs: Every way leads to the app's capture screen: type a note or task, record a voice memo (keeps recording with the screen locked; transcribed when your instance can) or take/choose a photo.
Way What it offers
Quick capture widget Note, task, voice memo, photo – into the place chosen in the widget

Siri and Shortcuts (English, German, French) "Add a note to Flowplan" (into your capture inbox), "Add a task to Flowplan", "What's on today in Flowplan", "What's due today in Flowplan", "Open a page in Flowplan", "Search Flowplan", "Start the timer in Flowplan", "Stop the timer in Flowplan", "Record a voice memo in Flowplan", "Start focus in Flowplan"
Control Center and the Action button (iOS 18) New note, Quick capture, Today's tasks (shows how many are due), Voice memo, Start focus, Timer (a switch)
Long-press the app icon (iPhone, iPad) Inbox, My tasks, Search, New note, Switch profile. The iPhone shows the first four of them, Switch profile when signed out.

Long-press the app icon (Android) New note and Quick capture (always there, even before the first sign-in), then the pages you opened last, Inbox, My tasks, Search, Voice memo and Switch profile. Most launchers show four of them; every shortcut can be dragged to the home screen. Shortcuts to pages of another profile are greyed out until that profile is active again.

Android Quick Settings "New note" and "Quick capture" tiles (also from the lock screen). From Android 13, App settings → Widgets → Add “Quick capture” to Quick Settings adds the tile with one tap; otherwise use the pencil of Quick Settings.

Quick capture (tile and shortcut on Android) opens a compact window: choose where it goes – the inbox (your default capture database, see Capture into a database) or another page or database, with search –, type title and text, take or choose photos if you like, Save.
What Siri does without opening the app:

– Add a task: Siri asks for the task; in the Shortcuts app you can also set a due date and the list or database it goes to (otherwise your capture default). In a database the due date goes into its first date property.
– What's due today: Siri reads out how many tasks are due today and overdue and the first three, and shows the list.

– Search Flowplan: searches pages, records and comments in all your workspaces and shows the best hits; in a shortcut, the hits can be passed on (e.g. to Open a page). The action Search in the app opens Flowplan's own search with the text instead.
– Open a page: Siri asks which page – say part of its title – and opens it in the app. In Shortcuts you pick the page from a list.

Siri, Shortcuts and the controls use the active profile. Pages of end-to-end encrypted spaces do not appear (not even their titles). Adding tasks, what's due, opening pages, searching, the new controls and focus filters need a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer.

en.page: Capturing, sharing and scanning in the apps
en.heading: Capture right on opening
paragraphs: Under Settings → Appearance & language → On opening you choose for When opening on a phone between Home (the default) and Quick capture (from the Normal level on). With Quick capture, Flowplan on a phone – in the app, as an installed web app or in the browser – opens with capturing over the full screen: the title has the cursor, the target is your default capture database, and Improve text works as in the capture window. After saving it shows "Captured." with One more and To the app (the workspace's home page). This applies when you open or reload the plain address; links to a page, notifications, quick actions, invitations, sharing to Flowplan and back/forward still open their target, and tablets and computers always open the app. Without a connection the record waits on the device ("Saved on this device …"). The choice applies to your account on all devices.

en.page: Capturing, sharing and scanning in the apps
en.heading: Share from other apps
paragraphs: In any app that can share (browser, Photos or gallery, Files, mail, scanner …), Share → Flowplan (iPhone, iPad) or Share → Save to Flowplan (Android) opens a small window with title, text, link and files.
– What works: text, links, photos and PDFs – several files at once too (at most 10). Other file types are not taken.

– Where to: the inbox, your default capture database, is preselected (set it in the browser with Use as default for capturing, see Capture into a database). Save to (iPhone, iPad) or Change (Android) lists every page and database you may write to, with search.

– What you get: in a database (the inbox included) a record – the link in the first URL property (if there is one), the files in the first files property and in the record itself. On a page a sub page with text, link, photos and PDFs.

On iPhone and iPad you stay in the app you share from. Flowplan remembers the last choice of where to save per profile. The sheet uses the sign-in of the app: open Flowplan once and sign in, otherwise it asks you to. Photos in HEIC become JPEG.

On Android the window lists under Not taken what it cannot take (other file types, more than 10 files). PDFs get a preview of their first page in the record. You can change the title; left empty it is the first line of the text, the link's address or the first file name. After Save, Back to the app returns to the app you shared from; Open shows the result in Flowplan. Not signed in yet? Text and links then go to the instance's preview as in the browser and continue after signing in.
The share sheet on iPhone and iPad as well as photos and PDFs on Android need a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer. Up to 0.6.0, Android takes only text and links, through the instance's preview.

en.page: Capturing, sharing and scanning in the apps
en.heading: Scan documents and Spotlight (iPhone and iPad)
paragraphs: Scan documents. In a page, type / and choose Scan document (only in the iPhone and iPad app). The camera finds the edges and straightens each page; take as many pages as you like. Flowplan recognises the text on the device (German, English, French) and adds one PDF at the end of the page – or of the record you are in. The PDF carries the text invisibly, so you can select and search it in any PDF viewer, and Flowplan's search finds the scan by its text right away. The link flowplan://scan (e.g. in a shortcut) opens the scanner with the choice of inbox, page or database. The PDF does not stay on the phone after saving.

Spotlight. The app puts the titles of your most recently changed pages (up to 500, with where they are and a line of their content) and your open tasks – including database records assigned to you, those with a due date first – into the phone's search. A tap on a result opens it in Flowplan. Nothing of end-to-end encrypted spaces, pages behind a journal PIN or journal days goes there; signing out or switching profiles empties it. The index stays on the phone.
The scanner and Spotlight need a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer.

en.page: Capturing, sharing and scanning in the apps
en.heading: Voice notes in pages
paragraphs: In the app, Voice note (/voice) in a document records with the phone's microphone – up to 30 minutes, also with the screen locked. Insert puts the recording into the page as audio:

– Insert as text (iPhone and iPad): the spoken words become text on the device with Apple's speech recognition – the recording does not leave the phone for it. The text follows below the audio as a Transcript with timestamps. The app asks once for permission to use speech recognition. It works for the languages the device can recognise by itself (set by the device's language; most major languages, depending on the iOS version).
– Where the device cannot (Android, other languages), your instance's speech recognition turns it into text if it is set up (Voice notes); otherwise the audio stays on its own.
– Then summarise with AI puts a summary below the text when the AI is available to you.
This needs a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer. In the browser, /voice records as before.

en.page: Capturing, sharing and scanning in the apps
en.heading: On-device AI and Writing Tools (iPhone and iPad)
paragraphs: Optional: on an iPhone or iPad with iOS/iPadOS 26 or later that supports Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence switched on (Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri), the writing assistant and the summary of open pages run with Apple's language model on the device. The text does not leave the device, also in encrypted spaces; the instance needs no AI provider for it. Results carry the label On this device. This needs a Flowplan server newer than 0.7.0 (currently the beta image).

– Switch it off: Settings → AI → On this device (Apple) → Off – Flowplan then never asks the device. It also shows whether Apple Intelligence on this device is available, turned off in Settings or not supported. Administrators can switch it off for the whole instance.
– Server AI stays: questions to the workspace, AI in databases and AI actions keep running through the instance when it is set up; it also takes over texts that are too long.
– Older devices and iOS versions (from iOS 16.4) use the app as before, just without this path.
– Writing Tools: Apple's Writing Tools (proofread, rewrite, summarise) work right in the editor – select text and choose Writing Tools in the text menu (from iOS 18 with Apple Intelligence).
More: on-device AI.

en.page: Capturing, sharing and scanning in the apps
en.heading: Calendars in Apple Calendar
paragraphs: Settings → Calendars & issues → Calendars on iPhone, iPad and Mac: choose calendar views and tap Set up in Apple Calendar. The app opens a configuration profile in Safari; confirm the download, then install it under Settings → Profile Downloaded (on the Mac: System Settings → Profiles). Each view becomes a CalDAV account in Apple Calendar, in both directions – see Sync both ways. On a computer the page shows a QR code instead; scan it with the iPhone's camera. The link works once and for ten minutes.

en.page: Capturing, sharing and scanning in the apps
en.heading: iPad: windows, keyboard and Handoff
paragraphs: – Several windows: in a page's menu (right-click or long-press it in the sidebar), Open in new window gives the page a window of its own – side by side in Split View, in Slide Over or in Stage Manager. On iPhone Duo this works on the open display; on the closed one the menu item is not there. Links that would open a new tab do the same. Long-press the app icon → Show All Windows lists them. The first window holds the app settings, notifications and widgets; the others show a page and come back with it after a restart. All windows use the active profile and the app lock.

– Hardware keyboard: hold ⌘ and the iPad lists Flowplan's shortcuts – search ⌘ K, new page ⌘ N, quick capture ⌘ ⌥ N, the overview ⌘ / and the others with ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥, including your own. A shortcut works in the window in front. The editor's shortcuts (bold, undo …) work as in the browser.
– Trackpad and mouse: the pointer hovers over buttons and links as in Safari.

– Handoff: the page in front is offered to your Mac and your other devices (same Apple Account, Handoff on under Settings → General → AirPlay & Continuity). On the Mac it opens in the desktop app, without it in the browser. Pages from the Mac or another device open in the app on the profile of their instance; pages of an instance without a profile open in Safari. Pages behind the app lock are not offered while it is locked.

en.page: Widgets and notifications in the apps
paragraphs: On iPhone, iPad and Android: home screen widgets, buttons on notifications, Live Activities and Focus filters.

en.page: Widgets and notifications in the apps
en.heading: Widgets
paragraphs: Each widget shows one thing and has settings of its own. A widget you just added works right away with sensible defaults; small sizes show less. A tap opens the task or page in the app.
Change the settings: iPhone and iPad: Long-press the widget → Edit Widget (iOS 17 or later). Android: Long-press the widget → Settings (you can skip this step when adding it).
The lists to choose from (databases, views, properties, calendars, forms …) come straight from your Flowplan instance.
Widget What it shows Settings
Quick capture Buttons for note, task, voice memo, photo Where to save (default: your capture inbox), which buttons
Tasks Open tasks – check them off right in the widget My tasks, records of a database (with view) or to-dos of a page; all open, due today or overdue; number
Today Appointments and tasks due Calendars, range (today, 3 days, week), tasks due on/off
Page and favorites Your favorites, or one page / database view Page, view, up to two properties
Database counter One number (count, sum, average) with its last 14 days Database, view, value, group, history
Journal and habits Whether today is written, your streak; habits to check off Journal, habit database
Time this week Hours this week and today; start/stop the timer Which timer "Start" starts
Mentions Who mentioned you or gave you a task; mark as read Mentions and/or new tasks, unread only
Form responses New responses to a form Form
Flowplan Tasks due at a glance With or without the inbox, running timer on/off
Flowplan Inbox Number of unread notifications –
Flowplan Instance, Live, Storage Administrators only: state, one live number, storage What to show or which metric

"My tasks" shows, besides tasks from documents, the open records of databases in which you are in a person property (such as "Assignee") – with the database and due date (the database's due date), and you can check them off right away if you may edit the record. By the same rules these records also appear in the Flowplan widget (including the count on the app icon and the reminders without push), with their due date in the Today widget and so in Siri's "What's on today in Flowplan", and in Spotlight on iPhone and iPad. Private records of others, databases behind a journal PIN, end-to-end encrypted spaces and properties hidden from you stay out everywhere; a record that a chosen calendar view in the Today widget already shows appears there only once.
Good to know:
– Counter history: Flowplan keeps the value of every day. Days before the widget was set up are estimated and drawn lighter and dashed.
– Privacy: widgets only show what you may see in Flowplan. Pages behind a journal PIN or end-to-end encrypted only show their state in a widget, never content.
– Signed out? When your session ends (e.g. a short SSO session), every widget shows Open Flowplan to sign in. Its settings stay; after signing in, the widgets fill again at once.
– Profiles: every widget shows the profile set in its settings (see Colour and profile per widget).
– Colours: every widget has a colour of its own (see Colour and profile per widget). Red, amber and green always keep their meaning.
– Check off today's tasks: add the Tasks widget and choose Due today in its settings.

– Updates: when you change something in Flowplan, when the app comes to the foreground, and in the background about every 30 minutes (iOS decides how often). On iPhone with iOS 26 also right away by push.

– Requirements: the configurable widgets, the Live Activities other than the timer, and Siri and Shortcuts need a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer. Flowplan, Flowplan Inbox and the running timer work from 0.4.0.

en.page: Widgets and notifications in the apps
en.heading: Next appointment, Continue reading, Key figure and Deadline
paragraphs: Widget What it shows Settings
Next appointment The next one to three appointments with a countdown and the location; a Join button for a video link Calendars (as in Today), range (today, 48 hours, week), Join on/off
Continue reading Pages you opened last, or the books of the library with your reading progress Source (recently opened or library), number (1–6)
Key figure One number tile of a dashboard with its history as a line and the change since the day before Dashboard, tile
Deadline A countdown to the due date of a record or task; red when overdue Database and record, or one of your tasks

– Join appears only for links of known video services – Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Webex, Jitsi Meet and Whereby – in the location, a link or text property or the appointment's description (where synced Google and Microsoft calendars put them). Administrators add their own services (such as BigBlueButton or their own Jitsi) as host names in MEETING_HOSTS, comma-separated: MEETING_HOSTS=bbb.example.org,meet.example.org. Other links never get a Join button.
– Reading progress: for library books, the page you read last, measured against all pages of the book.
– Key figure: Flowplan keeps the value of every day; the line shows up to 30 days, from the day the widget was set up.
– As everywhere: pages behind a journal PIN and end-to-end encrypted spaces only show their state, and properties hidden from you (such as a hidden due date) stay empty.

en.page: Widgets and notifications in the apps
en.heading: Colour and profile per widget
paragraphs: In the settings of every widget:

– Profile: which profile the widget shows – by default the active one. So a widget can show your work tasks while the personal profile is open in the app. A profile that is not active stays signed in for this; only the active profile gets notifications. Its widgets go only when you remove the profile or sign out.

– Colour: Accent (default: the accent colour of the workspace the content comes from), Profile colour (the profile's colour dot), System (Material You from the wallpaper or theme on Android 12 and later, the system tint on iPhone) or Flowplan. You choose the profile colour in the app under Manage profiles; it also shows in the profile list and when switching.
– On iPhone the widgets also look right tinted, accented and in the clear Liquid Glass look of iOS 26.

en.page: Widgets and notifications in the apps
en.heading: Accent colour, "Widgets only" and instant updates
paragraphs: – Accent colour: the instance sends every widget the accent colour of its workspace (Settings → Workspace → Appearance), checked for legibility in light and dark mode like the web app. Workspaces without their own colour, and people who chose Flowplan's own look, get Flowplan's colours. Older servers send no accent colour; the widgets then use Flowplan's colours.
– "Widgets only": under Settings → Account → Signed-in devices, a profile that is not active in the app right now shows as Widgets only; the test notification sends it nothing.
Instant updates on iPhone

From iOS 26 the instance tells your iPhones as soon as something changes that your widgets could show – new notifications, tasks, records and pages in your workspaces, time tracking, focus, flashcards, dashboards. The widgets then reload. To stay within what iOS allows, the instance collects changes for about 30 seconds and sends at most one push per device every 5 minutes; when nothing changes, none is sent. The push goes through the push relay like notifications and carries no content – only the signal to reload; the widget fetches its data from your instance itself. Without the push relay (PUSH_RELAY=off, MOBILE_PUSH=off) the background updates remain.

en.page: Widgets and notifications in the apps
en.heading: Widgets for administrators
paragraphs: People who administer the instance (members of the admin group, OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP, default flowplan-admins) get three more widgets in the app for iPhone, iPad and Android. Each shows one thing big; on the iPhone you choose which in the widget's settings.
Widget Sizes (iOS) Setting (default first) Tapping opens

Flowplan Instance small, medium, lock screen Show: state (All fine, notices or problems with the most important one), last backup, or version with available update Administration (Monitoring when there are notices or problems)

Flowplan Live small, medium, large, lock screen Metric: active now, requests/min, error rate (1 h) or sign-ins today; from medium up the other numbers small and the requests of the last 24 hours as a chart Administration → Monitoring
Flowplan Storage small, medium, lock screen (ring) Metric: disk used, database and files, or fullest workspace (quota) Administration → Storage
– Everyone else sees Administrators only in these widgets; without a sign-in they say Open Flowplan to sign in.

– Like the other widgets they read their data with the app's device token (GET /api/mobile/admin-summary). The instance checks on every call that the person of the session the device is bound to is an administrator right now – leaving the admin group, signing out or removing the device under Signed-in devices stops it. API tokens never get this data.
– Only numbers and states are sent – no names, e-mail addresses or workspace names.
– With the statistics switched off (FLOWPLAN_METRICS=off or in the administration under Monitoring → Statistics), Flowplan Live says "Statistics switched off"; state and storage stay.
– Older instances without this endpoint show Administrators only.

en.page: Widgets and notifications in the apps
en.heading: Buttons on notifications
paragraphs: Long-press a notification (or pull it down) for its buttons. They do their work in the background; the app does not open.
Notification Buttons
A task is due (a task assigned to you is due today, a date reminder of a record) Done ticks it off; Tomorrow moves its date to tomorrow – the time of day stays, a date further ahead moves one day on
Comment, reply, mention in a comment Reply – type the answer right in the notification; it goes into the thread (or comments on the page) under your name. Mark as read
Everything else Mark as read
– Each button also marks the notification as read; the number on the app icon follows.
– Done, Tomorrow and Reply need the phone unlocked; Mark as read works on the lock screen.

– Done on a record uses the database's “done” state (a status option such as Done, or a checkbox Done); databases without one only offer Mark as read. If the task changed meanwhile, nothing is ticked off – a notification says so, and a tap opens the page.
– Your rights apply as in the browser, and the change shows in the activity, versions and automations like any other.

– Done, Tomorrow and Reply only appear when the notification brings its text along – without it, nobody could tell which task a button acts on. Through the push relay that is the default, because the text is end-to-end encrypted (operators can turn it off with MOBILE_PUSH_CONTENT=off); older app versions through Expo only get it with MOBILE_PUSH_CONTENT=on. Otherwise there is Mark as read only.

Reminders without push: if your instance does not send push notifications to the app (switched off by the operators, or a test build without push), the app reminds you of your tasks itself – at 09:00 on the day a task is due, as long as notifications are allowed for Flowplan. It uses the tasks the app knows from its summary (the next eight).

en.page: Widgets and notifications in the apps
en.heading: Live Activities and ongoing notifications
paragraphs: On iPhone what is running appears on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island, on Android as a notification (a Live Update on Android 16):
What runs Shows Button
Timer a running clock –
Focus e.g. 25 minutes of focus, then the break End
Meeting now the time left Open notes – creates the meeting note in your journal if there is none yet
Imports and exports their progress –
Voice memo recording Stop recording
Incident of the instance administrators only, only while it lasts –
Meetings, imports/exports and incidents can be switched off in the app settings under Live Activities; the timer, focus and voice memos always appear while they run.

If you start or stop the timer or focus elsewhere – in the browser, on another device – or focus moves on to the break, the instance updates the Live Activity on the iPhone by push through the push relay, even when the app is not open. By default this push holds only times and the phase; the Live Activity already knows the title and link from when it started on the device.

en.page: Widgets and notifications in the apps
en.heading: Focus filters
paragraphs: On the iPhone and iPad, a Focus (Settings → Focus → e.g. Work → Add filter → Flowplan) can choose:

– Profile or workspace: a profile ("all workspaces") or one workspace of a profile. When the Focus starts, the app switches to that profile and opens the workspace; when it ends, it goes back to the profile you had before – unless you switched yourself in the meantime.

– Hide notifications from other workspaces: while the Focus is on, your instance does not send this phone push notifications from other workspaces – or none at all if the Focus belongs to another profile. They still arrive in the inbox. If the Focus is never switched off, the rule ends by itself after a day.
Workspaces appear in the list once the app has been signed in to that profile; open the app on the profile once if one is missing.
Watch the instance live: figures, statistics, alerts via webhook, maintenance notices and Prometheus.

en.heading: Administration → Monitoring
paragraphs: Administration → Monitoring shows the instance live – refreshed every 15 seconds, paused while the tab is in the background:

– Health: database, file storage (with disk usage), S3 mirror, backup, e-mail, AI provider (reachable and response time, checked at most every five minutes), push relay (reachable, checked at most every minute, see Push notifications), background workers and update. Each tile leads to the section in charge.

– Key figures: five tiles in a row, each with a value and a small trend; storage, AI tokens and errors compare with the period before once it has been collected: Active 24 h (plus active now and since midnight), Storage (change over 7 days, with disk usage), Deliveries 7 days (plus those given up), AI tokens 14 days (vs. last week) and Errors 24 h (5xx, vs. the day before, with the error rate). Each tile jumps to its card.

– Charts: across the full width Requests & errors (5xx) – 1 hour, 24 hours or 7 days, with requests per minute and p95 response time –, below it the cards in two columns (one on narrow screens): Active people per hour (7 days), Sign-ins successful and failed per day (14 days), Refused requests, Storage by kind and the largest workspaces, Deliveries (webhooks, push, e-mail) per day and AI usage (tokens per day and per feature). Every chart shows its values on hover, tap or with the arrow keys and has As a table.
– Queues: what is waiting to be processed right now – search index, mail queue, push delivery, AI fields and AI search index, S3 upload, webhooks retrying.
– Events: errors, warnings and notes of the last 14 days, filterable.
– Quick actions: Back up now, Check AI provider, Check alerts, Test alert, the way to Maintenance & notices and the activity log as CSV.
– Below: Background workers, Instance in numbers (size of the database and uploads, versions, uptime, demos …), Alerts by webhook and Statistics.
In detail:

– Refused requests: failed sign-ins, requests a limit refused with 429 (sign-in attempts, invitations, AI, MCP, forms …) and anonymous uploads over the daily budget (forms, share links) – per day over the last 14 days. A rise points to attacks or limits that are too tight. The counters are kept for 35 days and cleaned up daily.
– Background workers: last run and last error of backup, Markdown export, AI background work, calendar and issue sync and LDAP sync; “off” means not set up.

– Storage: usage by kind and the largest workspaces with bars against the quota (yellow from 80 %, red from 95 %). Quotas are set under Administration → Workspaces and Administration → Limits & retention.

– Deliveries: delivered webhooks, push messages and e-mails per day; what is waiting, given up and the latest errors are under Queues. Only the host of a webhook address is shown, never its path or token.

en.heading: Errors in detail
paragraphs: Below the error chart, Errors in detail shows where the errors (5xx) come from – one row per kind of error with route or command (such as POST /api/command · row.update), error name and short message, count and trend in the chosen range, and when it last happened; sorted by last seen or count. A click into the error chart shows only that time slot. The Errors 24 h tile jumps here.

Opened, a row shows the place in the code (the top stack frames in Flowplan's own code, to copy) and the last 20 occurrences with time, error ID, status, instance (in a cluster), version and role. Copy for an issue copies a plain-text report without personal data. In the Docker image you see compiled files and function names; source files with line only when the build's source maps are next to them. Clear deletes all error details; the count in the chart stays.

Every answer carries an error ID in the X-Request-Id header, and for an error also in the JSON (requestId). The app shows it in the message "Something went wrong on the server" as "Error ID: …" – with it you find the occurrence.

Captured are answers from 500 up, failures of background workers and jobs and failed MCP tools, also with statistics switched off. Stored are only the route as a pattern (without IDs and query), command, status, error name, the message (at most 500 characters; keys, tokens, passwords, e-mail and IP addresses and IDs masked), stack frames, database error code, error ID, instance, version and role (administrator, member, guest, not signed in, API token, MCP). Never stored: IP addresses, request contents, headers or who it was. Kept 14 days, at most 500 kinds of errors.

en.heading: Restarts
paragraphs: When the container restarts without any visible error, Restarts under Administration → Monitoring helps after the fact: every restart of the last 30 days is listed with its time, how long Flowplan ran before, the reason and the memory at the last heartbeat (process and container against its limit).
Reason Means
Clean Flowplan got SIGTERM or SIGINT and shut down in order – an update, docker stop, a restart.
Crash An error ended the process; the error with its stack is shown.

Likely out of memory At the last heartbeat memory was at 90 % or more of the container's limit (or of the JavaScript heap's), or the container reports an OOM kill, or the whole server had 5 % or less of its memory available.
Killed without trace Neither a signal nor an error: e.g. SIGKILL after a failed healthcheck, by the host or kill -9, a power cut – or an OOM kill that left no trace.

Opened, an unexpected restart shows the last 200 lines of the server log before the end – Flowplan's own output and Litestream's – as text to scroll through; Download as .txt saves them with reason and memory. A clean restart is a short entry without lines.

How it works: every 30 seconds Flowplan writes a heartbeat (time, uptime, memory of the process and the container's limit from cgroup v2 or v1) to /app/data/logs/, and when it shuts down, whether it was clean. The next start reads it and records the restart. Next to it lies the server log: per container two files with about 2,000 lines together (at most 1 MB each), the same for Litestream (litestream.log). The output in the container log (docker logs) stays as it was.

Redacted before a line reaches the disk: the values of environment variables whose name contains TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD or KEY (S3 keys, encryption key, passwords …), bearer tokens, credentials in addresses (https://name:password@…), password=… and the like, e-mail and IP addresses. Flowplan never writes page contents to the log.

Entries are kept 30 days. In a cluster every instance records its own restarts; when several containers share one data folder, the files carry their container's name (FLOWPLAN_INSTANCE_ID or the host name). FLOWPLAN_LOG_FILE=off switches the log on disk off – restarts are then listed without lines.

A crash or two unexpected restarts within an hour make an incident: once per incident an alert goes out by webhook (ops.unexpected_restart) and to the administrators' chat apps, the Monitoring tile on the administration's start page shows it for a day, and the activity log records it.

> Limits of the OOM detection: when the kernel ends the process for lack of memory, Flowplan cannot write anything any more. "Likely out of memory" is therefore a guess from the last heartbeat – up to 30 seconds old, a fast rise after it stays invisible – or from the container's OOM counter, which Docker and Kubernetes usually reset on a restart. docker inspect --format '{{.State.OOMKilled}}' or kubectl describe pod ("OOMKilled") tell for sure. Without a memory limit on the container the JavaScript heap and the whole server's available memory count – when the server runs out, the kernel ends some process, such as Litestream; dmesg then shows Killed process … (litestream). And because Litestream is the container's first process, its very last line when it stops can be missing from the file.

en.heading: Statistics
paragraphs: For the charts, Flowplan counts requests, errors and response times per minute, active people per hour, storage per day and AI tokens per feature – numbers only, without IP addresses, paths, user agents or names. Who was active is held in memory for the running hour only, so that each person counts once. Successful sign-ins are counted with their time (without the person). AI tokens come from the provider where it reports them, otherwise they are estimated (four characters per token).
Resolution Kept for
Minutes 48 hours
Hours 35 days
Days (storage, AI tokens) 400 days

Switch the statistics off under Administration → Monitoring → Statistics (Collect usage statistics) or for the whole instance with FLOWPLAN_METRICS=off (see Configuration); the switch is then locked. Delete statistics removes all counted requests, active people, storage history, AI tokens and successful sign-ins; the counters of refused requests stay.

en.heading: Alerts by webhook
paragraphs: Under Administration → Monitoring → Alerts by webhook, enter an https:// address (with FLOWPLAN_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true also http:// and internal addresses) and choose the events:
Event When
Backup failed The last scheduled backup ended with an error.
Storage > 90 % A workspace with a quota is more than 90 % full.
Worker error A worker that is set up reported an error in the last 24 hours.
Many failed sign-ins 50 or more failed sign-ins within an hour.
Security incidents Right away for every new incident of the detection rules (ops.security, with rule and severity).
Litestream replica stuck Right away, once per incident: the Litestream replica in the bucket is stuck (ops.litestream_stuck). {since=0.10.0}
Unexpected restarts Right away, once per incident: a crash or two unexpected restarts within an hour (ops.unexpected_restart). {since=0.10.0}
Flowplan checks every ten minutes and sends at most one message per event and day as a POST with JSON:
{ "event": "ops.storage_high", "title": "Speicher > 90 %", "detail": "Agency: 93 %", "instance": "Flowplan", "url": "https://flowplan.example.org", "at": "2026-10-22T08:10:00.000Z" }
The title is in German, as alerts are sent outside of a request; match on event.

The header X-Flowplan-Signature: sha256= is made with the signing secret shown, X-Flowplan-Event names the event. Send test sends ops.test right away, Check now checks out of turn, New secret creates a new signing secret. The latest alerts sent are listed below with their status code. An empty address turns alerts off.

en.heading: Maintenance & notices
paragraphs: Administration → Maintenance & notices holds two banners and the banners to click away. The notice for everyone – e.g. “The new filing applies from Monday” – stays until you clear the field. A maintenance notice with text, start and end appears to everyone signed in as a banner at the top of the window from saving on – before the start as “Scheduled maintenance”, during it as “Maintenance in progress”, in each person's time zone and language. After the end it disappears by itself, also in windows already open (they check every five minutes). Everyone can hide the notice for themselves. Remove notice withdraws it at once. Saving and removing are in the activity log.
Banners to click away

For news each person should see only once – e.g. “Flowplan is now an app” or your Discord server – New banner creates a banner everyone sees until they close it or follow its link. After that it never appears for them again, on no device; whoever opens Flowplan next sees it at the top of the window.

– Content: an optional heading (bold), the text (at most 300 characters) and an optional link with its own label – an https:// address (opens in a new tab) or a page of this instance (#… or /…). The preview shows it while you write.
– Colour: notice (blue), promotion (accent), news (green) or important (yellow).
– Who and where: everyone or administrators only; everywhere or browser only – then not in the desktop app and the apps, e.g. when it promotes the apps.
– Period: optional From and Until; without them it applies right away and until you end it.
– Templates fill in the form for the apps (link to flowplan.org/download, browser only) or for Discord.

The list shows each banner with its state (shown, planned, paused, ended) and how many closed it and how many followed the link. Pause hides it without losing its numbers; Show again shows it to everyone once more, also to those who closed it; Delete removes it with its numbers for everyone right away. At most three banners appear at a time, newest first. Creating, changing and deleting are in the activity log.
