en.heading: Storage overview
paragraphs: Administration → Storage & backup shows in the cards Backups, Usage and Content:
– whether the S3 storage is reachable, how long the check took and how many files are still waiting,
– what is local and what is in the bucket: files by kind (images, videos, documents …) and how the database is split,
– how many workspaces, pages, databases, records, whiteboards, files, accounts and comments there are.

en.heading: Prometheus
paragraphs: With FLOWPLAN_METRICS_TOKEN (at least 16 characters), /api/metrics delivers metrics: sizes, queues, search backlog, storage and quota per workspace, flowplan_object_storage_pending and flowplan_build_info with version and commit.
scrape_configs:
- job_name: flowplan
metrics_path: /api/metrics
authorization:
credentials: <FLOWPLAN_METRICS_TOKEN>
static_configs:
- targets: ["flowplan:3000"]
Without a token the endpoint is switched off. The same token unlocks the details of /api/health (see above).

> For load tests: FLOWPLAN_METRICS_LOOP=1 also measures the delay and utilisation of the Node event loop and the time spent in SQLite, and adds them to /api/metrics. The values cover the time since the previous scrape – meant for a single scraper such as the load test script, not for a shared Prometheus. Off by default.
The move tool has the new instance fetch everything from the old one – database, files, keys – with a short downtime; plus troubleshooting a move.

en.heading: Way A: The move tool
paragraphs: Under Administration → Storage & backup (admins only), the new instance fetches everything straight from the old one: server to server, resumable and with checksums.
On the old instance – "Prepare the move"
– Move instance → Prepare the move. For safety Flowplan asks for your password; with SSO the sign-in must be at most 15 minutes old (otherwise sign out and in once).

– Flowplan shows the transfer address and the move token (fpmove_…) – only this once. The token is valid for 24 hours and only for the move: it may read the instance, make it read-only for the final sync and complete the move, nothing else. Only a hash is stored; Revoke invalidates it at once, and a new token replaces the old one. Creating, revoking and every step of the move are in the activity log and a security event under Administration → Security. Ten wrong token attempts from one address lock it out for 15 minutes.
On the new instance – "Take over from another instance"
The new instance is fresh: only the first admin account you create on first start. If it already has content, Flowplan asks for an explicit confirmation, because everything is replaced.

> Same domain, but DNS still points to the old server? Then you cannot reach the new instance at its final address yet, and its proxy cannot get a certificate for it. Two options: - Temporary address: point a second name at the new server (say new.flowplan.example.org), start the new instance with APP_URL=https://new.flowplan.example.org first and do the move there. The pre-flight check then warns about APP_URL – that is expected. Before the restart in step 6, set APP_URL to the final address (the proxy may serve both names). - Without the interface: the command line on the new server.
– Move instance → Take over from another instance: enter the address of the old instance (its APP_URL) and the move token, Start the takeover.

– If the old server is only in your own network (LAN, a VPN such as WireGuard or Tailscale, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:3000), set FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true on the new instance for the move. Without it, as for every request the server makes, only public https:// addresses are allowed.

– First copy: a consistent database snapshot, every file in uploads/ one by one with a SHA-256 checksum, web-push-keys.json and secrets.key. The page shows bytes, files and the estimated time left. The old instance keeps running as usual. If the connection drops or a server restarts, Resume continues where it stopped – files already checked are not fetched again, a half file continues from its last byte.

– Pre-flight check → Check. Flowplan compares the settings of both instances – only names and check values (an HMAC keyed with the move token), never the values themselves – and checks whether the new instance reaches S3, SMTP and the OIDC provider. The result is a list of OK, Warning and Error:
Check Meaning
Version Error if the new instance is older than the old one: update it first.

FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY Error if it is missing or different: encrypted backups, the encrypted files in the bucket, stored tokens and calendar connections would be unreadable. Set the old key (a new one only in addition, the old one then in …_PREVIOUS).
Stored secrets Error if their key is missing (FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY or FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY). A generated secrets.key comes along by itself.
APP_URL Warning for a different address, with everything that must then be set up again.
OIDC, S3, SMTP, push, AI, other Variables missing here, with a different value, or set only here. Missing OIDC_ISSUER/OIDC_CLIENT_ID is an error – nobody would get in with SSO.
Same bucket Warning: both instances would write into the same folder (see way C).
S3, SMTP, OIDC reachable Error with the service's message. Many providers block outgoing ports 25 and 465 – use port 587 then.
Change the new instance's variables and restart it until no errors remain; the move continues after the restart.

– Make the source read-only and fetch the last state: downtime starts here. The old instance accepts no more changes – everyone sees "Move in progress: This instance is read-only", reading and signing in still work, changes (also through the API, CalDAV, webhooks, inbound e-mail) are refused with a clear message. The new instance fetches a fresh database snapshot and only the files that are new or changed since the first copy; removed ones go. This usually takes minutes.

– Apply on restart → Apply: Flowplan checks the database and prepares everything for the next start – exactly like Restore from backup. The old instance is told: it now shows "This instance has moved to …", stays read-only, and its move token is used up.

– Restart the new instance (the container, the pod or the service). On start Flowplan swaps in database, files and keys; the new instance's previous state stays in the data folder as pre-move-. The log says Instanz wiederhergestellt; vorheriger Stand in …/pre-move-….
– Switch DNS (below) and check afterwards.

You now sign in on the new instance with the accounts of the old one; the new one's first admin account is replaced. Existing sign-ins (browsers, apps) stay valid as long as the domain stays the same.

On the old instance, Move instance also offers Redirect the web interface: whoever opens it in the browser goes straight to the new address. Lift read-only makes it writable again – only when the move is called off.

While the old instance is read-only, its background services pause: incoming mail (the IMAP mailbox stays unread for the new instance), calendar and issue sync, workflows, reminders, deliveries of e-mail, push, webhooks and messengers, and scheduled backups. The app can't change anything there either.

en.heading: Without the interface (command line)
paragraphs: The same without a web interface on the new instance – before any account exists there, say, or over SSH while DNS still points to the old server. The tool is in the image as /app/move.mjs and in the source as scripts/move.mjs (npm run move). It fetches the first copy, makes the old instance read-only, fetches the last state, prepares everything for the next start and tells the old instance the new address (--target-url, otherwise APP_URL). Interrupted? Run the same command again – it continues where it stopped.
# Docker Compose (in the new instance's folder; same .env, same volume)
docker compose run --rm flowplan node /app/move.mjs \
--from https://flowplan.example.org --token fpmove_…
docker compose up -d          # starts and applies the copy
# docker run
docker run --rm -v flowplan-data:/app/data -e APP_URL=https://flowplan.example.org \
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan node /app/move.mjs --from https://flowplan.example.org --token fpmove_…
# (writes as UID 1000; with PUID/PGID add -e PUID=… -e PGID=…, with user: --user UID:GID)
# Kubernetes (Helm chart)
kubectl -n flowplan exec deploy/flowplan -- node /app/move.mjs --from https://flowplan.example.org --token fpmove_…
kubectl -n flowplan rollout restart deploy/flowplan
# without Docker
npm run move -- --from https://flowplan.example.org --token fpmove_… --data /var/lib/flowplan
Option Meaning
--from Address of the old instance. On the command line internal addresses and http:// are allowed too – you decide where it connects.
--token The move token (or FLOWPLAN_MOVE_TOKEN in the environment, to keep it out of the shell history).
--data Data folder, default FLOWPLAN_DATA_DIR or ./data.
--target-url Address of the new instance for the notice on the old one (default APP_URL).
--copy-only Only the first copy; the old instance stays writable. Later run it again without the option for the final sync.
--yes Replace a data folder that already has content (its previous state stays as pre-move-…).
The pre-flight check is only in the interface; on the command line compare the variables yourself (list above).

en.heading: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: Message or state Cause and fix

"Internal addresses are only allowed with FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true" The old instance has a private address (LAN, VPN, localhost) or only http://. Set FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true on the new instance, restart, remove it after the move.
"Invalid or expired move token" Copied wrongly, older than 24 hours, revoked, replaced by a new one or used up by a completed move. Create a new one on the old instance.
"Too many invalid move requests" Ten wrong tokens from one address: wait 15 minutes.
The transfer stops Resume (or run the command again). Finished files stay, half ones continue.
"Checksum does not match" The file arrived damaged and is fetched again automatically; if it keeps happening, check the connection (proxy, VPN).
"This database snapshot no longer exists" The old instance made a new snapshot in the meantime (new token, restart). Resume fetches it.

Time-out at the start (502/504) The first time, the old instance computes the checksums of all files. A proxy with a short time limit in front (nginx: proxy_read_timeout 60 s, Cloudflare 100 s) gives up. Raise the limit or use the address without the proxy (with FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE).
Pre-flight: error for FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY or stored secrets Set the old instance's key on the new one and restart. Only then switch.
SMTP not reachable Many providers block outgoing ports 25 and 465. Use SMTP_PORT=587 with STARTTLS.
Nothing happens after Apply Applying needs a restart of the new instance. The log must say Instanz wiederhergestellt.
The old instance says "read-only" although the move was called off Move instance → Lift read-only.
How to move a whole Flowplan instance to another server – say from a home server to a rented one – with all accounts, workspaces, files and keys, usually with only a few minutes of downtime.
A Flowplan instance consists of exactly four things:
Part What Moves along
Container the image ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan (for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64) install anew, the same or a newer version
Data folder /app/data flowplan.sqlite (+ -wal, -shm), uploads/, web-push-keys.json, secrets.key; ocr/ and tmp/ are recreated yes – this is the actual move
Environment variables APP_URL, keys, OIDC_*, S3_*, SMTP_* … copy by hand, above all the keys
Domain and reverse proxy DNS record, HTTPS certificate switch DNS, set up the proxy again

This holds for every way of running it: docker run, Docker Compose, Kubernetes with the Helm chart, without Docker or in a deployment panel. If you use a panel, recreate the same container with the same volume and the same variables there.
More on this topic: Moving with the move tool

en.heading: Prepare
paragraphs: – Write down the environment variables. All the old instance gets – depending on the setup from the .env, with docker inspect (section Env), docker compose config or helm get values flowplan. The full list is under Configuration.
– Keep the keys safe, apart from the data (password manager):

– FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (or the file of FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE) and FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS: without them, encrypted backups, the encrypted files in the bucket and the stored secrets sealed with it cannot be read.

– FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY (or …_FILE), if set. If neither is set, the key for stored secrets is secrets.key in the data folder – the built-in move tool takes it along; with the other ways you copy it yourself.

– What depends on it: AI keys, calendar connections (Google, Microsoft 365), chat app tokens, Git export tokens and the accounts' two-factor secrets. Without the key, accounts with two-factor sign-in only get in with recovery codes.

– Keep the domain. The same APP_URL means passkeys, the OIDC redirect, CalDAV and CardDAV accounts, the apps, incoming webhooks (Git, tickets, inbound e-mail) and share links simply keep working after the DNS switch. With a new domain all of that must be set up again (see Another domain).
– Lower the TTL of the DNS record at least as long beforehand as the current TTL (often 1 to 24 hours), e.g. to 300 seconds. The switch then takes effect within minutes.

– Set up the new server (example: Hetzner Cloud) with the same or a newer Flowplan version – an older one cannot open a newer database – and with the same environment variables. A bucket of its own for the new instance is simplest; with the same bucket see way C.
– Make a backup: Administration → Storage & backup → Whole instance → Download. It never hurts.
– Warn the users: Administration → Maintenance & notices shows everyone a maintenance window.

en.heading: Three ways
paragraphs: Way When Downtime
A: Move tool (recommended) whenever the new server can reach the old one minutes (only the final sync)
B: Download and upload a backup small instances, no network path between the servers from the backup until the new instance starts
C: S3 and Litestream the old instance already runs with S3 and Litestream from stopping the old to starting the new instance

en.heading: Way B: Download and upload a backup
paragraphs: – On the old instance announce maintenance – changes after the download are lost.
– Administration → Storage & backup → Whole instance → Download. With FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY the file is encrypted (.zip.enc) – the new instance then needs the same key.

– The instance backup holds the database and files but not secrets.key and web-push-keys.json. Copy both by hand (or set the keys as variables): ``bash # old docker compose cp flowplan:/app/data/secrets.key . docker compose cp flowplan:/app/data/web-push-keys.json . # new docker compose cp secrets.key flowplan:/app/data/ docker compose cp web-push-keys.json flowplan:/app/data/ docker compose exec -u root flowplan chown 1000:1000 /app/data/secrets.key /app/data/web-push-keys.json # with PUID/PGID or user: that user and group instead of 1000:1000 ``

– On the new instance Restore from backup → Choose backup. The proxy in front must let such large uploads through (Caddy does by itself, nginx with client_max_body_size, Cloudflare at most 100 MB); otherwise bring the file to the server with scp and upload it there. At most 50 GB.
– Restart; the previous state stays as pre-restore-…. Then switch DNS.

en.heading: Way C: S3 and Litestream
paragraphs: If the old instance runs with S3 (files in the bucket) and Litestream (a continuous copy of the database under /db/), the new instance can start straight from the bucket:
– Stop the old instance – the Litestream of two instances must never write into the same folder at the same time.

– Start the new instance with the same S3_* variables, the same FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY and an empty data folder. Litestream restores the database; Flowplan fetches files on first access right away and all others in the background.
– Copy secrets.key and web-push-keys.json as in way B unless the keys are set as variables.
– Switch DNS.

With FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM=off there is no continuous copy: use the newest scheduled backup from /backups/ instead (see Restore). The pre-flight check of way A notices a Litestream copy in the bucket and points to this way.

> Active workflows arrive on the new instance paused – with their draft, versions and held runs. So nothing starts twice while the old instance is still running. Check them afterwards and activate them again.

en.heading: Switch DNS
paragraphs: – After the final sync (way A) or the start of the new instance, change the domain's A record (IPv4) and AAAA record (IPv6) to the new server. Remove a port forwarding or tunnel at the old location.
– The new server's proxy gets its certificate as soon as the domain points to it (with Let's Encrypt over port 80) – give it a minute.

– Check what the world sees with dig +short flowplan.example.org (or nslookup). Whoever still has the old address cached reaches the old instance until the TTL runs out – which then shows the notice with the new one.
– Raise the TTL again afterwards.

en.heading: Check afterwards
paragraphs: – Sign in: with password, passkey and SSO. Existing sessions stay valid.
– Administration → Monitoring: all green? Administration → Encryption shows the same key ID as before.
– Administration → Storage & backup: S3 connected, the queue drains (with S3, Flowplan uploads every file once after a takeover), Back up now succeeds.
– Administration → E-mail → Send test email and Administration → Push notifications → Send test notification.
– Open a few pages, images and attachments; upload a file.
– AI, calendar connections, chat apps: if they work without signing in again, the stored secrets are readable.
– Refresh CalDAV/CardDAV in an app, open the desktop and mobile apps, trigger incoming webhooks (Git, tickets) once.

en.heading: Clean up
paragraphs: – Remove FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE on the new instance.
– Delete pre-move-… (or pre-restore-…) in the data folder after a few days, e.g. docker compose exec flowplan sh -c 'rm -rf /app/data/pre-move-*'.
– Keep the old instance running with its notice for a few days, then stop it, wipe its volume and revoke its S3 credentials (if it had its own). The move token is already used up.
– Turn on or check a scheduled backup on the new instance (Backups).

en.heading: Going back if something goes wrong
paragraphs: Until the DNS switch nothing is lost: on the old instance Administration → Storage & backup → Move instance → Lift read-only, and everything runs as before. After the switch: switch DNS back and lift the read-only state – what was changed on the new instance in the meantime only comes back with a move in the other direction. The new instance itself returns to its previous state when you replace flowplan.sqlite* and uploads/ with the contents of pre-move-… while the container is stopped.

en.heading: Another domain
paragraphs: If the instance gets a new address, set APP_URL to it and then set up again:
– Passkeys are bound to the domain: everyone signs in with password or SSO and creates them again.
– OIDC: change the redirect address at the provider to /api/auth/callback.
– CalDAV and CardDAV: set up the accounts in the calendar and contacts apps again.
– Incoming webhooks (Git, ticket sync, inbound e-mail) and share links point to the old address.

– Desktop and mobile apps store the server's address. They keep connecting to the old instance; there everyone sees the notice "This instance has moved to …", and changes are refused with a message naming the new address. Sign out in the app and enter the new address (desktop: Profiles → Add profile …). Leave Redirect the web interface off meanwhile: the apps refuse an address that redirects to another site.

en.heading: Example: Hetzner Cloud
paragraphs: A concrete way from a home server to a server at Hetzner, with Docker Compose and Caddy. Plan names and prices change – the Hetzner Console is what counts.

en.heading: Server
paragraphs: Setting Recommendation

Type CAX21 (Arm64, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM) or CX32 (x86, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM), or their current successor. 4 GB is enough for small teams; text recognition of scanned PDFs needs CPU for a moment, local AI (Ollama) much more. The image exists for linux/arm64 and linux/amd64, both types fit.
Location Falkenstein (fsn1) or Nuremberg (nbg1) – Object Storage is available there too.
Image Ubuntu 24.04
Networking Public IPv4 and IPv6. Keep an IPv4 address: not every registry and mail server is reachable over IPv6.
SSH key Add your own public key; never use password sign-in.

Firewall Create and assign a Hetzner Cloud Firewall: inbound TCP 22 only from your address (or your VPN), TCP 80 and 443 and UDP 443 (HTTP/3) from anywhere. Docker bypasses ufw on the server; the Cloud Firewall in front still applies.
Backups Turn on the server's Backups (a surcharge on the server price): daily images of the whole disk, in addition to Flowplan's own backups.

en.heading: Object Storage as S3
paragraphs: – In the Hetzner Console Object Storage → Create bucket, same location as the server (e.g. Falkenstein), visibility private. The name must be unique, e.g. flowplan-.
– Security → S3 credentials → Generate credentials. The secret is shown only once.
– Into the .env:
S3_BUCKET=flowplan-example
S3_ENDPOINT=https://fsn1.your-objectstorage.com
S3_REGION=fsn1
S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=<access key>
S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<secret key>
S3_PREFIX=flowplan

Endpoint and region follow the location: https://.your-objectstorage.com with fsn1 (Falkenstein), nbg1 (Nuremberg) or hel1 (Helsinki) as S3_REGION. With FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, files and backups are stored there encrypted; the Litestream copy is not (see Litestream and encryption). Object Storage is billed monthly, with a base price that includes a quota – see Hetzner for current prices.

en.heading: Docker, Flowplan and Caddy
paragraphs: Install Docker following the official guide for Ubuntu (docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu), then:
mkdir -p /opt/flowplan && cd /opt/flowplan
curl -o .env https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannicschuller/flowplan/main/.env.example
# create compose.yaml and Caddyfile from below, fill in .env
docker compose up -d
compose.yaml:
# Flowplan with Caddy in front (HTTPS from Let's Encrypt). Exactly one instance (SQLite).
services:
flowplan:
image: ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:${FLOWPLAN_VERSION:-latest}
env_file: .env
environment:
FLOWPLAN_DATA_DIR: /app/data
# Caddy is the one proxy in front and sets X-Forwarded-For.
FLOWPLAN_TRUSTED_PROXIES: "1"
volumes:
- flowplan-data:/app/data
restart: unless-stopped
healthcheck:
test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health').then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(1))"]
interval: 30s
timeout: 5s
start_period: 20s
retries: 3
caddy:
image: caddy:2
ports:
environment:
FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN: ${FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN}
volumes:
- ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
- caddy-data:/data
- caddy-config:/config
depends_on:
- flowplan
restart: unless-stopped
volumes:
flowplan-data:
caddy-data:
caddy-config:
Caddyfile:
{$FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN} {
encode zstd gzip
reverse_proxy flowplan:3000
In the .env, besides the old instance's values:
FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN=flowplan.example.org
APP_URL=https://flowplan.example.org
# SMTP: Hetzner blocks outgoing ports 25 and 465 for new accounts – use 587 with STARTTLS.
SMTP_PORT=587
SMTP_SECURE=false
# Only for the move, when the home server is reachable only in the LAN/VPN:
# FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true

For a temporary address during the move, set FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN=new.flowplan.example.org and the matching APP_URL; after Apply, change both to the final domain and restart with docker compose up -d – the same restart applies the move. Caddy can also serve both names: {$FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN}, new.flowplan.example.org { … }.
Prefer Kubernetes? The repository's Helm chart runs on a single server too (with k3s, say); the move then goes through the interface or kubectl exec … node /app/move.mjs (above).

en.heading: The run with the home server
paragraphs: – A day before, lower the DNS record's TTL to 300 seconds.
– Set up the Hetzner server as above, with the same variables as at home (the keys!), and start it with docker compose up -d; create the first account.
– At home Prepare the move; on the Hetzner server Take over from another instance with the home server's public address (or its VPN address with FLOWPLAN_MOVE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true).
– Pre-flight check until no errors remain. Make the source read-only and fetch the last state, Apply, docker compose restart flowplan.
– Point the A and AAAA records to the Hetzner server's addresses, remove the port forwarding at the router.
– Check afterwards, clean up after a few days.
Pens, eraser, shapes, lasso, pictures and audio in a notebook – and the keyboard shortcuts that switch between them.

en.heading: Keyboard shortcuts
paragraphs: Key Does
P H E L T K Pen, highlighter, eraser, lasso, text, laser pointer
⌘ Z / ⇧ ⌘ Z Undo / redo
⌘ C, ⌘ V, ⌘ D, Delete Copy, paste, duplicate, delete the selection
⌘ + / ⌘ − / ⌘ 0 Zoom in, zoom out, fit to width
⇧ ⌘ ↵ New sheet after the current one
⌥ ↓ / ⌥ ↑ Next / previous sheet
⌘ S Save now
On Windows and Linux use Ctrl instead of ⌘ and Alt instead of ⌥. On an iPad with a keyboard the same shortcuts apply.

en.heading: Tools, favourite pens and eraser
paragraphs: Tap the selected tool again (or the gear) to open its settings: line width with presets and a slider, colour with a custom colour (colour area, hex value, eyedropper where the browser has one), and for text the size and font. + saves the current setting as a favourite pen (up to 8, text too); favourites appear in the toolbar and can be reordered or removed with the pencil button next to them. Favourites are kept per device. The eraser has three kinds: whole strokes, parts only (strokes are split, adjustable size) and highlighter only – the writing underneath stays. "Clear page" deletes everything on the sheet after asking; Undo brings it back.

Restyle text afterwards. With the Text tool, tap an existing text box: it opens for editing with a bar above it – font, size (presets, slider or a number, 8–96 pt), bold, italic, underline, alignment (left, centre, right) with line spacing, and colour; ⌘ B, ⌘ I and ⌘ U work while typing. Several text boxes at once: select them with the lasso – the selection bar then shows a second row with the same settings, applied to every selected text box; where they differ it shows "—". Each change can be undone on its own. "Edit text" in the selection bar opens a single text box for typing. The Text tool's panel sets how new text looks. In the PDF export, bold and italic use the standard Helvetica, Times and Courier fonts; the handwriting fonts appear as Helvetica there. Older app versions show such text without this styling; if they save the page, the text stays but the styling is lost.

en.heading: Shapes and ruler
paragraphs: Hold the pen still at the end of a stroke and it straightens into a line, arrow, rectangle, circle, triangle, diamond, polygon or star – squares and circles come out exact, lines snap to 15° steps, ends attach to the corners of other shapes. Keep moving without lifting to resize; Undo brings back the freehand stroke. The Shapes tool (S key) draws shapes directly or recognises them when you lift, optionally with a semi-transparent fill or dashed lines; in the tool's panel you pick the line style by its line sample (the name shows as a tooltip). Tap a shape with the lasso to move its corners, rotate or resize it, or change its colour, fill, line style and arrow heads. The ruler in the toolbar lies on the page at real scale (cm or inches): move it with one finger, turn it with two (it snaps at 0/15/30/45/60/90°); strokes along its edge come out straight and show their length. The set square measures angles between lines, and the compass draws circles and arcs of a set radius.

en.heading: Selecting with the lasso
paragraphs: With the lasso (key L), tap a stroke or text to select just it, or draw a loop around several. Drag the selection to move it; the four corners resize it (Shift or a finger keeps the proportions), the round handle above it rotates it (snapping to 15° steps). On the iPad, two fingers on the selection scale and rotate it. The bar above the selection changes the colour (custom colours too) and line width, cuts, copies, duplicates, brings to front or sends to back, and deletes. Paste cut ink onto another sheet: tap the sheet, then ⌘ V or "Paste". Copied ink is also put on the clipboard as a picture for other apps. Every action can be undone on its own.

en.heading: Converting handwriting to text
paragraphs: When AI is set up on your instance and allowed for the page, "Convert to text" turns the selected handwriting into text with the instance's AI model (it must understand images, e.g. a vision model in Ollama). The selected snippet is sent to the model as a picture. You can edit the recognised text, then insert it in place of the handwriting or next to it, or copy it. The feature is not offered in journals with a PIN or on pages closed to the AI.

en.heading: Pictures, stickers and own paper templates
paragraphs: Pictures and stickers. Use Insert (picture icon) to put a picture from a file, straight from the camera, from the page's pictures, or a sticker on the sheet; you can also paste pictures (⌘ V) or drag them onto a sheet. A picture appears in a frame: drag to move, drag a corner to resize (Shift: freely), use the handle above to rotate. The frame offers crop, bring to front/send to back (over or under the handwriting), opacity, duplicate, delete and "Save as sticker". Tap a picture with the lasso to edit it again. Pictures are attachments of the page, included in search and in the PDF export. Your own stickers (from pictures or lasso selections) are visible only to you, in every notebook of the workspace.

Own paper templates. In the paper dialog, Own › Add template … turns a picture or a PDF page (a planner page, say) into paper, stretched or tiled. Templates belong to the workspace; whoever added one (or an owner) can rename or delete it. Sheets keep their paper even when the template is deleted.

en.heading: Recording audio
paragraphs: Tap the microphone in the notebook bar and choose Start recording. While it runs (up to three hours), Flowplan remembers for everything you write the moment in the recording. The bar shows the time and the level; you can pause and stop. When you stop, the recording is uploaded and attached to the notebook; it counts against your storage. If the page reloads or the connection drops, the recording stays on the device and Flowplan offers to save it the next time you open the notebook.

To play it, choose the recording in the list. What was written during it starts out faded and appears as the recording reaches it. With Play from here (hand icon) or a long press with your finger you jump to the moment something was written. Speed: 1×, 1.5×, 2×. Recordings can be renamed, downloaded and deleted (they go to the trash); they come along with copies and exports of the notebook. In the app, Flowplan needs access to the microphone (Settings › Flowplan › Microphone).

A notebook is a page of sheets to write on – with the Apple Pencil, another tablet pen, a mouse or a finger, like a paper notebook. The sheets sit one below the other and you scroll through them. Each sheet has its paper (lined, grid, dotted, Cornell, music staff …) or a page of a PDF as its background. There is also handwriting in documents: a drawing block in the middle of the text.

en.heading: Creating a notebook
paragraphs: New page → Notebook (or New notebook in the command palette). A new notebook starts with one sheet of lined A4 paper.

From a PDF: in the same dialog, choose a file under Open a PDF as the notebook. Every page of the PDF becomes a sheet with that page as its background – lecture slides, worksheets or forms are then written on as if printed. ⋯ → Import PDF … adds more PDF pages to an existing notebook, after the current sheet. Up to 500 pages per import and 1000 sheets per notebook.

From GoodNotes and other note apps: export the notebooks as PDF and import them under Settings → Import & export → Import with the source GoodNotes – several at once or as a ZIP, every PDF becomes a notebook. Step by step: Moving from GoodNotes.

en.heading: Paper
paragraphs: Template Looks like
Blank no lines
Lined (college) lines 7.1 mm apart (college ruled) with a margin
Lined (wide) lines 8.7 mm apart (wide ruled) with a margin
Grid (5 mm) squared paper
Dotted dots every 5 mm
Cornell notes title band, cue column on the left, summary at the bottom
Music staff 12 staves (8 in landscape)
Plus A4 or Letter, portrait or landscape, and light or dark. On dark paper, black ink shows light and the highlighter glows.
The lines icon in the toolbar (or Change paper … in a sheet's menu) opens the choice. Apply to:
– This sheet – only the current sheet gets its own paper;
– Notebook default – for all sheets without their own paper and for new sheets;
– All sheets – sets the default and removes every sheet's own paper.
Sheets from a PDF keep their PDF page and its size.

en.heading: Writing
paragraphs: Whoever may edit the page writes right away – there is no "Annotate" step as in the PDF viewer. At the top is the toolbar: Pen (with pressure), Highlighter, Eraser (whole strokes or partial), Lasso (move, resize, recolour, copy, duplicate, delete), Text and Laser pointer, three favourite pens, colours, widths and the pen settings. They work as when annotating PDFs: only the pen writes once you have used it, fingers scroll and zoom, a resting hand leaves no marks; holding still at the end of a stroke straightens it into a line, rectangle, ellipse …

Everything is saved as you write (on the right of the toolbar: Saved). Every change of a sheet is a version. When two people write on the same sheet at the same time, both keep their strokes; a notice says that someone wrote along. What others write appears after a few seconds.
Readers of the page see all sheets, zoom and export, but no tools.

Besides the preset widths, the slider button sets any line width, with a preview. The + after the colours opens a custom colour (colour field, hue, hex value); your recent custom colours are remembered on the device. For Text you choose the size (8–96 pt) and the font there: Default, Instrument Sans, Instrument Serif, JetBrains Mono, Caveat or Patrick Hand. In the PDF export Caveat and Patrick Hand come out as Helvetica, Instrument Serif as Times and JetBrains Mono as Courier.

With 'Insert PDF …' (in the plus menu or under 'More actions') you add a PDF to an existing notebook – before the first sheet, after any sheet or at the end; in the page overview, a sheet's menu offers 'Insert PDF before/after …' directly. Each PDF page becomes a sheet of its own with the page as background that you write on as usual (at most 500 pages per PDF, 1000 sheets per notebook). Two fingers zoom smoothly at the spot between them and move the sheets; on a trackpad, pinch or use Ctrl + scroll, and the Apple Pencil keeps writing undisturbed.

PDF as an attachment {since=0.10.2}: in the Insert PDF dialog you choose As sheets (as before) or As an attachment. An attachment stays a whole PDF and does not become a sheet: it sits in the Attachments strip above the sheets and opens with a tap in the side panel beside your sheets – to read, annotate and take regions from, which land on the sheet as a picture with a link to the PDF page. The × on an attachment takes it off the strip; the file stays on the page.
Every tool in detail – keyboard shortcuts, favourite pens, shapes and ruler, lasso, handwriting to text, pictures and stickers, audio – is under Notebook tools.

en.heading: Page overview
paragraphs: Overview, contents and presenting. "All sheets and contents" opens every sheet as a grid. Tap a sheet's bookmark and filter with "Bookmarks only". Search finds titles, typed text and recognised handwriting and marks the matches. To reorder, drag a sheet with the mouse, hold and drag it with a finger or the Pencil, or move it with Alt + arrow keys. Under "Select" (Shift for a range) you duplicate, move or copy several sheets to another notebook, change their paper, export them as PDF or delete them. Deleting can be undone at once and restored for 30 days from "Deleted sheets …". The "Contents" tab lists your chapters (a sheet's menu → "Mark page as a chapter", indent, outdent, rename) and your bookmarks; a tap jumps there. "Insert link …" links to another sheet or page. "Present" shows the notebook full screen, sheet by sheet (arrow keys, Page Up/Down, swipe), with a laser pointer and a marker that fades after a few seconds. Anyone who has the notebook open, even read-only, sees "Follow" and then your sheet and pointer live. Select typed text with the lasso and 'Add to the contents as a heading' adds an entry to the contents that jumps to that spot. With several sheets selected in the overview, 'Paper …' changes the paper of all of them at once.

The sidebar icon on the left of the toolbar shows all sheets as previews; a tap jumps to the sheet. With ⋯ on a preview: New sheet after, Duplicate (with everything on it), Change paper …, Move up, Move down and Delete. You also change the order by dragging a preview or with ⌥ ↑/↓ on the focused preview. + in the toolbar adds a sheet after the current sheet or at the end, as does Add sheet below the last sheet.

en.heading: Exporting as PDF
paragraphs: ⋯ → Export as PDF downloads the notebook as a PDF: one page per sheet in the sheet's size, paper and handwriting as vectors (sharp at any zoom), PDF sheets with their original page including its text. The Markdown export puts the notebook into the ZIP as a PDF as well and writes a short Markdown file with a link to it and the recognised text. The PDF, Word and EPUB exports show the sheets as pictures (Word: only their text). Published and shared notebooks are read-only.

en.heading: Handwriting in documents
paragraphs: Type /draw in a document (also /zeichnen, /dessin, /handwriting or /sketch): a drawing block across the full width appears and you draw in it right away – the toolbar with the block's paper (Blank, Lined, Grid) and Done is already there. {since=0.9.8} With the first new drawing block on a device, a short tip at the top of the block shows for a few seconds where you change the height after Done; tap it to hide it at once. {since=0.10.0} Drag the bottom edge to change the height (or use the arrow keys on the handle); while you draw, the handle is hidden so a resting hand can't move it. {since=0.10.0}

Resting your hand {since=0.9.8}: when you open the block with a pen or a finger, the rest of the app is protected from touches until Done – a resting hand or a stray pen stroke next to the block doesn't scroll, tap anything or move the cursor. To finish, use Done on the block or Esc; when the block's toolbar is scrolled out of view, a separate Done button appears at the top (or bottom) of the screen. If the block scrolls out of sight entirely – say after a swipe with momentum – touches scroll the page again so you can swipe back to it; drawing goes on until Done. {since=0.10.2} While you draw there's no cursor in the text, so what you write with the Apple Pencil stays handwriting and isn't turned into text by Scribble. A hovering Pencil shows a dot where it would draw and highlights the button under it. Opened with the mouse, there is no protection; a click next to the block ends drawing as before.

Drawing again {since=0.10.0}: you open an existing drawing block only with Draw at its top right – with a pen, a finger and the mouse alike, so editing is always intentional. On the surface of a closed block the Pencil behaves like a finger: it scrolls the document and taps, but doesn't draw. A new drawing block still starts in drawing mode right away.

Block menu {since=0.10.0}: next to Draw, … opens the block's actions: Move up and Move down move it by one block, Duplicate puts an independent copy with the same drawing below it, Reset height restores the default height, and Delete removes it (Undo brings it back). This way you reach these actions on an iPad too, where the handle to the left of the block is hard to hit with the pen in your hand. On locked or read-only pages there is neither Draw nor ….

The handwriting belongs to the block and is saved as you draw. For working together this means: when several people draw in the same block at once, their strokes are merged instead of overwritten; the text around it you edit together as always. Copied or duplicated blocks (also into another document) take their drawing along and are independent afterwards. Permissions, locking and the trash work as for the document; on published pages, in share links and in exports the block shows as a picture.

en.heading: Recognising handwriting (iPhone and iPad)
paragraphs: In the Flowplan app for iPhone and iPad the device itself recognises what you write – the strokes do not leave the device for this:

– Search: shortly after saving, the handwriting of a sheet, a drawing block or a PDF page is recognised and its text saved along. Search then also finds notebooks, documents and PDFs by what is handwritten.

– Convert to text: select handwriting with the lasso and choose Convert to text (the Aa icon) in the selection's bar. In a notebook and on PDFs, typed text replaces the strokes in their place; in a drawing block the text becomes a paragraph below the block. Undo brings the strokes back.
In the browser and the desktop app there is no recognition; Convert to text does not appear there. Text typed on sheets, in drawing blocks and on PDFs is searchable everywhere.

en.heading: Limits
paragraphs: – Encrypted spaces have no notebooks and no drawing blocks.
– Locked pages show the handwriting; it can be changed after unlocking.
– A notebook's page versions only hold its appearance; each sheet has its own versions of the handwriting.
– Drawing blocks exist in documents and journal days, not in the documents of database records.
What lands in the inbox and how you hear about it: by e-mail, as a push on phone and desktop or in Telegram, Gotify, ntfy and Matrix.

en.heading: Inbox
paragraphs: The Inbox collects:
– mentions,
– comments that concern you (see below) and replies in text comments you took part in,
– date reminders,
– comments and records from guests via share links,
– pages and workspaces shared with you,
– changes on pages you follow (you follow your own pages when creating them; the bell at the top right toggles following, on a phone Follow in the ⋯ menu),
– messages from automations.

en.heading: Who hears about comments
paragraphs: A new comment – on a page, on a database record or as a new text comment – does not notify the whole workspace, only:
– who follows the page (whoever creates a page follows it automatically; for a record: who follows the database),
– the page's owner,
– for a record: who created it and the people in its person properties (such as Assignee),
– who already commented on the same page or record,

– who is mentioned in the comment with @ – in page and record comments by full name or e-mail address (@Anna Berg). Someone mentioned who would be notified anyway gets a single notification, the mention.

Replies in a text comment reach everyone who has written in that thread and the people mentioned in it. The author and anyone who may not see the page or the record are never notified. To keep up with a page, follow it with the bell.

By default what concerns you directly – mentions, shared pages, comments, reminders – arrives in the inbox, as push, by e-mail and in connected chat apps. Guest comments come without e-mail and chat app. Changes on pages you follow and automations only land in the inbox, so that not every small edit triggers a notification or mail. Under Settings → Notifications this can be changed per kind and channel; Reset to defaults restores the initial state.
Retention: read notifications are deleted after 90 days, unread ones after a year; at most the newest 1,000 per person are kept. The inbox shows the newest 100.

For administrators: security incidents of the instance. Admins see their own row Security incidents of the instance among the notification kinds: what the detection rules find on the whole instance (password guessing, new admin rights, probing …). Each admin chooses how incidents arrive – inbox, push, e-mail and chat apps are on by default – and which: All incidents (default) or Critical only. The choice applies to every channel of this kind; every incident still shows under Administration → Threats & incidents. Clicking or tapping the notification opens the incident's page. The row Security notices is only about your own account (a new sign-in, a wrong journal PIN, a chat app switched off); whoever had switched channels off there before the update has them off for security incidents too. Other people don't see the row.

Unread items are marked and can be filtered. A click opens the spot, for text comments the thread directly. Notifications without a page lead to their place in the app: a security incident to its page under Administration → Threats & incidents, a new sign-in to the signed-in devices, a chat app switched off to its connections – also when tapping the push notification and through the link in e-mails and chat apps.

en.heading: Notifications from workflows
paragraphs: Workflows use two kinds of their own that you can switch off per channel under Settings → Notifications: Messages from workflows (what a workflow sends) and Errors, pauses and approvals of workflows – so you never miss an approval when you mute the messages. An approval notification opens the workflow page on the Approvals tab.

en.heading: Study reminders
paragraphs: The daily study reminder of flashcards is a kind of its own: Study reminders. By default it comes as push only – not into the inbox, not by e-mail and not in chat apps; unlike the other kinds, push does not hang on the inbox here. Switch the inbox on for it and it is listed there too. A tap opens Study. You set the time under Study, not here.

en.heading: E-mail
paragraphs: If a mail server is set up on the instance, unread notifications arrive by e-mail as a digest after ten minutes – one mail for everything that has piled up, each notification at most once. Under Settings → Notifications, the E-mail column can be switched on and off per kind. Invitations to a workspace and pages shared with you arrive by e-mail right away.

en.heading: Weekly digest
paragraphs: Under Settings → Notifications → Weekly digest you subscribe to an e-mail that arrives every Monday at 7 am in your time zone (your browser's time zone is saved when you switch it on):
– Changed in pages you follow – with the workspace and who changed it (changes of the last seven days, by others only),
– Overdue tasks and Open tasks – as in My tasks, across all workspaces.

With a short AI summary of the changes (only shown when AI is on for you) puts a few bullet points before the list. The AI only reads pages it may read for you, with your AI provider. If AI is off or the request fails, the e-mail comes as a plain list. If there is nothing to report in a week, no e-mail is sent. The digest needs a mail server to be set up.

en.heading: Push notifications
paragraphs: Under Settings → Notifications:
– Enable push – the browser asks for permission. This applies per device.
– In the card Notification kinds, set the switches Inbox, Push and E-mail per kind – every change is saved at once. On a phone every kind is a card of its own with three labelled switches.
– Use Send test notification to check that everything arrives (see below).
Push notifications open the page concerned. No document content appears on the lock screen.
> iPhone and iPad (iOS 16.4 or later): open Flowplan in Safari over HTTPS, Add to Home Screen and start it from that icon. Only there can push be enabled.
Signing out, the end of a session or a locked account end the push subscription; enable it again after the next sign-in if needed.

In the apps for iPhone, iPad and Android, notifications come through the app: it asks for permission after the first sign-in, and the number of unread ones shows on the app icon. Notification kinds apply there as well. These notifications are end-to-end encrypted and therefore show their text – the relay, Apple and Google cannot read it, see Push relay.

en.heading: Test notification
paragraphs: Settings → Notifications → Send test notification immediately sends a notification "Test notification – everything works." to all your push targets: every browser with push enabled and every app with notifications allowed. It takes the same way as every notification – Web Push, the push relay or Expo – but leaves nothing in the inbox. Tapping it opens these settings.
After at most ten seconds, each device is listed with the channel it went through (Relay · end-to-end encrypted, Expo or Web Push) and what happened:
– Delivered – handed to Apple, Google or the browser's push service. If nothing shows up anyway, check the device: are notifications allowed for Flowplan? An active Focus is mentioned.
– Registration expired – open the app once, it registers again. For a browser whose subscription expired, enable push there again.
– Notifications turned off – allow them in the app or in the device's system settings.

– Push relay not set up, unreachable or instance not verified – this concerns the instance, not your device; the message gives the reason (e.g. PUSH_RELAY=off, APP_URL without HTTPS, /.well-known/flowplan-push not reachable). See Configuration.
– No devices registered – enable push above or open the app and allow notifications.

The test only goes to your own devices, regardless of Notification kinds and Focus filters – the device's own permission and Focus still apply. At most five tests in ten minutes. The result never shows tokens or keys; administrators also see a diagnostics line with the relay address, whether /.well-known/flowplan-push is enabled and the instance's address (APP_URL).

> The desktop app has no Web Push. It asks for new notifications itself and shows them as system notifications, with the unread count on the app icon. There, Settings → Notifications shows a switch for the app's notifications instead of Enable push; Do Not Disturb and All Profiles are in the app's Notifications menu. Notification kinds apply here too: only kinds with push pop up.

en.heading: Chat apps
paragraphs: Instead of (or besides) push and e-mail, notifications arrive right away in a chat app: Telegram, Gotify, ntfy or Matrix. Under Settings → Notifications → Chat apps you connect one target per service; which kinds arrive there you choose in the Notification kinds card, column Chat apps. By default these are mentions, shared pages, comments, reminders and security notices – not guest comments, changes on pages you follow or automations. What is switched off for the inbox does not reach the chat app either.
Service What you enter

Telegram – the instance's bot Nothing: Create a connection link, open the link on the device with Telegram and tap Start (or send the bot /start ). The code is valid for 15 minutes and only once. Only available when the administration has set up a bot.

Telegram – own bot Bot token (from @BotFather), your chat ID (e.g. from @userinfobot) or @channelname, optionally an own API address – for a self-hosted Bot API server or a relay/proxy. Message your bot once so it may write to you.
Gotify Server address and app token (create one in Gotify under Apps). Tapping the notification opens Flowplan.

ntfy Server (empty: https://ntfy.sh), topic, optionally an access token or user and password. On ntfy.sh every topic is public – choose a name that is hard to guess, or your own server with authentication.
Matrix Homeserver, room ID (!abc:example.org, in Element under Room settings → Advanced) and the access token of an account that is in the room – preferably a separate bot account.

Send test message sends a message right away and shows the outcome: delivered, Credentials refused (HTTP 401), Not found (HTTP 404) (address, topic, room or chat ID), Server not reachable or Internal addresses are blocked. Change takes new details; an empty token field keeps the stored token. Disconnect deletes the connection with its credentials.

What a message says: as with push, the kind, a short excerpt of the notification and a link to the place. With Include the text off, only “New notification in Flowplan” with the link. Notifications from end-to-end encrypted spaces always arrive without content. Tokens or other secrets are never part of a message.

Credentials (bot, app and access tokens, passwords) are stored only encrypted, like other stored secrets, and never shown again – only “Token set (…abcd)”. Connecting and disconnecting appear under Settings → Security check → Sign-ins & changes.

Delivery: messages go through a queue like push and e-mail. If the service does not answer, Flowplan retries with growing pauses and gives up after six attempts; if the service throttles (HTTP 429), Flowplan waits as long as asked. At most 20 messages a minute go to one target. What you already read in the app is not sent any more. If the service refuses a target three times in a row (401/403/404 or a blocked internal address), Flowplan switches it off and tells you in the inbox; Switch on again resumes it once fixed.

For administrators: the switch Operations alerts sends failed backups, full storage, errors of background workers and many failed sign-ins (at most once a day per alert) to your chat apps – also without a webhook under Monitoring. Security incidents arrive through the row Security incidents of the instance of the notification kinds, not twice.
Which services and servers are allowed is up to the administration (Administration → Chat apps).
Flowplan runs in the browser, can be installed as an app and keeps working without a connection.
More on this topic: What works offline · Desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux · Apps for iPhone, iPad and Android · Widgets and notifications · Capturing, sharing and scanning in the apps

en.heading: Work without a connection
paragraphs: Flowplan always saves documents locally in the browser first (IndexedDB) and syncs them with the server as soon as it can be reached. If the connection drops, you simply keep writing; other people's changes are merged when you reconnect.

Without a connection, a small yellow icon sits at the right of the top bar instead of a full-width banner. A tap explains that you see the last saved state; Esc or a tap outside closes it. Screen readers still hear the change. {since=0.9.7}

While the server restarts (an update, maintenance) the reverse proxy answers instead of Flowplan – Traefik for example with “404 page not found”. Flowplan stays on the page you are on and keeps what you type; it is sent as soon as the server is back. Reloading the page in that time opens the stored copy if offline use is on on this device. {since=0.9.7}

en.heading: Turn on offline use
paragraphs: Under Settings → Offline & devices, the device also stores the app, the workspace, all readable pages and the records and files you open later. Then you can open pages, read documents and databases and edit text even without a connection.
– Online, the current state always comes from the server; the copy only serves without a connection.
– If the sign-in has expired, Flowplan shows the sign-in page online – without a connection, the stored copy still opens.
– The copies contain private content. They are removed when you sign out, when you turn the feature off and when another person signs in.

Flowplan asks. {since=0.9.7} Offline is off on every new device. The introduction offers it on its device; every further browser and device asks once with a small card: Work offline on this device too? with Use offline, Later and Don't ask again. The device remembers the answer; Later asks again after a week. No card where offline cannot work (such as plain http), in the phone and tablet apps (they ask themselves), for guests, in the demo or with the copy already on.
The whole app on the device

The copy holds the whole app – not only the parts you already opened online. The editor, calendar, timeline and gallery views, dashboards, charts, whiteboards, notebooks, math, Mermaid diagrams and the PDF viewer then load without a connection as well.
– Storage: about 18 MB on the device (around 5 MB to download), once per version. Flowplan only stores the app's files when the device has enough space.

– New version: after an update, Flowplan loads the new version's files with the next refresh; files that did not change are taken over instead of downloaded again. As soon as the new version is stored completely, the old one is removed.
– Settings → Offline & devices shows a line like “The app is stored for offline use (version 0.7.0) · 18 MB” – or how many files are still missing.

– If a part is missing without a connection after all, Flowplan shows “Not available offline – try again when you're online” with Try again in its place; the rest of the app keeps working, and the part loads by itself once the connection is back. A record whose content is not in the copy shows “This record is not available offline.”
The copy stays current

While Flowplan is open, it keeps the copy up to date on its own: at start, when the connection comes back, when you bring the app back to the foreground, and every 6 hours. It only loads what changed since the last update – usually two small requests.
– New pages are added; changed pages, records and documents are loaded again.
– Deleted pages and pages you may no longer read (including a journal behind a PIN) leave the copy together with their records and files.
– When an update takes a moment, Updating offline copy … shows briefly in the bottom left corner.
– When the sign-in has expired, Flowplan does not update – the existing copy stays as it is.
Settings → Offline & devices shows the state, for example “Offline copy updated 2 h ago · 312 pages · 85 MB”. Update now loads every page again.

Also store record contents and files also stores the documents of all database records and the files of the pages, even ones you have never opened – at most 200 MB and only while the device has enough space. Without it, only records and files you opened once are kept. Turning it off removes the records and files stored in addition.
Without a connection, Flowplan also shows the date of the copy when it is older than 7 days (“Offline copy from Oct 12”).

> Installed as an app (Chrome, Edge, Android), Flowplan also updates the copy in the background while the app is closed, when the browser allows it (Periodic Background Sync). The browser decides whether and how often – usually only for apps used often. Records and files never opened are loaded only by the open app.

en.heading: Database records offline
paragraphs: Changes to records without a connection appear in the views right away and are collected on the device. As soon as the connection is back, they go to the server one after another. If the server is briefly unreachable while they are sent – say, during a restart behind the proxy (answers 502, 503, 504, 429 or 408) –, the changes stay queued and go out on the next attempt instead of being discarded. If someone changed the same record in the meantime, Flowplan merges the changes field by field; if the same field was changed on both sides or the record was deleted, you decide in the conflict dialog.
> A database's schema – properties and views – can only be changed with a connection.

en.heading: Offline in the app for iPhone and iPad
paragraphs: The app for iPhone and iPad keeps the offline copy itself – for every instance, self-hosted ones included. (iOS gives apps no service worker for addresses of your choice; in Safari and in the Android app, Flowplan works offline as in the browser.)

– Turn it on as everywhere under Settings → Offline & devices – per profile of the app. It also says “Stored in the Flowplan app”; state, size, version, Update now, Also store record contents and files and Remove offline copies work as in the browser.

– Without a connection – at start or when the instance cannot be reached – the app opens the stored copy: the same page you were on, with the offline icon in the top bar. {since=0.9.7} Pages, databases, records, calendars, dashboards and the editor run from the copy. The app shows its “No connection” screen only when there is no copy for the profile.

– Changes offline: text in documents and changes to records are collected on the device as in the browser and synced as soon as the instance answers again. Then the app switches to the current page by itself – once you are not typing.
– Kept current: as in the browser while the app is open, and also every time it comes to the foreground; only what changed is loaded.

– Where it is stored: in the app's container, encrypted until the first unlock after a restart and not in backups. The copy belongs to the profile: Sign out in Flowplan and Sign out and remove the profile in the app's settings delete it; another profile never sees it.

– Limits: files over 25 MB, the PDF viewer and text recognition (OCR) need a connection in the app; at most 2 GB per profile, and the app always leaves 300 MB free. The copy needs a Flowplan server with this offline support (0.7.0 or newer); with older servers the app shows its “No connection” screen without a connection, as before.

en.heading: Install as an app
paragraphs: Browser on a computer:
– Chrome, Edge: the install icon in the address bar.
– Safari on the Mac: File → Add to Dock. iPhone and iPad:
Share → Add to Home Screen. Only this way are push notifications possible there. Android:
Menu → Install app.
The installed app opens in its own window without browser bars.

en.heading: Share to Flowplan
paragraphs: When Flowplan is installed as an app on Android (Chrome), it appears in the Share menu of other apps. Shared text and links land in a preview; Save as page creates a page from it in the chosen space. Without being signed in, you first go to the sign-in and then back to the preview. iOS does not offer this menu to web apps.

The preview asks whether to save as a page, as a record in a database or – for links – as a bookmark. As a record, title, text and link (or the article text) go into the record; the link lands in the database's first URL property, otherwise in the text, and the database's default record template applies. If there is a default capture database (see below), as a record is preselected with it. Include article text loads the web page on the server and keeps its main text without navigation, ads and scripts (public addresses only).

en.heading: Web clipper in the browser
paragraphs: Under Settings → Web clipper you find the button Save to Flowplan. Dragged into the bookmarks bar, it opens a small window on any web page with the title, address and selected text – the same preview as when sharing. After saving, the window closes.

en.heading: Capture into a database
paragraphs: For an inbox, e.g. with PARA: Quick capture on the start page, ⌘ ⌥ N, > capture in the quick search or – with the installed app – a long press on the app icon → its capture shortcut open a small window with title and text. It is saved as a record in the chosen database; without a connection it waits on the device and is created once the connection is back.

Improve text (with the AI icon) below the fields has the writing assistant improve the spelling and grammar of title and text. The result appears as a preview: Use puts it into the fields, Keep original leaves everything as it was – nothing is saved until Capture. The AI is told to keep shorthand such as #tag, @person, !high or "tomorrow" and links as they are; if it changed or removed any of them, the preview lists them before you take it. The button is only there with a connection and when the writing assistant is allowed for you and the chosen database; as in the editor, it runs through the server or on the device. The desktop app's capture window gets the same button with its next version (see Quick capture (desktop)).
Phones can open straight into capturing: Capture right on opening. {since=0.9.7}

Use as default for capturing (in the window) or Settings → Web clipper → Capture sets the database that share, the web clipper and quick capture preselect – per person and workspace. The database's default record template applies, so new records land e.g. straight in the "Inbox" view.

en.heading: Bookmarks
paragraphs: Bookmarks land in the Bookmarks database of the chosen space; it is created the first time, with link, website, folder, note, date and "read" as well as the views All, Cards and Unread. The article text that was taken along is in the record. Choose bookmarks file imports the HTML file that Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari create when exporting bookmarks – including folders and dates; links that already exist are skipped.

en.heading: Light and dark
paragraphs: Flowplan follows your device's light or dark mode by itself – also when it changes while Flowplan is open (for example automatically in the evening). Under Settings → Appearance & language → Appearance you choose a fixed Light or Dark instead; Automatic follows the device again. The choice applies per device. Sign-in, public pages and forms, the website and this documentation follow the device as well, the apps also with their own screens and widgets.

Animations sets how much moves in Flowplan. Normal: menus and dialogs fade in briefly and grow slightly from where they open, side panels and sheets slide in from the edge; opening a page only cross-fades the content area, and the title is in its place at once. Reduced: only a short fade, nothing slides or grows. Off: nothing moves. Toggles, drag and drop and side panels work the same at every level. If "Reduce motion" is on in your device's settings, animations always stay off. The setting belongs to your account and applies on all devices, including the desktop app and phones. {since=0.9.6}

Under Editor, Always show block handles shows the handle ⋮⋮ next to every block, not only at the one under the pointer or cursor (see Working with blocks), and Show line numbers by default turns on line numbers for every code block without a setting of its own – both on this device only, like the appearance. Formatting toolbar shows or hides the fixed bar above the text; hidden, the text menu carries all formatting (see Format text). Show pages at full width makes all pages and records opened as a page use the whole width of the window, as if each had Full width on. Only your view changes; each page's own Full width (… menu, then marked "Your setting") still applies for everyone else. {since=0.9.6} Text comments shows open text comments on wide screens in the margin beside the text or below the document. {since=0.10.2} These choices apply to your account on all devices.

Below pages and records Flowplan shows Related pages, Linked from and Unlinked mentions. If you don't need them, turn off Settings → Appearance & language → Show related pages and backlinks – also on this device only. The panels then appear neither below pages nor in records.

Settings → Appearance & language → Page icon sets where a page's icon sits: Above the title (the default) shows it large above the title, Next to the title small to the left of the title on its first line – like a classic document, with less space above the text. This applies to documents, databases, whiteboards, journal days and every other page; a cover stays above it. The choice applies to your account on all devices and only changes what you see: the page's title and icon stay as they are, others keep their own setting, and published pages show the icon above the title.

Settings → Appearance & language → What's new after updates decides whether New in Flowplan appears once after Flowplan was updated: Show all (the default) shows the notes of every skipped version, Only breaking changes appears only when one of them has changes you need to adapt to, and shows only those, Never does not show the dialog. The choice applies to your account on all devices, including the iPhone, iPad and Android apps. Whatever you choose, What's new opens the latest versions' notes any time: in the account menu ⋯ at the bottom of the sidebar (on a phone under More), with ⌘/Ctrl K → "What's new", under Settings → Appearance & language and under About Flowplan. Published pages never show the dialog.

After a reload Flowplan opens the workspace that was last open on this device. For this the browser keeps only the workspace's id in the cookie flowplan-workspace; an invitation or a link to a page in another workspace takes precedence. The width of the sidebar and the width and pinned state of the Ask AI panel are kept in the cookie flowplan-layout – a functional cookie holding just three numbers, valid for one year.

en.heading: Workflows on the phone
paragraphs: On a phone, a workflow page shows the status, the on/off switch, the flow as a list, the runs and the approvals; editing happens on a tablet or computer. An approval notification opens the page right at the Approvals tab. Workflow pages are not available offline.
No server of your own yet? Three ways to a running instance without setting up Docker by hand. All of them use the same image as the Compose file below.
Method Data HTTPS and address
Render SQLite on a persistent disk Automatic, https://.onrender.com or your domain
DigitalOcean App Platform PostgreSQL (dev database), files in a Spaces bucket Automatic, https://.ondigitalocean.app or your domain
Any server (Hetzner, Netcup, IONOS …) SQLite in a Docker volume on the server Caddy with a Let's Encrypt certificate for your domain

en.heading: Render
paragraphs: Deploy to Render →

The button reads the Blueprint render.yaml from the repository: a web service from the image ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest in Frankfurt, a 5 GB disk on /app/data and the health check on /api/health.
– Click the button, sign in to Render and confirm the Blueprint. The SMTP fields can stay empty (see E-mail).

– Render generates FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN. Once the deploy is done, copy it from the service's Environment tab and open https://.onrender.com/register?setup= – this first account administers the instance.

Costs: persistent disks need a paid instance – the Blueprint uses Starter, the smallest one with a disk; the disk is billed per GB on top (see Render's pricing). For more than a handful of people choose a larger instance (Sizing). On the free instance the data would be lost on every restart.

Address: without APP_URL, Flowplan uses Render's own address (RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL, or else https:// with RENDER_EXTERNAL_HOSTNAME). For your own domain, add it under Settings → Custom Domains and set APP_URL=https://flowplan.example.com under Environment – ideally before the first account, because passkeys are bound to the address.

Persistence and updates: everything lives on the disk – Render runs a service with a disk as exactly one instance and stops it briefly on every deploy. Render keeps snapshots of the disk; for backups away from Render, add S3 (Storage, S3 and backups). To update, start a Manual Deploy: Render pulls the :latest image again.

en.heading: DigitalOcean App Platform
paragraphs: Deploy to DigitalOcean →
The button reads .do/deploy.template.yaml: a service from the image, a PostgreSQL 16 dev database and the health check on /api/health, in Frankfurt (fra).

App Platform has no persistent volumes: the container's disk is reset on every deploy and restart. That is why the template uses PostgreSQL instead of SQLite (DATABASE_URL points at the database) and expects a bucket for files:

– Uploads: create a Spaces bucket and a Spaces access key, and fill in S3_BUCKET, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (S3_ENDPOINT is preset for Frankfurt, https://fra1.digitaloceanspaces.com). Flowplan then puts every file into the bucket and fetches missing ones back after a deploy. Without a bucket, uploaded files are lost on the next deploy.
– FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN (generate with openssl rand -hex 24): the first account only via /register?setup=.

– FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (generate with openssl rand -base64 32): encrypts the files in the bucket and protects stored secrets such as API keys. It must be set here, because a secrets.key on the container's disk would be replaced on every deploy. Keep a copy in a password manager.

– Optional WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY and WEB_PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY (npx web-push generate-vapid-keys): without them, new keys are made on every deploy and push in the browser stops until people turn it on again. Push to the apps is not affected.

App Platform cannot generate secrets itself, so you enter these values when creating the app (or later under the component's Settings → Environment Variables). APP_URL is App Platform's ${APP_URL}: the ondigitalocean.app address, or your domain once you add it under Settings → Domains – then deploy again.

Database: a dev database has no backups and is meant for trying out. For real use, upgrade it to a managed database cluster, or attach an existing one with PostgreSQL 16 or newer (PostgreSQL). The image ships pg_dump and pg_restore, so Flowplan's own scheduled backups work on PostgreSQL too – store them in the bucket (Storage, S3 and backups). The connection is encrypted; uselibpqcompat=true in DATABASE_URL accepts DigitalOcean's own certificate authority, as psql does with sslmode=require. If the log reports permission denied for schema public, the dev database's role may not create tables – use a managed database cluster, where the database owner can (Role without superuser rights).
Updates: start a new deploy (Actions → Force Rebuild and Deploy); App Platform pulls the :latest image again.

en.heading: Any server: cloud-init or install script
paragraphs: For a virtual server (VPS) with Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 12 at any provider. Most of them – Hetzner Cloud, Netcup, IONOS, DigitalOcean Droplets, Vultr, Scaleway, OVHcloud – accept a cloud-init file as "user data" or "cloud config" when you create the server.
– Point your domain's DNS record (A, and AAAA for IPv6) to the server – with a new server, as soon as you know its address.
– Copy deploy/cloud-init.yaml, set the one line FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN=flowplan.example.com and paste it as user data when creating the server.
– After a few minutes, sign in with SSH and read /root/flowplan-README.txt: it holds the address and the link for the first account. Progress is logged in /var/log/flowplan-install.log.
On a server that already runs, the install script does the same:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannicschuller/flowplan/main/deploy/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- flowplan.example.com
What the script sets up:
– Docker with the Compose plugin from Docker's own package repository (skipped when it is already there).

– /opt/flowplan with compose.yaml (Flowplan and Caddy, which fetches and renews the HTTPS certificate itself), the Caddyfile and a .env readable only by root. Its secrets are generated on the server with openssl: FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN and FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY – keep a copy of the key in a password manager, encrypted backups cannot be read without it.
– The data in the Docker volume flowplan-data. It survives updates and restarts; for backups off the server add S3 or SFTP (Storage, S3 and backups).

– Firewall (ufw): only SSH, 80 and 443 stay open. On a server with a firewall of its own, run the script with FLOWPLAN_FIREWALL=off. Ports 80 and 443 must be free – if another web server already holds them, put Flowplan behind it instead (Coolify and reverse proxies).
– Automatic security updates of the system (unattended-upgrades).

– Image updates are off by default: you update when it suits you with cd /opt/flowplan && docker compose pull && docker compose up -d – the administration tells you about new releases. For an automatic weekly update (Sunday night), set FLOWPLAN_AUTO_UPDATE=weekly in the cloud-init file (or before bash in the command), or later run systemctl enable --now flowplan-update.timer.

Without a domain (FLOWPLAN_DOMAIN= left empty, or the script without an argument), Flowplan starts at http:// without a certificate – fine for a test, see Without HTTPS. To switch to a domain later, point its DNS record to the server and run the script again with the domain: it sets APP_URL and the Caddyfile, and keeps the data and secrets. Do it before the first account if you can, because passkeys are bound to the address.
Further settings (e-mail, single sign-on, S3) go into /opt/flowplan/.env, followed by docker compose up -d in /opt/flowplan – see Configuration.
Every instance describes its own API as an OpenAPI 3.1 document:
– GET /api/openapi.json – the document. Its servers entry carries the instance's address (APP_URL).
– /api/docs – the same description for reading: every path by section, parameters, requests, answers and schemas.

Both are only available to signed-in people and with an API token (Authorization: Bearer fp_…, any scope); without signing in /api/openapi.json answers 401 and /api/docs asks to sign in. Instances that want to show the description publicly set FLOWPLAN_PUBLIC_API_DOCS=true; visitors then only see the major version (0.x) under info.version, signed-in people the exact one.
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer fp_…" https://flowplan.example.com/api/openapi.json > openapi.json

It lists every endpoint an API token may call: workspace and pages, search, files, imports and exports, webhooks, the MCP server and POST /api/command with a schema for each commonly used action (page.create, row.create, row.update, webhook.delete …) plus the list of all other actions. Each endpoint names its error codes (400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 413, 429) and the rate limits; calendar subscriptions and CalDAV are noted as external accesses with their own link.

Uploaded images have a placeholder: the answer of POST /api/upload names, under placeholder, the size the image is shown in (w, h) and a ThumbHash (hash, base64) – a blurred preview in about 25 bytes. GET /api/files/placeholders?ids=… returns the same for up to 100 files and profile pictures (avatar:), but only for files you may download; anything else is left out of the answer. For older files the placeholder is computed on the first request. Files of encrypted spaces never have one – the server cannot see their content.

The document is built from the code: where the server validates input with zod (properties and views of a database, the actions, export options), the same schemas are used; the rest is described from the routes in lib/openapi.ts. A test keeps them together – every route under app/api, every action of command() and the SDKs.

en.heading: Clients
paragraphs: Two thin, dependency-free clients are generated from the document, in the source under sdk/:
– TypeScript (sdk/typescript/flowplan.ts): one file, ESM, built on fetch, with types for every answer and action. Copy the file into your project and you are done:
import { FlowplanClient } from "./flowplan.js";
const client = new FlowplanClient({ baseUrl: "https://flowplan.example.com", token: "fp_…" });
const { workspace, pages } = await client.bootstrap();
