paragraphs: When a rule is not enough any more – several steps, waits, approvals, AI, e-mails or other services –, the Open in canvas icon next to the rule opens it as a workflow: a workflow page next to the database with the rule as its draft. The rule keeps running until you activate the workflow; then it is replaced by a reference in the same change (“Extended as a workflow”). So both never run at once, and never neither.
The difference: a rule acts for the database, a workflow runs as the person who activates it – the activate dialog says so.

> Rules run on the server, however a record changes. What a rule changes does not trigger further rules, so rules cannot loop. Flowplan checks overdue records every few minutes; each rule fires once per record and date. Notifications appear as “Database automations” and can be switched off in the settings.

en.heading: Scheduled automations
paragraphs: With the trigger it is time (schedule) a rule creates a new record regularly, for weekly reports, monthly closings or maintenance:

– When: daily or every N days, weekly or every N weeks on a weekday, or monthly or every N months on a day (the 31st becomes the last day in shorter months), each at a time in your time zone. Examples: “Every Monday at 09:00”, “Monthly on day 1”, “Every 3 days”.

– Then: Create a record from a record template (properties and text) or empty. Date fields can be set relative to the run, e.g. “Due: +3 days”; 0 means the same day. Or create a task as a record in a task database, such as “Standup {{Today}}” for the person who saves the rule {since=0.10.2}. If that fails once, the date counts as done and the message is in your inbox.
The suggestion “Create a record every Monday at 09:00” sets this up with the default template.

> A scheduled rule runs once per date – also after a restart – and only from the moment it was saved. Dates on which the server was not running are not made up one by one; the latest missed one runs once. The rule creates records on behalf of the person who last changed it; if they lose edit rights or the database is locked, the rule rests. Switching it on or off does not change the person.
Repeating tasks, whose next record only appears once the previous one is done, are set in the record, see Repeating tasks.

en.heading: WIP limits
paragraphs: On a board, View → WIP limits sets a maximum per column, e.g. “In progress: 3”.
– The column header then shows 2/3.
– When it holds more, the column is marked.
– With lock, the column takes no further records – wherever they come from.

en.heading: Sprints
paragraphs: A view of the type Sprints (backlog and planning) plans work in time boxes. Set up sprints adds the “Sprint” property and the first sprint the first time.

– Planning: drag records from the backlog into a sprint – with the mouse by the record, on touch devices hold the ⋮⋮ handle briefly and drag – or use Move to, also on phones. With the keyboard: focus the handle, press Space, choose the section with ↑/↓, Space or Enter drops, Esc cancels.
– A sprint has a name, start, end and goal; + Sprint adds the next one.
– Start and Complete: when completing, choose where unfinished records go – the next sprint or back to the backlog.
– Measure size in: number of records or a number property such as story points.
– Burndown: the running sprint shows the work left per day against the ideal line.
– Velocity: closed sprints show what was committed and what was completed.

en.heading: Time tracking
paragraphs: A property of the type Time tracking adds up the time worked on a record. Optionally it shows an estimate from a number property in hours next to it.
– In the record: Start and Stop – each person has at most one running timer, a new one stops the old one.
– Add time: a duration as 45, 1:30 or 1.5h, with a date and a note.
– Correcting: you delete your own entries; owners can correct everyone's.

– … → Time report: the time report of this database, switchable to the whole workspace (see Time reports and billing). The report across all databases is also under Settings → Time; there the filters carry their labels above the report, two side by side on phones.

en.heading: Time reports and billing
paragraphs: The time report sums up the time entries of a database or of the whole workspace.
– Period: This week (from Monday), This month, Last month or a custom period with start and end date (at most three years). The server's time zone applies.

– Filters: person, database (in the workspace), project, billing status and billable yes/no. Project is the record a record's first relation points to (not the parent relation of subtasks) – such as the project of a task. Records without a relation are listed under No project.

– Group by person, project, record, database, day or week. The totals come first (total, open, billed, not billable and – with hourly rates – the amount), then a bar chart and a table per group. Clicking a bar filters by that person, project or database.
– Time entries: the single entries with date, person, record, project, note, duration and billing status (the first 1000; the export contains all).

– Export: CSV (commas, decimal points) for spreadsheets and scripts, CSV for Excel with semicolons, decimal commas and a BOM, as a German Excel opens it correctly with a double click. Cells a spreadsheet would run as a formula start with an apostrophe.
– Print outputs totals, chart and table (also save as PDF); expanded time entries come along.

Who sees what: everyone sees their own time entries and the entries of others on records they may read. If the permissions of the property (who may read it, see Property visibility) hide the time property from someone, they only see their own time there. Own time on a record that has become private since appears without a title as “Record without access”.

Billing status: every time entry is open, billed or not billable. Whoever may edit the record and the time property changes the status – one by one in the list of time entries, or with Mark as billed for all open entries of the current selection. Entries that are not billable stay as they are, as do running timers. Every change is in the activity log (time.billing).

Hourly rates (optional): workspace owners set a rate per person and/or per project under Hourly rates, plus the currency (e.g. EUR, CHF). A project's rate takes precedence over the person's. Members with edit rights in the workspace see amounts; readers and guests see hours only.

Through the API: GET /api/time-reports with page or workspace and the same filters (format=csv or format=excel for the files), POST /api/time-reports with { "action": "billing", "status": "billed", "filter": { … } }.

en.heading: Records from all databases
paragraphs: My tasks shows the records of every database of the workspace that has a status or a done checkbox in one list, together with the tasks from documents (My tasks). {since=0.9.8} By default these are the open ones assigned to you – through any person property.
– You can filter by due date and person; Source: Databases shows only records, and under Databases only: you pick databases and search text. {since=0.9.8}
– Which date counts as the due date is set per database – see When is a record due?
– Save as view turns a filter into a personal view of its own, e.g. “All my open tickets in all projects”.

en.heading: Import from Jira and Trello
paragraphs: Settings → Import & export → Import → Jira or Trello takes a Jira CSV export (all fields) or a Trello JSON export.
It becomes a new database with a table and a board. It brings over:
– status or list, priority, type, labels, dates and story points,
– assignees – as a person property when they are all members,
– checklists, and parent issues as subtasks,
– descriptions as content and comments as comments,
– attachments as links (the files stay at Jira or Trello).
Relations connect databases, rollups calculate across linked records, formulas calculate values from the properties of the same record.
> This is about the properties of database records. The properties of pages (under the page title) apply in the whole workspace or only in one space, see Scope.

en.heading: Edit properties
paragraphs: A click on the column header or View and properties opens the property dialog: name, type (one of 24 property types), options and format. Changing the type keeps existing values as far as they fit. Number formats cover currencies, percent, decimal places and thousands separators and also apply to formulas with a numeric result; date fields show short, long or ISO dates and optionally times. Below the field, + Time shows a time field that starts at 09:00 (on today if there is no date yet); Remove time makes it an all-day date again, and Remove date clears both date and time. {since=0.9.8}

If a date needs no time – for example in a form other people fill in – switch off With time in the property dialog. {since=0.10.0} Then + Time no longer appears anywhere for that property: not in the table, the record, forms and surveys, the calendar or quick capture. Values that already have a time keep it and still show it; Remove time stays available for them, but no new time can be added. The dialog shows how many records still have a time. The API and MCP refuse a new time; the CSV import, automations ("Now") and quick capture take the date only. Switched on (the default), everything works as before.

URL, email and phone properties show as links in tables, lists, boards, galleries and records: web addresses open in a new tab (shortened to host and path, the full address in the tooltip), email addresses in your mail app, phone numbers in your phone app. To change one, click the pencil next to the link (on hover or via Tab on a computer, always shown on phones) or the empty part of the cell; Enter saves, Esc discards. Only http:// and https:// addresses, email addresses and phone numbers become links – anything else stays plain text.

en.heading: Rename and merge options
paragraphs: Records store a select or multi-select value as the option's name. When you rename an option in the property dialog, the dialog lists what changes along with it before saving, for example Rename “Open” to “To do” in 12 records.

– Update records carries the new name everywhere: into the records (also record templates, the trash and form drafts), into the views' filters, groups and board columns, into linked views of the database on other pages and into the database's rules – done rule, workflow, automations, form conditions and the issue sync's status mapping. Records keep their value under the new name; workflow checks and automations don't fire for it. Flowplan first keeps a version in the version history.

– Merge: write another option's name in an option's place and the two are merged (Merge “Done” into “Finished”). The records get the remaining option, which keeps its own rules; the merged option's settings under Status rules and done go away – the dialog points this out.
– Save options only saves just the list; records, filters and rules stay on the old names, as before.
– Formulas are not rewritten: if a formula compares against an option's name (such as prop("Status") == "Open"), adjust it yourself.
Renaming needs edit access to the property. For the workspace tags, renaming happens under Settings → Tags & properties.

en.heading: Aliases
paragraphs: The property type Aliases (other names) holds further names of a record, such as "PAC" and "Pompe à chaleur" for the record "Chauffage". A database has at most one such property. In the record you enter the names separated by commas; up to 10 aliases of up to 100 characters each count, surrounding spaces and duplicate names (ignoring case) are dropped.
Aliases work like the title:
– @ mentions and the quick search also find the record by an alias and then show the real title with the alias in grey: "Chauffage · PAC". In the search, aliases weigh as much as the title.
– Unlinked mentions also look for every alias – as a whole word, from two characters, ignoring case. Link keeps the text as written: "PAC" becomes a link to "Chauffage" that still reads "PAC".
– The Markdown export writes them as aliases: into the frontmatter, the Markdown import reads aliases: and alias: back (Frontmatter).

Filters ("contains", "is"), sorting, formulas (as a list, like multi-select), CSV and the other exports treat aliases as a list of texts. An alias may be used by several records; then both appear. Only people who may read a record find it by its aliases.
Pages keep their aliases under … → Aliases … – see Pages and spaces.

en.heading: Property visibility
paragraphs: Single properties such as "Salary" or "Internal note" can be limited to certain people. In the property dialog, the Visibility section sets who may read the property and who may edit it:
Choice Read Edit
Everyone with access (default for reading) Everyone who may read the database –
Editors and owners (default for editing) Edit and owner roles Edit and owner roles
Owners only Owners of the database Owners of the database
Selected groups Members of these groups Members of these groups with edit rights
– Only owners of the database change the visibility; they always see and edit everything themselves.

– Restricted properties show a lock in the column header. Whoever may not read a property does not get the column at all; cells someone may only read are read-only and say on hover who may edit them ("Editable only by …").
– The rules only narrow page and record permissions: whoever may only view the database does not edit a property for "selected groups" either.
– Everyone with access always sees the title property (the first one).

– The server enforces the rules everywhere: in the database itself, in linked views, dashboards, whiteboard cards, exports (Markdown, CSV, JSON, Word, EPUB, print), versions, through the API and the MCP server, for the AI and in calendar subscriptions. It refuses changes to properties someone may not edit – in the record, through bulk editing, import, API, AI or CalDAV – with a message.
– Restricted properties are never public: publications, links with their own permissions, forms, the customer portal and webhooks leave them out, even when a link allows editing.
– Full-text search and the AI's semantic search do not index restricted properties, for anyone.

– Formulas, rollups, AI properties, progress and time that read a hidden property count as hidden for that person as well – their result would otherwise give the value away. A formula with a computed prop() name depends on every property. A rollup is hidden when the person may not read the property in the target database.

– Whoever does not see a property can neither lose nor delete it when changing the schema. Versions of a database with restricted properties are restored by owners only, and records with hidden properties cannot be turned into a page or moved to another database (copying leaves the hidden values out).
Filters and sorting of a view that use a hidden property work on empty values for that person; the condition itself (such as the value compared with) stays stored in the view.

en.heading: Relations
paragraphs: – Add property → Relation and choose the target database.
– Optionally in both directions: the target database gets a counterpart property, and changes are kept in sync on both sides.
– In the cell, search for records and link them; several links can be removed one by one or cleared together.
Relations appear as links in the record. The database search also finds records by the names of linked records, and relation filters offer these names directly.

Linked records show their icon, in the cell and in the picker. Clicking a linked record opens it in a window over the current table – you stay in your database and return to it with Close. Open in database switches to the record's own database.

en.heading: Rollups
paragraphs: – Create a relation first.
– Add property → Rollup, then choose the relation and a property of the target database.

– Choose a calculation – 22 are available, depending on the type: original values, unique values, count, empty/not empty (also as a percentage), sum, average, median, minimum, maximum, range, checked/unchecked, earliest and latest date, date range.

Earliest and latest date over Created at or Edited at give an instant in UTC, shown in your time zone. Number rollups appear as a number, progress bar, progress ring or rating, with an adjustable target value. Values from databases someone may not read are not loaded for that person.

en.heading: AI properties
paragraphs: When AI is switched on, a property can take its value from an instruction to the AI – such as a summary or a category from other properties. Everything about it under AI in databases.

en.heading: Formulas
paragraphs: Choose the type Formula in the property dialog. The editor offers 58 functions with search, categories, signatures and examples, suggestions while you type and a live preview on a record of your choice.
round(prop("Effort") * prop("Hourly rate"), 2)
if(prop("Done"), "✓", concat(format(dateBetween(prop("Due"), today(), "days")), " days"))
– References with prop("Name") stay valid when the property is renamed.
– Syntax errors show their position and prevent saving.
– Numeric results are available in filters, sorting, charts and column calculations.
– Date functions calculate in UTC unless a zone is given; now() and today() update every minute.

– If a date is empty, date functions return an empty result instead of #ERROR. In comparisons an empty value counts as 0 – so dateBetween(prop("Due"), today()) < 3 also matches records without a date; guard it with !empty(prop("Due")) && dateBetween(prop("Due"), today()) < 3.
– Formulas read Created at and Edited at as an instant in UTC (such as 2026-11-05T17:39:02Z), so every date function works with them, e.g. formatDate(prop("Created at"), "MM/DD", "America/New_York").
– Formulas do not run JavaScript; length, nesting and result size are limited.

en.heading: Function groups
paragraphs: Group Examples
Logic if, ifs, coalesce, and, or, not, empty
Numbers sum, average, min, max, round, ceil, floor, abs, mod, pow, sqrt
Text concat, length, contains, replace, replaceAll, trim, slice, lower, upper, format, toNumber
Date now, today, parseDate, formatDate, dateAdd, dateSubtract, dateBetween, year, month, day, hour, timestamp
Lists list, count, at, first, last, join, split, unique, sort, reverse
The formula editor shows the complete list.
Table of contents, collapsible sections, reading and focus mode, showing authors – and presenting a document as slides.

en.heading: Table of contents
paragraphs: The list icon at the top right of a document opens the table of contents beside the text – in every document, journal days and database records included. It is built from the headings and grows while you write, marks the section you are reading and jumps to a heading on click. Its header with the close button stays at the top while you scroll a long list; press Esc to close the list. {since=0.9.6} Whether it is open is remembered in this browser for all documents. On a phone a round button at the bottom right opens it.

en.heading: Collapsing sections
paragraphs: Every heading can be collapsed: the small arrow to the left of a heading (it shows on hover; on touch devices and for collapsed headings always) hides everything below it – up to the next heading of the same or a higher level. A collapsed heading shows how much is hidden behind it (… 3 blocks); another click expands it again. With the cursor in the heading, ⌘ ⌥ Enter does the same. On a phone the arrow sits at the end of the heading, in right-to-left text on the other side.

– Collapse / expand all sections: in a document's page menu ⋯, at the top of the table of contents, in quick search (> sections) or with ⌘ ⌥ X and ⌘ ⌥ O (changeable). With a database record open, it applies to the record's text.
– Just for you: what is collapsed is remembered on this device (per page or record) – it does not change the document, others still see everything. Documents you open for the first time are expanded.

– Nothing gets lost: when the cursor gets into a collapsed part (arrow keys, undo, a click in the table of contents), it expands. So it does when Find on page (⌘ F) goes to a match inside, or a search hit, backlink or notification leads there. You can keep typing in the collapsed heading itself; it stays collapsed.
– Moving: dragging a collapsed heading by its handle ⋮⋮ (or moving it with ⌘ ⇧ ↑/↓) takes its whole section along.
– Printing and PDF always show everything; so do export, presentations and published pages.

– Headings directly in the document collapse – in reading mode and in encrypted spaces too. Headings inside callouts, toggles, tables, columns or lists have no arrow; such blocks simply belong to the section they are in.

en.heading: Reading mode
paragraphs: The book icon in the top bar (on a phone Reading mode in the ⋯ menu, or ⌘ ⌥ E, quick search → > reading) opens a document for reading only: nothing changes by accident, handles and the block menu disappear – handy on the phone and when reading aloud or presenting. The pencil switches back to editing. Tasks cannot be ticked off in reading mode – hovering the box shows "Cannot be changed in reading mode". {since=0.9.6} The device remembers the mode per page; permissions stay the same, and others keep their own mode. Database records have the same book icon at the top of the record (see Databases).

Reading mode also covers everything embedded in the page: in linked databases you can't edit cells, add, delete or move records, or change views; a record opened from there is read-only too. Other people's changes keep showing up live. Synced blocks, drawings, metrics, function graphs and extension blocks are locked in reading mode as well.

en.heading: Focus mode
paragraphs: Focus mode (quick search → > focus) hides the sidebar, toolbar and page margins; the top bar only appears on hover. At the bottom, a bar counts the words of the page and those added in this session. With a goal (e.g. 500 words) a bar shows the progress; the device remembers the goal per page. Esc ends the mode.

en.heading: Present
paragraphs: Present in the … menu at the top right (or ⌘ ⌥ P, quick search → > present) shows a document as full-screen slides – without rebuilding it:
– Each heading 1 starts a new slide. If the document has none, each heading 2 does. A divider (---) always starts a new slide.
– Whatever comes before the first heading becomes a title slide with the page title.
– Images, tables, code, formulas and diagrams are scaled down so the whole slide fits on the screen.
Key Effect
→, ↓, Space, Page Down Next slide
←, ↑, Page Up Previous slide
Home / End First / last slide
Esc End the presentation

A click into the right two thirds of the slide moves on, into the left third back. At the bottom, a counter and a bar show where you are; the bar of buttons fades out while the mouse rests. It also switches between light and dark slides. If “Reduce motion” is set on your system, slides change without a fade.

en.heading: Speaker notes and presenter view
paragraphs: A callout (/callout, kind “Note”) as the last block of a slide holds the speaker notes: it does not appear on the slide. Presenter view (notepad icon in the bar) opens a second window with the current and the next slide, the notes and the elapsed time – handy on the laptop while the projector shows the slides. Both windows stay in step: you can move on in either of them.

en.heading: Slides as PDF
paragraphs: The printer icon in the bar prints the slides – each on its own page in landscape. Choose Save as PDF in the print dialog to pass the slides on.

en.heading: Show authors
paragraphs: Show authors (in the toolbar or the page menu …) colours the text by the person who wrote it – each person always in the same colour. A legend shows names and shares; Hide authors turns the colouring off again.
– The content itself doesn't change; the colouring is just a view.
– Recording starts with this feature: older, imported or restored text appears as "earlier", and so does text written by guests through links with their own permissions.
– Images, mentions and other embedded objects are not coloured.
– Only people who may read the page see names.
Bringing an instance back from a backup, from the S3 bucket or to an earlier point in time – and repairing Litestream when its replica is stuck.

en.heading: Ways to restore
paragraphs: – From an instance backup: upload it under Administration → Storage & backup → Restore from backup (at the very end). Flowplan checks it and applies it on the next restart; the previous state stays as pre-restore-… in the data directory.

– From a scheduled backup, with the app stopped: decrypt an encrypted one first, then move the existing flowplan.sqlite with -wal and -shm aside and put the backup in place as /app/data/flowplan.sqlite. With S3, the files follow from the bucket.

– On a new host with S3: start a new installation with the same S3_* variables and an empty volume. Litestream restores the database, the files follow in the background. Stop the old instance first; secrets.key and web-push-keys.json are not in the bucket (see Moving an instance, way C).
– Moving to another server: see Moving an instance – the built-in move tool fetches database, files and keys straight from the old instance, with a few minutes of downtime.

– From a scheduled backup of an instance with PostgreSQL (flowplan-….dump, .dump.enc): also upload it under Restore from backup, or on the setup screen of a new instance with PostgreSQL. Only the database is replaced, the files stay. Only the data of Flowplan's tables is loaded; an archive with custom functions, views or triggers in Flowplan's schema is refused – see PostgreSQL, restoring.
– An earlier point in time, with the app stopped:
litestream restore -config /etc/litestream.yml \
-timestamp 2026-09-26T12:00:00Z -o /app/data/flowplan.sqlite
Move the existing flowplan.sqlite with -wal and -shm aside first.

en.heading: Repair the Litestream state
paragraphs: If two containers replicated on the same volume at the same time (see Roll out SQLite without overlap), the log shows compaction failed … level=1 … close reader 0: file checksum mismatch every 30 seconds. The database is fine – one of Litestream's change files (LTX) is broken. Litestream does not repair it: compaction stays stuck on that file, old change files pile up, and a restore from the bucket through that file fails.

Flowplan detects and repairs this by itself. {since=0.10.0} Every 15 minutes, the container that replicates lists /db/0000/ in the bucket once. Change files older than an hour there, while Litestream has run in this container for more than 30 minutes, mean the replica is stuck. {since=0.10.2} Litestream's memory shows it earlier: each failed compaction buffers all change files since the broken one, until the system ends Litestream (and the container) for lack of memory. Flowplan reads it every minute: above max(512 MB, 25 % of the container's or host's memory) and rising steadily for 10 minutes counts as stuck, too. Then Administration → Monitoring shows a warning, administrators get one message per incident (alerts by webhook, event ops.litestream_stuck, and their chat apps), and the activity log gets an entry. Flowplan makes a scheduled backup if they are on and schedules the repair for the next restart; if the backup fails, nothing is scheduled and it tries again after six hours.

On that start, Flowplan deletes only /db/ in the bucket, resets the local state, and Litestream begins afresh with a full snapshot. Uploads, backups and the database in the volume stay; without a database in the volume the replica is kept. If deleting fails, Flowplan starts normally, logs it and tries again on the next start.

Flowplan does not restart by itself: the repair waits for the next update or restart. Restart now does it right away – the container comes back through its restart policy (restart: unless-stopped, the default in Coolify). Cancel the repair takes it back. With FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM_AUTOHEAL=off you only get the warning and the message; Rebuild the replica now in the warning schedules the repair by hand.
By hand, step 1 – reset the local state. This removes only the local change files in .flowplan.sqlite-litestream/ltx, never the database (litestream reset):
– In the running container (in Coolify under Terminal): touch /app/data/litestream-reset.
– Stop the container and start it again – not as a rolling update.

– On start, the log shows Litestream: resetting the local replication state, then detected database behind replica and fetched latest L0 file from replica: Litestream takes over the last position from the bucket and carries on from there. Flowplan deletes the litestream-reset file by itself afterwards.
Without a running container, do the same by hand: stop the container, delete only the folder .flowplan.sqlite-litestream in the volume (never flowplan.sqlite, -wal or -shm), start the container.
Step 2 – only if the message keeps coming afterwards: then the broken file is in the bucket too, and Litestream reads it from there when compacting. Start replication afresh:
– To be safe, create and download a backup under Administration → Storage & backup.
– In the running instance, echo remote > /app/data/litestream-reset (the same as Rebuild the replica now), then stop the container and start it again. {since=0.10.0}

– On start, Flowplan deletes only /db/ in the bucket, resets the local state and starts Litestream. Litestream finds no state in the bucket, starts from scratch and uploads a full snapshot of the database right away (/db/0009/).

Without remote (an empty litestream-reset file), Flowplan only resets the local state as in step 1. You can also delete the folder /db/ in the bucket yourself while the container is stopped – not /uploads/ or /backups/, those are the files and backups.
Until that snapshot is in the bucket, there is no earlier point in time to restore from there; the database in the volume and your backups stay untouched.

en.heading: Restore while setting up
paragraphs: A new, still empty instance takes over a backup right on the setup screen: under Create account, click Restore from a backup (Installation, first start). You can use

– File: a scheduled backup (flowplan-….sqlite, .sqlite.enc) or the backup of the whole instance (flowplan-instanz-….zip, .zip.enc), up to 50 GB. The upload is written straight to disk and shows its progress. If attachments are then missing – neither in the backup nor in the instance's file storage –, the page says how many; if the old instance kept its files in S3 or on an SFTP server, restore from there.
– S3: the newest scheduled backup from /backups/ of a bucket, with the files from /uploads/ – any missing there come from /.deleted/uploads/.

– SFTP: the newest backup from the folder, with the files from uploads/ (if Include files was on) – any missing there come from .deleted/uploads/. Flowplan shows the host key first; it only signs in once you confirm The fingerprint matches.

If the backup is encrypted, the page asks for the old instance's key (FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY) – or it is already set on the new one. Flowplan checks the database (intact, a Flowplan database, not from a newer version – older ones are brought up to date when they open, as with an update), puts the empty initial state aside as pre-restore-… and applies the backup right away. Afterwards you sign in with an account from the backup. If Litestream runs (S3 without FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM=off), the backup is applied on the next restart of the container – the page says so.

This is only possible while the instance has no account, and with FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN set only via the setup link. As soon as an account exists, the server refuses every request for it; then Administration → Storage & backup → Restore from backup remains.

> Stored secrets (authenticator apps, AI and messenger keys, the SFTP password) can only be read with the same FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY or FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY as on the old instance; without either, the key is in secrets.key in the data folder, which is in no backup. If you entered a key while restoring, set it as FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY afterwards.

en.page: Users from a directory: SCIM and LDAP
paragraphs: Have the identity provider create and remove accounts via SCIM, or check sign-ins against an LDAP directory such as Active Directory.

en.page: Users from a directory: SCIM and LDAP
en.heading: User provisioning (SCIM)
paragraphs: With SCIM 2.0 your identity provider creates accounts in Flowplan, keeps name and address up to date and deactivates accounts as soon as someone leaves – without the person having to sign in first. Flowplan speaks SCIM 2.0 as in RFC 7643/7644 (users and groups, filters, PATCH).
Setting up
– Administration → Sign-in & SSO → SCIM tokens: Create token. The token starts with fpscim_ and is shown only once; only its hash is stored. You can revoke it at any time.
– At the provider, enter the SCIM base URL /api/scim/v2 and the token as bearer token.
– Assign people and groups to the app at the provider, or turn on "Push Groups".
What Flowplan does with it

– Accounts: a new SCIM account is an SSO account. If an account with the same e-mail address exists, it is linked instead of duplicated. At the first OIDC sign-in the person takes over the prepared account – by the externalId (= the provider's sub) or a verified e-mail address.

– Deactivating: active: false disables the account like Block in the administration – all sessions end at once, API tokens stop working. active: true enables it again. Deleting (DELETE) deactivates and unlinks; the content and the account itself stay, final deletion is still done in the administration. The last admin account with a password cannot be deactivated over SCIM.

– Groups: SCIM groups do not create groups in Flowplan. Their display name counts like an SSO group from the token: the SSO group mappings give the role and workspace groups, and all rules from there apply (the mapping always wins, the last owner stays). Membership changes take effect at once, not only at the next sign-in. A person's OIDC groups and SCIM groups are combined.
– Accounts with e-mail and password can be linked and deactivated, but mappings do not change their memberships.
– The last SCIM requests with their status are listed in the administration – useful when the provider reports errors.
Not supported: bulk, sorting, /Me and password changes (Flowplan stores no password for SCIM accounts).

en.page: Users from a directory: SCIM and LDAP
en.heading: SCIM with common providers
paragraphs: – Okta: app integration (SAML or OIDC) → Provisioning → "SCIM connector base URL" = /api/scim/v2, "Unique identifier field for users" = userName, authentication mode HTTP Header with the token. Under "To App" turn on Create Users, Update User Attributes and Deactivate Users; add groups under Push Groups.

– Microsoft Entra ID: enterprise application → Provisioning → mode Automatic, "Tenant URL" = /api/scim/v2, "Secret Token" = the token, Test connection. Keep userPrincipalName → userName and objectId → externalId in the attribute mappings; set the scope to "Sync only assigned users and groups". Entra works in cycles of about 40 minutes.

– Authentik: Applications → Providers → create a SCIM provider, URL /api/scim/v2, enter the token; attach the provider to the Flowplan application as backchannel provider. Groups are sent with their names.
– Keycloak: Keycloak has no SCIM client of its own; install a SCIM extension (e.g. "keycloak-scim") or use LDAP or OIDC groups.

en.page: Users from a directory: SCIM and LDAP
en.heading: Sign-in with LDAP
paragraphs: With LDAP_URL set, the password field of the sign-in page checks names against an LDAP directory (OpenLDAP, 389 DS, Active Directory, …). The field is then called E-mail address or user name.

– Accounts with e-mail and password keep signing in with their Flowplan password. Every other name is searched with the search account (LDAP_BIND_DN) and LDAP_USER_FILTER below LDAP_BASE_DN, and the password is checked by binding as that person. Empty passwords are never sent; the name is escaped as in RFC 4515, so * or ) in a name do not change the filter.

– An LDAP account is a directory account like an SSO account: the first time it is created by its DN or linked to an existing SSO/SCIM account with the same address. An account with e-mail and password of the same address is never taken over.

– Groups come from LDAP_GROUP_ATTRIBUTE (default memberOf): Flowplan takes the group's name (the first RDN, usually the CN, e.g. flowplan-admins) and the full DN. Either can be used in the SSO group mappings and as OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP.

– Hourly sync: Flowplan reads all LDAP accounts again – groups, name, address. Whoever is missing from the directory or locked there (Active Directory userAccountControl, 389 DS nsAccountLock, OpenLDAP ppolicy pwdAccountLockedTime) is disabled; once they are back, they are enabled again. Accounts disabled by an admin stay disabled. A run that would disable more than half of the accounts (at least five) stops – that is more likely a wrong configuration.
– Two-factor sign-in applies as for passwords: LDAP accounts can set up an authenticator app, and the instance's policy ("admins" or "everyone") applies to them too.
– Administration → Sign-in & SSO → LDAP directory shows the status, Test connection and Sync now with the last result.
Variable Default Meaning
LDAP_URL empty ldap://host:389 or ldaps://host:636. Without it, no LDAP.
LDAP_BIND_DN / LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD empty Search account. Without it, the search is anonymous.
LDAP_BASE_DN – Where people are searched, e.g. ou=people,dc=example,dc=org.
LDAP_USER_FILTER (\ (uid={user})(mail={user})) {user} is replaced by the escaped name. Active Directory: (\ (sAMAccountName={user})(userPrincipalName={user})(mail={user})).
LDAP_GROUP_ATTRIBUTE memberOf Attribute with the person's groups.
LDAP_TLS_CA empty CA certificate for ldaps:// or StartTLS (file path or PEM text).
LDAP_TLS_SERVERNAME empty The name the certificate is checked against when LDAP_URL uses an IP address or another name (e.g. dc1.corp.local). {since=0.9.7}

LDAP_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED empty (verify) false turns certificate verification off – only this value; Flowplan then warns at startup, under Sign-in & SSO and in the security overview. Better: LDAP_TLS_CA and LDAP_TLS_SERVERNAME. Also applies to contacts from the directory. {since=0.9.7}
LDAP_STARTTLS false true: encrypt ldap:// with StartTLS.
LDAP_TIMEOUT_MS 8000 Time limit per LDAP operation.

en.page: Users from a directory: SCIM and LDAP
en.heading: Examples
paragraphs: OpenLDAP (with the memberof overlay):
LDAP_URL=ldaps://ldap.example.org LDAP_BIND_DN=cn=flowplan,ou=services,dc=example,dc=org LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD=… LDAP_BASE_DN=ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
Active Directory:

LDAP_URL=ldaps://dc1.corp.example.com LDAP_BIND_DN=CN=svc-flowplan,OU=Service,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com LDAP_BASE_DN=OU=Staff,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com LDAP_USER_FILTER=(&(objectCategory=person)( (sAMAccountName={user})(userPrincipalName={user})(mail={user})))
Keycloak as the source: Keycloak itself is no LDAP server – connect Flowplan to the same directory Keycloak uses through "User Federation", or use OIDC.

Authentik: create an LDAP outpost (provider "LDAP", base DN e.g. dc=ldap,dc=goauthentik,dc=io), a service account with "Search full LDAP directory" as LDAP_BIND_DN (cn=,ou=users,), LDAP_USER_FILTER=( (cn={user})(mail={user})). Groups are in memberOf.

en.page: Users from a directory: SCIM and LDAP
en.heading: Contacts from LDAP
paragraphs: Contacts databases import people from the directory and keep them in sync (directory → Flowplan only). Flowplan uses the server, search account and TLS of the LDAP sign-in (LDAP_URL, LDAP_BIND_DN/LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD, LDAP_TLS_CA, LDAP_STARTTLS, LDAP_TIMEOUT_MS). Base and filter can be separate:
Variable Default Meaning
LDAP_CONTACTS_BASE_DN LDAP_BASE_DN Where contacts are searched; the OU tree of the import dialog starts here. Entries outside it cannot be reached.
LDAP_CONTACTS_FILTER (&(\ (objectClass=inetOrgPerson)(objectClass=user)(objectClass=contact))(!(objectClass=computer))) Which entries are people.
LDAP_CONTACTS_SYNC_MINUTES 60 Interval of the sync (15–1440).
LDAP_CONTACTS_ATTRIBUTES – More attributes mappings may use (separated by commas or spaces). Without it only the attributes of the default mapping are allowed.
LDAP_CONTACTS on off turns contacts from the directory off.
For contacts alone, LDAP_URL with LDAP_CONTACTS_BASE_DN is enough; without LDAP_BASE_DN, sign-in with LDAP stays off.

Administration → Sign-in & SSO → Contacts from LDAP shows where base and filter come from and overrides them: base DN, filter, sync every … minutes, More attributes (attributes allowed on top of LDAP_CONTACTS_ATTRIBUTES, separated by commas) and Allowed (off: nobody can import, the sync rests). Stored values take precedence over the environment; empty fields fall back to the environment. Test connection checks the bind and the base. The search account's password stays in the environment and is never stored. Changes and imports are recorded as the security event “Security-relevant setting changed”.

Who may use the directory: instance administrators, accounts that sign in with LDAP and full members (not guests) of at least one workspace someone else created – never guests of the contacts database's workspace and never an API token. Someone with only workspaces of their own therefore cannot reach the directory, even though anyone may create workspaces. See Contacts from the LDAP directory.
Limits: at most 500 people per list in the dialog (search for more), 2000 linked contacts and 20 OUs per database; every operation has the LDAP_TIMEOUT_MS time limit.
The quick search finds content right down into file attachments. The inbox and push notifications tell you when someone needs you.
More on this topic: Inbox and notifications

en.heading: Quick search
paragraphs: ⌘ K (Windows/Linux Ctrl K) or Search in the sidebar.
It searches:
– page titles and aliases as well as document text,
– tags and property values of pages,
– database records and their content,
– comments,
– file names,
– the text of PDF attachments (up to 50 MB, the first 100,000 characters),
– scanned PDFs and images with text recognition (German and English, French or Chinese (Simplified) on request via FLOWPLAN_OCR_LANGS),
– Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OpenDocument files.

Hits can be filtered by type and space. Journal days come after all other hits; Without journal days leaves them out completely and stays on for the next search. File text is indexed in the background and can be found after a few seconds. The search only shows what you may read. Enter opens the first hit.

Aliases of pages and records weigh as much as the title. When the search only matches an alias, the hit shows the real title with the alias in grey, e.g. "Chauffage · PAC". The same applies in the @ mention dialog.

en.heading: Order, path and recently viewed
paragraphs: Hits whose title is exactly your search come first, then titles that start with it (or have a word that does), then other title hits, and hits only in the text last. Within these, pages and records you open often and recently move up; pages you edited lately and your favourites count a little too. Each hit shows its path (space / … / parent page, for records including the database) and when it was last edited. Above the list are the number of hits and the order: Best match, Last edited or Recently created.
With nothing typed, the quick search lists the pages and records you opened last (up to 20, newest first), grouped by day: Today, Yesterday, then the date.

For this, Flowplan keeps the times of your last ten visits per page and record (to the minute). This history is yours alone: it only affects your own search and nobody else sees it, not even administrators in the app. Visits older than 180 days are deleted, and at most 500 pages and records per person are kept; the history goes when you leave a workspace and when your account is deleted. Access through API tokens does not count.

en.heading: Filter by tags and properties
paragraphs: These words act as filters in the search:
Input Finds
#customer pages with the tag “customer” (case does not matter) and database records carrying it in a multi-select with the workspace's tags; tags with spaces as #"New idea"
-#internal leaves out pages and records with the tag
Status:Open property “Status” with the value “Open” (select and multi-select: exactly this option; text, URL, email, phone: contains)
Budget:>1000, Budget:<=50, Budget:10..20 compare numbers
Due:2026-12, Due:>2026-11-01, Due:2026-11-01..2026-11-30 dates: day, month or year; after, between (also =, <=)
Billed:yes / Billed:no checkbox
Owner:Emil, Owner:me person by name; me is you
Status:* / Status:- property set / empty

Names with spaces go in quotes: "Next step":Offer. Several filters apply together; the remaining text is searched as usual. Filters without text list all matching pages, most recently changed first. Records count with their own tags and those of their database page. Words that name no tag and no property (like #123) stay ordinary search words.

Tags and properties can apply in one space only, and two spaces may have ones of the same name. #Urgent is a name: it finds the pages with any tag of that name you may see – in each space the one that applies there. The Tag … field next to the search field shows, with a space chosen, only its tags and the workspace's; for all spaces all of them with the space's name as a hint. The tag view, in contrast, shows exactly one tag (same-named ones of other spaces on request).

Recognised filters appear as chips under the search field; ✕ removes one. The Tag … field next to the space adds a tag filter: type a few letters and the list shows only the matching tags – case and accents do not matter, tags that start with them come first. ↑ and ↓ choose, Enter or Tab take the tag, Esc closes the list. {since=0.10.0} The search field itself suggests tags the same way as soon as you type # and a letter: Enter or Tab replace what you typed with the tag, in quotes for names with spaces; without suggestions the arrow keys move through the matches as usual. Command mode (>) shows no suggestions. {since=0.10.0} Collections keep the filters. Tag names and values are also ordinary words of the page: “customer” also finds pages tagged “customer”.

en.heading: Combine: AND, OR, NOT
paragraphs: Conditions combine freely, in the search and in collections:
Input Meaning
#customer #open both (AND; you may write AND between them)
#open OR #waiting, #open \ #waiting either
-#internal, NOT #internal, -draft without; - or NOT works before any condition and before parentheses
(#open OR #waiting) -#internal parentheses group
created_by:Anna, creator:me created by (a name, or me for you)
updated_by:Emil, editor:me last changed by
created:-7d, updated:this-week created or changed in the last 7 days, this week
created:2026-03, updated:>2026-01-01, created:2026-01-01..2026-01-31 year, month or day; after (>, >=), before (<, <=), a range
type:document, type:database\ whiteboard, type:record only documents, databases, whiteboards or database records (also notebook, journal)
in:"Team Marketing" only in this space
title:offer only the title contains the word

Relative dates: -7d, -2w, -3m and -1y mean the last 7 days, 2 weeks, 3 months or a year, including today. You can also use today, yesterday, this-week, last-week, this-month, last-month, this-year and last-year. Weeks start on Monday. "Today" is the day in your time zone. These also work for date properties: Due:this-week.
Precedence: NOT/- binds tightest, then AND, then OR. So #A #B OR #C means (#A #B) OR #C. Use parentheses when in doubt. OR, AND and NOT only count in capitals. A lower-case "or" stays a search word.
Words: Words right next to each other are searched as one phrase, as before. With AND between them (invoice AND open), they can appear anywhere.

Keys: created_by, creator, updated_by, editor, created, updated, type, in and title are English and ignore case. If a property has the same name, put its name in quotes: "Type":Book. For database records, Property:value first checks the record's own property of that name (e.g. Priority:High), then the database page's.

All existing searches work as before. Searches that use the new conditions list the matching pages and records without a text snippet, most recently changed first. The server does not search end-to-end encrypted spaces.

en.heading: Commands
paragraphs: The same quick search also runs commands: if the input starts with >, only commands appear, such as > new database, > tasks, > dark or > focus; Enter runs the first one. Matching commands also appear above the search hits without >. With a page open there are page commands as well: favourite, follow, comments, export, print/PDF, version history, share and focus mode.

en.heading: Collections
paragraphs: A collection is a saved search with its own place in the sidebar. Each time you open it, Flowplan searches again. New and changed pages and records that match appear by themselves.
– Create: In the quick search, choose Save as collection (the search's kind and space become type: and in:), or select + next to Collections in the sidebar.

– Filters or text: In the editor, build the query under Filters. Groups require all conditions (AND) or any condition (OR). You can exclude any condition or group (NOT). The conditions are tag, created by, last edited by, property (by type: select, multi-select, text, number, date, checkbox, person), created and updated (relative or fixed), type, space, title contains and text contains. Text shows the same query in the search language. Both views stay in step: what you change in the text shows up in the filters again. If a text cannot be shown as filters (for example because of a missing parenthesis), the editor stays in text mode and says so. Below the query you see right away how many matches there are.

– Results: As a list or a table with title, type, space, tags, updated and created by. Most recently changed come first; select a column heading to sort the matches loaded so far. You see 500 matches at first. If more match, the end shows “500 of N matches” and Load more – each click appends the next 500 until all are there. When something changes in the workspace meanwhile, every match you have loaded stays. {since=0.9.6}

– Manage: The … menu next to a collection has Edit (name, emoji, filters, sharing), Duplicate, Move up/Move down and Delete. You can also drag collections into order; the order is yours alone. After you delete a collection, Undo brings it back.

– Sharing: New collections are private. With Share with the workspace, all members see it under Shared; guests do not. Only you and the workspace's owners can change or delete it. Only you can share it or stop sharing it. Others can choose Duplicate as my collection.

– Permissions: In a collection, each person sees only what they may read themselves. This also applies to shared collections: no private spaces, no private records of others, no hidden properties, no journals behind a PIN, nothing from the trash. End-to-end encrypted spaces are left out, and the collection says so.
– Limits: 100 collections per person and workspace, 100 shared ones per workspace.
Saved searches from earlier versions became private collections when you updated. Searches for comments or files keep their words, but not the kind.
Which security events Flowplan records, how it detects attacks and how to pass them on to logs, OpenTelemetry, fail2ban or CrowdSec.

en.heading: Security
paragraphs: Flowplan records security-relevant events, detects typical attacks in them and hands both to your own tools. It all works without setup; the variables below only connect it to the outside.

en.heading: What is recorded
paragraphs: – Sign-in: successful, failed, refused (limit or block), from a new device
– Account: password changed or reset, passkey added or removed, two-factor on or off, API token created or revoked, sessions ended, account deleted
– Rights: admin rights granted or removed (also through SSO or LDAP groups at sign-in), roles, invitations, accounts disabled or reset by admins
– Sharing and data: share links, published pages, all exports and backups
– Refused: requests from a foreign origin, internal addresses (SSRF), scripts in submitted content, many refused API requests from one address

– Administration: LDAP, SCIM, restore, extensions, domains, AI provider, alerts and other security-relevant settings; sign-up, demo, invite links, the two-factor requirement and emergency access switched on or off, SSO group mappings added or removed {since=0.9.8}

Privacy: for an address, the database keeps only its network (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48) and a hash keyed with a secret of the instance – enough to group and block, not the address itself. Accounts of failed sign-ins are only stored masked (ma***@example.com). Events are deleted after 90 days (FLOWPLAN_SECURITY_RETENTION_DAYS).

en.heading: Administration → Threats & incidents
paragraphs: The page /#admin/threats (group Security) sums it up and refreshes every 30 seconds:
– State: open incidents (critical ones in red), hints on missing connections, numbers of the last 24 hours and sign-ins per hour

– Incidents of the detection rules, with actions right next to them: resolved, block the address or network for 24 hours, end all sessions of the person, disable the account. Details & next steps opens an incident's own page (/#admin/threats/incident/): on the left what happened – why the rule fired (with its thresholds), the period, the origin and whether it is already blocked, the accounts tried, successful sign-ins in the same period (red when an account may have been taken over afterwards), networks, countries, devices and the timeline of all its events; for probing also the requested paths with answer and count (IDs and tokens replaced by :id, :n and :token). On the right what the incident means, when it is harmless and what to do step by step – with the matching action (block the address, end sessions, disable the account, resolve) or the link to it right at the step.
– Addresses with failures, events with filters (severity, kind) and export as CSV or JSON
– Signed-in people (admins first), open ways in (API tokens, share links, public pages of the whole instance) to revoke
– Blocks of addresses and networks, for a time or indefinitely. Blocked addresses only get 403 – signed-in people in them too. Your own address and network cannot be blocked.

New incidents go to all instance admins as notifications of the kind Security incidents of the instance. Each admin chooses how under Settings → Notifications: the channels (by default inbox, push, e-mail and chat apps) and whether all incidents or critical only arrive; the notification leads straight to the incident's page, and the top of the incident list says how you are notified right now. When a webhook is set up under Monitoring → Alerts by webhook, every incident also goes there right away (event ops.security with rule and severity). At most 30 reports an hour, so an attack floods nobody.
Whoever signs in with a device not seen for 90 days gets a security notice themselves – a taken-over account is often noticed by its owner first.

en.heading: Detection rules
paragraphs: Rule Trigger Severity
Password guessing on an account 10 failures on one account in 15 minutes warning
Many failures from one address 20 failures from one address in 15 minutes warning
Many accounts from one address 5 different accounts from one address in 15 minutes (credential stuffing) critical
Sign-in after many failures successful sign-in after 5 failures on the same account critical
Admin from a new device an admin signs in with a device not seen for 90 days warning
Two countries in a short time sign-ins from two countries within 2 hours (needs FLOWPLAN_COUNTRY_HEADER) critical

Rights changed admin rights granted or removed (also through the SSO or LDAP group at sign-in), LDAP/SCIM, restore, extensions, domains. Removed admin rights count too: whoever takes over an admin account locks the others out this way. {since=0.9.8} critical

Two-factor of an admin off an admin turns off their two-factor sign-in, or another admin resets it – from then on the password alone opens the account that runs the instance. For other accounts this is only an event. critical {since=0.9.8}

Access to the instance opened sign-up for everyone, demo, invite links or emergency access switched on, the two-factor requirement relaxed, or an SSO group mapping added or removed. Closing something again is only an event. warning {since=0.9.8}

Emergency access granted a trusted contact gets read access to an account's content (waiting period over or inactivity message) or exports through it; one incident per account and trusted contact a day warning {since=0.9.8}
Encryption key reset an account resets its key for encrypted spaces (passphrase and recovery key lost) – only affects its own access to those spaces warning {since=0.9.6}
Several keys reset 3 accounts reset their encryption key within an hour critical {since=0.9.6}
Many exports more than 20 exports by one person in an hour (and far above their usual) warning
Probing 60 refused API requests (401/403/404) from one address in 10 minutes warning
Attacks through content 5 refused scripts or internal addresses in an hour warning

The same thing within a day counts on the open incident instead of opening a new one. For Access to the instance opened that is the same setting or, for SSO group mappings, the same admin – ten mappings in a row are one incident. {since=0.9.8}

Critical or warning: admin rights and an admin's two-factor sign-in concern the whole instance and are critical – they arrive even with “critical only” in the notifications. Emergency access and opened access are warnings: usually they are meant that way (the person had the waiting period to deny it, an admin chose the setting on purpose), but you should know. {since=0.9.8}

en.heading: Logs (stdout, JSON)
paragraphs: Every event is a JSON line on stdout – Docker, Loki, Elastic, Graylog or Datadog pick them up as they are:

{"ts":"2026-10-30T19:11:27.536Z","level":"warn","logger":"flowplan.security","event":"login.failure","severity":"warn","ip":"203.0.113.7","network":"203.0.113.0/24","subject":"ma***@example.com","device":"Chrome · macOS","detail":"password"}

More fields depending on the event: user (account id), country. The full address (ip) is only in this line – for fail2ban and CrowdSec. FLOWPLAN_SECURITY_LOG=anonymous leaves it out, =off writes no lines.

en.heading: OpenTelemetry
paragraphs: With OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT) Flowplan sends the events as OTLP logs (HTTP/JSON, /v1/logs) to your collector, e.g. Grafana Alloy, the OpenTelemetry Collector, Grafana Cloud, Honeycomb or Datadog. Credentials go in OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS (api-key=…,x-scope-orgid=…), the service name in OTEL_SERVICE_NAME (default flowplan). The fields of the log line arrive as attributes flowplan.*.

en.heading: Prometheus
paragraphs: /api/metrics also has flowplan_security_events_total{event,severity}, flowplan_security_incidents_open{rule,severity} and flowplan_security_blocks. An alert in Prometheus or Grafana:
- alert: FlowplanSecurityIncident
expr: sum(flowplan_security_incidents_open{severity="critical"}) > 0
for: 1m

en.heading: fail2ban
paragraphs: With the journald logging driver (logging: { driver: journald } in the Compose service) fail2ban reads the lines directly:
# /etc/fail2ban/filter.d/flowplan.conf
[Definition]
failregex = "logger":"flowplan\.security","event":"login\.(failure|refused)","severity":"[a-z]+","ip":"<HOST>"
"logger":"flowplan\.security","event":"request\.probing","severity":"[a-z]+","ip":"<HOST>"
# /etc/fail2ban/jail.d/flowplan.conf
[flowplan]
enabled = true
backend = systemd
journalmatch = CONTAINER_NAME=flowplan
filter = flowplan
maxretry = 10
findtime = 10m
bantime = 1h
When fail2ban blocks in the firewall in front of the reverse proxy, the request never arrives. The blocks in Flowplan itself also work behind Cloudflare or a proxy fail2ban does not control.

en.heading: CrowdSec
paragraphs: A parser for the log lines and a scenario for password guessing (example; the acquisition with labels: { type: flowplan }):
# parsers/s01-parse/flowplan.yaml
name: flowplan/flowplan-logs
description: "Flowplan security events"
filter: "evt.Line.Labels.type == 'flowplan'"
onsuccess: next_stage
nodes:
- filter: "UnmarshalJSON(evt.Line.Raw, evt.Unmarshaled, 'flowplan') in ['', nil] && evt.Unmarshaled.flowplan.logger == 'flowplan.security'"
statics:
- meta: log_type
expression: "'flowplan_' + replace(evt.Unmarshaled.flowplan.event, '.', '_')"
- meta: source_ip
expression: evt.Unmarshaled.flowplan.ip
# scenarios/flowplan-bf.yaml
type: leaky
name: flowplan/login-bf
description: "Flowplan password guessing"
filter: "evt.Meta.log_type in ['flowplan_login_failure', 'flowplan_login_refused']"
groupby: evt.Meta.source_ip
capacity: 10
leakspeed: 30s
blackhole: 5m
labels:
remediation: true

en.heading: More variables
paragraphs: Variable Default Effect
FLOWPLAN_SECURITY_LOG on on (with address), anonymous (without), off (no log lines)
FLOWPLAN_SECURITY_RETENTION_DAYS 90 How long events stay in the database (at least 7)

FLOWPLAN_COUNTRY_HEADER empty The proxy's header with the country of the request, e.g. CF-IPCountry behind Cloudflare – turns on the rule "two countries". Only set it when the proxy sets the header itself.
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT empty OTLP collector for the events (see above)

OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_HEADERS OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS Headers for the collector, for the logs only: api-key=abc,x-scope=flowplan (comma-separated, values URL-encoded). Without it, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS applies.
Everything with addresses needs the reverse proxy to set X-Forwarded-For and a correct FLOWPLAN_TRUSTED_PROXIES (Configuration). When no address arrives, the page shows a hint.
How long a session lasts is set under Administration → Sign-in & SSO → Sessions (Administration); without a setting there, the environment variables and their defaults apply.
Where How long (default) Setting · variable
Browser without Stay signed in 8 hours after signing in – even while Flowplan is open Browser without “Stay signed in” · SESSION_HOURS (1–24)

Browser with Stay signed in 7 days after the last use, at most 30 days after signing in Offer “Stay signed in” in the browser · SESSION_REMEMBER (default off), Browser with “Stay signed in” · SESSION_IDLE_HOURS

Desktop and mobile app 90 days after the last use of the app or its widgets, at most 365 days after signing in Desktop and mobile apps · SESSION_APP_REMEMBER (default on), Apps: end without use · SESSION_APP_DAYS

– In the browser the sign-in page shows the Stay signed in box as soon as the administration offers it – for password, passkey and SSO (also through “Connect account”). It is meant for your own devices: when ticked, the session lives on while Flowplan is used. The longest lifetime (SESSION_MAX_DAYS, default 30 days, never shorter than the time without use) limits how long a stolen cookie is good for.

– The apps run on personal devices and always stay signed in – whether you signed in with a password in the app or with a passkey or SSO through the browser. The widgets keep the session alive as well. The app has to prove the sign-in is its own; that the app's name is in the user agent is not enough, because any browser can send it:
– Passkey, SSO or “Sign in in the browser”: the hand-off back to the app is the proof – only the app that started the sign-in can redeem it. This works with every app version.

– Password in the app: newer apps (iPhone, iPad and Android after 1.0.5, desktop after 1.3.0) create a random device key per server on first launch, keep it in the system's key store (Keychain, Android Keystore, the desktop's key store) and send it with the password. The first sign-in of an account on that device registers the key; later sign-ins need the same key. The server keeps only a hash.

– Older app versions (such as 1.0.5) have no device key: after a password sign-in they stay signed in like a browser – 8 hours, or with Stay signed in where the instance offers it (the box then appears in the app as well). Sign-ins with a passkey or SSO keep the app's lifetime; so do app sessions that existed before this change. An instance that does not want this sets Desktop and mobile apps to As in the browser without “Stay signed in” (SESSION_APP_REMEMBER=false). The app lock in the app's settings (Face ID, Touch ID, fingerprint or device passcode, on iPhone, iPad and Android) protects the phone further.

– SSO sessions extend the same way. Group changes at the provider follow through SCIM, the LDAP sync or the next sign-in. Only when SESSION_GROUPS_HOURS is set does an SSO session that stays signed in end after that many hours already: signing in at the provider again fetches the current groups, so OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUP and OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP apply by then at the latest, even without SCIM.
– A disabled account loses access immediately, as before.

– When the same person signs in again on a device (for example because the session ran out), the app's registration survives – notifications, widgets, Live Activities and Shortcuts move over to the new session. Only an explicit Sign out (in the app or under Signed-in devices) removes it.

– Shorter times apply from the next sign-in; longer ones extend sessions that stay signed in the next time they are used. Turning “Stay signed in” or the apps' staying signed in off stops the extending; running sessions then end at their next expiry.
Settings → Account & security → Signed-in devices lists all your own sessions with device, last use and end; Sign out ends a single one, Sign out all other devices all but the current one.
The introduction after your first sign-in, the “Getting started” list and how to find what you need in Settings.

en.heading: The introduction
paragraphs: After creating an account, Flowplan walks you through the essentials once. Every step can be skipped, and everything can be changed later in the settings:
– Welcome: language and appearance (automatic, light or dark).
– Set up the instance (admins only): a traffic light for address and HTTPS, e-mail delivery, backup, sign-in and AI, each with the way into the administration (Set up the instance). {since=0.9.7}

– Where are you coming from? Notion, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Evernote, Confluence, Google Docs / Word, BookStack {since=0.10.0} or Start fresh. When you pick a tool, Flowplan shows step by step where its export is and which file you need, and with Choose file and import imports it right into your first space – with progress and result (Moving to Flowplan). {since=0.9.7} For BookStack you enter its address and an API token instead (From BookStack). {since=0.10.0}
– What it's called here (only after picking a tool): what you know from the tool and what it is called in Flowplan – the same, similar or without a counterpart (Terms when moving). {since=0.9.7}

– What would you like to start with? Set the workspace's name (as its owner) and say what you mainly use Flowplan for: Personal, Team & knowledge, Projects & tickets, Study & writing or Something else. Flowplan then suggests matching pages – such as a task list, journal, habit tracker and reading list for yourself, or a team wiki, meeting log, decision log and project plan for a team – which you click and create as you go on (for example Create 2 and continue). Create sample space makes a private space with sample pages (a project, a wiki with a meeting note, a whiteboard); Remove sample space takes exactly these pages out again, pages of your own in it stay. If you have no settings level of your own yet, the answer sets one: Personal Beginner, team, projects and study Normal; Something else keeps the instance's default. {since=0.9.7}
– What Flowplan does: a short tour of pages and blocks, databases, whiteboards, the journal, collaboration, sharing, search and offline – each with a tip and a link into this documentation.
– Notifications: e-mail summaries (when the instance sends e-mail) and push on this device.

– Work without a connection too? offers offline use on this device, with what gets stored for it: Use offline, Later or Don't ask again. Left out where offline cannot work, in the apps (they ask themselves) and when it is on already. {since=0.9.7}
– All set: the created and imported pages to open and the most important shortcuts.

Later, Settings → Appearance & language → Show introduction (or "introduction" in the search with ⌘/Ctrl K) opens it again. Accounts that existed before the introduction was added do not see it automatically.

> Moving from Notion, AFFiNE, Obsidian, Evernote, Confluence or Google Docs? You can do it in the introduction (step Where are you coming from?) and at any time under Settings → Import & export. What comes along and how best to go about it is in Moving to Flowplan.

en.heading: Getting started in the sidebar
paragraphs: After the introduction, the Getting started list waits in the sidebar with its progress ("2 of 6"): Write a first page, Create a task, Invite someone (for owners), Install the app, Try search and commands and Import content – the last one not if you already imported in the introduction. Every item has a button that takes you there (such as New page or Open import). Page, task, invitation and import tick themselves once you have done them; the app and the search are reported by the browser, and you can tick any item by hand. The list can be folded (the browser remembers it) and hidden for good with Hide the list; Show getting started in the command palette (⌘/Ctrl K) brings it back. If there is a sample space, you can remove it here too. Only people who went through the introduction get the list.

en.heading: Settings: overview and search
paragraphs: You open Settings in the sidebar. The overview has one tile per section in the groups Personal, Connections, Workspace and Help & info; the search at the top (“Search settings …”) finds single settings, also those above your level (see below). Every section has its own link, e.g. /#settings/notifications. For admins, the instance's settings are under Administration.

en.heading: Settings levels
paragraphs: So that not everything is there at once at the start, every personal setting belongs to one of three levels: Beginner (the essentials to start with – such as language, appearance, name, password, passkeys, the basics of notifications and capturing), Normal (most settings) and Expert (all of them, also those for developers and advanced use – such as API tokens, webhooks, block extensions or customizing the formatting toolbar). You see the settings up to your level; higher ones are hidden.
– Switch level: at the very top of Settings under Settings level. The choice applies to your account on all devices.
– Marks: settings with a level of their own carry a sign – a green circle for Beginner, a yellow diamond for Normal, a red triangle for Expert (the tooltip says "Level: …").

– What is missing: below a section it says how many settings belong to higher levels ("3 more settings belong to higher levels."); Show anyway shows them for now. Sections that lie entirely above your level are left out of the overview and the navigation.

– The search finds everything: settings above your level also appear in the search, with their sign and, for example, "Expert level". When you open one, Flowplan says "This setting belongs to the Expert level." and offers Switch level: Expert and Show anyway.

New accounts start with the instance's default – Normal, unless the administration sets another one (Settings level for new accounts); the answer in the introduction can adjust it. Accounts that existed before the levels are on Expert and so see everything as before. Admins can set a person's level under Users. The Administration itself has no levels: admins always see everything there.

en.heading: Show and hide features
paragraphs: If you don't need something, hide it under Settings → Appearance & language → Features (Normal level). There is a switch per feature: Flashcards, Whiteboards, Notebooks, Journal, Dashboards, Workflows, draw.io, AI, More view types (board, calendar, timeline, gallery, chart, feed and sprints – table and list always stay), Forms and Meetings.

Hidden means: the feature is left out of New page, the "/" menu and the formatting toolbar, the quick search, the sidebar (such as Study), the home page widgets and Add view. With AI, every way into the AI goes. What exists stays: pages, records and views of that kind – also other people's – still show and open from links, the sidebar and the search, and permissions do not change. The choice applies to your account on all devices.

New accounts start with the choice the administration sets (Features for new accounts); as long as you switch nothing, it says Instance default there. Once you have chosen yourself, Default goes back to it. Accounts that existed before see everything.

If the administration switched a feature off for the whole instance (Features of this instance), its switch is off and locked, with the notice Switched off for this instance by the administration – it is then not only hidden: existing pages of that kind open read-only. Your own choice is kept and applies again once the feature is switched on.

Share at the top right of every page (on a phone at the top of the ⋯ menu) opens Share page. A line at the top sums up how the page is shared right now – space, people, links and whether it is published. Below, three tabs handle one thing each: People (who in the workspace may access it), Links (named links for outsiders; only for those who may do more than read) and Web (publishing). Longer explanations sit behind the small (i). At the bottom, Copy link to page copies the page's address for everyone with access, and Done closes the dialog.

en.heading: Access in the workspace
paragraphs: Pages inherit the permissions of their space and parent pages; below the list, the People tab names who comes in through the space (such as “Plus all 8 members of the space Team”, with Manage space for those who may). In addition, individual people or groups can be given permissions:
Role May
View Read and comment
Edit Change content, records and views
Private spaces and pages are only visible to the people they are shared with. Guests only see what has been explicitly shared with them (see Workspaces, members and permissions).

en.heading: Share a page with a person
paragraphs: A page or database can be shared with someone who is not in the workspace – without taking them into the whole workspace. Share → People: enter an e-mail address (members are suggested), choose View or Edit, Add.

– The person already has an account on this instance (with a confirmed address): they have access to the page and its sub-pages right away and get a notification in the inbox ("… shared “Page” with you") and – when the instance sends e-mail – right away an e-mail with a link to the page. Settings → Notifications → Pages shared with you turns the e-mail off. If they are not in the workspace yet, they join as a guest and see only what is shared with them.

– No account yet: they get an invitation by e-mail (when set up) and are listed as "Invited". Once they create an account with this address, the page is there. The same goes for an account whose address is not confirmed yet – then only the invitation link (Settings → Members → Pending invitations → Copy link) opens the page.
– Guests do not see the list of people with access; only those who may share see e-mail addresses. Each person sends at most a few dozen invitations an hour, and each address gets only a few e-mails.
– In the list, roles can be changed and people removed. A guest without any shared page left is no longer in the workspace either.
– Owners of the workspace and owners of the page's space may share. Everyone else only sees the list.

en.heading: Links with their own permissions
paragraphs: In the Links tab, + New link creates as many named links as you like, e.g. "Feedback from the customer": choose a name and permission, optionally sub-pages, a password and an expiry date, then Create link. Each link in the list has a copy button and a ⋯ menu.
Link permission Visitors may
Read look at the page
Read and comment also comment; comments carry a guest note
Read, comment and edit also change the title, text and visible properties of existing records
– Links work without an account and can be revoked one by one (⋯ → Revoke).

– With edit links, guests write along live: changes by members and other guests appear right away, and cursors are visible both ways – guests appear as "Guest · ". They write in the same editor as in the workspace: a toolbar with text style, formatting, lists, alignment, formula, diagram and file; / or + opens the block menu (headings, lists, quote, callout, code, divider, formulas, Mermaid, file). {since=0.9.6}
– Optionally they also apply to the sub-pages that exist right now; new sub-pages are not added automatically.
– Edit links cannot change permissions, members, private relations or files properties. Before every guest edit, Flowplan saves the previous content.
– A journal with a PIN can be neither shared by link nor published; setting the PIN revokes existing links and publications. Sharing a page above it with its sub-pages leaves it out.

en.heading: Editing whiteboards and notebooks with guests
paragraphs: If you share a whiteboard or notebook via a link with Read, comment and edit, guests see an Edit whiteboard or Edit notebook button above the preview picture. They then work in the same editor as you, without an account and live: everyone sees the others' changes right away.
– Whiteboard: add, move and delete notes, text, shapes, connectors, frames, tables and emoji, draw and comment. Their pointer shows as "Guest · ".
– Notebook: write and draw on the sheets and add, duplicate, delete and reorder sheets.

– Not possible: uploading files, templates, AI and facilitation features (votes, timer, private mode), linking pages and exporting. Guests see existing images and PDFs, but not references to pages outside the link.
– If the page is locked, or the link expires or is revoked, editing stops right away. Pages in encrypted spaces and journals with a PIN can't be edited this way.

en.heading: Password and expiry date
paragraphs: Links with their own permissions and publications can have a password and an expiry date – when creating them or later: for links via ⋯ → Password and expiry date, for the publication in the Web tab under Password and Expires. The list shows "Password" or "expires on …".
– Visitors enter the password once per device. It is valid for up to 12 hours and only for this link; a new password signs all visitors out.
– Ten wrong attempts within 15 minutes block that address for the link.

– Editing links have daily budgets: per link, guests upload at most 200 MB of files per day (20 files per 10 minutes) and send at most 100 MB of changes per day; a document does not grow beyond 3 MB of text through a link. For the whole instance FLOWPLAN_ANONYMOUS_UPLOAD_MB applies on top (Configuration).
